title: 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch)

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 1
summaryBullets: The words of the blessing of Enoch, with which he blessed the elect and righteous, who will be living in the day of tribulation, when all the wicked and godless are to be removed. (1:1).

And he took up his parable and said--Enoch a righteous man, whose eyes were opened by God, saw the vision of the Holy One in the heavens, which the angels showed me, and from them I heard everything, and from them I understood as I saw, but not for this generation, but for a remote one which is for to come. (1:2).
Concerning the elect I said, and took up my parable concerning them: The Holy Great One will come forth from His dwelling, (1:3).
And the eternal God will tread upon the earth, (even) on Mount Sinai, And appear from His camp And appear in the strength of His might from the heaven of heavens. (1:4).
And all shall be smitten with fear And the Watchers shall quake, And great fear and trembling shall seize them to the ends of the earth. (1:5).
And the high mountains shall be shaken, And the high hills shall be made low, And shall melt like wax before the flame (1:6).
And the earth shall be wholly rent in sunder, And all that is upon the earth shall perish, And there shall be a judgement upon all (men). (1:7).

But with the righteous He will make peace. And will protect the elect, And mercy shall be upon them. And they shall all belong to God, And they shall be prospered, And they shall all be blessed. And He will help them all , And light shall appear to them, And He will make peace with them . (1:8).

And behold! He comes with ten thousands of His holy ones To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy all the ungodly: And to convict all flesh Of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, And of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him. (1:9).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 33:2: Moses blesses Israel with God coming from Sinai and shining forth from ten thousands of holy ones, the same arrival this chapter describes.
Jude 1:14-15: Jude quotes the last verse of this chapter word for word and credits it to Enoch, the seventh from Adam.
Micah 1:3-4: The LORD comes down and treads the high places of the earth, and the mountains melt like wax before the fire, the exact image used here.
Numbers 23:7: Balaam takes up his oracle in the Hebrew idiom that this chapter renders as taking up a parable.
Isaiah 2:19-21: Men crawl into caves and holes in the rocks before the terror of the LORD when He rises to terrify the earth.

translationNotes.original: Aramaic: עִיר (ir), plural עִירִין (irin) - Greek: ἐγρήγορος (egregoros)
translationNotes.note: The word means a wakeful one, an angel who does not sleep. In Scripture it appears only in the Aramaic chapters of Daniel, where a watcher and holy one comes down from heaven and the sentence is issued by their decree, Daniel 4:13 and 4:17. The oldest surviving fragments of 1 Enoch, found in the caves at Qumran, are in that same Aramaic.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נָשָׂא מָשָׁל (nasa mashal) - Greek: ἀναλαβὼν παραβολήν (analabon parabolen)
translationNotes.note: Not a story with a moral. The Hebrew idiom introduces a formal spoken oracle, and it is how Balaam's oracles are introduced at Numbers 23:7 and again at 24:3. English readers hear the word parable and expect a teaching story; the text is announcing a pronouncement.

The chosen. It is the standing title for the righteous throughout this book, and it is the same word used of the servant God upholds at Isaiah 42:1 and of the offspring who inherit the mountains at Isaiah 65:9.

translationNotes.term: Ten thousands of His holy ones
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רִבְבֹת קֹדֶשׁ (ribebot qodesh) - Greek: μυριάσιν ἁγίων (myriasin hagion)
translationNotes.note: A myriad is ten thousand, the largest counted unit in Greek numbering, so the plural means a host past counting. Daniel 7:10 gives the same picture, ten thousand times ten thousand standing before the throne, and holy ones here means angels, not human saints.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הַר סִינַי (Har Sinai) - Greek: Σινᾶ (Sina)
translationNotes.note: The mountain of the covenant, also called Horeb, where the law was given in fire, cloud, and earthquake at Exodus 19:16-20. The chapter puts God's final coming on the same mountain as the first one, which is why Sinai appears in a passage about the end and not about Moses.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יוֹם צָרָה (yom tsarah) - Greek: θλῖψις (thlipsis)
translationNotes.note: The Greek word means crushing pressure, the squeezing of grapes or the weight of a load. Daniel 12:1 names such a time of trouble as never was since there was a nation, and the same Greek word carries into Matthew 24:21.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch blesses the elect who will live in the day of tribulation, and says the vision is for a distant generation and not his own. God comes out from His dwelling and treads on Sinai, mountains melt like wax, the Watchers quake, and He arrives with ten thousands of His holy ones to judge all flesh.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 2
summaryBullets: Observe you everything that takes place in the heaven, how they do not change their orbits, and the luminaries which are in the heaven, how they all rise and set in order each in its season, and transgress not against their appointed order. (2:1).

Behold you the earth, and give heed to the things which take place upon it from first to last, how steadfast they are , how none of the things upon earth change, but all the works of God appear to you . (2:2).
Behold the summer and the winter, how the whole earth is filled with water, and clouds and dew and rain lie upon it . (2:3).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 31:35-36: The LORD fixes the sun for day and the moon and stars for night, and stakes Israel's survival on that order holding, which is the argument this chapter makes from the sky.
Psalm 148:3-6: Sun, moon, and shining stars are called to praise, because He established them forever by a decree that will not pass away.
Job 38:31-33: God asks whether Job can bind the Pleiades, loose Orion, or knows the ordinances of the heavens.
Genesis 1:14: The lights in the expanse are set for signs and for seasons and for days and years, which is the appointed order this chapter says they keep.
Isaiah 1:3: The ox knows its owner and the donkey its master's crib, but Israel does not know, the same move from creation's obedience to human failure.

translationNotes.note: Light-bearers. It is the word Genesis 1:14-16 uses for sun, moon, and stars, and it is deliberately flat: the surrounding nations named these bodies as gods, and this vocabulary makes them lamps that were hung.

A choq is a fixed decree or an allotted portion, the same word used for a law that cannot be revised. Jeremiah 33:25 calls the courses of day and night a covenant, which is why breaking rank would be a legal violation and not just an oddity of nature.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קַיִץ וָחֹרֶף (qayits va-choreph) - Greek: θέρος καὶ χειμών (theros kai cheimon)
translationNotes.note: The land has two seasons, not four. From about May to October no rain falls at all; from about November to April it does. Genesis 8:22 names them as a fixed pair, and the whole agricultural year turns on the switch.

Two rains, and both are named separately. The early rain falls in October and November and softens baked ground for plowing; the latter rain falls in March and April and fills the grain before harvest. Deuteronomy 11:14 promises both in their season, and Joel 2:23 celebrates their return.

Through the rainless summer, heavy night dew rolling in off the Mediterranean is the only water the western hills and coastal plain get, and it is enough to keep vines and melons alive. That is why dew stands for blessing at Genesis 27:28 and why its withdrawal in 1 Kings 17:1 is a threat.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch tells the reader to look up and look around. The lights of heaven rise and set in their appointed order and never break it, everything on earth runs from first to last without changing, and summer and winter come as they are told, filling the earth with water, cloud, dew, and rain.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 3
summaryBullets: Observe and see how in the winter all the trees seem as though they had withered and shed all their leaves, except fourteen trees, which do not lose their foliage but retain the old foliage from two to three years till the new comes. (3:1).
crossRefs: Isaiah 40:6-8: All flesh is grass and the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever, the same sorting of what withers from what does not.
Psalm 1:3: The righteous man is a tree planted by streams of water whose leaf does not wither.
Jeremiah 17:8: The one who trusts the LORD is a tree by water that does not fear when heat comes, whose leaves stay green in a year of drought.
Ezekiel 47:12: Trees on the river flowing from the sanctuary whose leaves never wither and whose fruit never fails, the evergreen image pushed as far as it goes.
Mark 13:28: The fig putting out leaves is given as a sign to be read, the same use of a tree's seasonal habit as a lesson.

translationNotes.note: The text gives a count and no list. The evergreens of the land it is describing include the olive, the myrtle, the carob, the bay laurel, the evergreen oak, the Aleppo pine, the cypress, the cedar of Lebanon, the juniper, and the oleander.

translationNotes.term: Retain the old foliage from two to three years
translationNotes.note: This is exact botany, not a figure of speech. Evergreens are not leaves-forever trees; they shed and replace foliage gradually over two or more years instead of dropping it all in autumn, so the tree is never bare. Aleppo pine needles and olive leaves both run about two to three years.

The wet half of the year, roughly November to April, when all the region's rain falls. It is a season of cold and mud rather than deep snow outside the mountains, and Song of Songs 2:11 marks its end as the start of everything blooming.

To dry out. The same verb covers a dried-up brook, withered grass, and a shrivelled hand, so the picture is not death by cold but loss of water. It is the verb behind Isaiah 40:7, where the grass withers when the breath of the LORD blows on it.

The evergreen a reader is least likely to think of as one. An olive holds its grey-green leaves year round, bears for centuries, and sends up new shoots from the stump after it is cut down, which is the picture behind the children like olive shoots in Psalm 128:3 and the grafted branches of Romans 11:17-24.

stories.keyTakeaway: A single verse of observation. In winter the trees look dead and drop their leaves, except for fourteen kinds that hold last year's foliage for two or three years until new growth comes to replace it.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 4
summaryBullets: And again, observe you the days of summer how the sun is above the earth over against it. And you seek shade and shelter by reason of the heat of the sun, and the earth also burns with growing heat, and so you cannot tread on the earth, or on a rock by reason of its heat. (4:1).
crossRefs: Jonah 4:8: A scorching east wind and the sun beat on Jonah's head until he was faint, the same summer heat this verse describes.
Psalm 121:5-6: The LORD is your shade at your right hand, so the sun will not strike you by day nor the moon by night.
Isaiah 25:4-5: God is a shade from the heat and a shelter from the storm, the two things this verse says a man goes hunting for.
Isaiah 4:6: A booth for shade by day from the heat, and a refuge and shelter from storm and rain.
James 1:11: The sun rises with its scorching heat, withers the grass, and the flower falls and its beauty is gone.

translationNotes.note: In a land with no rain from May to October, shade is not comfort but survival, which is why the word for shadow became the standard word for protection. The shadow of God's wings in Psalm 17:8 and Psalm 36:7 is built on exactly this experience.

The worst heat there does not come straight down; it blows in. The sharav or khamsin is a dry wind off the eastern desert that can lift the temperature sharply and strip the humidity within hours, most often in spring and autumn. It is the east wind that withers Jonah's plant in Jonah 4:8 and blasts the grain in Genesis 41:6.

The same word means both the hot season and the summer fruit harvest, mostly figs. Amos 8:1-2 turns on that: a basket of summer fruit, qayits, is shown to the prophet, and the word spoken over it is qets, the end has come.

translationNotes.term: You cannot tread on the earth, or on a rock
translationNotes.note: The limestone and black basalt of the Judean wilderness and the Jordan valley soak up the day's sun and give it back well into the night, so bare stone runs far hotter than the air. Travel across that country was done at dawn and dusk for that reason.

stories.keyTakeaway: A second observation from the same year. In summer the sun stands overhead, the heat drives a man to look for shade and shelter, and the ground and the bare rock grow too hot to walk on.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 5
summaryBullets: Observe you how the trees cover themselves with green leaves and bear fruit: wherefore give you heed and know with regard to all His works , and recognize how He that liveth for ever has made them so. (5:1).
And all His works go on thus from year to year for ever, and all the tasks which they accomplish for Him, and their tasks change not, but according as God has ordained so is it done. (5:2).
And behold how the sea and the rivers in like manner accomplish and change not their tasks from His commandments . (5:3).

But you--you have not been steadfast, nor done the commandments of the Lord, But you have turned away and spoken proud and hard words With your impure mouths against His greatness. Oh, you hard-hearted, you will find no peace. (5:4).

Therefore shall you execrate your days, And the years of your life shall perish, And the years of your destruction shall be multiplied in eternal execration, And you will find no mercy. 6 a . In those days you will make your names an eternal execration to all the righteous, b . And by you shall all who curse, curse, And all the sinners and godless shall imprecate by you, 7 c . And for you the godless there shall be a curse. 6 d . And all the . . . shall rejoice, e . And there shall be forgiveness of sins, f . And every mercy and peace and forbearance: g . There shall be salvation to them, a goodly light. i . And for all of you sinners there shall be no salvation, j But on you all shall abide a curse. 7 a . But for the elect there shall be light and joy and peace, b . And they shall inherit the earth. 8 And then there shall be bestowed upon the elect wisdom, And they shall all live and never again sin, Either through ungodliness or through pride: But they who are wise shall be humble. 9 And they shall not again transgress, Nor shall they sin all the days of their life, Nor shall they die of (the divine) anger or wrath, But they shall complete the number of the days of their life. And their lives shall be increased in peace, And the years of their joy shall be multiplied, In eternal gladness and peace, All the days of their life. (5:5).
crossRefs: Isaiah 57:21: There is no peace, says my God, for the wicked, which is the sentence this book repeats over the guilty from here to the end of the section.
Jeremiah 29:22: The exiles will turn the names of two condemned men into the words of a curse, which is what it means for a name to become an execration.
Psalm 37:11: The meek shall inherit the land and delight themselves in abundant peace.
Isaiah 65:20-22: In the age promised, no one dies as an infant or fails to fill out his days, and the chosen enjoy the work of their hands for a long time.
Jeremiah 8:7: The stork, the turtledove, the swift, and the crane keep the times set for them, but the people do not know the rule of the LORD.

translationNotes.note: An old English word for a curse, and here it means something precise. To make a name an execration is to have it used inside the curse formula itself, the way Jeremiah 29:22 says the exiles will say to a man, the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵין שָׁלוֹם (ein shalom) - Greek: οὐκ ἔσται ὑμῖν εἰρήνη (ouk estai hymin eirene)
translationNotes.note: The refrain of the Book of the Watchers. It lands here first, then on the Watchers at 1 Enoch 12:5, on Azazel at 1 Enoch 13:1, and it is the last thing Enoch is told to say to them at 1 Enoch 16:4. The wording comes from Isaiah 48:22.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קָשׁוֹת (qashot) - Greek: σκληροί λόγοι (skleroi logoi)
translationNotes.note: Hard means insolent or stiff, not merely harsh. It is the same charge Jude brings when he quotes this book: all the harsh things ungodly sinners have spoken against Him, Jude 1:15.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ (yireshu arets) - Greek: κληρονομήσουσιν τὴν γῆν (kleronomesousin ten gen)
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew word erets means both the land of Israel and the whole earth, and the promise carries both at once. Psalm 37:11 says it of the meek, and Matthew 5:5 repeats it in the Beatitudes.

translationNotes.term: Complete the number of the days of their life
translationNotes.note: To die old and full rather than cut off early. It is stated as a covenant blessing at Exodus 23:26, where God says He will fulfil the number of a man's days, and Job 5:26 pictures it as a sheaf coming to the threshing floor in its season.

stories.keyTakeaway: The argument turns on the hearer. Trees leaf and bear, sea and rivers hold to their tasks, but you have not been steadfast and have spoken hard words against His greatness. Your names become a curse other men swear by, while the elect are given light, wisdom, peace, and the earth.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 6
summaryBullets: And it came to pass when the children of men had multiplied that in those days were born to them beautiful and comely daughters. (6:1).
And the angels, the children of the heaven, saw and lusted after them, and said to one another: 'Come, let us choose us wives from among the children of men and beget us children.' (6:2).
And Semjâzâ, who was their leader, said to them: 'I fear you will not indeed agree to do this deed, and I alone shall have to pay the penalty of a great sin.' (6:3).
And they all answered him and said: 'Let us all swear an oath, and all bind ourselves by mutual imprecations not to abandon this plan but to do this thing.' (6:4).
Then sware they all together and bound themselves by mutual imprecations upon it. (6:5).

And they were in all two hundred; who descended in the days of Jared on the summit of Mount Hermon, and they called it Mount Hermon, because they had sworn and bound themselves by mutual imprecations upon it. (6:6).

And these are the names of their leaders: Sêmîazâz, their leader, Arâkîba, Râmêêl, Kôkabîêl, Tâmîêl, Râmîêl, Dânêl, Êzêqêêl, Barâqîjâl, Asâêl, Armârôs, Batârêl, Anânêl, Zaqîêl, Samsâpêêl, Satarêl, Tûrêl, Jômjâêl, Sariêl. (6:7).
These are their chiefs of tens. (6:8).
crossRefs: Genesis 6:1-4: The sons of God take wives from the daughters of men and the Nephilim are on the earth in those days, the four verses this chapter is unpacking.
Genesis 5:18-20: Jared's place in the line from Adam, which is the date this chapter puts on the descent.
Deuteronomy 3:8-9: Mount Hermon named as the great northern peak, called Sirion by the Sidonians and Senir by the Amorites.
Daniel 4:13: A watcher, a holy one, comes down from heaven, the only place in Scripture that uses the word this book uses for these angels.
Exodus 18:21-25: Moses appoints chiefs of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, the military and judicial structure this chapter borrows for the two hundred.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הַר חֶרְמוֹן (Har Chermon) - Greek: Ἀερμών (Aermon)
translationNotes.note: The highest mountain in the region, about 9,200 feet, standing at the north end of the Anti-Lebanon range on the border of modern Lebanon and Syria. Its snowmelt feeds the springs that become the Jordan. Deuteronomy 3:9 records its other names, Sirion and Senir, and Song of Songs 4:8 pairs Senir with Hermon.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חֵרֶם (cherem), from the root ח-ר-ם
translationNotes.note: The verse states a wordplay that English cannot show. The root behind the mountain's name gives cherem, a thing placed under a ban or devoted by curse, and the text says they called it Hermon because they bound themselves there by mutual curses. Joshua 6:17 uses cherem of a city devoted to destruction.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יֶרֶד (Yered), from the root י-ר-ד (y-r-d), to go down
translationNotes.note: A second wordplay hidden by English. The angels descend in the days of the man whose name is built on the verb to descend. Genesis 5:18-20 gives Jared 962 years and makes him the father of Enoch.

Spelled Semjaza and Semiazaz in this English. The Aramaic fragments of 1 Enoch recovered from Cave 4 at Qumran spell the name Shemichazah, which carries the element shem, name, together with a form of the verb chazah, to see.

Two hundred angels under leaders of ten each. Several of the names on this list carry the subject the angel is later said to have taught: Kokabiel from kokab, star, and Baraqijal from baraq, lightning, both of whom turn up teaching the constellations and astrology in 1 Enoch 8:2.

stories.keyTakeaway: Two hundred angels see the daughters of men, and their leader Semyaza makes them all swear a binding oath first so that no one can back out and leave him to pay alone. They come down on the summit of Mount Hermon in the days of Jared, and the chapter lists their chiefs of tens by name.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 7
summaryBullets: And all the others together with them took to themselves wives, and each chose for himself one, and they began to go in to them and to defile themselves with them, and they taught them charms and enchantments, and the cutting of roots, and made them acquainted with plants. (7:1).
And they became pregnant, and they bare great giants, whose height was three thousand ells: (7:2).
Who consumed all the acquisitions of men. And when men could no longer sustain them, (7:3).
the giants turned against them and devoured mankind. (7:4).
And they began to sin against birds, and beasts, and reptiles, and fish, and to devour one another's flesh, and drink the blood. (7:5).
Then the earth laid accusation against the lawless ones. (7:6).
crossRefs: Genesis 6:4: The Nephilim are on the earth in those days when the sons of God went in to the daughters of men, and they were the mighty men of old.
Genesis 9:4: Flesh with its life, that is its blood, may not be eaten, the line the giants cross in this chapter.
Numbers 35:33: Bloodshed pollutes the land and no atonement can be made for it except by the blood of the one who shed it, which is why the earth itself can lay a charge.
Deuteronomy 3:11: Og's iron bedstead measured nine cubits by four by the common cubit, the only place Scripture puts a number on a giant's size.
Deuteronomy 18:10-12: Divination, sorcery, charms, and consulting the dead are listed by trade and forbidden outright.

translationNotes.note: Ell is an old English cloth measure the translator used for the cubit. A common cubit is about 18 inches, the forearm from elbow to fingertip, so the figure describes creatures roughly 4,500 feet tall. For a measured comparison, Og's bed at Deuteronomy 3:11 was nine cubits, about thirteen feet.

A recognised ancient trade. A rhizotomos was a professional root-cutter who dug medicinal and magical plants under set rules about the hour, the direction of the cut, and the words spoken over it. Josephus describes one such root, called baaras, dug in the ravine near Machaerus and used to drive out demons.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כֶּשֶׁף (kesheph), sorcery - Hebrew: חֶבֶר (chever), a binding spell
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew chever means a knot or a tie, so a spell was pictured as something bound onto a person. Deuteronomy 18:10-12 lists the whole trade by name and forbids every branch of it, and Exodus 22:18 makes practising it a capital matter.

Blood is forbidden as food from Noah onward at Genesis 9:4, and Leviticus 17:11 gives the reason: the life of the flesh is in the blood, and God assigned it to the altar to make atonement. The apostolic letter at Acts 15:29 keeps the prohibition in force for Gentile believers.

The ground is treated as a party that can bring a legal case. Genesis 4:10-11 has Abel's blood crying out from the ground and the ground opening its mouth to take it, and Leviticus 18:25 has the land vomiting out its inhabitants when it has had enough.

stories.keyTakeaway: The angels take wives and teach them charms, spells, and the cutting of roots. Their sons are giants who eat through everything men can produce, then turn on the men themselves, and then on birds, beasts, reptiles, and fish, devouring flesh and drinking blood, until the earth brings a charge against them.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 8
summaryBullets: And Azâzêl taught men to make swords, and knives, and shields, and breastplates, and made known to them the metals of the earth and the are of working them, and bracelets, and ornaments, and the use of antimony, and the beautifying of the eyelids, and all kinds of costly stones, and all colouring tinctures. (8:1).

And there arose much godlessness, and they committed fornication, and they were led astray, and became corrupt in all their ways. Semjâzâ taught enchantments, and root-cuttings, Armârôs the resolving of enchantments, Barâqîjâl, paragraph continues (taught) astrology, Kôkabêl the constellations, Ezêqêêl the knowledge of the clouds , Araqiêl the signs of the earth, Shamsiêl the signs of the sun , and Sariêl the course of the moon. And as men perished, they cried, and their cry went up to heaven . . . (8:2).
crossRefs: Genesis 4:22: Tubal-cain forges every kind of tool of bronze and iron, the same craft this chapter says was handed down.
2 Kings 9:30: Jezebel paints her eyes and dresses her hair at the window, the only narrative picture of the eye paint named here.
Isaiah 47:13-14: Those who divide the heavens, gaze at the stars, and predict by new moons cannot save themselves from the fire that burns them.
Deuteronomy 4:19: A warning against looking up at the sun, moon, and stars and being drawn away to bow down to them.
Jeremiah 10:2: Do not learn the way of the nations or be dismayed at the signs of the heavens, because it is the nations who are dismayed at them.

translationNotes.term: Antimony and the beautifying of the eyelids
translationNotes.note: Powdered stibnite, a lead-grey antimony ore, ground and mixed with oil and drawn along the lids with a small stick. It darkened the eye and cut the desert glare. Jezebel puts it on at 2 Kings 9:30, and Job's daughter at Job 42:14 is named Keren-happuch, horn of eye paint, after the container it was kept in.

Dyes, and the trade behind them was enormous. The costliest was the purple of Tyre, pressed from a gland of the murex sea snail; thousands of snails yielded a few grams, which is why purple cloth marked royalty. Lydia of Thyatira dealt in it at Acts 16:14.

Reading the future from the positions of stars and planets, which is a different job from tracking them for a calendar. Babylon ran it as a state office with salaried practitioners. Daniel 2:27 lists the enchanters, magicians, and astrologers who could not tell the king his dream, and Isaiah 47:13 mocks the ones who divide the heavens month by month.

Body armour of overlapping bronze scales sewn onto a coat, not a single plate. Goliath wears one at 1 Samuel 17:5 weighing five thousand shekels of bronze, roughly 125 pounds, which is why the text bothers to give the number.
Armaros is credited with the counter-spell: undoing a binding another had laid. The list puts the spell and its cure side by side as two things taught in the same lesson.

The same trade named in the previous chapter, here credited to Semyaza himself. Roots and herbs were the working material of ancient magic and ancient medicine alike, and the text does not separate the two.

stories.keyTakeaway: The chapter itemizes what was taught. Azazel gives men metalwork, swords, knives, shields, and armour, and gives women eye paint, jewellery, gemstones, and dyes. The others teach spells and counter-spells, astrology, the constellations, and the reading of clouds, sun, earth, and moon.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 9
summaryBullets: And then Michael, Uriel, Raphael, and Gabriel looked down from heaven and saw much blood being shed upon the earth, and all lawlessness being wrought upon the earth. (9:1).

And they said one to another: 'The earth made †without inhabitant cries the voice of their crying† up to the gates of heaven. 3 And now to you, the holy ones of heaven , the souls of men make their suit, saying, "Bring our cause before the Most High.".' (9:2).
And now to you, the holy ones of heaven, the souls of men make their suit, saying, "Bring our cause before the Most High." (9:3).

And they said to the Lord of the ages : 'Lord of lords, God of gods, King of kings, and God of the ages , the throne of Your glory (standeth) to all the generations of the ages, and Your name holy and glorious and blessed to all the ages! (9:4).
You have made all things, and power over all things have You: and all things are naked and open in Your sight, and You see all things, and nothing can hide itself from You. (9:5).
You see what Azâzêl has done, who has taught all unrighteousness on earth and revealed the eternal secrets which were (preserved) in heaven, which men were striving to learn : (9:6).
And Semjâzâ, to whom You have given authority to bear rule over his associates. (9:7).
And they have gone to the daughters of men upon the earth, and have slept with the women, and have defiled themselves, and revealed to them all kinds of sins. (9:8).
And the women have borne giants, and the whole earth has thereby been filled with blood and unrighteousness. (9:9).

And now, behold, the souls of those who have died are crying and making their suit to the gates of heaven, and their lamentations have ascended: and cannot cease because of the lawless deeds which are wrought on the earth. (9:10).
And You know all things before they come to pass, and paragraph continues You see these things and You do suffer them, and You do not say to us what we are to do to them in regard to these.' (9:11).
crossRefs: Genesis 4:10: The voice of Abel's blood cries to God from the ground, the first time shed blood makes its own case.
Revelation 6:9-10: The souls of the slain under the altar cry out asking how long before God judges and avenges their blood.
Hebrews 4:13: No creature is hidden from His sight, but all are naked and exposed to the eyes of Him to whom we must give account, almost word for word what the angels say here.
Deuteronomy 10:17: God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, the mighty, and the awesome, the title formula the angels stack up in their address.
Exodus 3:7-9: God says He has seen the affliction and heard the cry and has come down, the pattern of an outcry reaching heaven and getting an answer.

translationNotes.note: Only Michael and Gabriel are named in Scripture, at Daniel 10:13 and Luke 1:19. Raphael names himself at Tobit 12:15 as one of the seven who stand before the Lord. Uriel answers Ezra at 2 Esdras 4:1. Every name ends in el, God: Michael is who is like God, Gabriel God is my strength, Raphael God heals, Uriel God is my light.

translationNotes.term: Lord of lords, God of gods, King of kings
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֱלֹהֵי הָאֱלֹהִים וַאֲדֹנֵי הָאֲדֹנִים (Elohei ha-elohim va-Adonei ha-adonim)
translationNotes.note: A set formula rather than four separate compliments. Deuteronomy 10:17 and Psalm 136:2-3 use the first pair of it, and 1 Timothy 6:15 uses King of kings and Lord of lords.

The vocabulary here is courtroom vocabulary from start to finish: a charge is laid, a petition is filed, a ruling is requested. In an Israelite town legal business was done at the town gate, as at Ruth 4:1-2 and Deuteronomy 21:19, so a petition arriving at the gates of heaven is a case reaching the court.

The charge against Azazel is not that he taught what was false but that he disclosed what was being kept. Deuteronomy 29:29 draws the same line: the secret things belong to the LORD our God, and the things revealed belong to us and our children.

translationNotes.term: The dagger marks in this translation
translationNotes.note: The crossed dagger symbols that appear here and in later chapters are the translator's flags, not part of the text. They mark spots where the surviving copies are damaged, disagree, or make no clear sense, and the translator has printed what the manuscripts give rather than repair it.

stories.keyTakeaway: Four archangels look down, see the blood soaking the earth, and carry the case upward. They address God with a stacked formula of titles, name Azazel and Semyaza as the ones responsible, report that the souls of the dead are crying at the gates of heaven, and ask what He wants them to do about it.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 10
summaryBullets: Then said the Most High, the Holy and Great One spoke, and sent Uriel to the son of Lamech, and said to him: (10:1).

' Go to Noah and tell him in my name "Hide yourself!" and reveal to him the end that is approaching: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a deluge is about to come upon the whole earth, and will destroy all that is on it. (10:2).
And now instruct him that he may escape and his seed may be preserved for all the generations of the world.' (10:3).
And again the Lord said to Raphael: 'Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness: and make an opening in the desert, which is in Dûdâêl, and cast him therein. (10:4).
And place upon him rough and jagged rocks, and cover him with darkness, and let him abide there for ever, and cover his face that he may not see light. (10:5).

And on the day of the great judgement he shall be cast into the fire. And heal the earth which the angels have corrupted, and proclaim the healing of the earth, that they may heal the plague, and that all the children of men may not perish through all the secret things that the Watchers have disclosed and have taught their sons. (10:6).
And heal the earth which the angels have corrupted, and proclaim the healing of the earth, that they may heal the plague. (10:7).
And the whole earth has been corrupted through the works that were taught by Azâzêl: to him ascribe all sin.' (10:8).

And to Gabriel said the Lord: 'Proceed against the bastards and the reprobates, and against the children of fornication: and destroy the children of fornication and the children of the Watchers from amongst men and cause them to go forth : send them one against the other that they may destroy each other in battle: for length of days shall they not have. (10:9).

And no request that they (i.e. their fathers) make of you shall be granted to their fathers on their behalf; for they hope to live an eternal life, and that each one of them will live five hundred years.' (10:10).
And the Lord said to Michael: 'Go, bind Semjâzâ and his associates who have united themselves with women so as to have defiled themselves with them in all their uncleanness. (10:11).

And when their sons have slain one another, and they have seen the destruction of their beloved ones, bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement and of their consummation, till the judgement that is for ever and ever is consummated. (10:12).

In those days they shall be led off to the abyss of fire: and to the torment and the prison in which they shall be confined for ever. And whoever shall be condemned and destroyed will from thenceforth be bound together with them to the end of all generations. (10:13).
And whoever shall be condemned and destroyed will from thenceforth be bound together with them to the end of all generations. (10:14).

And destroy all the spirits of the reprobate and the children of the Watchers, because they have wronged mankind. Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: and it shall prove a blessing; the works of righteousness and truth shall be planted in truth and joy for evermore. 17 And then shall all the righteous escape, And shall live till they beget thousands of children, And all the days of their youth and their old age Shall they complete in peace. 18 And then shall the whole earth be tilled in righteousness, and shall all be planted with trees and be full of blessing. (10:15).
Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear. (10:16).
And then shall all the righteous escape, And shall live till they beget thousands of children, And all the days of their youth and their old age Shall they complete in peace. (10:17).
And then shall the whole earth be tilled in righteousness, and shall all be planted with trees and be full of blessing. (10:18).

And all desirable trees shall be planted on it, and they shall plant vines on it: and the vine which they plant thereon shall yield wine in abundance, and as for all the seed which is sown thereon each measure (of it) shall bear a thousand, and each measure of olives shall yield ten presses of oil. (10:19).

And cleanse you the earth from all oppression, and from all unrighteousness, and from all sin, and from all godlessness: and all the uncleanness that is wrought upon the earth destroy from off the earth. (10:20).

And all the children of men shall become righteous , and all nations shall offer adoration and shall praise Me, and all shall worship Me. And the earth shall be cleansed from all defilement, and from all sin, and from all punishment, and from all torment, and I will never again send (them) upon it from generation to generation and for ever. (10:21).
crossRefs: Genesis 6:13-14: God tells Noah that the end of all flesh has come and gives him the order to build the ark, the warning this chapter puts in Uriel's mouth.
Leviticus 16:8-10: Two goats on the Day of Atonement, one for the LORD and one for Azazel, the second sent out into the wilderness.
Isaiah 24:21-22: The host of heaven is punished, gathered as prisoners in a pit, shut up in a prison, and only after many days sentenced, the same two-stage binding used here.
Jude 1:6: Angels who left their proper dwelling are kept in eternal chains under gloomy darkness until the judgment of the great day.
Amos 9:13: The plowman overtakes the reaper and the mountains drip sweet wine, the same picture of impossible yield on the far side of judgment.

translationNotes.note: Leviticus 16:8-10 casts lots over two goats, one for the LORD and one for Azazel, and the second is driven into the wilderness carrying the people's iniquities to a land cut off. English Bibles usually render the word as scapegoat. This chapter has a figure of that name bound in a desert place.

The desert place where Azazel is bound, spelled several ways across the copies of this book. The Mishnah, in the tractate Yoma, names a place in the wilderness called Beth Hiddudo in connection with the goat sent away on the Day of Atonement.

The giants. The Hebrew term behind the English means a child of a forbidden union rather than simply an illegitimate child. Deuteronomy 23:2 bars a mamzer from the assembly to the tenth generation, and Zechariah 9:6 uses the word for the mixed population settled in Ashdod.

The term of the binding, after which the final sentence falls. The chapter never converts it into years. Isaiah 24:22 uses the same two-stage structure without a number: shut up in prison, and after many days punished.

translationNotes.term: Each measure shall bear a thousand
translationNotes.note: A thousandfold seed yield, and the olive figure beside it works the same way. Scripture treats a hundredfold as the outer edge of the remarkable, which is what Isaac reaps at Genesis 26:12 and the top figure in the parable at Mark 4:8. A thousand is deliberately past anything a farmer had seen.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נֵצֶר מַטָּעַי (netser matta'ai), the shoot of my planting
translationNotes.note: The restored people pictured as something planted rather than rebuilt. Isaiah 60:21 calls them the shoot of God's planting, the work of His hands, that He may be glorified.

stories.keyTakeaway: God issues four orders. Uriel warns Noah that the flood is coming, Raphael binds Azazel under jagged rocks in the desert place called Dudael, Gabriel turns the giants loose on each other, and Michael binds Semyaza and his associates for seventy generations before the abyss of fire. Then the earth is healed.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 11
summaryBullets: And in those days I will open the store chambers of blessing which are in the heaven, so as to send them down upon the earth over the work and labour of the children of men. (11:1).
And truth and peace shall be associated together throughout all the days of the world and throughout all the generations of men .' (11:2).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 28:12: The LORD opens His good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain to the land in its season and to bless the work of your hands.
Malachi 3:10: God dares the people to test Him, promising to open the windows of heaven and pour out blessing until there is no more room for it.
Psalm 85:10: Steadfast love and faithfulness meet, righteousness and peace kiss each other, the same pairing of two things that had come apart.
Zechariah 8:19: Truth and peace named together as the two things the people are told to love, in the same breath as fasts turned into feasts.
Isaiah 32:17: The effect of righteousness will be peace, and the result of righteousness quietness and trust forever.

translationNotes.note: A treasury or storehouse, the same word used for a granary, an armoury, and a king's vault. Scripture keeps rain, snow, hail, and wind in stock this way, at Deuteronomy 28:12 and Job 38:22, so blessing is issued from a store rather than made on the spot.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֱמֶת וְשָׁלוֹם (emet ve-shalom) - Greek: ἀλήθεια καὶ εἰρήνη (aletheia kai eirene)
translationNotes.note: Shalom is not the absence of fighting. It means whole, intact, with nothing missing, which is why it works as a greeting, a description of a settled town, and a name for what is restored here. Zechariah 8:19 puts the same two words side by side.

translationNotes.term: The work and labour of the children of men
translationNotes.note: Bene adam means sons of Adam, that is human beings generally and not males; English hides that it is a set Hebrew phrase for humanity. The blessing lands on their labour rather than replacing it, which is how Deuteronomy 28:12 puts it as well.

In a land where rain falls only between November and April and the whole year's crop hangs on it, opening the sky is a literal transaction before it is an image. Deuteronomy 11:10-12 sets it against Egypt, watered by foot from the Nile, where the farmer does not depend on rain at all.

stories.keyTakeaway: Two verses close the speech. God opens the storehouses of blessing kept in heaven and pours them down on the work and labour of human hands, and truth and peace are joined together for every generation from then on.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 12
summaryBullets: Before these things Enoch was hidden, and no one of the children of men knew where he was hidden, and where he abode, and what had become of him. (12:1).
And his activities had to do with the Watchers, and his days were with the holy ones. (12:2).
And I, Enoch was blessing the Lord of majesty and the King of the ages, and lo! the Watchers called me--Enoch the scribe--and said to me: (12:3).

'Enoch, you scribe of righteousness, go, †declare† to the Watchers of the heaven who have left the high heaven, the holy eternal place, and have defiled themselves with women, and have done as the children of earth do, and have taken to themselves wives: "You have wrought great destruction on the earth: (12:4).
And you will have no peace nor forgiveness of sin: and inasmuch as †they† delight themselves in †their† children, (12:5).

The murder of †their† beloved ones shall †they† see, and over the destruction of †their† children shall †they† lament, and shall make supplication to eternity, but mercy and peace shall you not attain."' (12:6).
crossRefs: Genesis 5:24: Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him, which is the being hidden this chapter opens with.
Hebrews 11:5: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he should not see death, and he was not found because God had taken him.
Sirach 44:16: Enoch pleased the Lord and was taken up, and is set down as an example of repentance to all generations.
2 Peter 2:4: God did not spare the angels when they sinned but committed them to chains of gloomy darkness to be kept until the judgment.
Jude 1:6: The angels who did not keep their own position but left their proper dwelling are held for the judgment of the great day, which is the charge Enoch carries.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סֹפֵר (sofer) - Greek: γραμματεὺς τῆς δικαιοσύνης (grammateus tes dikaiosynes)
translationNotes.note: A scribe was a professional writer attached to a court, a temple, or an army: he drew contracts, kept accounts, took dictation, and drafted petitions. Giving Enoch that title is what makes him the man the Watchers hire in the next chapter. Jeremiah 36:4 shows the job being done, with Baruch writing from dictation on a scroll.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לָקַח (laqach), took - Greek: μετατίθημι (metatithemi), to transfer
translationNotes.note: Genesis 5:24 says God took him, using the same verb that carries Elijah away at 2 Kings 2:3. Hebrews 11:5 renders it with a Greek word meaning to move something from one place to another. The book takes that single line and builds the rest of Enoch's biography inside it.
The refrain of this section lands on the Watchers themselves here for the first time. It is repeated to Azazel by name at 1 Enoch 13:1 and given as the last word of the whole message at 1 Enoch 16:4.

Angels, not human saints. That is how the word works throughout this book and at Daniel 4:13, where a watcher and a holy one come down from heaven, and at Psalm 89:5-7, where the assembly of the holy ones is the heavenly council.

translationNotes.term: Have left the high heaven, the holy eternal place
translationNotes.note: The offence is stated as desertion of a post, not only as lust. Jude 1:6 puts it in the same terms: they did not keep their own position but left their proper dwelling, which is why the punishment is confinement.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch has already been taken and hidden away, and his days are spent with the holy ones. He is called as the scribe of righteousness and sent to the Watchers who left heaven, carrying a verdict rather than a warning: no peace, no forgiveness, and they will watch their own sons destroyed.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 13
summaryBullets: And Enoch went and said: 'Azâzêl, you will have no peace: a severe sentence has gone forth against you to put you in bonds: (13:1).

And you will not have toleration nor †request† granted to you, because of the unrighteousness which you have taught, and because of all the works of godlessness and unrighteousness and sin which you have shown to men.' (13:2).
Then I went and spoke to them all together, and they were all afraid, and fear and trembling seized them. (13:3).
And they besought me to draw up a petition for them that they might find forgiveness, and to read their petition in the presence of the Lord of heaven. (13:4).
For from thenceforward they could not speak (with Him) nor lift up their eyes to heaven for shame of their sins for which they had been condemned. (13:5).
Then I wrote out their petition, and the prayer in regard to their spirits and their deeds individually and in regard to their requests that they should have forgiveness and length of days †. (13:6).
And I went off and sat down at the waters of Dan, in the land of Dan, to the south of the west of Hermon: I read their petition till I fell asleep. (13:7).
And behold a dream came to me, and visions fell down upon me, and I saw visions of chastisement, and a voice came bidding (me) I to tell it to the sons of heaven, and reprimand them. (13:8).
And when I awaked, I came to them, and they were all sitting gathered together, weeping in ’Abelsjâîl, which is between Lebanon and Sênêsêr, with their faces covered. (13:9).
And I recounted before them all the visions which I had seen in sleep, and I began to speak the words of righteousness, and to reprimand the heavenly Watchers. (13:10).
crossRefs: Judges 18:27-29: The Danites take Laish, burn it, rebuild it, and rename it Dan, which is how the town at the Jordan's source got the name used here.
Deuteronomy 3:9: Senir given as the Amorite name for Mount Hermon, fixing the country this chapter puts the Watchers in.
Ezra 9:6: Ezra says he is ashamed and cannot lift his face to God, the exact posture this chapter gives the Watchers.
Luke 18:13: The tax collector stands far off, will not lift his eyes to heaven, and beats his breast.
Daniel 9:20-23: Daniel is answered in a vision while he is still speaking his written prayer of confession, the same order of petition and then dream.

translationNotes.note: The spring at Tel Dan, at the southwestern foot of Mount Hermon, is the largest of the three headwaters of the Jordan and runs on snowmelt off that mountain. The town was called Laish until the tribe of Dan took it, Judges 18:27-29, and it marked the north end of the land in the phrase from Dan to Beersheba at 1 Samuel 3:20.

translationNotes.term: Tel Dan and the house of David
translationNotes.note: The mound at Dan gave up a broken Aramaic victory inscription in 1993 and 1994 carrying the letters bytdwd, the house of David. It is the earliest reference to David recovered outside Scripture, and it was found at the site this chapter names.

Deuteronomy 3:9 gives Senir as the Amorite name for Mount Hermon, and Song of Songs 4:8 names Senir and Hermon together as high wild country with lions and leopards in it. The chapter puts the weeping Watchers in the range between Lebanon and that peak.

A formal written request lodged with a superior, and the standard instrument of Greek and Roman administration: the petitioner set out the facts, stated the request, and filed it with the office. The Watchers are asking Enoch to act as their advocate and file on their behalf, which is why they need a scribe.

translationNotes.term: Azazel, you will have no peace
translationNotes.note: The sentence is spoken to a named individual here before it is spoken to the group. The same words fall on the Watchers collectively at 1 Enoch 12:5 and close the message at 1 Enoch 16:4.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch delivers the sentence to Azazel first and then to the rest, and they are terrified. They ask him to draft a petition for forgiveness, because they can no longer speak to God or lift their eyes. He writes it, goes down to the waters of Dan below Hermon, reads it until he falls asleep, and dreams the answer.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 14
summaryBullets: The book of the words of righteousness, and of the reprimand of the eternal Watchers in accordance with the command of the Holy Great One in that vision. (14:1).
I saw in my sleep what I will now say with a tongue of flesh and with the breath of my mouth: which the Great One has given to men to converse therewith and understand with the heart. (14:2).
As He has created and given to man the power of understanding the word of wisdom, so has He created me also and given me the power of reprimanding the Watchers, the children of heaven. (14:3).

I wrote out your petition, and in my vision it appeared thus, that your petition will not be granted to you throughout all the days of eternity, and that judgement has been finally passed upon you: yea (your petition) will not be granted to you . (14:4).
And from henceforth you shall not ascend into heaven to all eternity, and in bonds of the earth the decree has gone forth to bind you for all the days of the world. (14:5).
And (that) previously you shall have seen the destruction of your beloved sons and you will have no pleasure in them, but they shall fall before you by the sword. (14:6).
And your petition on their behalf shall not be granted, nor yet on your own: even though you weep and pray and speak all the words contained in the writing which I have written. (14:7).

And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and hastened me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven. (14:8).

And I went in till I drew near to a wall which is built of crystals and surrounded by tongues of fire: and it began to affright me. And I went into the tongues of fire and drew near to a large house which was built of crystals: and the walls of the house were like a tesselated floor (made) of crystals, and its groundwork was of crystal. (14:9).

And I went into the tongues of fire and drew near to a large house which was built of crystals: and the walls of the house were like a tesselated floor (made) of crystals, and its groundwork was of crystal. (14:10).
Its ceiling was like the path of the stars and the lightnings, and between them were fiery cherubim, and their heaven was (clear as) water. (14:11).
A flaming fire surrounded the walls, and its portals blazed with fire. (14:12).
And I entered into that house, and it was hot as fire and cold as ice: there were no delights of life therein: fear covered me, and trembling got hold upon me. (14:13).
And as I quaked and trembled, I fell upon my face. (14:14).
And I beheld a vision, And lo! there was a second house, greater than the former, and the entire portal stood open before me, and it was built of flames of fire. (14:15).
And in every respect it so excelled in splendour and magnificence and extent that I cannot describe to you its splendour and its extent. (14:16).
And its floor was of fire, and above it were lightnings and the path of the stars, and its ceiling also was flaming fire. (14:17).
And I looked and saw therein a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim. (14:18).
And from underneath the throne came streams of flaming fire so that I could not look thereon. (14:19).
And the Great Glory sat thereon, and His raiment shone more brightly than the sun and was whiter than any snow. (14:20).
None of the angels could enter and could behold His face by reason of the magnificence and glory and no flesh could behold Him. (14:21).
The flaming fire was round about Him, and a great fire stood before Him, and none around could draw near Him: ten thousand times ten thousand (stood) before Him, yet He needed no counselor. (14:22).
And the most holy ones who were near to Him did not leave by night nor depart from Him. (14:23).
And until then I had been prostrate on my face, trembling: and the Lord called me with His own mouth, and said to me: 'Come here, Enoch, and hear my word.' (14:24).
And one of the holy ones came to me and waked me , and He made me rise up and approach the door: and I bowed my face downwards. (14:25).
crossRefs: Daniel 7:9-10: Thrones set in place, the Ancient of Days in clothing white as snow, a throne of fiery flames with burning wheels, a stream of fire flowing out, and ten thousand times ten thousand standing before Him.
Ezekiel 1:26-28: A throne like sapphire above the expanse, with the appearance of fire and a brightness all around, the vision this chapter is built out of.
Exodus 24:9-10: The elders see the God of Israel with a pavement of sapphire stone under His feet, clear as the heavens themselves.
Exodus 33:20: No one may see God's face and live, which is why this chapter says no angel could look at Him.
1 Timothy 6:16: God dwells in unapproachable light, whom no one has ever seen or can see.

translationNotes.note: Kavod means weight before it means splendour, so glory is heaviness: a presence with too much mass to stand near. The book uses the title in place of a name, the way Exodus 24:16-17 has the glory of the LORD settle on Sinai looking like a devouring fire.

Not winged infants. They are the throne guard: a pair overshadows the ark at Exodus 25:18-22, a pair with a flaming sword blocks Eden at Genesis 3:24, and Ezekiel 10:14 gives each of them four faces, with a man taking burning coals from between them earlier in that chapter. Assyrian and Babylonian palaces set winged composite guardians in their doorways, which is the world this image comes out of.

translationNotes.original: Greek: κρύσταλλος (krystallos), from κρύος (kryos), icy cold
translationNotes.note: The Greek word means ice first and rock crystal second; clear quartz was taken for water frozen so hard it could not melt. That is why the house here is built of crystal and cold as ice in the same breath, and why Revelation 4:6 puts a sea of glass like crystal before the throne.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גַּלְגַּל (galgal), whirling thing - Greek: τροχός (trochos)
translationNotes.note: Ezekiel 1:15-21 sets wheels beside the living creatures, full of eyes and moving without turning, and Daniel 7:9 gives the throne itself wheels of burning fire. A seat on wheels is a chariot, which is exactly what 1 Chronicles 28:18 calls the golden cherubim over the ark.

A myriad of myriads, which works out to one hundred million. It is used as the largest figure Greek arithmetic could name conveniently rather than as a headcount. Daniel 7:10 has the identical phrase and Revelation 5:11 repeats it of the angels around the throne.

The line settles a question the throne scene raises: a king with a court takes advice. Isaiah 40:13-14 asks who has been the LORD's counselor and who taught Him the path of justice, and expects the answer nobody.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch reports the dream. Wind and cloud carry him through a crystal wall ringed with fire into a house that is hot as fire and cold as ice, then into a second and greater house built of flame. A throne of crystal stands there with wheels like the sun and rivers of fire beneath it, and God calls him forward.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 15
summaryBullets: And He answered and said to me, and I heard His voice: 'Fear not, Enoch, you righteous man and scribe of righteousness: approach here and hear my voice. (15:1).
And go, say to the Watchers of heaven , who have sent you to intercede for them: "You should intercede" for men, and not men for you: (15:2).

Wherefore have you left the high, holy, and eternal heaven, and lain with women, and defiled yourselves with the daughters of men and taken to yourselves wives, and done like the children of earth, and begotten giants (as your) sons? (15:3).

And though you were holy, spiritual, living the eternal life, you have defiled yourselves with the blood of women, and have begotten (children) with the blood of flesh, and, as the children of men, have lusted after flesh and blood as those also do who die and perish. (15:4).
Therefore have I given them wives also that they might impregnate them, and beget children by them, that thus nothing might be wanting to them on earth. (15:5).
But you were formerly spiritual, living the eternal life, and immortal for all generations of the world. (15:6).
And therefore I have not appointed wives for you; for as for the spiritual ones of the heaven, in heaven is their dwelling. (15:7).
And now, the giants, who are produced from the spirits and flesh, shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling. (15:8).

Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from men , and from the holy Watchers is their beginning and primal origin; they shall be evil spirits on earth, and evil spirits shall they be called. (15:9).
As for the spirits of heaven, in heaven shall be their dwelling, but as for the spirits of the earth which were born upon the earth, on the earth shall be their dwelling. (15:10).

And the spirits of the giants afflict , oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble: they take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst, and cause offences. And these spirits shall rise up against the children of men and against the women, because they have proceeded from them . (15:11).
crossRefs: Matthew 22:30: In the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage but are like the angels in heaven.
Matthew 12:43-45: An unclean spirit goes out of a man, passes through waterless places seeking rest and finding none, then comes back with seven others.
Mark 5:1-13: The man among the tombs whose spirits call themselves Legion beg not to be sent out of the country and ask to enter the pigs instead.
Hebrews 1:14: Angels are ministering spirits sent out to serve those who are to inherit salvation, the direction of service this chapter says was reversed.
Genesis 6:3: God says His Spirit shall not abide in man forever, for he is flesh, and sets his days at a hundred and twenty years.

translationNotes.note: This chapter is the book's own account of where such spirits come from, and it is put in God's mouth rather than the narrator's. The giants are half spirit and half flesh; when the flesh dies the spirit half is left on earth with no body and no place assigned to it, so it stays.

Both words mean breath or wind before they mean spirit, which is why a spirit is always described as something that goes out of a body or comes into one. Ecclesiastes 12:7 uses it exactly that way: the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

translationNotes.term: They take no food, but hunger and thirst
translationNotes.note: The text says the spirits keep the appetites of the bodies they came out of and have no way to satisfy them. Matthew 12:43 describes the same restlessness from the other side: the unclean spirit goes through waterless places looking for rest and finds none.

translationNotes.term: You should intercede for men, and not men for you
translationNotes.note: Intercession runs downward from heaven, and the Watchers have inverted the chain by hiring a man to file on their behalf. Hebrews 1:14 states the proper direction: angels are ministering spirits sent out to serve.

translationNotes.term: Defiled yourselves with the blood of women
translationNotes.note: The charge is crossing a category, spirit taking on flesh and blood, and not only immorality. Hebrews 2:14 uses the same pair, flesh and blood, as the shorthand for what being human consists of.

stories.keyTakeaway: God answers the petition Himself. The Watchers had the order backwards, since angels intercede for men and not men for angels. They were spirit and immortal and were never assigned wives, and the giants they fathered are flesh and spirit mixed, so what leaves those bodies at death stays here as evil spirits.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 16
summaryBullets: From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants , from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement--thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great judgement in which the age shall be consummated, over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated." (16:1).

And now as to the Watchers who have sent you to intercede for them, who had been aforetime in heaven, (say to them): "You have been in heaven, but all the mysteries had not yet been revealed to you, and you knew worthless ones, and these in the hardness of your hearts you have made known to the women, and through these mysteries women and men work much evil on earth." (16:2).

You have been in heaven, but all the mysteries had not yet been revealed to you, and you knew worthless ones, and these in the hardness of your hearts you have made known to the women, and through these mysteries women and men work much evil on earth. (16:3).
Say to them therefore: "You have no peace."' (16:4).
crossRefs: Jude 1:6: Angels kept in eternal chains under gloomy darkness until the judgment of the great day, the deferred sentence this chapter describes.
2 Peter 2:4: God committed the angels who sinned to chains of gloomy darkness to be kept until the judgment, not to punish them on the spot.
Isaiah 48:22: There is no peace, says the LORD, for the wicked, the wording behind the sentence this chapter ends on.
Matthew 8:29: The demons ask whether He has come to torment them before the time, which assumes a fixed date the way this chapter does.
1 Corinthians 2:7-8: A hidden wisdom of God, decreed before the ages, which none of the rulers of this age understood.

translationNotes.note: Not a puzzle to be solved. A mysterion is something deliberately concealed that only an initiate is shown, and the word was at home in the Greek initiation cults before the New Testament took it over. The charge here is disclosure, which is the line Deuteronomy 29:29 draws between the secret things and the revealed.

The sting of the chapter. The Watchers are told they had not been shown the real mysteries at all, so what they traded away was rejected material, and men and women went on to build evil out of it anyway.

translationNotes.original: Greek: συντέλεια (synteleia), a completing or winding up
translationNotes.note: The same Greek word the disciples use at Matthew 24:3 when they ask about the end of the age, and the word for the harvest at Matthew 13:39. It marks a scheduled completion rather than a collapse.

The spirits are stated to be outside the reach of sentencing for the time being, because the sentence is fixed for the day of consummation and not before. Matthew 8:29 shows demons who know the schedule and complain about it.
The third and last delivery of the refrain, after 1 Enoch 12:5 and 1 Enoch 13:1. The wording is taken from Isaiah 48:22, where it is spoken over the wicked.

stories.keyTakeaway: The message ends. The spirits that came out of the dead giants will keep destroying without being called to account until the day of consummation. The Watchers are told they never knew the mysteries they sold; what they passed on was worthless, and men and women built much evil on it. Last words: you have no peace.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 17
summaryBullets: And they took and brought me to a place in which those who were there were like flaming fire, and, when they wished, they appeared as men. (17:1).
And they brought me to the place of darkness, and to a mountain the point of whose summit reached to heaven. (17:2).

And I saw the places of the luminaries and the treasuries of the stars and of the thunder and in the uttermost depths , where were a fiery bow and arrows and their quiver, and a fiery sword and all the lightnings. (17:3).
And they took me to the living waters, and to the fire of the west, which receives every setting of the sun. (17:4).
And I came to a river of fire in which the fire flows like water and discharges itself into the great sea towards the west. (17:5).
I saw the great rivers and came to the great river and to the great darkness, and went to the place where no flesh walks. (17:6).
I saw the mountains of the darkness of winter and the place from where all the waters of the deep flow. (17:7).
I saw the mouths of all the rivers of the earth and the mouth of the deep. (17:8).
crossRefs: Psalm 104:4: He makes His messengers winds and His ministers a flame of fire, which is how the beings at the start of this journey are described.
Job 38:22-24: The storehouses of snow and hail, and the way by which light is distributed and the east wind scattered over the earth.
Habakkuk 3:9-11: God's bow is uncovered, His arrows go out, and sun and moon stand still at the light of the flying shafts.
Daniel 7:10: A stream of fire issues and flows out from before Him, the river of fire this chapter travels along.
Genesis 7:11: The fountains of the great deep burst open, the source this chapter says it has reached the mouth of.

translationNotes.term: Treasuries of the stars and of the thunder
translationNotes.note: Weather and light are pictured as kept in stock and issued. Job 38:22 has storehouses of snow and hail, Psalm 135:7 has God bringing wind out of His storehouses, and Deuteronomy 28:12 calls the sky itself His good treasury.

translationNotes.term: A fiery bow and arrows and a fiery sword
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קֶשֶׁת (qeshet), bow - Hebrew: חֶרֶב (cherev), sword
translationNotes.note: The standing picture of God's armoury, and the arrows are lightning. Psalm 18:14 sends out arrows and flashes of lightning in the same line, and Deuteronomy 32:41-42 has the flashing sword and arrows drunk with blood. This bow is a weapon, not the covenant bow set in the cloud at Genesis 9:13.

The deep is the body of water under and around the world in Hebrew description. Genesis 1:2 has darkness over its face, Genesis 7:11 has its fountains burst open to flood the earth, and the Greek word that renders it is where the English word abyss comes from.

translationNotes.term: The great sea towards the west
translationNotes.note: The Mediterranean, which lies west of Israel and serves as the standing western boundary in Numbers 34:6 and Joshua 15:12. Hebrew uses the same word for sea and for west, so travelling toward the setting sun and travelling seaward are one direction.

The beings are described as fire that takes human shape when it chooses to. Judges 13:20 shows the reverse happening: the visitor Manoah and his wife had taken for a man goes up in the flame from the altar in front of them.

stories.keyTakeaway: The first journey begins. Enoch is taken past beings who look like flaming fire and can pass for men, to a mountain whose summit reaches heaven, to storerooms holding the stars and the thunder, to a fiery bow and sword, along a river of fire running west, and out to where the deep and every river on earth begin.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 18
summaryBullets: I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He had furnished with them the whole creation and the firm foundations of the earth. (18:1).
And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear the earth and the firmament of the heaven. (18:2).
And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven , and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven . (18:3).
I saw the winds of heaven which turn and bring the circumference of the sun and all the stars to their setting. (18:4).

I saw the winds on the earth carrying the clouds: I saw the paths of the angels. I saw at the end of the earth the firmament of the heaven above. And I proceeded and saw a place which burns day and night, where there are seven mountains of magnificent stones, three towards the east, and three towards the south. (18:5).
And I proceeded and saw a place which burns day and night, where there are seven mountains of magnificent stones, three towards the east, and three towards the south. (18:6).
And as for those towards the east, one was of coloured stone, and one of pearl, and one of jacinth , and those towards the south of red stone. (18:7).
But the middle one reached to heaven like the throne of God, of alabaster, and the summit of the throne was of sapphire. (18:8).
And I saw a flaming fire. And beyond these mountains (18:9).
is a region the end of the great earth: there the heavens were completed. (18:10).
And I saw a deep abyss, with columns of heavenly fire, and among them I saw columns of fire fall, which were beyond measure alike towards the height and towards the depth. (18:11).

And beyond that abyss I saw a place which had no firmament of the heaven above, and no firmly founded earth beneath it: there was no water upon it, and no birds, but it was a waste and horrible place. (18:12).
I saw there seven stars like great burning mountains, and to me, when I inquired regarding them, (18:13).
The angel said: 'This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven. (18:14).

And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of the Lord in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times. (18:15).
And He was wroth with them, and bound them till the time when their guilt should be consummated (even) for ten thousand years .' (18:16).
crossRefs: Job 38:4-7: God asks who laid the earth's cornerstone while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy.
Job 26:11: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astounded at His rebuke, the supports this chapter identifies with the winds.
Psalm 135:7: He makes lightning for the rain and brings out the wind from His storehouses, the treasuries opened at the start of this chapter.
Jude 1:13: Wandering stars for whom the gloom of utter darkness has been reserved forever, the sentence this chapter passes on the seven.
Isaiah 14:12-15: The one who said he would set his throne above the stars of God is brought down to Sheol, to the far reaches of the pit.

translationNotes.note: One Greek word covering a deep blue to violet colour and a blue stone. Revelation 21:20 names jacinth as the eleventh foundation of the city wall, and Revelation 9:17 uses the adjective for the colour of breastplates in a vision.

Modern translations often render the Hebrew as lapis lazuli, the deep blue stone flecked with gold-coloured pyrite, mined in Badakhshan in what is now Afghanistan and carried west by caravan. It is the stone under God's feet at Exodus 24:10 and the throne at Ezekiel 1:26.

A soft banded stone, calcite or gypsum, quarried in Egypt and carved into jars and lamps because it is translucent and glows when lit from inside. It is the material of the flask of nard broken over Jesus at Mark 14:3.

Hebrew description sets the sky on supports and the earth on foundations. Job 26:11 has the pillars of heaven trembling at His rebuke, 1 Samuel 2:8 says the pillars of the earth are the LORD's, and Job 9:6 has Him shaking the earth so that its pillars shudder.

The stars are treated as beings under orders, and the offence named is a calendar offence: they did not come out at their appointed times. Jude 1:13 uses the phrase wandering stars for the same charge, and the Greek word behind wandering is the one that gives us planet.
The term of the sentence, repeated at 1 Enoch 21:6. Like the seventy generations of 1 Enoch 10:12, it is a fixed period that ends in judgment rather than a permanent condition.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees the winds both stored and at work: they hold up the sky, carry the clouds, and drive the sun and stars to their setting. He reaches seven mountains of jewelled stone with a throne-shaped peak at the centre, then a waste past the world's edge where seven stars burn, bound for rising off schedule.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 19
summaryBullets: And Uriel said to me: 'Here shall stand the angels who have connected themselves with women, and their spirits assuming many different forms are defiling mankind and shall lead them astray into sacrificing to demons as gods , (here shall they stand,) till the day of the great judgement in which they shall be judged till they are made an end of. (19:1).
And the women also of the angels who went astray shall become sirens.' (19:2).
And I, Enoch, alone saw the vision, the ends of all things: and no man shall see as I have seen. (19:3).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 32:17: They sacrificed to demons that were not God, to gods they had never known, new ones that had lately come in.
Psalm 106:37: They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons, and the land was polluted with blood.
1 Corinthians 10:20: What pagans sacrifice they offer to demons and not to God, which is why Paul will not let believers share that table.
Isaiah 13:21-22: Wild creatures and howling animals take over the ruins of Babylon, the passage whose Greek uses the word rendered sirens here.
Acts 17:31: God has fixed a day on which He will judge the world in righteousness, the same structure of a scheduled reckoning.

translationNotes.note: Two pictures ride on one word. In Greek poetry a siren sings sailors onto the rocks, and Homer has Odysseus plug his crew's ears with wax and lash himself to the mast to get past them. The Greek Old Testament also uses the word for the wild creatures that haunt ruined cities, at Isaiah 13:21 and Job 30:29.

Deuteronomy 32:17 and Psalm 106:37 both use the Hebrew word, and Psalm 106:37 states plainly what was offered: sons and daughters. The Hebrew shed matches the Akkadian shedu, a protective spirit, the winged guardian figures set at Assyrian palace gates, which is what the surrounding cultures believed they were dealing with.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אוּרִיאֵל (Uriel), from אוּר (ur), flame or light, with אֵל (el), God
translationNotes.note: The guide for this stretch of the journey. He is not named in Scripture, but he answers Ezra's questions at 2 Esdras 4:1, and the next chapter of this book assigns him the world and Tartarus.

The text says the spirits are not fixed in shape, and it gives that as the mechanism by which men are led into worshipping them: what appears can appear as anything, including as a god worth a sacrifice.

translationNotes.term: No man shall see as I have seen
translationNotes.note: The claim that closes the first journey, and it matches the claim the book opens with at 1 Enoch 1:2, that Enoch saw what was not meant for his own generation but for a remote one.

stories.keyTakeaway: Uriel names the place. The angels who took wives stand here until the day of judgment, and their spirits take many shapes and lead men into sacrificing to demons as though they were gods. The women become sirens. Enoch says that he alone saw the vision, the ends of all things.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 20
summaryBullets: And these are the names of the holy angels who watch. (20:1).
Uriel, one of the holy angels, who is over the world and over Tartarus. (20:2).
Raphael, one of the holy angels, who is over the spirits of men. (20:3).
Raguel, one of the holy angels who †takes vengeance on† the world of the luminaries. (20:4).
Michael, one of the holy angels, to wit, he that is set over the best part of mankind and over chaos. (20:5).
Saraqâêl, one of the holy angels, who is set over the spirits, who sin in the spirit. (20:6).
Gabriel, one of the holy angels, who is over Paradise and the serpents and the Cherubim. (20:7).
Remiel, one of the holy angels, whom God set over those who rise. (20:8).
crossRefs: Tobit 12:15: Raphael names himself as one of the seven holy angels who present the prayers of the saints and go in before the glory of the Holy One.
