Daniel 12:1: Michael, the great prince who has charge of the people, stands up at a time of trouble such as never was.
Luke 1:19: Gabriel says he stands in the presence of God and was sent to speak, one of only two names on this list that Scripture gives.
2 Peter 2:4: God cast the angels who sinned into Tartarus, the single New Testament use of the word this list assigns to Uriel.
Revelation 8:2: Seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets given to them.

translationNotes.note: In Greek religion Tartarus is the pit below Hades where the Titans were shut up after their defeat, described in Hesiod's Theogony as lying as far below Hades as heaven is above earth, behind bronze gates. 2 Peter 2:4 uses the verb built on that name for what God did with the angels who sinned, and most English Bibles render it simply as hell.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵל (el), God, the ending on all seven
translationNotes.note: Uriel, Raphael, Raguel, Michael, Saraqael, Gabriel, Remiel. Only Michael and Gabriel are named in Scripture, at Daniel 10:13 and Luke 1:19, and Raphael names himself at Tobit 12:15. Michael means who is like God, Gabriel God is my strength, Raphael God heals, Uriel God is my light. Raguel is the Hebrew name Reuel, friend of God, borne by Moses' father-in-law at Exodus 2:18.
Raphael's name is built on the verb to heal, and Tobit 12:14 has him sent to cure Tobit's blindness and to free Sarah, which is the one narrative that shows this office being worked.

Remiel's department is the resurrection, those who rise from the dead. Daniel 12:2 states it: many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

translationNotes.term: Paradise and the serpents and the Cherubim
translationNotes.original: Greek: παράδεισος (paradeisos), a walled garden or park
translationNotes.note: Gabriel's list is the furniture of Eden. Genesis 3:24 posts cherubim and a flaming sword east of the garden to guard the way to the tree of life, and the serpent is the other creature that account names. The Greek word paradeisos is a Persian loanword for an enclosed royal park, and the Greek Old Testament uses it for the garden in Genesis 2:8.
The same word the book uses for the fallen ones in chapter six is used here for the loyal ones. Watcher names the office and not the crime; the seven in this list are watchers who kept their posts.

stories.keyTakeaway: A list and nothing else. Seven holy angels are named with the department each one holds: Uriel over the world and Tartarus, Raphael over the spirits of men, Raguel over the luminaries, Michael over mankind, Saraqael over spirits that sin, Gabriel over Paradise, and Remiel over those who rise.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 21
summaryBullets: And I proceeded to where things were chaotic. (21:1).
And I saw there something horrible: I saw neither a heaven above nor a firmly founded earth, but a place chaotic and horrible. (21:2).
And there I saw seven stars of the heaven bound together in it, like great mountains and burning with fire. (21:3).
Then I said: 'For what sin are they bound, and on what account have they been cast in here?' (21:4).
Then said Uriel, one of the holy angels, who was with me, and was chief over them, and said: 'Enoch, why do you ask, and why are you eager for the truth? (21:5).

These are of the number of the stars of heaven , which have transgressed the commandment of the paragraph continues Lord, and are bound here till ten thousand years, the time entailed by their sins, are consummated.' (21:6).

And from from there I went to another place, which was still more horrible than the former, and I saw a horrible thing: a great fire there which burnt and blazed, and the place was cleft as far as the abyss, being full of great descending columns of fire: neither its extent or magnitude could I see, nor could I conjecture. (21:7).
Then I said: 'How fearful is the place and how terrible to look upon!' (21:8).

Then Uriel answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said to me: 'Enoch, why have you such fear and affright?' And I answered: 'Because of this fearful place, and because of the spectacle of the pain.' (21:9).
And he said to me : 'This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.' (21:10).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:2: The earth was without form and void, with darkness over the face of the deep, the condition this chapter has travelled back into.
Jeremiah 4:23-26: The prophet looks and the earth is without form and void, the heavens have no light, and there is no man left, creation running backwards.
Jude 1:13: Wandering stars for whom the gloom of utter darkness has been reserved forever.
Revelation 9:1-2: A star fallen from heaven is given the key to the shaft of the bottomless pit, and smoke rises out of it as from a great furnace.
2 Peter 2:4: The angels who sinned are committed to chains of gloomy darkness and kept there until the judgment, which is the second place in this chapter.

translationNotes.note: The Hebrew pair at Genesis 1:2 is usually rendered without form and void, meaning unshaped and empty. This chapter describes a place that still is what the world was before it was made, and Jeremiah 4:23 uses the same two words for what judgment turns inhabited land back into.

The same seven Enoch saw at 1 Enoch 18:13-16, and the charge is repeated word for word: they did not come out at their appointed times. In this book the stars are ranked beings on a duty roster, which is why a scheduling failure is stated as a criminal offence.

A fixed term, given here and at 1 Enoch 18:16. It is worth setting against the sentence in the second half of this same chapter, where the prison of the angels is described as forever, with no term attached.

The Greek Old Testament uses this word for the tehom, the deep, of Genesis 1:2. It is what the demons beg not to be sent into at Luke 8:31, and Revelation 9:1-2 gives it a shaft with a lock and a key, so it is pictured as a sealed place rather than open space.

The guides change from stage to stage on this journey, and the book keeps naming them. Uriel handles the stars and the places of punishment, Raphael the places of the dead in the next chapter, Raguel the fire in the west, and Michael the mountain of the throne.

stories.keyTakeaway: Two prisons, seen one after the other. Seven stars burn bound together in a chaotic place with no heaven above and no earth below, held ten thousand years for breaking the commandment about their rising. Past that lies a worse place, split open to the abyss with columns of fire falling through it.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 22
summaryBullets: And from there I went to another place, and he showed me in the west another great and high mountain and of hard rock. E 2 And there was in it †four† hollow places, deep and wide and very smooth. †How† smooth are the hollow places and deep and dark to look at. G g (22:1).

And there were †four† hollow places in it, deep and very smooth: †three† of them were dark and one bright; and there was a fountain of water in its midst. And I said: '†How† smooth are these hollow places, and deep and dark to view.' (22:2).

Then Raphael answered, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said to me: 'These hollow places have been created for this very purpose, that the spirits of the souls of the dead should assemble therein, yea that all the souls of the children of men should assemble here. And these places have been made to receive them till the day of their judgement and till their appointed period till the period appointed , till the great judgement (comes) upon them.' E (22:3).
And these places have been made to receive them till the day of their judgement and till their appointed period, till the great judgement comes upon them. (22:4).
I saw (the spirit of) a dead man making suit, and his voice went forth to heaven and made suit. (22:5).
And I asked Raphael the angel who was with me, and I said to him: 'This spirit which makes suit, whose is it, whose voice goes forth and makes suit to heaven?' (22:6).

And he answered me saying: 'This is the spirit which went forth from Abel, whom his brother Cain slew, and he makes his suit against him till his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is annihilated from amongst the seed of men.' E (22:7).
Then I asked regarding all the hollow places : 'Why is one separated from the other?' (22:8).

And he answered me saying: 'These three have been made that the spirits of the dead might be separated. And this division has been made for the spirits of the righteous, in which there is the bright spring of water. (22:9).
And this has been made for sinners E been made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth and judgement has not been executed on them in their lifetime. (22:10).

Here their spirits shall be set apart in this great pain, till the great day of judgement, scourgings, and torments of the accursed for ever, so that (there maybe) retribution for their spirits. There He shall bind them for ever. (22:11).
And this division has been made for the spirits of those who make their suit, who make disclosures concerning their destruction, when they were slain in the days of the sinners. (22:12).

And this has been made for the spirits of men who shall not be righteous but sinners, who are godless, and of the lawless they shall be companions: but their spirits shall not be punished in the day of judgement nor shall they be raised from from there. (22:13).
Then I blessed the Lord of Glory and said: 'Blessed are You, Lord of righteousness, who rulest over the world.' (22:14).
crossRefs: Genesis 4:10: The voice of your brother's blood is crying to Me from the ground, the case this chapter says Abel is still pressing.
Luke 16:22-26: The rich man and Lazarus are held apart after death by a great chasm that no one can cross from either side.
Revelation 6:9-11: The souls of the slain are under the altar and are told to rest a little longer until the number of their fellow servants is complete.
Daniel 12:2: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
2 Esdras 4:35: The souls of the righteous ask in their chambers how long they must stay and when the harvest of their reward will come.

translationNotes.note: The place of the dead in Hebrew description: under the earth, where everyone goes and from which no one walks back. English Bibles render the one Hebrew word as grave, as pit, and as hell, which is why it can look like three different ideas. Genesis 37:35 has Jacob say he will go down to Sheol mourning for his son.

The count is four and the dagger marks in this translation show the copies are not steady on it. The sorting given is the righteous, with the bright spring of water; sinners who were not punished during their lifetime; those who were murdered and are still bringing the charge; and sinners who will not be raised.

translationNotes.term: A fountain of water in its midst
translationNotes.note: Water marks the good compartment, and it is the only feature that separates the bright one from the three dark ones. Psalm 36:9 calls God the fountain of life, and Revelation 7:17 has the Lamb leading them to springs of living water.

The vocabulary is legal, as it was in chapter nine. A murdered man is a plaintiff whose case is still open and unheard, which is exactly the standing Genesis 4:10 gives Abel's blood when it cries from the ground.

The guide for this stage is the angel whose department 1 Enoch 20:3 gives as the spirits of men, so the chapter hands the tour of the dead to the one assigned to them. The book is consistent about this.

translationNotes.term: Nor shall they be raised from thence
translationNotes.note: One group is sorted as neither punished at the judgment nor raised out of the place at all. Daniel 12:2 sorts the sleepers only two ways, to everlasting life or to shame and contempt, so this chapter is making a division the reader will not find there.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch is shown where the dead wait. A high rock in the west holds four hollow places, three dark and one bright with a spring of water in it, and the dead are sorted between them by what they were and by what was done to them. Abel is still there pressing a case against Cain. Nothing is settled until the judgment.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 23
summaryBullets: From from there I went to another place to the west of the ends of the earth. (23:1).
And I saw a burning fire which ran without resting, and paused not from its course day or night but (ran) regularly. (23:2).
And I asked saying: 'What is this which rests not?' (23:3).

Then Raguel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered me and said to me : 'This course of fire which you have seen is the fire in the west which †persecutes† all the luminaries of heaven.' (23:4).
crossRefs: Psalm 19:4-6: The sun comes out like a bridegroom and runs its course with joy from one end of the heavens to the other, and nothing is hidden from its heat.
Ecclesiastes 1:5: The sun rises and the sun goes down and hurries back to the place where it rises, the circuit this chapter puts a fire behind.
Job 38:19-20: God asks where the way is to the dwelling of light and where darkness has its place, the sort of question this whole journey is answering.
Psalm 104:19-20: He made the moon to mark the seasons and the sun knows its time for setting, and He makes darkness and it is night.
1 Enoch 72:2: The Astronomical Book takes up the courses of the luminaries in full, with Uriel showing Enoch the gates the sun comes out by.

translationNotes.note: The book has already named this at 1 Enoch 17:4, calling it the fire of the west which receives every setting of the sun. Here the same fire is described as chasing the luminaries rather than only receiving them, so it is both a destination and a driver.

The word is printed between dagger marks because the surviving copies do not give a clean reading here. The translator has left the difficulty visible rather than smoothing it, which is why the sentence reads strangely in English.

The guide for this stop is the angel that 1 Enoch 20:4 puts over the world of the luminaries, which is exactly the subject he is asked about here. He is not named anywhere in Scripture, and outside that one list this is the only place in the Book of the Watchers he speaks.

translationNotes.term: West of the ends of the earth
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יָם (yam), sea and also west
translationNotes.note: Hebrew uses the same word for the sea and for the west, because the Mediterranean lies on that side. In this book west is where things end: the fire that takes the sun, and the mountain of the dead described in the previous chapter.

Regularity is the standard this book measures everything by. The luminaries do not deviate, 1 Enoch 2:1, the seven stars that failed to appear on time are imprisoned, 1 Enoch 18:15, and this fire is described first of all by the fact that it never pauses.

stories.keyTakeaway: A short stop west of the ends of the earth. Enoch sees a fire that runs without ever resting, keeping a regular course by day and night. Raguel names it for him: this is the fire in the west, and it pursues all the luminaries of heaven.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 24
summaryBullets: And from from there I went to another place of the earth , and he showed me a mountain range of fire which burnt day and night . (24:1).

And I went beyond it and saw seven magnificent mountains all differing each from the other, and the stones (thereof) were magnificent and beautiful, magnificent as a whole, of glorious appearance and fair exterior: three towards the east, one founded on the other, and three towards the south, one upon the other, and deep rough ravines, no one of which joined with any other. (24:2).
And the seventh mountain was in the midst of these, and it excelled them in height, resembling the seat of a throne: and fragrant trees encircled the throne. (24:3).

And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit resembles the dates of a palm. (24:4).
Then I said: ' How beautiful is this tree, and fragrant, and its leaves are fair, and its blooms very delightful in appearance.' (24:5).
Then answered Michael, one of the holy and honoured angels who was with me, and was their leader. (24:6).
crossRefs: Genesis 2:9: The tree of life stands in the midst of the garden, along with the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
Ezekiel 47:12: Trees on both banks of the river from the sanctuary whose leaves do not wither and whose fruit does not fail, bearing fresh every month.
Revelation 22:1-2: The tree of life stands on either side of the river of the water of life, yielding twelve kinds of fruit, its leaves for the healing of the nations.
Ezekiel 28:13-14: A figure in Eden, the garden of God, covered in precious stones and walking among the stones of fire on the holy mountain of God.
Isaiah 2:2-3: The mountain of the house of the LORD is established as the highest of the mountains, and all the nations flow to it.

translationNotes.term: Resembling the seat of a throne
translationNotes.note: The seventh mountain is described by its shape and by nothing that stands on it; the next chapter says outright whose seat it is. A mountain as God's seat runs right through Scripture, from Sinai to Zion to the highest mountain of Isaiah 2:2.

The aromatics catalogued in the chapters ahead are real trade goods, and the ancient incense road ran from southern Arabia up the western side of the peninsula to Gaza and Damascus. Describing a holy place by its smell made sense to readers for whom fragrance was among the most valuable cargo on the road.

translationNotes.term: Its fruit resembles the dates of a palm
translationNotes.note: The date palm was the staple tree of the Jordan valley and the desert oases. Jericho is called the city of palms at Deuteronomy 34:3, and a mature palm bears for decades. Comparing this fruit to dates puts a known taste and shape in the reader's mouth instead of leaving it abstract.

translationNotes.term: Its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever
translationNotes.note: The same three-part claim Ezekiel 47:12 makes for the trees along the river out of the sanctuary: their leaves will not wither and their fruit will not fail, and the reason given there is that the water comes from the sanctuary.
The guide changes again. Michael is the angel this book puts over mankind at 1 Enoch 20:5, and he is the one who answers Enoch's question about the tree in the chapter that follows.

stories.keyTakeaway: Past a range of fire, Enoch finds seven mountains of magnificent stone, the seventh standing highest in the middle and shaped like the seat of a throne. Fragrant trees ring it, and among them is one tree with a scent past anything, whose leaves and wood never wither and whose fruit looks like dates.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 25
summaryBullets: And he said to me: 'Enoch, why do you ask me regarding the fragrance of the tree, and why do you wish to learn the truth?' Then I answered him saying : 'I wish to know about everything, but especially about this tree.' And he answered saying: 'This high mountain which you have seen , whose summit is like the throne of God, is His throne, where the Holy Great One, the Lord of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness. (25:1).
Then I answered him saying: 'I wish to know about everything, but especially about this tree.' (25:2).

And he answered saying: 'This high mountain which you have seen, whose summit is like the throne of God, is His throne, where the Holy Great One, the Lord of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.' (25:3).

And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. (25:4).

Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of the Lord, the Eternal King. 6 Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as your fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.' 7 Then blessed I the God of Glory, the Eternal King, who has prepared such things for the righteous, and has created them and promised to give to them. (25:5).
crossRefs: Genesis 3:22-24: Man is put out of the garden so that he cannot reach out and take from the tree of life and live forever, and the way to it is guarded.
Revelation 2:7: To the one who conquers, God will grant to eat of the tree of life which is in the paradise of God.
Revelation 22:14: Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city by the gates.
Isaiah 65:19-22: No more weeping in the city, no infant who lives only a few days, and the chosen enjoying the work of their hands for a long time.
Ezekiel 43:6-7: God calls the temple the place of His throne and the place of the soles of His feet, where He will dwell among Israel forever.

translationNotes.term: No mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement
translationNotes.note: The tree is under guard and the guard has an end date. Genesis 3:24 posts cherubim and a flaming sword east of Eden to keep the way to the tree of life, and Revelation 22:14 has the right of access restored to those who wash their robes.

translationNotes.term: Transplanted to the holy place, to the temple
translationNotes.note: The picture is a tree lifted off the mountain and replanted inside the sanctuary. Ezekiel 47:1-12 runs the same connection the other way round, with water flowing out from under the temple threshold and trees growing up along its banks.

translationNotes.term: Its fragrance shall be in their bones
translationNotes.note: A Hebrew way of saying something reaches all the way in. Bones stand for the innermost self and for the seat of feeling, which is why Psalm 51:8 asks that the bones God has broken rejoice and Proverbs 3:8 calls good sense refreshment to the bones.
The long lifespans before the flood. Genesis 5:5-27 gives Adam 930 years and Methuselah 969. Enoch is the short entry in that list at 365 years, and the reason the list gives is that God took him.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם (melech olam) - Greek: βασιλεὺς τῶν αἰώνων (basileus ton aionon)
translationNotes.note: One of this book's standing titles for God, used alongside the Lord of Glory and the Holy Great One. Jeremiah 10:10 calls the LORD the everlasting King, and 1 Timothy 1:17 gives the same title in Greek.

stories.keyTakeaway: Michael explains the mountain and the tree. The peak is God's throne, where He will sit when He comes down to visit the earth. No living man may touch the tree until the judgment; then it is given to the righteous, moved to the temple, and its fruit becomes their food and its scent goes into their bones.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 26
summaryBullets: And I went from from there to the middle of the earth, and I saw a blessed place in which there were trees with branches abiding and blooming of a dismembered tree . (26:1).
And there I saw a holy mountain, and underneath the mountain to the east there was a stream and it flowed towards the south. (26:2).
And I saw towards the east another mountain higher than this, and between them a deep and narrow ravine: in it also ran a stream underneath the mountain. (26:3).

And to the west thereof there was another mountain, lower than the former and of small elevation, and a ravine deep and dry between them: and another deep and dry ravine was at the extremities of the three mountains . (26:4).
And all the ravines were deep and narrow , (being formed) of hard rock, and trees were not planted upon them. (26:5).
And I marveled at the rocks, and I marveled at the ravine, yea, I marveled very much. (26:6).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 5:5: This is Jerusalem, which God set in the centre of the nations with countries all around her, the position this chapter is describing.
Ezekiel 38:12: A people gathered from the nations who dwell at the centre of the earth, the phrase behind the middle of the earth here.
1 Kings 1:38-40: Solomon is taken down to Gihon and anointed king at the spring on the east side of the city.
2 Chronicles 32:30: Hezekiah blocks the upper outlet of the Gihon and channels its water down to the west side of the city of David.
Zechariah 14:4: The Mount of Olives splits from east to west into a very wide valley, the ridge that stands across the ravine from the city.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: טַבּוּר הָאָרֶץ (tabbur ha-arets), the navel of the earth
translationNotes.note: Ezekiel 5:5 says God set Jerusalem in the centre of the nations, and Ezekiel 38:12 uses the navel phrase for where the people live. Everything this chapter describes, a holy mountain with a spring beneath it and three ravines around it, matches the ground at Jerusalem, and the next chapter names the valley.

The temple mount has exactly one water source, the Gihon spring, which rises in the Kidron valley on the east side and runs south. 2 Chronicles 32:30 has Hezekiah cut a tunnel to redirect it inside the walls, and 1 Kings 1:38-40 has Solomon anointed at it.

translationNotes.term: Another mountain higher than this, to the east
translationNotes.note: The Mount of Olives, which rises to about 2,700 feet and stands a few hundred feet above the temple platform across the Kidron valley. That height is why the city is always described as looked down on from there, and it is where Zechariah 14:4 puts the LORD's feet.

translationNotes.term: Deep and narrow ravines of hard rock
translationNotes.note: Jerusalem sits on a limestone spur boxed in by three valleys: the Kidron on the east, the Hinnom on the south and west, and the central valley Josephus called the Tyropoeon cutting through the middle. All of them are dry except in the rainy season, which is exactly what this chapter says.
The phrase is obscure in the surviving copies and the English shows the damage rather than repairing it. What the verse is clear about is the place: blessed, wooded, and at the centre.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch arrives at the middle of the earth: a blessed place full of trees, a holy mountain with a stream running out from under it toward the south, a higher mountain to the east across a deep narrow ravine, a lower one to the west, and dry gorges of bare rock cut between all three.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 27
summaryBullets: Then said I: 'For what object is this blessed land, which is entirely filled with trees, and this accursed valley between ?' (27:1).

Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said: 'This accursed valley is for those who are accursed for ever: Here shall all the accursed be gathered together who utter with their lips against the Lord unseemly words and of His glory speak hard things. E Here shall they be gathered together, and here shall be their place of judgement. (27:2).
In the last times, in the days of the true judgement in the presence of the righteous for ever: here shall the godly bless the Lord of Glory, the Eternal Kin. (27:3).
In the days of judgement over the former, they shall bless Him for the mercy in accordance with which He has assigned them (their lot).' (27:4).
Then I blessed the Lord of Glory and set forth His glory and lauded Him gloriously. (27:5).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 23:10: Josiah defiles Topheth in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom so that no one could burn his son or daughter as an offering to Molech there.
Jeremiah 7:31-32: The high places of Topheth in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, with the promise it will be renamed the Valley of Slaughter until there is no room left to bury.
Jeremiah 19:2-6: Jeremiah is sent out to that same valley by the Potsherd Gate to smash a jar and pronounce judgment on the place.
Mark 9:47-48: Better to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to be thrown into Gehenna with two, where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
Isaiah 66:24: They go out and look on the corpses of the men who rebelled, whose worm shall not die and whose fire shall not be quenched.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גֵּיא בֶן־הִנֹּם (ge ben-hinnom), the Valley of the Son of Hinnom
translationNotes.note: Jerusalem's southern and western boundary. Joshua 15:8 uses it to mark the tribal border, so it is a real ravine a reader could walk into, running below the city wall and joining the Kidron at the southeast corner.

translationNotes.term: Topheth and what was done there
translationNotes.note: 2 Kings 23:10 says Josiah defiled Topheth in that valley so that no one could burn a son or a daughter as an offering to Molech. Jeremiah 7:31 and Jeremiah 32:35 name the same site for the same practice. Children were burned there, and that is how the ravine came to stand for judgment by fire.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Γέεννα (Geenna), from Hebrew ge hinnom
translationNotes.note: The Greek name of that valley, and the word rendered hell in the sayings of Jesus at Matthew 5:22, Matthew 10:28, and Mark 9:47-48. He is naming a specific ravine outside the wall that His hearers could see, not an abstraction.

translationNotes.term: Here shall they be gathered together
translationNotes.note: The valley is described as an assembly point before it is described as a place of punishment. Joel 3:2 uses the same structure with a named valley where the nations are brought down, and Joel 3:12 has God sit there to judge.

translationNotes.term: The godly bless the Lord of Glory
translationNotes.note: The chapter puts the righteous at the site as onlookers, blessing God for the lot assigned to them. Isaiah 66:24 closes the book of Isaiah the same way, with them going out and looking at the bodies of the rebels.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch asks what the accursed valley beside the blessed land is for. Uriel answers that it is the gathering place and the place of judgment for everyone who speaks against the Lord and says hard things about His glory, and that the godly will stand there afterward and bless God for how their lot fell.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 28
summaryBullets: And from there I went towards the east , into the midst of the mountain range of the desert , and I saw a wilderness and it was solitary, full of trees and plant s. (28:1).
And water gushed forth from above. (28:2).
Rushing like a copious watercourse which flowed towards the north-west it caused clouds and dew to ascend on every side. (28:3).
crossRefs: Isaiah 35:6-7: Waters break out in the wilderness and streams in the desert, the burning sand becomes a pool and the thirsty ground springs of water.
Isaiah 41:18-19: God opens rivers on the bare heights and sets the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle, and the olive in the wilderness.
Psalm 107:35: He turns the desert into pools of water and a parched land into springs of water.
Ezekiel 47:8-9: The river from the sanctuary runs down into the Arabah, and everything will live wherever the river goes.
Numbers 20:11: Moses strikes the rock, water comes out abundantly, and the congregation and their livestock drink.

translationNotes.note: Not dunes. A midbar is grazing country, too dry to farm but carrying thin scrub and seasonal grass, the land a shepherd drives flocks out into. That is where Israel spends forty years, where David keeps sheep, and where John baptises.

The water in this desert comes down from the heights rather than up from a spring, which is how the Judean wilderness actually behaves: rain falls on the watershed ridge and runs east down the wadis in flash floods that arrive without warning under a clear sky.

translationNotes.term: It caused clouds and dew to ascend
translationNotes.note: The verse notices that running water puts moisture into the air, which comes back down as dew. Job 36:27-28 describes the same loop from the other end: God draws up the drops of water, which distil as rain from the mist He has made.

The word marks the place as having nobody in it, which in this book is a property of the far places rather than a lack. The journey has already passed through country described as where no flesh walks, at 1 Enoch 17:6.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch turns east into the desert mountains and finds a solitary wilderness that is nevertheless full of trees and plants, because water pours down from above and runs off to the north-west hard enough to throw up cloud and dew on every side.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 29
summaryBullets: And from there I went to another place in the desert, and approached to the east of this mountain range. (29:1).
And there I saw aromatic trees exhaling the fragrance of frankincense and myrrh, and the trees also were similar to the almond tree. (29:2).
crossRefs: Exodus 30:23-25: Liquid myrrh heads the recipe for the holy anointing oil, measured out by shekel alongside cinnamon, aromatic cane, cassia, and olive oil.
Exodus 30:34-38: Stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense make the holy incense, and copying the formula for private use cuts a man off from his people.
Matthew 2:11: The wise men open their treasures and offer gold, frankincense, and myrrh, the two resins this chapter names.
Jeremiah 1:11-12: The almond branch and the wordplay on watching, which is the tree these are compared to.
Song of Songs 4:14: Nard, saffron, calamus, cinnamon, frankincense, myrrh, and aloes listed together as the choice spices.

translationNotes.note: A resin bled from Boswellia trees by slashing the bark and letting the sap harden into lumps, grown in southern Arabia and the Horn of Africa and carried north by caravan. Exodus 30:34 makes it one of the four spices of the holy incense, and Leviticus 2:1-2 puts a handful of it on the grain offering.

A gum resin from thorny Commiphora shrubs of Arabia and East Africa, bitter enough that the name comes from the word for bitter. It goes into the anointing oil at Exodus 30:23, into six months of cosmetic preparation at Esther 2:12, and into burial: John 19:39 has Nicodemus bring about seventy-five pounds of myrrh and aloes.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שָׁקֵד (shaqed), almond - Hebrew: שֹׁקֵד (shoqed), watching
translationNotes.note: The almond is the first tree in the land to bloom, in late January or February, putting out flowers before its own leaves. Jeremiah 1:11-12 turns on the two words: the prophet sees a branch of shaqed, and God says He is shoqed, watching over His word to perform it.

Resin was money. The incense road ran from southern Arabia up the western side of the peninsula to Gaza and Damascus, and the cities along it lived on the traffic. That is why a description of the far country in this book keeps stopping to name spices.

stories.keyTakeaway: A short stage further east. Enoch finds trees giving off the smell of frankincense and myrrh, and he notes that they look like almond trees.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 30
summaryBullets: And therein there was a tree, the colour (?) of fragrant trees such as the mastic. (30:2).
And on the sides of those valleys I saw fragrant cinnamon. And beyond these I proceeded to the east. (30:3).
crossRefs: Exodus 30:23: Sweet-smelling cinnamon measured into the holy anointing oil at two hundred and fifty shekels.
Proverbs 7:17: A bed perfumed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon, which shows what these imported goods were actually used for in a house.
Revelation 18:13: Cinnamon heads the list of cargo nobody buys any more when the great city falls, alongside spice, incense, myrrh, and frankincense.
Susanna 1:54-55: Daniel asks the first elder which tree he saw them under, and the answer, a mastic tree, is turned straight back on him.
Song of Songs 4:14: Cinnamon listed among the choice spices growing in the enclosed garden.

translationNotes.original: Greek: σχῖνος (schinos), the tree - Greek: μαστίχη (mastiche), the resin
translationNotes.note: A resin from Pistacia lentiscus, chewed as gum and used in medicine and varnish, with the trade concentrated on the Greek island of Chios. Susanna 1:54-55 runs a pun on it: the elder says he saw them under a schinos, and Daniel answers that the angel will split him in two, schisei.

The inner bark of a Cinnamomum tree, peeled, dried, and rolled into quills as it curls. It grows in South and Southeast Asia, so every stick of it in the ancient Near East had crossed the Indian Ocean before it reached a market. Exodus 30:23 puts two hundred and fifty shekels of it into the anointing oil.

translationNotes.term: Growing on the sides of those valleys
translationNotes.note: None of these plants grow anywhere near the country Enoch set out from, and cinnamon in particular came from the other side of the Indian Ocean. Finding them growing wild is part of what marks this stretch as the far end of the world rather than a stop on a trade route.

The question mark printed in this verse is the translator's, marking a word the copies do not settle. What survives is a comparison of appearance rather than of scent, which is why the sentence reads oddly next to the rest of the catalogue.

The chapter as carried here opens at 30:2. The numbering follows the manuscript tradition of this book, and the English used in this app has no verse 30:1, which is why the first line is numbered the way it is.

stories.keyTakeaway: Two verses. Enoch names a tree the colour of the fragrant kinds, like the mastic, and finds fragrant cinnamon growing on the sides of the valleys before he goes on further east.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 31
summaryBullets: And I saw other mountains, and amongst them were groves of trees, and there flowed forth from them nectar, which is named sarara and galbanum. (31:1).
And beyond these mountains I saw another mountain to the east of the ends of the earth , whereon were aloe trees , and all the trees were full of stacte , being like almond-trees. (31:2).
And when one burnt it, it smelt sweeter than any fragrant odour. (31:3).
crossRefs: Exodus 30:34: Stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense named as the four ingredients of the holy incense, two of which turn up in this chapter.
Numbers 24:6: Balaam compares Israel's tents to aloe trees the LORD has planted and to cedars beside the waters.
Psalm 45:8: The king's robes are fragrant with myrrh and aloes and cassia, out of ivory palaces.
John 19:39: Nicodemus brings a mixture of myrrh and aloes weighing about seventy-five pounds for the burial.
Proverbs 7:17: Myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon sprinkled over a bed, showing how these resins were used indoors.

translationNotes.note: Not the aloe vera plant people put on burns. Biblical aloes is aloeswood or agarwood, the dark resin-soaked heartwood of Aquilaria trees from Southeast Asia, burned as incense, and it has long been one of the most expensive raw materials in that trade. It scents the king's robes at Psalm 45:8 and goes into the burial at John 19:39.

A gum resin tapped from a Ferula plant of Persia, and one of the four spices Exodus 30:34 names for the holy incense. On its own the smell is sharp and bitter; in a blend it holds and prolongs the other scents rather than contributing its own.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נָטָף (nataph), a drop - Greek: στακτή (stakte), from a verb meaning to drip
translationNotes.note: The name describes how it is collected. Stacte is resin that oozes out of the tree by itself rather than being cut for, which is why both the Hebrew and the Greek call it a drip. It is the first ingredient listed for the holy incense at Exodus 30:34.

The word is left untranslated because the surviving copies give nothing that can be identified with a known product. Galbanum stands beside it in the same sentence, so the pair is being presented as two resins off the same groves.
Incense only works burning. Resin on a hot coal is the entire point of the trade, and Exodus 30:7-8 has Aaron burning it on the altar every morning and every evening as a standing order.

stories.keyTakeaway: More mountains, with groves whose trees run a resin the text calls sarara, and galbanum. Beyond them, at the eastern edge of the earth, stands a mountain of aloe trees loaded with stacte, and Enoch notes that burning it smelled sweeter than any scent he knew.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 32
summaryBullets: To the north-east I beheld seven mountains full of choice nard and mastic and cinnamon and pepper. (32:1).

And from there I went over the summits of all these mountains, far towards the east of the earth , and passed above the Erythraean sea and went far from it, and passed over the angel Zotîêl. E (32:2).

And I came to the Garden of Righteousness, and from afar off trees more numerous than these trees and great--†two† trees there, very great, beautiful, and glorious, and magnificent, and the tree of knowledge, whose holy fruit they eat and know great wisdom. (32:3).

That tree is in height like the fir, and its leaves are like (those of) the Carob tree: and its fruit is like the clusters of the vine, very beautiful: and the fragrance of the tree penetrates afar. (32:4).
Then I said: ' How beautiful is the tree, and how attractive is its look!' (32:5).

Then Raphael the holy angel, who was with me, answered me and said : 'This is the tree of wisdom, of which your father old (in years) and your aged mother, who were before you, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked and they were driven out of the garden.' (32:6).
crossRefs: Genesis 2:9: The tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil beside it.
Genesis 3:6-7: They eat, their eyes are opened, and they know that they are naked, the exact sequence Raphael repeats here.
Genesis 3:23-24: They are sent out of the garden, and cherubim with a flaming sword are set to guard the way to the tree of life.
Mark 14:3-5: A flask of pure nard is broken open and poured out, and the bystanders price it at more than three hundred denarii.
Song of Songs 4:13-14: An orchard of pomegranates with henna, nard, saffron, calamus, cinnamon, frankincense, myrrh, and aloes, the same kind of catalogue by scent.

translationNotes.note: Spikenard, an oil pressed from the root of Nardostachys jatamansi, which grows high in the Himalayas, so every drop of it in the Mediterranean world had crossed Asia. Mark 14:3-5 values one flask at more than three hundred denarii, and a denarius is a day's wage at Matthew 20:2, so that jar was close to a year's pay.

Black pepper, Piper nigrum, from the Malabar coast of southwest India, and one of the great cargoes of the Indian Ocean trade. Pliny the Elder records the Roman price in his Natural History, book twelve: black pepper at four denarii a pound, white at seven, long pepper at fifteen, and he complains that the eastern spice trade was draining Roman coin.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Ἐρυθρὰ Θάλασσα (Erythra Thalassa), the Red Sea
translationNotes.note: In Greek geography the name did not mean only the Red Sea. It covered the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden, the Persian Gulf, and the northwestern Indian Ocean as one body of water. The Greek Old Testament uses it for the sea Israel crossed, the Hebrew Yam Suph, at Exodus 15:4.

The angel Enoch passes over on the approach to the garden. The chapter gives the name and the position and nothing else. Genesis 3:24 posts cherubim east of Eden in the same role, guarding the way in.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע (ets ha-da'at tov va-ra)
translationNotes.note: This chapter calls it the tree of wisdom and has Raphael identify it as the tree Adam and Eve ate from. Genesis 2:17 names it the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and Genesis 3:7 gives the result Raphael repeats here: their eyes were opened and they knew that they were naked.

The tree whose leaves this one is compared to. Its long curved pods were animal fodder and famine food, and they are the husks the son in the far country wanted to fill himself with at Luke 15:16; the Greek word used there means little horns, after the shape of the pod.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch crosses seven mountains of nard, mastic, cinnamon, and pepper, passes over the Erythraean sea and the angel Zotiel, and reaches the Garden of Righteousness. Raphael identifies the great tree there as the tree of wisdom, the one Enoch's own forefather and foremother ate from before they were driven out.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 33
summaryBullets: And from from there I went to the ends of the earth and saw there great beasts, and each differed from the other; and (I saw) birds also differing in appearance and beauty and voice, the one differing from the other. (33:1).
And to the east of those beasts I saw the ends of the earth whereon the heaven rests, and the portals of the heaven open. (33:2).

And I saw how the stars of heaven come forth, and I counted the portals out of which they proceed, and wrote down all their outlets, of each individual star by itself, according to their number and their names, their courses and their positions, and their times and their months, as Uriel the holy angel who was with me showed me. (33:3).
He showed all things to me and wrote them down for me: also their names he wrote for me, and their laws and their companies. (33:4).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:20-25: God brings out the birds, the sea creatures, and the beasts of the earth each according to its kind, the sorting this chapter notices.
Psalm 147:4: He determines the number of the stars and gives to all of them their names, which is the record this chapter says was written out.
Isaiah 40:26: Lift up your eyes and see who created these, who brings out their host by number and calls them all by name.
Psalm 78:23: He commanded the skies above and opened the doors of heaven, the same picture of gates in the sky.
Job 38:32: Can you bring out the constellations in their season, or guide the Bear with its children, the job this chapter hands to portals and a schedule.

translationNotes.note: In this book the sky has gates, and the sun, moon, and stars come out of assigned ones on a rota. The Astronomical Book that follows works the system out in full, with six gates in the east and six in the west, at 1 Enoch 72:3. Scripture uses the picture in passing at Genesis 7:11, the windows of the heavens, and Psalm 78:23, the doors of heaven.

translationNotes.term: The ends of the earth whereon the heaven rests
translationNotes.note: The description assumes a sky with edges that come down and meet the ground, which is what makes gates in it possible. Isaiah 40:22 stretches the heavens out like a curtain and spreads them like a tent to live in, and Job 26:11 sets them on pillars.

translationNotes.term: Their courses and their times and their months
translationNotes.note: This is calendar work rather than stargazing. The Astronomical Book uses exactly this data to lay out a year of three hundred and sixty-four days, and the reason for writing every outlet down is to know what should appear when, so that a deviation can be spotted.

Uriel is the guide for all the astronomical material in this book, and 1 Enoch 20:2 assigns him the world and Tartarus. The Astronomical Book opens by naming him as the one who showed Enoch the courses of the luminaries and wrote them down for him.

translationNotes.term: Great beasts, and each differed from the other
translationNotes.note: The chapter's interest is variety and distinction, not size, and it applies the same test to birds by appearance, beauty, and voice. Genesis 1:21-25 sorts living creatures the same way, by kind.

stories.keyTakeaway: At the eastern edge of the earth Enoch sees great beasts and birds that differ one from another, and the place where heaven rests on the ground with its portals standing open. He counts the gates the stars come out of and writes down every star by name, course, position, and season, with Uriel showing him.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 34
summaryBullets: And from from there I went towards the north to the ends of the earth, and there I saw a great and glorious device at the ends of the whole earth. (34:1).
And here I saw three portals of heaven open in the heaven: through each of them proceed north winds: when they blow there is cold, hail, frost, snow, dew, and rain. (34:2).
And out of one portal they blow for good: but when they blow through the other two portals, it is with violence and affliction on the earth, and they blow with violence. (34:3).
crossRefs: Job 37:9-10: Out of its chamber comes the whirlwind and cold from the scattering winds, and by the breath of God ice is given.
Job 38:22-23: The storehouses of snow and hail, held in reserve for the time of trouble, for the day of battle and war.
Proverbs 25:23: The north wind brings forth rain, and a backbiting tongue angry looks.
Psalm 148:8: Fire and hail, snow and mist, and stormy wind fulfilling His word.
Jeremiah 1:14: Out of the north disaster shall be let loose on all the inhabitants of the land, the quarter two of these three gates blow from.

translationNotes.note: In that country the cold and the winter rain arrive from the north and northwest, off the sea and the mountains, while the killing dry heat comes from the east. Proverbs 25:23 credits the north wind with bringing rain, and this chapter splits three northern gates into one that blows for good and two that do damage.

The destructive item on this list. Hail flattens standing grain in minutes and strips vines and fig trees, which is why Exodus 9:23-25 uses it to break every plant in the field of Egypt and Joshua 10:11 has hailstones kill more of the enemy than the sword did.

The book gives each direction three gates, twelve in all, and the Astronomical Book runs the winds through them one by one at 1 Enoch 76:1-3. This chapter is the compressed version of that system, reported as something seen rather than explained.

The English word device means a made structure, not a trick. The verse establishes that something built stands at the northern edge of the earth and that the three gates belong to it, and it gives no further description than great and glorious.

stories.keyTakeaway: North, to the ends of the earth. Enoch sees a great structure standing there and three open gates of heaven, and the north winds come out through them bringing cold, hail, frost, snow, dew, and rain. One gate blows for good; the other two blow with violence and affliction.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 35
summaryBullets: And from from there I went towards the west to the ends of the earth, and saw there three portals of the heaven open such as I had seen in the †east†, the same number of portals, and the same number of outlets. (35:1).
crossRefs: Psalm 103:12: As far as the east is from the west, so far does He remove our transgressions from us, the two edges used as the widest span there is.
Psalm 50:1: God summons the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting, naming the whole span by its two ends.
Malachi 1:11: From the rising of the sun to its setting God's name will be great among the nations.
Isaiah 45:6: That people may know, from the rising of the sun and from the west, that there is none besides Me.
Psalm 78:23: He commanded the skies above and opened the doors of heaven, the gates this verse is counting.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יָם (yam), sea - Hebrew: מַעֲרָב (ma'arav), the place of setting
translationNotes.note: Hebrew names the compass from the position of a man facing the sunrise: east is in front, west behind, south on the right hand, north on the left. West is also simply the sea, because the Mediterranean lies on that side of the land.

Symmetry is the point of the verse. Whatever goes out in the east comes in at the west through a matching set, and the Astronomical Book states the full system, six gates on each side for the sun, at 1 Enoch 72:3.

The openings the luminaries actually pass through, counted separately from the gates that hold them. The book treats the sky as a piece of engineering with parts that can be inventoried, which is what Enoch has been writing down since 1 Enoch 33:3.

The phrase runs through this whole section and it names a location in this book rather than serving as a figure of speech. Enoch travels to it in all four directions in turn, and every edge has something built on it.

stories.keyTakeaway: One verse. Enoch goes west to the ends of the earth and finds three open gates of heaven there, matching the eastern set gate for gate and outlet for outlet.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 36
summaryBullets: And from from there I went to the south to the ends of the earth, and saw there three open portals of the heaven: and from there there come dew, rain, †and wind†. (36:1).
And from from there I went to the east to the ends of the heaven, and saw here the three eastern portals of heaven open and small portals above them. (36:2).
Through each of these small portals pass the stars of heaven and run their course to the west on the path which is shown to them. (36:3).

And as often as I saw I blessed always the Lord of Glory, and I continued to bless the Lord of Glory who has wrought great and glorious wonders, to show the greatness of His work to the angels and to spirits and to men, that they might praise His work and all His creation: that they might see the work of His might and praise the great work of His hands and bless Him for ever. (36:4).
crossRefs: Job 38:24: God asks by what way the light is distributed and the east wind scattered over the earth, the mechanics this chapter claims to have watched.
Psalm 19:5-6: The sun runs its course from one end of the heavens to the other, and nothing is hidden from its heat.
Psalm 8:3-4: When I look at Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars You have set in place, what is man that You are mindful of him.
Psalm 145:10: All Your works give thanks to You, and Your saints bless You, the pattern of response this chapter ends on.
Revelation 4:11: Worthy are You to receive glory and honour and power, for You created all things and by Your will they existed and were created.

translationNotes.term: From there come dew, rain, and wind
translationNotes.note: The southern gates carry the moisture in this scheme. Rain there falls only in the winter half of the year and the summer is bone dry, which is why dew is listed alongside rain as something delivered on purpose rather than as weather that merely happens.

The stars get their own openings, set above the three larger eastern gates and separate from them. That keeps the star schedule independent of the sun's, which is the arrangement the Astronomical Book lays out from 1 Enoch 72:1 onward.

translationNotes.term: The path which is shown to them
translationNotes.note: The stars are described as running an assigned track. It is the same standard the earlier chapters convict the seven bound stars by, that they did not come forth at their appointed times, 1 Enoch 18:15.

translationNotes.term: I blessed the Lord of Glory
translationNotes.note: The formula that closes each stage of this journey and now closes the whole Book of the Watchers. It ends chapter twenty-two, chapter twenty-five, and chapter twenty-seven in the same words, and here it expands into a statement of why the tour was given at all.

translationNotes.term: To the angels and to spirits and to men
translationNotes.note: The closing verse names three audiences for God's works, and they are the three groups this whole section has dealt with: the Watchers and the holy ones, the spirits of the dead and of the giants, and human beings.

stories.keyTakeaway: The last two directions. Three southern gates let out dew, rain, and wind, and three eastern gates have small openings above them through which the stars come out and run west on the path set for them. Enoch closes the journey by blessing God for the work, over and over.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 37
summaryBullets: The second vision which he saw, the vision of wisdom--which Enoch the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Cainan, the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, saw. (37:1).

And this is the beginning of the words of wisdom which I lifted up my voice to speak and say to those which dwell on earth: Hear, you men of old time, and see, you that come after, the words of the Holy One which I will speak before the Lord of Spirits. (37:2).
It were better to declare (them only) to the men of old time, but even from those that come after we will not withhold the beginning of wisdom. (37:3).

Till the present day such wisdom has never been given by the Lord of Spirits as I have received according to my insight, according to the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits by whom the lot of eternal life has been given to me. (37:4).
Now three parables were imparted to me, and I lifted up my voice and recounted them to those that dwell on the earth. (37:5).
crossRefs: Genesis 5:1-24: The line from Adam through Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahalalel and Jared down to Enoch, which is the genealogy this chapter recites backwards.
Luke 3:37-38: Luke runs the same names in his genealogy of Jesus, Enoch, Jared, Mahalalel, Cainan, Enos, Seth and Adam.
Numbers 23:7: Balaam takes up his parable, the formula this chapter uses, which in Hebrew introduces a formal spoken oracle and not a short story.
Psalm 78:2: The psalmist opens his mouth in a parable and utters dark sayings of old, which shows the range the word covers.
Proverbs 8:1-11: Wisdom calls aloud at the gates to the sons of men and offers her instruction, the same summons Enoch makes to those who dwell on earth.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מָשָׁל (mashal) - Greek: παραβολή (parabole) - Ge'ez: mesale
translationNotes.note: Mashal covers far more than a short story with a lesson. It can be a proverb, a taunt song, a riddle, or a long spoken oracle: Balaam takes up his mashal at Numbers 23:7, and Job begins a long speech the same way at Job 27:1. The three parables announced at 37:5 are extended visions, which is why chapters 37 to 71 are also called the Similitudes.

These chapters are the second of the five works joined together in 1 Enoch. Eleven Aramaic copies of the book were found in Qumran Cave 4 and they carry the other four works, but no fragment of these chapters was found there. The three parables begin at 38:1, 45:1 and 58:1, and the third closes at 69:29.

The name is built on the verb chanakh, to dedicate or to train up, the same verb behind train up a child in the way he should go at Proverbs 22:6. Counting from Adam, Enoch stands seventh, and both 60:8 and Jude 1:14 use that exact count.

translationNotes.original: Ge'ez: egzi'a manafest - Hebrew: יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת (YHWH tseva'ot)
translationNotes.note: This is the standing title for God in these chapters. It appears in 31 of the 35 chapters from 37 to 71 and in none of the other 73 chapters of the book. The nearest fixed title in Hebrew Scripture is YHWH tseva'ot, rendered LORD of hosts, which names God as commander of the armies of heaven, at 1 Samuel 1:3 and Isaiah 6:3.

translationNotes.term: Those who dwell on the earth
translationNotes.original: Greek: οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς (hoi katoikountes epi tes ges)
translationNotes.note: This is a fixed phrase running through the Parables from 37:2 onward, and it means mankind in general seen from heaven rather than any one nation. The same phrase is standard in Revelation, at 3:10, 6:10, 8:13, 11:10 and 13:8, where it marks out those who are judged.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch begins a second vision, the vision of wisdom, and names his own line back through Jared, Mahalalel, Cainan, Enos and Seth to Adam. He addresses the men of old and those who come after, and says three parables were given to him.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 38
summaryBullets: The First Parable. When the congregation of the righteous shall appear, And sinners shall be judged for their sins, And shall be driven from the face of the earth: (38:1).

And when the Righteous One shall appear before the eyes of the righteous, Whose elect works hang upon the Lord of Spirits, And light shall appear to the righteous and the elect who dwell on the earth, Where then will be the dwelling of the sinners, And where the resting-place of those who have denied the Lord of Spirits? It had been good for them if they had not been born. (38:2).
When the secrets of the righteous shall be revealed and the sinners judged, And the godless driven from the presence of the righteous and elect, (38:3).

From that time those that possess the earth shall no longer be powerful and exalted: And they shall not be able to behold the face of the holy, For the Lord of Spirits has caused His light to appear On the face of the holy, righteous, and elect. (38:4).
Then shall the kings and the mighty perish And be given into the hands of the righteous and holy. (38:5).
And thenceforward none shall seek for themselves mercy from the Lord of Spirits For their life is at an end. (38:6).
crossRefs: Psalm 1:5: The ungodly do not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous, which is the assembly this chapter says will appear.
Acts 3:14: Peter tells Jerusalem they denied the Holy One and the Just One, which is the title used here for the figure revealed before the eyes of the righteous.
Acts 7:52: Stephen charges the council with betraying and murdering the Just One, using the same title of the one the prophets foretold.
Matthew 26:24: Jesus says of the man who betrays Him that it had been good for that man if he had not been born, the sentence 38:2 passes on those who deny.
Isaiah 2:11-12: The lofty looks of man are humbled and the day of the LORD comes on everyone proud and lifted up, which is the reversal described here for those who possess the earth.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צַדִּיק (tsaddiq) - Greek: ὁ δίκαιος (ho dikaios)
translationNotes.note: Tsaddiq is the ordinary adjective for a righteous man, used here at 38:2 as a title. The King James Bible renders the Greek as the Just One at Acts 3:14 and Acts 7:52, and 1 John 2:1 calls Jesus Christ the righteous. In these chapters the title stands beside the Elect One and the Son of Man.

Edah is the technical word for Israel assembled as a body, the congregation summoned at Exodus 12:3 and Numbers 27:2. The exact phrase adat tsaddiqim is in Psalm 1:5, where sinners do not stand in it. 38:1 opens the parable with that assembly appearing.

This pair, and the longer run of the kings, the mighty, the exalted and those who possess the earth, is the standing description of the powerful through these chapters. It returns at 46:4, 48:8, 53:5, 55:4, 62:1 and 63:1. The Parables never name a king.

translationNotes.term: Driven from the face of the earth
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה (me-al pene ha-adamah)
translationNotes.note: The picture is expulsion from the ground itself, which is what Cain hears at Genesis 4:14 when he is driven out from the face of the earth and hidden from God's face. 38:1 and 38:3 use it of sinners at the judgment, and 38:2 asks where their dwelling will then be.

translationNotes.term: It had been good for them if they had not been born
translationNotes.note: 38:2 uses this sentence of those who denied the Lord of Spirits. Jesus uses the same sentence of the man who betrays Him, at Matthew 26:24 and Mark 14:21. Job 3:3 and Jeremiah 20:14 have a man curse the day of his own birth, which is the same expression turned inward.

stories.keyTakeaway: The First Parable opens. When the congregation of the righteous appears and the Righteous One is revealed, sinners are driven from the earth and have nowhere to live. The kings and the mighty are handed over to the righteous, and after that no mercy is sought.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 39
summaryBullets: And it †shall come to pass in those days that elect and holy children †will descend from the high heaven, and their seed †will become one with the children of men. (39:1).
And in those days Enoch received books of zeal and wrath, and books of disquiet and expulsion. And mercy shall not be accorded to them, says the Lord of Spirits. (39:2).
And in those days a whirlwind carried me off from the earth, And set me down at the end of the heavens. (39:3).
And there I saw another vision, the dwelling-places of the holy, And the resting-places of the righteous. (39:4).

Here mine eyes saw their dwellings with His righteous angels, And their resting-places with the holy. And they petitioned and interceded and prayed for the children of men, And righteousness flowed before them as water, And mercy like dew upon the earth: Thus it is amongst them for ever and ever. 6 a . And in that place mine eyes saw the Elect One of righteousness and of faith, 7 a . And I saw his dwelling-place under the wings of the Lord of Spirits. 6 b . And righteousness shall prevail in his days, And the righteous and elect shall be without number before Him for ever and ever. 7 b . And all the righteous and elect before Him shall be †strong† as fiery lights, And their mouth shall be full of blessing, And their lips extol the name of the Lord of Spirits, And righteousness before Him shall never fail, And uprightness shall never fail before Him. (39:5).

And in that place mine eyes saw the Elect One of righteousness and of faith, And righteousness shall prevail in his days, And the righteous and elect shall be without number before Him for ever and ever. (39:6).

And I saw his dwelling-place under the wings of the Lord of Spirits. And all the righteous and elect before Him shall be strong as fiery lights, And their mouth shall be full of blessing, And their lips extol the name of the Lord of Spirits, And righteousness before Him shall never fail, And uprightness shall never fail before Him. (39:7).
There I wished to dwell, And my spirit longed for that dwelling-place: And there heretofore has been my portion, For so has it been established concerning me before the Lord of Spirits. (39:8).

In those days I praised and extolled the name of the Lord of Spirits with blessings and praises, because He has destined me for blessing and glory according to the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits. (39:9).
For a long time my eyes regarded that place, and I blessed Him and praised Him, saying: 'Blessed is He, and may He be blessed from the beginning and for evermore. (39:10).
And before Him there is no ceasing. He knows before the world was created what is for ever and what will be from generation to generation. (39:11).
Those who sleep not bless You: they stand before Your glory and bless, praise, and extol, saying: "Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of Spirits: He filleth the earth with spirits."' (39:12).
And here my eyes saw all those who sleep not: they stand before Him and bless and say: 'Blessed be You, and blessed be the name of the Lord for ever and ever.' (39:13).
And my face was changed; for I could no longer behold. (39:14).
crossRefs: Isaiah 6:1-3: The seraphim call to one another Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts, the whole earth is full of his glory, which is the cry repeated at 39:12 with two words changed.
Revelation 4:8: The four living creatures rest not day and night, saying Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, and they are the ones who never sleep.
2 Kings 2:11: Elijah goes up by a whirlwind into heaven, the same means of transport that lifts Enoch off the earth in 39:3.
Daniel 4:13: A watcher, a holy one, comes down from heaven, using the Aramaic term for a wakeful being that names this class of angel.
Psalm 91:4: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust, the same picture of shelter under wings that 39:7 uses.

translationNotes.note: Both words mean the wakeful or watchful ones. Daniel 4:13 calls the heavenly being who announces Nebuchadnezzar's sentence a watcher and a holy one, using irin, and the word comes again at 4:17 and 4:23. Egregoroi is the Greek word behind Watchers in the first part of this book, where it names the angels who fell. Here at 39:12-13 the same idea of never sleeping is used of the angels who never stop blessing.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ (qadosh qadosh qadosh) - Greek: ἅγιος ἅγιος ἅγιος (hagios hagios hagios)
translationNotes.note: 39:12 gives the cry as Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of Spirits, He filleth the earth with spirits. Isaiah 6:3 has Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts, the whole earth is full of his glory. Revelation 4:8 has Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty. Two words stand differently here, Spirits for hosts and spirits for glory.

Se'arah is a storm wind, not a dust devil. It is the wind that takes Elijah up at 2 Kings 2:11, the wind out of which God answers Job at Job 38:1, and the wind Ezekiel sees coming out of the north at Ezekiel 1:4. 39:3 uses it for the wind that carries Enoch off the earth and sets him at the end of the heavens.

39:2 says Enoch received books of zeal and wrath, of disquiet and expulsion. Heavenly books that record and sentence run through Scripture: the book Moses asks to be blotted out of at Exodus 32:32-33, the scroll of remembrance written before the LORD at Malachi 3:16, and the books opened before the throne at Daniel 7:10.

The dagger signs that fence off words at 39:1 and in many later verses belong to the translator, not to the book. R. H. Charles, whose English text this is, used them to mark wording he judged corrupt in the Ge'ez manuscripts. They are a warning that the words inside are uncertain, and they are not punctuation.

translationNotes.term: The a and b verse labels
translationNotes.note: The stray labels inside 39:5, such as 6 a and 7 b, are the editor's. Charles judged that the lines of 39:6 and 39:7 had come down out of order, so he printed them split into halves. That is why 39:5 in this text already contains material that 39:6 and 39:7 then give again in full.

39:14 ends the vision with Enoch unable to look any longer. The same physical effect is reported of Daniel, whose comeliness turned to corruption so that he retained no strength, at Daniel 10:8, and of Moses, whose face shone from speaking with God so that Israel was afraid to come near him, at Exodus 34:29-30.

stories.keyTakeaway: A whirlwind carries Enoch to the end of the heavens, where he sees the dwellings of the righteous and the angels who intercede for men. There he sees the Elect One under the wings of the Lord of Spirits, hears the sleepless ones cry Holy, holy, holy, and his face is changed.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 40
summaryBullets: And after that I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, I saw a multitude beyond number and reckoning, who stood before the Lord of Spirits. (40:1).

And on the four sides of the Lord of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those that sleep not, and I learnt their names: for the angel that went with me made known to me their names, and showed me all the hidden things. (40:2).
And I heard the voices of those four presences as they uttered praises before the Lord of glory. (40:3).
The first voice blesses the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever. (40:4).
And the second voice I heard blessing the Elect One and the elect ones who hang upon the Lord of Spirits. (40:5).
And the third voice I heard pray and intercede for those who dwell on the earth and supplicate in the name of the Lord of Spirits. (40:6).
And I heard the fourth voice fending off the Satans and forbidding them to come before the Lord of Spirits to accuse them who dwell on the earth. (40:7).

After that I asked the angel of peace who went with me, who showed me everything that is hidden: 'Who are these four presences which I have seen and whose words I have heard and written down?' (40:8).

And he said to me: 'This first is Michael, the merciful and long-suffering: and the second, who is set over all the diseases and all the wounds of the children of men, is Raphael: and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance to hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.' And these are the four angels of the Lord of Spirits and the four voices I heard in those days. (40:9).
crossRefs: Daniel 7:10: Thousand thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him, the same reckoning of the host that 40:1 gives.
Daniel 10:13: Michael, one of the chief princes, comes to help against the prince of Persia, the first place Scripture names him.
Luke 1:19: Gabriel tells Zechariah that he stands in the presence of God, which is the position 40:2 describes for the four presences.
Tobit 12:15: Raphael names himself as one of the seven holy angels who carry up the prayers of the saints and go in before the glory of the Holy One.

Zechariah 3:1-2: Joshua the high priest stands before the angel of the LORD with the accuser at his right hand to resist him, and the LORD rebukes the accuser, which is the work of the fourth voice in 40:7.

translationNotes.note: 40:2 puts four presences on the four sides of the Lord of Spirits, and 40:9 names them Michael, Raphael, Gabriel and Phanuel. Earlier in this book, at 9:1, the four who look down from heaven are Michael, Uriel, Raphael and Gabriel, so Phanuel stands here where Uriel stood there. Only Michael and Gabriel are named in Hebrew Scripture, and both only in Daniel.

The name is a question, who is like God. Daniel 10:13 and 10:21 call him one of the chief princes and the prince who stands for Daniel's people, and Daniel 12:1 has him stand up in the time of trouble. Jude 1:9 calls him the archangel and Revelation 12:7 has him fight the dragon. 40:9 calls him the merciful and long-suffering.

The name means God heals, built on rapha, to heal. He is not named in Hebrew Scripture. He names himself in Tobit 12:15 as one of the seven who stand before God, and in that book he cures Tobit's blindness. 40:9 sets him over all the diseases and wounds of men, and 10:7 gives him the task of healing the earth.

The name is built on gever, a strong man, and means man of God or strength of God. Daniel 8:16 and 9:21 have him explain the visions to Daniel, and Luke 1:19 and 1:26 send him to Zechariah and to Mary. 40:9 sets him over all the powers.

No angel of this name appears in Scripture, so the name means nothing to most readers. It is the same name as Peniel, the place Jacob names after wrestling through the night because he says he saw God face to face and his life was preserved, at Genesis 32:30. Anna the prophetess is called the daughter of Phanuel at Luke 2:36. 40:9 sets him over repentance.

Satan begins as a common noun meaning adversary or accuser, and Hebrew uses it of men: Hadad the Edomite is a satan to Solomon at 1 Kings 11:14, and the Philistine lords fear David will be one to them at 1 Samuel 29:4. Job 1:6 and Zechariah 3:1 give it the article, ha-satan, the accuser, standing as prosecutor before the heavenly court. 40:7 has it in the plural, and the fourth voice forbids them to bring accusations.

A myriad is ten thousand, the largest unit Greek counted with, so ten thousand times ten thousand was the way the language said a number past reckoning. Daniel 7:10 uses it of the host before the throne and Revelation 5:11 of the angels around it. Jude 1:14 quotes the opening of this book, where the Lord comes with myriads of His holy ones.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees a host beyond counting before the Lord of Spirits and four presences on His four sides. Their four voices bless, praise the Elect One, intercede for those on earth, and fend off the Satans. The angel names them Michael, Raphael, Gabriel and Phanuel.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 41
summaryBullets: And after that I saw all the secrets of the heavens, and how the kingdom is divided, and how the actions of men are weighed in the balance. (41:1).

And there I saw the mansions of the elect and the mansions of the holy, and mine eyes saw there all the sinners being driven from from there which deny the name of the Lord of Spirits, and being dragged off: and they could not abide because of the punishment which proceeds from the Lord of Spirits. XLI. 3-9. Astronomical Secrets . (41:2).

And there mine eyes saw the secrets of the lightning and of the thunder, and the secrets of the winds, how they are divided to blow over the earth, and the secrets of the clouds and dew, and there I saw from from where they proceed in that place and from from where they saturate the dusty earth. (41:3).

And there I saw closed chambers out of which the winds are divided, the chamber of the hail and winds, the chamber of the mist, and of the clouds, and the cloud thereof hovers over the earth from the beginning of the world. (41:4).

And I saw the chambers of the sun and moon, from where they proceed and where they come again, and their glorious return, and how one is superior to the other, and their stately orbit, and how they do not leave their orbit, and they add nothing to their orbit and they take nothing from it, and they keep faith with each other, in accordance with the oath by which they are bound together. (41:5).
And first the sun goes forth and traverses his path according to the commandment of the Lord of Spirits, and mighty is His name for ever and ever. paragraph continues (41:6).

And after that I saw the hidden and the visible path of the moon, and she accomplishes the course of her path in that place by day and by night--the one holding a position opposite to the other before the Lord of Spirits. And they give thanks and praise and rest not; For to them is their thanksgiving rest. (41:7).

For the sun changes often for a blessing or a curse, And the course of the path of the moon is light to the righteous And darkness to the sinners in the name of the Lord, Who made a separation between the light and the darkness, And divided the spirits of men, And strengthened the spirits of the righteous, In the name of His righteousness. (41:8).
For no angel hinders and no power is able to hinder; for He appoints a judge for them all and He judges them all before Him. (41:9).
crossRefs: Daniel 5:27: The writing on the wall reads Tekel, thou art weighed in the balances and art found wanting, a sentence passed on a king by weighing.
1 Samuel 2:3: Hannah says the LORD is a God of knowledge and by him actions are weighed, which is the picture 41:1 uses of the deeds of men.
Job 38:22: God asks Job whether he has entered the treasuries of the snow and the hail, the same storehouses 41:4 says are opened and divided.
Psalm 135:7: He brings the wind out of his treasuries and makes lightnings for the rain, the arrangement this chapter walks through chamber by chamber.
Jeremiah 33:20-21: The fixed order of day and night is called God's covenant, which is the kind of binding 41:5 describes holding the sun and moon to their courses.
