translationNotes.note: A balance was a beam hung from a cord with a pan at each end, loaded against cut stone weights carried in a bag. The law demands just balances and just weights at Leviticus 19:35-36 and forbids two sets of weights in the bag at Deuteronomy 25:13-15. Daniel 5:27 turns the instrument into a sentence, and 41:1 says the actions of men are weighed the same way.

Mansion in older English means a dwelling or a lodging, not a large house. It is the word the King James Bible uses at John 14:2, in my Father's house are many mansions. 41:2 uses it for the dwellings of the elect and the holy, and the same picture is at 39:4-5.

Scripture pictures weather as kept in locked storerooms and issued out by measure. Job 38:22 asks about the treasuries of snow and hail, Psalm 135:7 has the wind brought out of his treasuries, and Deuteronomy 28:12 calls the rain the LORD's good treasure. 41:3-4 walks through those chambers one at a time, hail, wind, mist and cloud.

translationNotes.term: The oath by which they are bound together
translationNotes.note: 41:5 says the sun and moon keep their orbits by an oath that binds them to each other. Chapter 69 is where this book explains that oath and names the angel who holds it, and 69:20 says the sun and moon complete their course through it. Jeremiah 33:20-21 calls the unbroken order of day and night God's covenant.

translationNotes.term: A separation between the light and the darkness
translationNotes.note: 41:8 says the God who divided light from darkness also divided the spirits of men. The verb badal used for that first division is at Genesis 1:4 and 1:18, and the priests are given the same verb as their duty, to put difference between holy and unholy and between unclean and clean, at Leviticus 10:10.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees how the deeds of men are weighed in the balance and how sinners are driven out from the dwellings of the elect. He is then shown the closed chambers of wind, hail, mist and cloud, and the courses of the sun and moon, which hold to their orbits by an oath.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 42
summaryBullets: Wisdom found no place where she might dwell; Then a dwelling-place was assigned her in the heavens. 2 Wisdom went forth to make her dwelling among the children of men, And found no dwelling-place: Wisdom returned to her place, And took her seat among the angels. 3 And unrighteousness went forth from her chambers: Whom she sought not she found, And dwelt with them, As rain in a desert And dew on a thirsty land. (42:1).
crossRefs: Job 28:12-28: Where shall wisdom be found, and where is the place of understanding, a search through mine and sea that ends with God alone knowing the way to her.
Proverbs 1:20-33: Wisdom cries aloud in the streets and is refused, and then will not answer when those who refused her call in their calamity.
Proverbs 8:22-31: Wisdom speaks as present with God before the world was made, set up from everlasting, which is the standing this chapter gives her.
Sirach 24:8-12: Wisdom seeks a resting place and is commanded to pitch her tent in Jacob and take her inheritance in Israel, the opposite outcome to the one here.
Baruch 3:29-37: No one has gone up to heaven and brought wisdom down, and God gave her to Jacob his servant, the same search this chapter describes.

translationNotes.note: Both words are grammatically feminine, which is why Wisdom is spoken of as she here and through Proverbs 1:20-33 and Proverbs 8:1-36. Chokmah covers practical skill as much as understanding: it is the word for the craftsmen filled to build the tabernacle at Exodus 31:3-6 and for the judgment Israel saw in Solomon at 1 Kings 3:28.

Manoach is a place to settle and stop, the word for the rest the dove could not find for the sole of her foot at Genesis 8:9 and the rest Naomi seeks for Ruth at Ruth 3:1. Sirach 24:7 has Wisdom seeking rest and asking in whose inheritance she shall abide, and there she is told to settle in Jacob.

translationNotes.term: Took her seat among the angels
translationNotes.note: This chapter sends Wisdom back to heaven when men will not have her. That is the reverse of Sirach 24:8, where the Creator tells Wisdom to pitch her tent in Jacob, and of Baruch 3:37, where God gives her to Jacob his servant and to Israel his beloved.

translationNotes.term: As rain in a desert and dew on a thirsty land
translationNotes.note: The picture is of water landing where nothing waited for it. In that country rain fell only in a short winter season, and dew off the sea was what kept crops alive through a rainless summer, which is why dew is part of the blessing at Genesis 27:28 and its withholding is a judgment at Haggai 1:10. The chapter uses both for unrighteousness settling among men who welcomed her.

The whole chapter is printed here as a single verse. The numerals 2 and 3 stand inside the line at the points where the second and third verses begin: Wisdom goes out to the children of men at 42:2, and unrighteousness goes out from her chambers at 42:3.

stories.keyTakeaway: Wisdom goes out to find a dwelling among the children of men, finds none, and returns to take her seat among the angels. Unrighteousness then goes out from her chambers, finds those she was not looking for, and settles among them like rain in a desert.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 43
summaryBullets: And I saw other lightnings and the stars of heaven, and I saw how He called them all by their names and they hearkened to Him. (43:1).

And I saw how they are weighed in a righteous balance according to their proportions of light: (I saw) the width of their spaces and the day of their appearing, and how their revolution produces lightning: and (I saw) their revolution according to the number of the angels, and (how) they keep faith with each other. (43:2).
And I asked the angel who went with me who showed me what was hidden: 'What are these?' (43:3).

And he said to me: 'The Lord of Spirits has showed you their parabolic meaning (lit. 'their parable'): these are the names of the holy who dwell on the earth and believe in the name of the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever.' (43:4).
crossRefs: Psalm 147:4: He telleth the number of the stars and calleth them all by their names, which is what 43:1 says he does.
Isaiah 40:26: Lift up your eyes and see who created these, who brings out their host by number and calls them all by names, so that not one fails.
Daniel 12:3: They that turn many to righteousness shall shine as the stars for ever and ever, the same use of stars for people that 43:4 makes.
1 Corinthians 15:41: One star differs from another star in glory, which is Paul's argument that the risen body has a brightness of its own.
Genesis 15:5: Abram is told to number the stars if he is able, and that his seed shall be as many, the first place in Scripture where stars stand for a people.

translationNotes.note: 43:2 says the stars are weighed by their proportions of light, by the width of their spaces, and by the day they appear. Ranking stars by brightness was ordinary ancient practice: the star catalogue in Ptolemy's Almagest, written at Alexandria in the second century AD, grades every star from first magnitude for the brightest to sixth for the faintest the eye can see, and that scale is still in use. 1 Corinthians 15:41 makes the same observation.

translationNotes.term: Called them all by their names
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לְכֻלָּם שֵׁמוֹת יִקְרָא (le-kullam shemot yiqra)
translationNotes.note: In Hebrew usage a name is identity and standing rather than a label, which is why naming is an act of authority: Adam names the animals at Genesis 2:19-20, and God renames Abram and Jacob when their standing changes at Genesis 17:5 and 32:28. Psalm 147:4 and Isaiah 40:26 say God names every star, and 43:1 adds that they hearken to Him.

The bracketed gloss in 43:4, literally their parable, is the translator's, and it shows that the word behind parabolic meaning is the same one behind the three parables of this book. The angel is saying the stars stand for something and then says what: the names of the holy who dwell on the earth.

43:4 makes the stars the names of the holy. Daniel 12:3 uses the same image for those who turn many to righteousness, and Revelation 1:20 makes seven stars the angels of the seven churches. Earlier in this book, at 21:3-6, stars that transgressed the commandment are bound in a chaotic place for ten thousand years, which is the same picture used the other way.

translationNotes.term: They keep faith with each other
translationNotes.note: 43:2 says the stars keep faith with each other in their revolution, and 41:5 says the sun and moon do the same in accordance with an oath. That fidelity of the heavenly bodies to a fixed course is what the Astronomical Book at chapters 72 to 82 sets out in detail, fixing the year at 364 days.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees the stars called by name and weighed in a righteous balance according to their light. When he asks what they are, the angel gives him their parable: they are the names of the holy who dwell on the earth and believe in the name of the Lord of Spirits.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 44
summaryBullets: Also another phenomenon I saw in regard to the lightnings: how some of the stars arise and become lightnings and cannot part with their new form. (44:1).
crossRefs: Jude 1:13: Jude calls the men he warns against wandering stars, for whom the blackness of darkness is reserved for ever.
Isaiah 14:12: How art thou fallen from heaven, O day star, son of the morning, a line from the taunt song Isaiah is told to raise against the king of Babylon.
Revelation 8:10: A great star burning as a lamp falls from heaven on the third part of the rivers and the fountains of waters.
Revelation 9:1: A star fallen from heaven to the earth is given the key of the bottomless pit.
Job 38:35: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go and say unto thee, Here we are, one of God's questions to Job about this same thing.

translationNotes.note: Baraq is the flash itself, and Scripture treats it as something God dispatches rather than a byproduct of a storm: Job 38:35 has God ask whether Job can send lightnings that report back, and Psalm 18:14 has him shoot out lightnings and rout an army. The judge Barak, called at Judges 4:6, carries this word as his name.

translationNotes.term: Cannot part with their new form
translationNotes.note: What the sentence reports is a change that runs one way: a star rises, becomes a lightning, and stays that way. The chapter does not say whether this is punishment or simply something Enoch was shown, and the book never returns to it.

Planetes is Greek for a wanderer, and it named the lights that moved against the fixed stars, which is where the English word planet comes from. Jude 1:13 uses the phrase of men and puts them under reserved darkness. This book uses stars out of place the same way at 21:3-6, where seven of them are bound for transgressing the commandment.

translationNotes.term: The firmament and the lights set in it
translationNotes.note: Raqia is the expanse God calls Heaven at Genesis 1:6-8, and the sun, moon and stars are set in it at Genesis 1:14-18 to divide day from night and to serve as signs and for seasons. Everything Enoch is shown from 41:3 through this chapter belongs in that expanse.

Chapters 42 and 44 are the shortest in the book, one verse each in this English text. Both sit inside the First Parable, which runs from 38:1 to the end of this chapter, and both break off the run of visions with a single statement and no comment.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch reports one further sight among the lightnings. Some of the stars rise, become lightnings, and cannot part with their new form. The chapter is a single verse and the book gives no explanation of what he saw.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 45
summaryBullets: And this is the Second Parable concerning those who deny the name of the dwelling of the holy ones and the Lord of Spirits. (45:1).

And into the heaven they shall not ascend, And on the earth they shall not come: Such shall be the lot of the sinners Who have denied the name of the Lord of Spirits, Who are thus preserved for the day of suffering and tribulation. (45:2).

On that day Mine Elect One shall sit on the throne of glory And shall try their works, And their places of rest shall be innumerable. And their souls shall grow strong within them when they see Mine Elect Ones, And those who have called upon My glorious name: (45:3).
Then will I cause Mine Elect One to dwell among them. And I will transform the heaven and make it an eternal blessing and light (45:4).
And I will transform the earth and make it a blessing: And I will cause Mine elect ones to dwell upon it: But the sinners and evil-doers shall not set foot thereon. (45:5).

For I have provided and satisfied with peace My righteous ones And have caused them to dwell before Me: But for the sinners there is judgement impending with Me, So that I shall destroy them from the face of the earth. (45:6).
crossRefs: Isaiah 65:17: Behold, I create new heavens and a new earth, and the former shall not be remembered nor come into mind.
Isaiah 66:22: The new heavens and the new earth God makes shall remain before him, and so shall the name and the seed of his people.
Revelation 21:1: A new heaven and a new earth, the first heaven and the first earth passed away, and no more sea.
2 Peter 3:13: We look for new heavens and a new earth, according to his promise, in which righteousness dwells.
Matthew 25:31-32: When the Son of Man comes in his glory he sits on the throne of his glory and all nations are gathered before him, the seat 45:3 describes.

translationNotes.note: 45:1 marks the start of the second of the three discourses. The first ran from 38:1 to the end of chapter 44. This one runs to 57:3, where the text says plainly that this is the end of the second Parable, and the third then begins at 58:1.

1 Samuel 2:8 has God set the poor on a throne of glory, and Jeremiah 17:12 calls the place of Israel's sanctuary a glorious high throne. In these chapters the phrase is fixed and returns at 47:3, 55:4, 61:8, 62:2-5, 69:27 and 71:7. Matthew 19:28 and 25:31 use it of the Son of Man seated to judge.

In Hebrew usage the name stands for the person who bears it, so denying the name is disowning the person and not refusing a word. 45:1 and 45:2 make that denial the thing that fixes the sinners' lot. The Greek verb for the same act, arneomai, is the one at Matthew 10:33 and 2 Timothy 2:12, where a man who disowns is disowned in turn.

translationNotes.term: Their places of rest shall be innumerable
translationNotes.note: Rest in Hebrew is a settled dwelling and not a pause for sleep. Menuchah is the inheritance Israel enters in the land at Deuteronomy 12:9, and Psalm 95:11 is God swearing that the wilderness generation would not enter into his rest. 45:3 gives the tried and approved a resting place past counting.

translationNotes.term: I will transform the heaven and the earth
translationNotes.note: 45:4-5 has God transform heaven and then transform earth so the elect may live on it and no sinner sets foot there. Isaiah 65:17 and 66:22 announce new heavens and a new earth, Revelation 21:1 repeats it, and 2 Peter 3:13 says righteousness dwells there. The word used twice in this chapter is transform, where those passages use the word new.

stories.keyTakeaway: The Second Parable opens on those who deny the name of the Lord of Spirits. They will neither climb into heaven nor stand on the earth. The Elect One sits on the throne of glory and tries their works, and heaven and earth are transformed for the elect to live on.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 46
summaryBullets: And there I saw One who had a head of days, And His head was white like wool, And with Him was another being whose countenance had the appearance of a man, And his face was full of graciousness, like one of the holy angels. (46:1).

And I asked the angel who went with me and showed me all the hidden things, concerning that Son of Man, who he was, and from where he was, (and) why he went with the Head of Days? And he answered and said to me: This is the son of Man who has righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because the Lord of Spirits has chosen him, And whose lot has the pre-eminence before the Lord of Spirits in uprightness for ever. 4, And this Son of Man whom you have seen Shall †raise up† the kings and the mighty from their seats, And the strong from their thrones And shall loosen the reins of the strong, And break the teeth of the sinners. (46:2).

This is the Son of Man who has righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because the Lord of Spirits has chosen him, And whose lot has the pre-eminence before the Lord of Spirits in uprightness for ever. (46:3).

And this Son of Man whom you have seen Shall raise up the kings and the mighty from their seats, And the strong from their thrones, And shall loosen the reins of the strong, And break the teeth of the sinners. (46:4).
And he shall put down the kings from their thrones and kingdoms Because they do not extol and praise Him, Nor humbly acknowledge from where the kingdom was bestowed upon them. (46:5).

And he shall put down the countenance of the strong, And shall fill them with shame. And darkness shall be their dwelling, And worms shall be their bed, And they shall have no hope of rising from their beds, Because they do not extol the name of the Lord of Spirits. (46:6).

And these are they who †judge† the stars of heaven, And raise their hands against the Most High , †And tread upon the earth and dwell upon it†. And all their deeds manifest unrighteousness, And their power rests upon their riches, And their faith is in the †gods† which they have made with their hands, And they deny the name of the Lord of Spirits, (46:7).
And they persecute the houses of His congregations, And the faithful who hang upon the name of the Lord of Spirits. (46:8).
crossRefs: Daniel 7:9: The Ancient of Days takes his seat, his garment white as snow and the hair of his head like the pure wool, the description 46:1 works from.
Daniel 7:13-14: One like the Son of man comes with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of Days and receives dominion, glory and a kingdom that shall not pass away.
Revelation 1:14: His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow, and his eyes as a flame of fire.
Daniel 2:21: God removes kings and sets up kings, which is the thing 46:5 says these kings never acknowledged.
Isaiah 14:13-14: The king of Babylon says in his heart that he will set his throne above the stars of God, the boast behind the charge in 46:7 of judging the stars of heaven.

translationNotes.original: Aramaic: עַתִּיק יוֹמִין (attiq yomin) - Ge'ez: re'esa mawa'el
translationNotes.note: Daniel 7:9 has attiq yomin, rendered the Ancient of Days, for the figure who takes the throne with hair white as wool. 46:1 uses Head of Days for the same description, white like wool. The title appears in 6 chapters of the Parables, at 46:1, 47:3, 48:2, 55:1, 60:2 and 71:10, and nowhere else in the book.

translationNotes.original: Aramaic: בַּר אֱנָשׁ (bar enash) - Hebrew: בֶּן־אָדָם (ben adam) - Greek: ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου (ho huios tou anthropou)
translationNotes.note: In Hebrew and Aramaic the phrase means simply a human being. God addresses Ezekiel as ben adam more than ninety times, from Ezekiel 2:1 onward, marking him out as a man standing before God. Daniel 7:13 has one like a bar enash come with the clouds of heaven and receive dominion. Jesus uses the Greek form of Himself throughout the Gospels, at Matthew 8:20 and Mark 2:10 and many places besides.

translationNotes.term: Three Ge'ez phrases, one English title
translationNotes.original: Ge'ez: walda sab'e - walda be'esi - walda egwala emmaheyaw
translationNotes.note: The English Son of Man in these chapters stands for three different Ge'ez expressions, meaning son of man, son of the male, and son of the offspring of the mother of the living. The English prints one phrase where the manuscripts have three. The title appears in 7 chapters of the Parables, 46, 48, 62, 63, 69, 70 and 71, and nowhere else in the book.

46:1 describes the second figure only by his face, which had the appearance of a man and was full of graciousness, like one of the holy angels. Daniel 7:13 describes its figure the same way, one like a son of man, and in both places the word like is carrying the weight.

translationNotes.term: The gods which they have made with their hands
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵי אָדָם (ma'aseh yede adam, the work of men's hands)
translationNotes.note: This is the standing phrase in Scripture for idols, and the charge is always that the worshipper made the thing he bows to. Psalm 115:4-8 runs the argument out: silver and gold, mouths that do not speak, eyes that do not see, and those who make them become like them. Isaiah 44:14-17 has a man cut a tree, burn half of it to warm himself and bake bread, and worship the other half. 46:7 lays that charge on the kings.

46:6 gives the powerful darkness for a dwelling and worms for a bed. Isaiah 14:11 says of the king of Babylon that the worm is spread under thee and the worms cover thee, and Job 17:14 has a man call corruption his father and the worm his mother and sister. The image is burial and decay, not torment.

46:8 closes the charge sheet: the kings persecute the houses of His congregations and the faithful who hang upon the name of the Lord of Spirits. 53:6 uses the same expression the other way, for the house of his congregation that the Righteous and Elect One will cause to appear.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees One with a head of days, white like wool, and with Him another whose face has the appearance of a man. The angel calls him the Son of Man, who reveals what is hidden and puts down the kings and the mighty from their thrones because they never acknowledged who gave them the kingdom.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 47
summaryBullets: And in those days shall have ascended the prayer of the righteous, And the blood of the righteous from the earth before the Lord of Spirits. (47:1).

In those days the holy ones who dwell above in the heavens Shall unite with one voice And supplicate and pray and praise, And give thanks and bless the name of the Lord of Spirits On behalf of the blood of the righteous which has been shed, And that the prayer of the righteous may not be in vain before the Lord of Spirits, That judgement may be done to them, And that they may not have to suffer for ever. (47:2).

In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated himself upon the throne of His glory, And the books of the living were opened before Him: And all His host which is in heaven above and His counselors stood before Him, 4 And the hearts of the holy were filled with joy; Because the number of the righteous had been offered , And the prayer of the righteous had been heard, And the blood of the righteous been required before the Lord of Spirits. (47:3).
crossRefs: Revelation 6:9-11: The souls under the altar cry out how long before their blood is avenged, and are told to rest until the number of their fellow servants is filled up.
Genesis 4:10: The voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground, the first place in Scripture where shed blood makes a claim of its own.
Daniel 7:9-10: The Ancient of Days takes his seat, thousands minister to him, the judgment is set and the books are opened.
Psalm 69:28: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living and not written with the righteous, the register 47:3 says is opened before the throne.
Zechariah 1:12: The angel of the LORD asks how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem, the same petition the holy ones make here.

translationNotes.note: In Hebrew law shed blood is not only a loss but an unpaid claim on the ground it fell on. Genesis 4:10 has Abel's blood crying out from the ground, and Numbers 35:33 says blood defiles the land and that nothing cleanses the land except the blood of the man who shed it. 47:1 and 47:4 carry that claim up to the Lord of Spirits and have it answered.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סֵפֶר חַיִּים (sepher chayyim, book of life)
translationNotes.note: A city kept a written roll of its citizens, and a name struck off it meant losing every right that came with belonging. Scripture uses that register: Moses asks to be blotted out of God's book at Exodus 32:32-33, Psalm 69:28 asks that enemies be erased from the book of the living, and Revelation 20:12 has the books and the book of life opened at the judgment.

translationNotes.term: Because the number of the righteous had been offered
translationNotes.note: 47:4 makes the joy of the holy depend on a count being complete. Revelation 6:9-11 puts the same idea under the altar, where the martyrs are given white robes and told to rest a little longer until the number of their fellow servants who would be killed as they were is fulfilled.

47:3 sets the whole host of heaven and His counsellors standing before the throne. Scripture describes the same court at 1 Kings 22:19-22, where Micaiah sees the LORD sitting on his throne with all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left, and at Job 1:6, where the sons of God come to present themselves.

translationNotes.term: That they may not have to suffer for ever
translationNotes.note: 47:2 gives the content of the angels' petition: that judgment be done for the righteous and that their suffering not run on without end. Zechariah 1:12 has the angel of the LORD ask the same thing in the same shape, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem, after seventy years of indignation.

stories.keyTakeaway: The prayer of the righteous and the blood of the righteous go up together before the Lord of Spirits, and the holy ones in heaven join in asking that the blood be required. The Head of Days takes the throne, the books of the living are opened, and the number of the righteous is complete.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 48
summaryBullets: And in that place I saw the fountain of righteousness Which was inexhaustible: And around it were many fountains of wisdom; And all the thirsty drank of them, And were filled with wisdom, And their dwellings were with the righteous and holy and elect. (48:1).
And at that hour that Son of Man was named In the presence of the Lord of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days. (48:2).
Yea, before the sun and the signs were created, Before the stars of the heaven were made, His name was named before the Lord of Spirits. (48:3).
He shall be a staff to the righteous whereon to stay themselves and not fall, And he shall be the light of the Gentiles, And the hope of those who are troubled of heart. (48:4).
All who dwell on earth shall fall down and worship before him, And will praise and bless and celebrate with song the Lord of Spirits. (48:5).
And for this reason has he been chosen and hidden before Him, Before the creation of the world and for evermore. (48:6).

And the wisdom of the Lord of Spirits has revealed him to the holy and righteous; For he has preserved the lot of the righteous, Because they have hated and despised this world of unrighteousness, And have hated all its works and ways in the name of the Lord of Spirits: For in his name they are saved, And according to his good pleasure has it been in regard to their life. (48:7).

In these days downcast in countenance shall the kings of the earth have become, And the strong who possess the land because of the works of their hands; For on the day of their anguish and affliction they shall not (be able to) save themselves. (48:8).

And I will give them over into the hands of Mine elect: As straw in the fire so shall they burn before the face of the holy: As lead in the water shall they sink before the face of the righteous, And no trace of them shall any more be found. (48:9).

And on the day of their affliction there shall be rest on the earth, And before them they shall fall and not rise again: And there shall be no one to take them with his hands and raise them: For they have denied the Lord of Spirits and His Anointed. The name of the Lord of Spirits be blessed. (48:10).
crossRefs: Isaiah 42:6: I will give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles, spoken of the servant God upholds.
Isaiah 49:6: It is a light thing to raise up the tribes of Jacob, so the servant is given for a light to the Gentiles and for salvation to the end of the earth.
Luke 2:32: Simeon in the temple calls the child a light to lighten the Gentiles and the glory of thy people Israel.
Psalm 2:2: The kings of the earth set themselves and the rulers take counsel together against the LORD and against his Anointed, the pairing 48:10 uses.
Jeremiah 2:13: They have forsaken me the fountain of living waters and hewed out broken cisterns that can hold no water, the contrast behind the fountain in 48:1.

translationNotes.note: Mashiach means anointed, and Christos is simply its Greek translation, so Christ is a title and not a surname. Kings and priests were anointed by having oil poured on the head: Aaron at Exodus 29:7, Saul at 1 Samuel 10:1, David at 1 Samuel 16:13. Psalm 2:2 sets the kings of the earth against the LORD and against his Anointed, and 48:10 uses the same pair.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אוֹר גּוֹיִם (or goyim, light of the nations)
translationNotes.note: Goyim is the ordinary Hebrew word for the nations, meaning everyone outside Israel. Isaiah 42:6 and 49:6 give the servant as a light to them, and Simeon uses the phrase over the infant Jesus at Luke 2:32. Paul and Barnabas quote Isaiah 49:6 as their own commission at Acts 13:47. 48:4 applies it to the Son of Man.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִשְׁעֶנֶת (mish'enet, a support or staff)
translationNotes.note: The staff here is the thing a man puts his weight on, not a rod of office. It is the walking staff of Exodus 21:19, which a recovering man goes out leaning on, and the second word of Psalm 23:4, thy rod and thy staff they comfort me. 48:4 says the righteous stay themselves on him and do not fall.

translationNotes.term: Before the sun and the signs were created
translationNotes.note: 48:3 and 48:6 say the name was named, and the one who bears it was chosen and hidden, before the world was made. The signs are the heavenly bodies set in the expanse to be for signs and for seasons at Genesis 1:14. The same language of being foreordained before the foundation of the world and manifested in the last times is at 1 Peter 1:20.

translationNotes.term: As straw in the fire, as lead in the water
translationNotes.note: 48:9 gives two pictures of vanishing without trace. Straw is the stalk left after threshing, worth nothing and burned as fuel, which is why Malachi 4:1 says the day comes that shall burn the proud as stubble. Lead was the heaviest metal in common use, cast into net sinkers and plumb weights, and Exodus 15:10 says the Egyptians sank as lead in the mighty waters.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מָקוֹר (maqor, a spring or source)
translationNotes.note: In a country that lived off springs and cisterns, a maqor is a source that keeps producing, while a cistern holds only what was poured into it and cracks. Jeremiah 2:13 sets the two against each other, the fountain of living waters against broken cisterns. 48:1 has an inexhaustible fountain of righteousness with fountains of wisdom around it, and everyone thirsty drinks.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees an inexhaustible fountain of righteousness ringed by fountains of wisdom. The Son of Man is named before the Head of Days, and his name was named before the sun and the stars were made. He is called a staff to the righteous and a light to the Gentiles.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 49
summaryBullets: For he is mighty in all the secrets of righteousness, And unrighteousness shall disappear as a shadow, And have no continuance; Because the Elect One standeth before the Lord of Spirits, And his glory is for ever and ever, And his might to all generations. (49:2).
And in him dwells the spirit of wisdom, And the spirit which gives insight, And the spirit of understanding and of might, And the spirit of those who have fallen asleep in righteousness. (49:3).
And he shall judge the secret things, And none shall be able to utter a lying word before him; For he is the Elect One before the Lord of Spirits according to His good pleasure. (49:4).
crossRefs: Isaiah 11:2: The Spirit of the LORD rests upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD.
Isaiah 11:3-4: He shall not judge after the sight of his eyes nor reprove after the hearing of his ears, but with righteousness shall he judge the poor.
Isaiah 42:1: Behold my servant whom I uphold, mine elect in whom my soul delighteth, I have put my spirit upon him and he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.
1 Corinthians 4:5: The Lord will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and make manifest the counsels of the hearts, which is the judging of secret things 49:4 describes.
Luke 23:35: The rulers scoff, let him save himself if he be Christ, the chosen of God, using chosen in the same sense as the title here.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּחִירִי (bechiri, my chosen) - Greek: ὁ ἐκλεκτός (ho eklektos)
translationNotes.note: The word means chosen, picked out for a purpose. Isaiah 42:1 has God call his servant mine elect, and Isaiah 45:4 uses the same word of Israel. Luke 23:35 has the rulers mock Jesus as the chosen of God. In these chapters the Elect One is a standing title, at 39:6, 40:5, 45:3, 49:2, 51:3, 52:6, 53:6, 55:4, 61:8 and 62:1, and it is used nowhere else in the book.

translationNotes.term: The spirit of wisdom and of might
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רוּחַ (ruach, spirit, breath or wind)
translationNotes.note: 49:3 lists what dwells in him: the spirit of wisdom, the spirit that gives insight, the spirit of understanding and of might, and the spirit of those who have fallen asleep in righteousness. Isaiah 11:2 builds its list the same way over the shoot from the stump of Jesse, pairing wisdom with understanding and counsel with might.

translationNotes.term: Unrighteousness shall disappear as a shadow
translationNotes.note: A shadow is the standing Hebrew picture for what has no substance and does not last. Job 8:9 says our days on earth are a shadow, 1 Chronicles 29:15 repeats it of Israel's days, and Psalm 144:4 says man's days are as a shadow that passeth away. 49:2 says unrighteousness has no continuance in the same way.

translationNotes.term: He shall judge the secret things
translationNotes.note: Deuteronomy 29:29 says the secret things belong unto the LORD our God, and Psalm 90:8 says he sets our secret sins in the light of his countenance. 49:4 gives the judging of those hidden things to the Elect One and adds that no lying word can be uttered before him. Paul says the same of the day of judgment at 1 Corinthians 4:5.

translationNotes.term: Those who have fallen asleep in righteousness
translationNotes.note: Sleep is the ordinary way both Testaments speak of the death of the faithful. Daniel 12:2 has many that sleep in the dust of the earth awake, and Paul writes about them which are asleep at 1 Thessalonians 4:13-14. 49:3 counts their spirit among what dwells in the Elect One.

The text here opens at 49:2. The first verse, which says that wisdom is poured out like water and glory does not fail before him for ever, is not carried in this edition. Chapters 52, 54 and 69 begin the same way, part of the way into the chapter.

stories.keyTakeaway: Unrighteousness passes away like a shadow and has no lasting hold. The Elect One stands before the Lord of Spirits, and in him dwell the spirits of wisdom, insight, understanding and might. He judges the secret things, and no lying word can be spoken in front of him.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 50
summaryBullets: And in those days a change shall take place for the holy and elect, And the light of days shall abide upon them, And glory and honour shall turn to the holy, (50:1).

On the day of affliction on which evil shall have been treasured up against the sinners. And the righteous shall be victorious in the name of the Lord of Spirits: And He will cause the others to witness (this) That they may repent And forgo the works of their hands. (50:2).
They shall have no honour through the name of the Lord of Spirits, Yet through His name shall they be saved, And the Lord of Spirits will have compassion on them, For His compassion is great. (50:3).
And He is righteous also in His judgement, And in the presence of His glory unrighteousness also shall not maintain itself: At His judgement the unrepentant shall perish before Him. (50:4).
And from henceforth I will have no mercy on them, says the Lord of Spirits. (50:5).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 18:30-32: Repent and turn yourselves from all your transgressions, for God has no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, so turn and live.
Isaiah 55:7: Let the wicked forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts and return unto the LORD, for he will abundantly pardon.
Jonah 3:6-10: Nineveh turns from its evil way and God relents from the destruction he had said he would bring on it.
1 Corinthians 3:15: If any man's work be burned he shall suffer loss, but he himself shall be saved, yet so as by fire, which is the shape of being saved without honour.
Romans 2:4: The goodness and forbearance and longsuffering of God leads a man to repentance, which is what the witnesses in 50:2 are given time to do.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שׁוּב (shuv, to turn back) - Greek: μετανοέω (metanoeo, to change the mind)
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew word is physical. Shuv is to turn round and walk the other way, which is why the prophets say return rather than say feel sorry, as at Ezekiel 18:30 and Isaiah 55:7. 50:2 has the witnesses repent and forgo the works of their hands, pairing the turning with the giving up of what they made.

In the prophets this phrase most often means idols, the images a man made and then bowed to. Jeremiah 1:16 and 25:6-7 use it that way, and 2 Kings 22:17 says Judah provoked God to anger with the works of their hands. Forgoing them at 50:2 is the concrete act the repentance consists of.

translationNotes.term: Yet through His name shall they be saved
translationNotes.note: 50:3 says these late turners get no honour through the name but are saved through it, because the compassion of the Lord of Spirits is great. 50:4 and 50:5 then shut the door on the unrepentant, who perish before him, and the chapter ends with God saying he will have no mercy on them from that time.

translationNotes.term: The light of days shall abide upon them
translationNotes.note: 50:1 gives the holy glory and honour and a light that stays on them. It is the same picture as 58:3-6, where the righteous are in the light of the sun and the darkness has already been destroyed. Isaiah 60:19-20 says the LORD will be an everlasting light and the days of mourning ended.

translationNotes.term: He is righteous also in His judgement
translationNotes.note: 50:4 says unrighteousness cannot hold itself up in the presence of his glory. Genesis 18:25 asks shall not the Judge of all the earth do right, and Deuteronomy 32:4 says all his ways are judgment, a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.

stories.keyTakeaway: A change comes for the holy and the elect, and the righteous are victorious in the name of the Lord of Spirits. Others are made to watch it so that they may repent and give up the works of their hands. They gain no honour, but through His name they are saved, and the unrepentant perish.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 51
summaryBullets: And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes. 5 a . For in those days the Elect One shall arise, (51:1).
And he shall choose the righteous and holy from among them: For the day has drawn near that they should be saved. (51:2).

And the Elect One shall in those days sit on My throne, And his mouth shall pour forth all the secrets of wisdom and counsel: For the Lord of Spirits has given (them) to him and has glorified him. (51:3).

And in those days shall the mountains leap like rams, And the hills also shall skip like lambs satisfied with milk, And the faces of all the angels in heaven shall be lighted up with joy. 5 b . And the earth shall rejoice, c . And the righteous shall dwell upon it, d . And the elect shall walk thereon. (51:4).
crossRefs: Revelation 20:13: The sea gave up the dead which were in it, and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them, and every man was judged.
Daniel 12:2: Many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
Isaiah 26:19: Thy dead men shall live, awake and sing ye that dwell in dust, for the earth shall cast out the dead.
Psalm 114:4-6: The mountains skipped like rams and the little hills like lambs, the picture 51:4 uses word for word.
Hosea 13:14: I will ransom them from the power of the grave, O grave I will be thy destruction, the demand this chapter makes on Sheol.

translationNotes.note: Sheol is the Hebrew name for the place of the dead, where everyone goes, and it is not described as a place of fire. Jacob says he will go down to Sheol mourning for his son at Genesis 37:35, and Psalm 16:10 asks that the soul not be left there. The King James Bible renders the one Hebrew word as grave, hell and pit in different verses. 51:1 names Sheol and hell separately, as two holders of the dead.

translationNotes.term: Give back that which has been entrusted to it
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פִּקָּדוֹן (piqqadon, a deposit left in trust)
translationNotes.note: The picture is legal. A piqqadon is property left with a neighbour for safekeeping, and Leviticus 6:2-5 sets out the penalty for lying about one. 51:1 treats the dead as goods deposited with the earth and with Sheol, which are now required to hand them over. Revelation 20:13 describes the same handing over.

translationNotes.term: The Elect One shall sit on My throne
translationNotes.note: 51:3 is God speaking, and the throne named is his own, which is the sharpest form of the seating in these chapters. Elsewhere the text says the throne of glory, as at 45:3 and 62:2. Revelation 3:21 uses the same picture of sitting down with the Father in his throne.

translationNotes.term: The mountains shall leap like rams
translationNotes.note: Psalm 114:4-6 says the mountains skipped like rams and the little hills like lambs, then asks the mountains why they did it. 51:4 takes the picture whole, down to the lambs satisfied with milk, and adds the faces of the angels in heaven lighted up with joy.

The labels 5 a inside 51:1 and 5 b, c and d at the end of 51:4 mark the four lines of verse 5, which this edition distributes into the surrounding verses rather than setting them out as a separate verse 5. In R.H. Charles's standard text these four lines stand together as verse 5, following verse 4.

stories.keyTakeaway: The earth gives back what was entrusted to it and Sheol gives back what it received. The Elect One rises, chooses out the righteous and the holy, and sits on God's own throne pouring out the secrets of wisdom. The mountains leap like rams and the earth rejoices.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 52
summaryBullets: There mine eyes saw all the secret things of heaven that shall be, a mountain of iron, and a mountain of copper, and a mountain of silver, and a mountain of gold, and a mountain of soft metal, and a mountain of lead. (52:2).
And I asked the angel who went with me, saying, 'What things are these which I have seen in secret?' (52:3).
And he said to me: 'All these things which you have seen shall serve the dominion of His Anointed that he may be potent and mighty on the earth.' (52:4).
And that angel of peace answered, saying to me: 'Wait a little, and there shall be revealed to you all the secret things which surround the Lord of Spirits. (52:5).

And these mountains which yours eyes have seen, The mountain of iron, and the mountain of copper, and the mountain of silver, And the mountain of gold, and the mountain of soft metal, and the mountain of lead, All these shall be in the presence of the Elect One As wax: before the fire, And like the water which streams down from above upon those mountains , And they shall become powerless before his feet. (52:6).

And it shall come to pass in those days that none shall be saved, Either by gold or by silver, And none be able to escape. 8 And there shall be no iron for war, Nor shall one clothe oneself with a breastplate. Bronze shall be of no service, And tin shall be of no service and shall not be esteemed, And lead shall not be desired. 9 And all these things shall be denied and destroyed from the surface of the earth, When the Elect One shall appear before the face of the Lord of Spirits.' Footnotes 69:1 Only six are mentioned; see Charles' note in his large edition--EDD. (52:7).
crossRefs: Numbers 31:22: The law names the six metals of the ancient world, gold, silver, brass, iron, tin and lead, the same six this chapter builds into mountains.
Ezekiel 22:18-20: Israel is called brass and tin and iron and lead gathered into the furnace, the same metals put to the fire.
Micah 1:4: The mountains shall be molten under him and the valleys cleft, as wax before the fire, the image 52:6 uses.
Zephaniah 1:18: Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD's wrath, which is the sentence 52:7 passes.
Isaiah 2:4: They shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruninghooks, and shall not learn war any more, the end of iron for war stated the other way round.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: זָהָב כֶּסֶף נְחֹשֶׁת בַּרְזֶל בְּדִיל עוֹפֶרֶת (zahav, keseph, nechosheth, barzel, bedil, ophereth)
translationNotes.note: Six metals were worked in the ancient Near East, and Numbers 31:22 lists all six: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin and lead. Brass in the King James Bible means copper or its alloy bronze, since true brass was not in use. This chapter builds a mountain out of each and then melts all six.

translationNotes.term: Iron and bronze, the war metals
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בַּרְזֶל (barzel, iron) - נְחֹשֶׁת (nechosheth, copper or bronze)
translationNotes.note: Iron gave the harder edge, and control of it was control of an army: 1 Samuel 13:19-22 says no smith was allowed in Israel, so that on the day of battle only Saul and Jonathan had a sword. Bronze is copper alloyed with roughly a tenth part tin, and it is what Goliath's helmet, coat of mail and greaves were made of at 1 Samuel 17:5-6. 52:8 says there will be no iron for war and no breastplate to put on.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כֶּסֶף (keseph, silver and also money)
translationNotes.note: Silver was money, weighed out rather than counted, which is why Abraham weighs 400 shekels of it for a burial plot at Genesis 23:15-16 and why the same Hebrew word means both silver and money. Gold was for overlay and vessels, as in the house Solomon covered with pure gold at 1 Kings 6:20-22. Lead was cheap and heavy, cast into weights and net sinkers, and Zechariah 5:7-8 uses a talent of lead as a lid on a basket.

Soft metal is the translator's literal rendering, and which metal it names is not certain. The lists keep it separate from tin: 52:2 gives iron, copper, silver, gold, soft metal and lead, and 67:4 has mountains of gold, silver, iron, soft metal and tin. 65:7-8 says silver comes from the dust of the earth and soft metal originates in the earth, while lead and tin come from a spring.

translationNotes.term: Melt like wax before the fire
translationNotes.note: Micah 1:4 says the mountains shall be molten under him as wax before the fire, and Psalm 97:5 says the hills melted like wax at the presence of the LORD. 52:6 puts the six metal mountains under the same picture, adds water streaming down over them, and says they become powerless before his feet.

translationNotes.term: The editor's footnote at the end of the chapter
translationNotes.note: The line beginning Footnotes at the close of 52:7 is not part of the book. It is a page note from the printed edition this English text was taken from, observing that only six mountains are named, and pointing the reader to Charles's larger commentary.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch is shown six mountains, of iron, copper, silver, gold, soft metal and lead. The angel says they serve the dominion of His Anointed. Before the Elect One they melt like wax, and in that day no one is saved by gold or silver and no iron is left for war.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 53
summaryBullets: There mine eyes saw a deep valley with open mouths, and all who dwell on the earth and sea and islands shall bring to him gifts and presents and tokens of homage, but that deep valley shall not become full. (53:1).

And their hands commit lawless deeds, And the sinners devour all whom they lawlessly oppress : Yet the sinners shall be destroyed before the face of the Lord of Spirits, And they shall be banished from off the face of His earth, And they shall perish for ever and ever. (53:2).
For I saw all the angels of punishment abiding (there) and preparing all the instruments of Satan. (53:3).
And I asked the angel of peace who went with me: 'For whom are they preparing these instruments?' (53:4).
And he said to me: 'They prepare these for the kings and the mighty of this earth, that they may thereby be destroyed. (53:5).
And after this the Righteous and Elect One shall cause the house of his congregation to appear: henceforth they shall be no more hindered in the name of the Lord of Spirits. (53:6).
And these mountains shall not stand as the earth before his righteousness, But the hills shall be as a fountain of water, And the righteous shall have rest from the oppression of sinners.' (53:7).
crossRefs: Isaiah 5:14: Hell hath enlarged herself and opened her mouth without measure, and their glory and their multitude descend into it.
Proverbs 27:20: Hell and destruction are never full, and the eyes of man are never satisfied, the appetite this valley has.
2 Kings 23:10: Josiah defiles Topheth in the valley of the children of Hinnom, so that no man could make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to Molech.

Jeremiah 7:31-32: The high places of Topheth in the valley of the son of Hinnom, where they burned their sons and daughters, will be called the valley of slaughter, and they will bury there till there is no room.
Isaiah 24:21-22: The LORD punishes the host of the high ones and the kings of the earth, and they are gathered together as prisoners in the pit and shut up in the prison.

translationNotes.term: A deep valley with open mouths
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גֵּיא (ge, a valley or ravine)
translationNotes.note: The valley in these chapters is a steep-sided ravine, not a broad plain. 53:1 has it swallow the gifts of everyone on earth and never fill, 56:3 calls it the chasm of the abyss of the valley, and 67:4 makes it a burning valley in the west. Isaiah 5:14 uses the same picture of a mouth opened without measure.

translationNotes.term: The Valley of Hinnom, whose Greek name is Gehenna
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גֵּי בֶן־הִנֹּם (ge ben-hinnom) - Greek: γέεννα (geenna)
translationNotes.note: The Valley of Hinnom runs along the south and west sides of Jerusalem. At the Tophet in that valley children were burned to Molech, which 2 Kings 23:10, Jeremiah 7:31 and Jeremiah 32:35 record and which Josiah defiled to stop. The Hebrew name of the valley became the Greek word geenna, and geenna is the word Jesus uses for hell, at Matthew 5:22, Matthew 10:28 and Mark 9:43-47. This book describes a burning valley and never gives it a name.

53:3 has the angels of punishment preparing instruments, and 54:3 says plainly what they are, iron chains of immeasurable weight. 53:5 says they are being made for the kings and the mighty of this earth. Through these chapters the chains and instruments are always described as prepared and waiting, never yet used.

translationNotes.term: Gifts and presents and tokens of homage
translationNotes.note: Minchah is the word for the tribute a weaker ruler sends a stronger one, the present Ehud carries to Eglon king of Moab at Judges 3:15 and the gifts the neighbouring kingdoms bring Solomon at 1 Kings 4:21. 53:1 has everyone on earth and sea and islands bringing it to the valley, and the valley never fills.

53:6 says the Righteous and Elect One will cause the house of his congregation to appear, and that from then on they will not be hindered. That is the same expression as 46:8, where the kings persecute the houses of His congregations. Here the two titles Righteous One and Elect One are joined into one name.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees a deep valley with open mouths that never fills, though the whole earth brings gifts to it. The angels of punishment are preparing the instruments of Satan, and the angel says they are for the kings and the mighty of the earth. Then the house of his congregation appears.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 54
summaryBullets: Noachic Fragment on the first World Judgement . (54:2).
And there mine eyes saw how they made these their instruments, iron chains of immeasurable weight. (54:3).
And I asked the angel of peace who went with me, saying: 'For whom are these chains being prepared?' paragraph continues (54:4).

And he said to me: 'These are being prepared for the hosts of Azâzêl, so that they may take them and cast them into the abyss of complete condemnation, and they shall cover their jaws with rough stones as the Lord of Spirits commanded. (54:5).

And Michael, and Gabriel, and Raphael, and Phanuel shall take hold of them on that great day, and cast them on that day into the burning furnace, that the Lord of Spirits may take vengeance on them for their unrighteousness in becoming subject to Satan and leading astray those who dwell on the earth.' LIV. 7.-LV (54:6).
'And in those days shall punishment come from the Lord of Spirits, and he will open all the chambers of waters which are above the heavens, and of the fountains which are beneath the earth. (54:7).
And all the waters shall be joined with the waters: that which is above the heavens is the masculine, and the water which is beneath the earth is the feminine. (54:8).
And they shall destroy all who dwell on the earth and those who dwell under the ends of the heaven. (54:9).
And when they have recognized their unrighteousness which they have wrought on the earth, then by these shall they perish. (54:10).
crossRefs: Jude 1:6: The angels which kept not their first estate are reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.
2 Peter 2:4: God spared not the angels that sinned but delivered them into chains of darkness, reserved unto judgment, which is the state the chains of 54:3-5 are being made ready for.
Leviticus 16:8-10: Two goats are set before the LORD, lots are cast, one goat is for the LORD and one for Azazel, and the second is sent alive into the wilderness.
Genesis 7:11: The fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven were opened, the double source of water 54:7-8 describes.
Revelation 20:1-3: An angel with the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand binds the dragon and casts him in, and shuts and seals it over him.

translationNotes.note: Leviticus 16:8-10 and 16:26 set two goats before the LORD on the Day of Atonement, one for the LORD and one for Azazel, and the second is driven alive into the wilderness carrying the people's iniquities. In this book Azazel is one of the angels who came down: 8:1 has him teach men to make swords, knives, shields and breastplates, to work the metals of the earth, and to paint the eyelids with antimony. 10:4-6 has Raphael bind him hand and foot, cast him into an opening in the desert called Dudael, cover him with jagged rocks and darkness, and hold him there until the day of the great judgment.

translationNotes.original: Aramaic: אַתּוּן נוּרָא (attun nura, furnace of fire)
translationNotes.note: Daniel 3:6 and 3:19-23 have a furnace of burning fire heated seven times hotter, used as an instrument of execution. The word names a working kiln for smelting ore and firing brick, which is why it was to hand for that purpose. 54:6 sends the hosts of Azazel into one, and Matthew 13:42 and 13:50 use the Greek equivalent for the end of the age.

translationNotes.term: The waters above and the waters beneath
translationNotes.note: 54:7-8 says the chambers of waters above the heavens and the fountains beneath the earth will both be opened and the two joined. That is how Genesis 7:11 describes the flood, the fountains of the great deep broken up and the windows of heaven opened, and Genesis 8:2 stops both again. The dividing of waters above from waters below is at Genesis 1:6-7.

54:8 says the water above the heavens is masculine and the water beneath the earth is feminine. Hebrew, Aramaic and Ge'ez have no neuter gender, so every noun in them is either masculine or feminine. 60:16 speaks the same way of the spirit of the sea, which it calls masculine and strong.

54:5 says the hosts of Azazel will have their jaws covered with rough stones when they are cast into the abyss. 10:5 gives Azazel himself the same treatment, rough and jagged rocks placed on him and his face covered so that he may not see light. The stones seal the mouth shut.

The line printed here as 54:2, Noachic Fragment on the first World Judgement, is a section heading the editor inserted and not a verse of the book. The same thing happens at the end of 41:2 with Astronomical Secrets, at 56:4, and at 69:25 with Close of the Third Parable. The chapter's own text begins with the chains at 54:3.

stories.keyTakeaway: The angel shows Enoch iron chains of immeasurable weight, prepared for the hosts of Azazel, who will be thrown into the abyss and have their jaws covered with rough stones. Michael, Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel will cast them into the burning furnace. Then the waters above and beneath are opened.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 55
summaryBullets: And after that the Head of Days repented and said: 'In vain have I destroyed all who dwell on the earth.' (55:1).

And He sware by His great name: 'Henceforth I will not do so to all who dwell on the earth, and I will set a sign in the heaven: and this shall be a pledge of good faith between Me and them for ever, so long as heaven is above the earth. And this is in accordance with My command.' LV. 3-LVI. (55:2).

When I have desired to take hold of them by the hand of the angels on the day of tribulation and pain because of this, I will cause My chastisement and My wrath to abide upon them, says God, the Lord of Spirits. (55:3).

You †mighty kings† who dwell on the earth, you will have to behold Mine Elect One, how he sits on the throne of glory and judges Azâzêl, and all his associates, and all his hosts in the name of the Lord of Spirits.' (55:4).
crossRefs: Genesis 8:21: The LORD says in his heart that he will not again curse the ground for man's sake, nor again smite every living thing as he has done.
Genesis 9:12-17: God sets his bow in the cloud as the token of the covenant between him and every living creature, so that the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
Isaiah 54:9-10: As God swore that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth, so he has sworn not to be wroth with his people, and the covenant of his peace shall not be removed.
Hebrews 6:13-17: Because God could swear by no greater, he swore by himself, and an oath for confirmation is the end of all argument among men.
Genesis 6:6-7: It repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart, the same verb this chapter uses.

translationNotes.note: Nacham covers grief, relenting, and turning back from a stated course. Genesis 6:6 says it repented the LORD that he had made man, Exodus 32:14 says the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people, and Jonah 3:10 says he repented of the evil he had said he would do to Nineveh. 55:1 uses it of the Head of Days looking at the flood he sent.

The word at Genesis 9:13 is qeshet, the ordinary word for a war bow, the same word used of the weapon at Psalm 46:9. 55:2 does not name the bow. It says only that a sign is set in the heaven as a pledge of good faith between God and men for as long as heaven is above the earth, which is the covenant of Genesis 9:12-17.

translationNotes.term: He sware by His great name
translationNotes.note: An oath was sworn by something greater than the man swearing it, which is why Genesis 22:16 has God say by myself have I sworn, and Hebrews 6:13 says he could swear by no greater. To swear by the name was to stake the name itself on the outcome. 55:2 has the Head of Days swear by his great name that he will not destroy all mankind again.

translationNotes.term: Judges Azazel and all his associates
translationNotes.note: 55:4 tells the kings they will see the Elect One sit on the throne of glory and judge Azazel, his associates and all his hosts. That is the judgment announced at 10:6, where Azazel is to be cast into the fire on the day of the great judgment, and 54:5-6 has the four named angels carry it out.

The characters at the end of 55:2, LV. 3-LVI, are the editor's reference marks from the printed book and not part of the verse. LV is 55 and LVI is 56, so the mark reads chapter 55 verse 3 through chapter 56, and it flags where the editor judged a new section to begin.

stories.keyTakeaway: The Head of Days says he destroyed everyone on the earth in vain, swears by his great name that he will not do so again, and sets a sign in the heaven as a pledge of good faith for as long as heaven is above the earth. The kings are told they will watch the Elect One judge Azazel.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 56
summaryBullets: And I saw there the hosts of the angels of punishment going, and they held scourges and chains of iron and bronze. (56:1).
And I asked the angel of peace who went with me, saying: 'To whom are these who hold the scourges going?' (56:2).
And he said to me: 'To their elect and beloved ones, that they may be cast into the chasm of the abyss of the valley. (56:3).

And then that valley shall be filled with their elect and beloved, And the days of their lives shall be at an end, And the days of their leading astray shall not thenceforward be reckoned. LVI. 5-8. Last struggle of heathen Powers against Israel . (56:4).

And in those days the angels shall return And hurl themselves to the east upon the Parthians and Medes: They shall stir up the kings, so that a spirit of unrest shall come upon them, And they shall rouse them from their thrones, That they may break forth as lions from their lairs, And as hungry wolves among their flocks. (56:5).

And they shall go up and tread under foot the land of His elect ones, And the land of His elect ones shall be before them a threshing-floor and a highway: 7 But the city of my righteous shall be a hindrance to their horses. And they shall begin to fight among themselves, And their right hand shall be strong against themselves, And a man shall not know his brother, Nor a son his father or his mother, Till there be no number of the corpses through their slaughter, And their punishment be not in vain. 8 In those days Sheol shall open its jaws, And they shall be swallowed up therein And their destruction shall be at an end; Sheol shall devour the sinners in the presence of the elect.' (56:6).
crossRefs: Isaiah 13:17: Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, which shall not regard silver, and as for gold they shall not delight in it.
Zechariah 12:2-3: Jerusalem is made a cup of trembling and a burdensome stone for all people, and all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces.
Ezekiel 38:21: Every man's sword shall be against his brother, the turning of an invading host on itself that 56:7 describes.
Numbers 16:31-33: The ground opens her mouth and swallows Korah and his company, and they go down alive into the pit.
Isaiah 14:9: Hell from beneath is moved to meet thee at thy coming, and it stirs up the dead kings of the nations for thee.

translationNotes.note: The Medes were the people of Media in what is now northwest Iran, the power that helped bring down Nineveh in 612 BC and that Isaiah 13:17 and Jeremiah 51:11 say God stirs up against Babylon. The Parthians were a later Iranian people whose empire, ruled by the Arsacid line from about 247 BC, took that territory from the Greek kings and became Rome's rival in the east. In 40 BC a Parthian army took Jerusalem, put Antigonus on the throne and carried off the high priest Hyrcanus, which Josephus records in the Antiquities and the Jewish War. Acts 2:9 lists Parthians and Medes first among the crowd at Pentecost.

A scourge was a short whip of several leather thongs used for judicial beating. Deuteronomy 25:2-3 caps a sentence at forty stripes so that a brother is not degraded, and Paul says he received forty save one five times, at 2 Corinthians 11:24. 56:1 puts scourges in the hands of the angels of punishment alongside chains of iron and bronze.

A threshing floor was a flat, hard, exposed patch of rock or beaten earth on high ground, where cut grain was spread and driven over by sledges and oxen until the husks broke off. 56:6 says the land of the elect will be a threshing floor and a highway under the invaders, which is ground beaten flat and walked across.

56:8 has Sheol open and swallow the invaders in the sight of the elect. Numbers 16:31-33 has the ground open its mouth and swallow Korah, Dathan and Abiram alive with their households, and Isaiah 5:14 has hell enlarge herself and open her mouth without measure. The picture is a mouth in the ground rather than a furnace.

56:7 says the city of the righteous will be an obstacle to the invaders' horses. This is the only mention of a city anywhere in chapters 37 to 71, and the book does not name it. Zechariah 12:2-3 uses the same picture of Jerusalem as a stone that injures whoever tries to lift it.

The words at the end of 56:4, giving Roman numerals and then a title about a last struggle of heathen powers against Israel, are the editor's heading for the verses that follow and not part of the book. The verse itself ends with the days of their leading astray.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees angels of punishment carrying scourges and chains of iron and bronze toward the valley. The angels then stir up the Parthians and the Medes, whose armies trample the land of the elect until they turn on one another, and Sheol opens its jaws and swallows the sinners.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 57
summaryBullets: And it came to pass after this that I saw another host of wagons, and men riding thereon, and coming on the winds from the east, and from the west to the south. (57:1).

And the noise of their wagons was heard, and when this turmoil took place the holy ones from heaven remarked it, and the pillars of the earth were moved from their place, and the sound thereof was heard from the one end of heaven to the other, in one day. (57:2).
And they shall all fall down and worship the Lord of Spirits. And this is the end of the second Parable. (57:3).
crossRefs: Isaiah 66:20: They shall bring all your brethren out of all nations upon horses, in chariots and in litters, as an offering unto the LORD.
Isaiah 43:5-6: Fear not, I will bring thy seed from the east and gather thee from the west, and say to the north give up and to the south keep not back.
Isaiah 11:11-12: The Lord sets his hand a second time to recover the remnant of his people and gathers the outcasts of Israel from the four corners of the earth.
1 Samuel 2:8: The pillars of the earth are the LORD's and he hath set the world upon them, the foundations 57:2 says were moved out of place.
Job 9:6: He shaketh the earth out of her place and the pillars thereof tremble, the same picture of the ground itself being disturbed.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֲגָלָה (agalah, cart or wagon) - רֶכֶב (rekev, chariot)
translationNotes.note: Hebrew keeps the wagon separate from the chariot. An agalah is a heavy ox-drawn cart for hauling, the kind Pharaoh sends to carry Jacob's household down to Egypt at Genesis 45:19-21 and the covered carts that carried the tabernacle at Numbers 7:3-8. A chariot is a light two-wheeled vehicle for fighting or travelling. 57:1 has a host of the heavy kind, with men riding on them.

translationNotes.term: From the east and from the west to the south
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קֶדֶם (qedem, east and also front)
translationNotes.note: Hebrew takes its bearings facing the sunrise, so east is in front, west is behind, south is on the right hand and north on the left. That is why the same word means east and front. Isaiah 43:5-6 gathers from all four directions in turn and Isaiah 11:11-12 from the four corners of the earth. 57:1 names three of the four.

Scripture describes the earth as a building set on foundations and pillars. 1 Samuel 2:8 says the pillars of the earth are the LORD's, Job 9:6 says he shakes the earth out of her place and her pillars tremble, and Psalm 75:3 has God bear up the pillars of it when the earth is dissolved. 57:2 says the noise of the wagons moved them.

translationNotes.term: They shall all fall down and worship
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שָׁחָה (shachah, to bow down or prostrate oneself)
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew word is physical, to go down with the face to the ground, which is what Abraham does before the three men at Genesis 18:2. It is the verb rendered worship all through the Old Testament, so worship in that language begins as a posture. 57:3 closes the parable with everyone doing it.

translationNotes.term: The end of the second Parable
translationNotes.note: 57:3 says in plain words that this is the end of the second Parable. That parable began at 45:1, so it runs across thirteen chapters. The third begins at once, at 58:1, and closes at 69:29.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees a host of wagons with men riding on them, coming on the winds from the east and from the west toward the south. The noise moves the pillars of the earth and is heard from one end of heaven to the other, and all of them fall down and worship. The second Parable ends here.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 58
summaryBullets: And I began to speak the third Parable concerning the righteous and elect. (58:1).
Blessed are you, you righteous and elect, For glorious shall be your lot. (58:2).
And the righteous shall be in the light of the sun. And the elect in the light of eternal life: The days of their life shall be unending, And the days of the holy without number. (58:3).
And they shall seek the light and find righteousness with the Lord of Spirits: There shall be peace to the righteous in the name of the Eternal Lord. (58:4).

And after this it shall be said to the holy in heaven That they should seek out the secrets of righteousness, the heritage of faith: For it has become bright as the sun upon earth, And the darkness is past. (58:5).

And there shall be a light that never endeth , And to a limit (lit. 'number') of days they shall not come, For the darkness shall first have been destroyed, And the light established before the Lord of Spirits And the light of uprightness established for ever before the Lord of Spirits. (58:6).
crossRefs: Matthew 13:43: Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.
Daniel 12:3: They that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament, and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.
Isaiah 60:19-20: The sun shall be no more thy light by day, for the LORD shall be an everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.
Revelation 21:23-25: The city has no need of the sun or the moon, for the glory of God lightens it, and there shall be no night there.
1 Peter 1:10-12: The prophets searched diligently what the Spirit in them was signifying, and the angels desire to look into these things.

translationNotes.note: 58:1 announces the third and last of the three discourses, which runs to 69:29, where the text says this is the Third Parable of Enoch. The first ran from 38:1 to the end of chapter 44 and the second from 45:1 to 57:3. Chapters 70 and 71 stand outside all three.

Ashre is a declaration and not a wish. It announces that a man stands in a good position, which is how Psalm 1:1 opens, blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly. The Greek makarios is the word behind each line of the Beatitudes at Matthew 5:3-11. 58:2 opens the parable in that form.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אוֹר (or, light) - חַיֵּי עוֹלָם (chayye olam, everlasting life)
translationNotes.note: Light and life stand together in Hebrew usage. Psalm 36:9 says with thee is the fountain of life, and in thy light shall we see light, and Job 33:30 speaks of being enlightened with the light of the living. Daniel 12:2 gives the phrase everlasting life. 58:3 puts the righteous in the light of the sun and the elect in the light of eternal life.

A nachalah was the family land, the portion allotted to a household that was not supposed to be sold out of the family, which is why Naboth refuses to hand his vineyard to Ahab at 1 Kings 21:3. 58:5 uses that word for the secrets of righteousness, so they are treated as property already assigned rather than a reward still to be won.

58:6 puts the events in an order: the darkness is destroyed first, and only then is the light established for ever. Isaiah 60:19-20 says the LORD will be an everlasting light and the sun shall no more go down, and Revelation 21:23-25 says the city needs neither sun nor moon and there is no night there.

stories.keyTakeaway: The Third Parable begins with a blessing on the righteous and the elect. Their days will have no end, they will live in the light of the sun and in the light of eternal life, and the holy in heaven are told to search out the secrets of righteousness now that the darkness is past.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 59
summaryBullets: In those days mine eyes saw the secrets of the lightnings, and of the lights, and the judgements they execute (lit. 'their judgement'): and they lighten for a blessing or a curse as the Lord of Spirits willeth. (59:1).

And there I saw the secrets of the thunder, and how when it resounds above in the heaven, the sound thereof is heard, and he caused me to see the judgements executed on the earth, whether they be for well-being and blessing, or for a curse according to the word of the Lord of Spirits. (59:2).
And after that all the secrets of the lights and lightnings were shown to me, and they lighten for blessing and for satisfying. (59:3).
crossRefs: Job 37:11-13: God causes the cloud to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy, so the same weather serves opposite ends.
Psalm 29:3-9: The voice of the LORD is upon the waters and breaks the cedars of Lebanon, a psalm that describes a thunderstorm as speech.
Exodus 9:23-26: Thunder and hail strike the whole land of Egypt, and only in Goshen, where the children of Israel are, is there no hail.
1 Samuel 12:17-18: Samuel calls for thunder and rain in wheat harvest, and the people fear the LORD, a storm sent as a sign against them.
Job 38:24-25: God asks who has divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קוֹל (qol, voice or sound) - רַעַם (ra'am, thunder)
translationNotes.note: Hebrew most often calls thunder the voice of God, using qol, the ordinary word for a voice. Exodus 19:16 has thunders and lightnings on Sinai, Psalm 29 repeats the voice of the LORD seven times over a storm, and John 12:29 has a crowd hear a voice from heaven and say that it thundered. 59:2 asks what the sound means when it resounds above in the heaven.

translationNotes.term: They lighten for a blessing or a curse
translationNotes.note: 59:1 and 59:2 say the same lightning and thunder serve opposite ends, decided by the word of the Lord of Spirits. Job 37:13 says God brings the cloud whether for correction, for his land, or for mercy. Exodus 9:23-26 works that out on the ground, where the hail falls across all Egypt and not at all in Goshen.

Meoroth is the word for the lights God sets in the expanse at Genesis 1:14-16, the sun, the moon and the stars, and the same word is used of the oil lamps of the tabernacle lampstand at Exodus 35:14. 59:1 and 59:3 pair the lights with the lightnings as two kinds of thing whose secrets Enoch is shown.

59:1 says the lightnings execute judgments, and 59:2 says Enoch was made to see those judgments carried out on the earth. The chapter names no place, no nation and no person. It reports only the two possible outcomes, well-being and blessing on one side and a curse on the other.

These three verses return to the weather secrets Enoch was already shown at 41:3-9, and they are the last of that material in the Parables. The chapter stands between the opening of the third Parable at 58:1 and the dated vision that begins at 60:1.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch is shown the secrets of the lightnings and the lights, and how the thunder sounds when it resounds above. He is made to see the judgments they carry out on the earth, which fall either for well-being and blessing or for a curse, according to the word of the Lord of Spirits.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 60
summaryBullets: In the year five hundred, in the seventh month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the life of †Enoch†. In that Parable I saw how a mighty quaking made the heaven of heavens to quake, and the host of the Most High, and the angels, a thousand thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, were disquieted with a great disquiet. (60:1).
And the Head of Days sat on the throne of His glory, and the angels and the righteous stood around Him. (60:2).

And a great trembling seized me, And fear took hold of me, And my loins gave way, And dissolved were my reins, And I fell upon my face. 4 And Michael sent another angel from among the holy ones and he raised me up, and when he had raised me up my spirit returned; for I had not been able to endure the look of this host, and the commotion and the quaking of the heaven. And Michael said to me: 'Why are you disquieted with such a vision? Until this day lasted the day of His mercy; and He has been merciful and long-suffering towards those who dwell on the earth. (60:3).

And Michael sent another angel from among the holy ones and he raised me up, and when he had raised me up my spirit returned; for I had not been able to endure the look of this host, and the commotion and the quaking of the heaven. (60:4).
