And Michael said to me: 'Why are you disquieted with such a vision? Until this day lasted the day of His mercy; and He has been merciful and long-suffering towards those who dwell on the earth.' (60:5).

And when the day, and the power, and the punishment, and the judgement come, which the Lord of Spirits has prepared for those who worship not the righteous law , and for those who deny the righteous judgement, and for those who take His name in vain--that day is prepared, for the elect a covenant, but for sinners an inquisition. (60:6).
And on that day were two monsters parted, a female monster named Leviathan, to dwell in the abysses of the ocean over the fountains of the waters. (60:7).

But the male is named Behemoth, who occupied with his breast a waste wilderness named †Dûidâin†, on the east of the garden where the elect and righteous dwell, where my grandfather was taken up, the seventh from Adam, the first man whom the Lord of Spirits created. (60:8).

And I besought the other angel that he should show me the might of those monsters, how they were parted on one day and cast, the one into the abysses of the sea, and the other to the dry land of the wilderness. (60:9).
And he said to me: 'You son of man, herein you do seek to know what is hidden.' (60:10).

And the other angel who went with me and showed me what was hidden told me what is first and last in the heaven in the height, and beneath the earth in the depth, and at the ends of the heaven, and on the foundation of the heaven. (60:11).

And the chambers of the winds, and how the winds are divided, and how they are weighed, and (how) the portals of the winds are reckoned, each according to the power of the wind, and the power of the lights of the moon, and according to the power that is fitting: and the divisions of the stars according to their names, and how all the divisions are divided. (60:12).
And the thunders according to the places where they fall, and all the divisions that are made among the lightnings that it may lighten, and their host that they may at once obey. (60:13).

For the thunder has †places of rest† (which) are assigned (to it) while it is waiting for its peal; and the thunder and lightning are inseparable, and although not one and undivided, they both go together through the spirit and separate not. (60:14).

For when the lightning lightens, the thunder utters its voice, and the spirit enforces a pause during the peal, and divides equally between them; for the treasury of their peals is like the sand, and each one of them as it peals is held in with a bridle, and turned back by the power of the spirit, and pushed forward according to the many quarters of the earth. And the spirit of the sea is masculine and strong, and according to the might of his strength he draws it back with a rein, and in like manner it is driven forward and disperses amid all the mountains of the earth. (60:15).

And the spirit of the sea is masculine and strong, and according to the might of his strength he draws it back with a rein, and in like manner it is driven forward and disperses amid all the mountains of the earth. (60:16).
And the spirit of the hoar-frost is his own angel, and the spirit of the hail is a good angel. (60:17).
And the spirit of the snow has forsaken his chambers on account of his strength--There is a special spirit therein, and that which ascends from it is like smoke, and its name is frost. (60:18).

And the spirit of the mist is not united with them in their chambers, but it has a special chamber; for its course is †glorious† both in light and in darkness, and in winter and in summer, and in its chamber is an angel. (60:19).

And the spirit of the dew has its dwelling at the ends of the heaven, and is connected with the chambers of the rain, and its course is in winter and summer: and its clouds and the clouds of the mist are connected, and the one gives to the other. (60:20).

And when the spirit of the rain goes forth from its chamber, the angels come and open the chamber and lead it out, and when it is diffused over the whole earth it unites with the water on the earth. And whensoever it unites with the water on the earth . . . (60:21).

For the waters are for those who dwell on the earth; for they are nourishment for the earth from the Most High who is in heaven: therefore there is a measure for the rain, and the angels take it in charge. (60:22).
And these things I saw towards the Garden of the Righteous. (60:23).
And the angel of peace who was with me said to me: 'These two monsters, prepared conformably to the greatness of God, shall feed . . . (60:24).

When the punishment of the Lord of Spirits shall rest upon them, it shall rest in order that the punishment of the Lord of Spirits may not come, in vain, and it shall slay the children with their mothers and the children with their fathers. Afterwards the judgement shall take place according to His mercy and His patience.' (60:25).
crossRefs: Job 40:15-24: Behemoth eats grass like an ox, his strength is in his loins, his tail moves like a cedar, and he lies under the shady trees by the river.
Job 41:1-34: Leviathan cannot be drawn out with a hook, his scales are shut up close as with a seal, and out of his mouth go burning lamps.
Isaiah 27:1: In that day the LORD with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent and slay the dragon that is in the sea.
2 Esdras 6:49-52: God separates Behemoth and Leviathan on the fifth day, gives the dry land to one and the sea to the other, and keeps them for whom he will.
Psalm 104:26: There go the ships, and there is that leviathan whom thou hast made to play therein.

translationNotes.note: Job 40:15-24 describes Behemoth, which eats grass like an ox, whose strength is in his loins and whose tail moves like a cedar. Job 41:1-34 describes Leviathan, whose scales are shut up close as with a seal and whom no hook will draw out. Isaiah 27:1 calls Leviathan the piercing serpent and the dragon in the sea. 60:7-9 has the two parted on one day, the female Leviathan sent to the abysses of the ocean and the male Behemoth to the dry wilderness.

Behemoth is the plural form of behemah, the ordinary word for a beast or cattle, used at Genesis 1:24. Hebrew sometimes puts a noun in the plural to intensify it rather than to count it, and that is how the name reads: the beast of beasts. Job 40:15 uses it of one creature, and 60:8 does the same.

60:8 puts Behemoth in a waste wilderness named Dudain, east of the garden where the elect and righteous dwell. The name is not in Scripture and this book uses it only here. It is not the same place as Dudael, the opening in the desert where 10:4 says Azazel was bound.

60:8 calls Enoch the seventh from Adam and the speaker calls him my grandfather, so the one speaking is a descendant rather than Enoch himself. Jude 1:14 uses the same count, Enoch, the seventh from Adam. Genesis 5:1-24 gives the line it comes from: Adam, Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch.

At 60:10 the angel addresses the seer as son of man, which in Hebrew and Aramaic simply means a human being. God addresses Ezekiel that way more than ninety times, from Ezekiel 2:1 onward. This is not the title used at 46:2 and 62:5. Here the same words are a form of address to the man being spoken to.

60:1 dates the vision to the five hundredth year, in the seventh month, on the fourteenth day, in the life of a man whose name the translator fenced with daggers to mark it uncertain. Genesis 5:23 gives Enoch 365 years in all. Genesis 5:32 says Noah was five hundred years old, and the speaker at 60:8 calls Enoch his grandfather.

translationNotes.term: My loins gave way and my reins were dissolved
translationNotes.note: Reins is old English for the kidneys, and Hebrew treats the kidneys as the seat of the deepest feeling and of conscience, as at Psalm 16:7 and Jeremiah 17:10, where God tries the heart and the reins. 60:3 is describing bodily collapse under fear. Daniel 5:6 says the joints of Belshazzar's loins were loosed and his knees smote one against another, and Daniel 10:8-9 reports the same weakness.

translationNotes.term: The chambers of the winds and the measure for the rain
translationNotes.note: 60:11-22 walks through storerooms for the winds, thunder, lightning, hoarfrost, hail, snow, mist, dew and rain, with an angel set over each one. 60:22 says there is a measure for the rain and the angels take it in charge. Job 38:22 asks whether Job has entered the treasuries of the snow and the hail, and Deuteronomy 28:12 calls the rain the LORD's good treasure.

translationNotes.term: The spirit of the sea is masculine
translationNotes.note: 60:16 calls the spirit of the sea masculine and strong, and says he draws the sea back with a rein and drives it forward again. Hebrew, Aramaic and Ge'ez have no neuter gender, so every noun in them is masculine or feminine, and 54:8 speaks the same way of the waters above and below. Job 38:8-11 has God shut the sea behind doors and bars and tell it how far it may come.

stories.keyTakeaway: A vision dated to a five hundredth year shakes the heaven of heavens, and the Head of Days takes his throne. Michael raises the seer and speaks of the day of mercy. Leviathan and Behemoth are parted, one to the deeps of the sea and one to a waste wilderness, and the storehouses of the weather opened.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 61
summaryBullets: And I saw in those days how long cords were given to those angels, and they took to themselves wings and flew, and they went towards the north. (61:1).
And I asked the angel, saying to him: 'Why have those (angels) taken these cords and gone off?' And he said to me: 'They have gone to measure.' (61:2).

And the angel who went with me said to me: 'These shall bring the measures of the righteous, And the ropes of the righteous to the righteous, That they may stay themselves on the name of the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever. (61:3).
The elect shall begin to dwell with the elect, And those are the measures which shall be given to faith And which shall strengthen righteousness. (61:4).

And these measures shall reveal all the secrets of the depths of the earth, And those who have been destroyed by the desert, And those who have been devoured by the beasts, And those who have been devoured by the fish of the sea, That they may return and stay themselves On the day of the Elect One; For none shall be destroyed before the Lord of Spirits, And none can be destroyed. (61:5).
And all who dwell above in the heaven received a command and power and one voice and one light like to fire. (61:6).
And that One (with) their first words they blessed, And extolled and lauded with wisdom, And they were wise in utterance and in the spirit of life. (61:7).
And the Lord of Spirits placed the Elect one on the throne of glory. And he shall judge all the works of the holy above in the heaven, And in the balance shall their deeds be weighed (61:8).

And when he shall lift up his countenance To judge their secret ways according to the word of the name of the Lord of Spirits, And their path according to the way of the righteous judgement of the Lord of Spirits, Then shall they all with one voice speak and bless, And glorify and extol and sanctify the name of the Lord of Spirits. (61:9).

And He will summon all the host of the heavens, and all the holy ones above, and the host of God, the Cherubic, Seraphin and Ophannin, and all the angels of power, and all the angels of principalities, and the Elect One, and the other powers on the earth (and) over the water. (61:10).

On that day shall raise one voice, and bless and glorify and exalt in the spirit of faith, and in the spirit of wisdom, and in the spirit of patience, and in the spirit of mercy, and in the spirit of judgement and of peace, and in the spirit of goodness, and shall all say with one voice: "Blessed is He, and may the name of the Lord of Spirits be blessed for ever and ever." (61:11).

All who sleep not above in heaven shall bless Him: All the holy ones who are in heaven shall bless Him, And all the elect who dwell in the garden of life: And every spirit of light who is able to bless, and glorify, and extol, and hallow Your blessed name, And all flesh shall beyond measure glorify and bless Your name for ever and ever. (61:12).

For great is the mercy of the Lord of Spirits, and He is long-suffering, And all His works and all that He has created He has revealed to the righteous and elect In the name of the Lord of Spirits. (61:13).
crossRefs: Zechariah 2:1-5: A man with a measuring line goes out to measure Jerusalem and is told the city will be inhabited as towns without walls, with the LORD a wall of fire around it.
Ezekiel 40:3: A man whose appearance was like brass stands in the gate with a line of flax in his hand and a measuring reed.
Revelation 11:1: John is given a reed like a rod and told to rise and measure the temple of God, the altar, and them that worship there.
Revelation 20:13: The sea gives up the dead which were in it, the same recovery of those who were lost where no grave was ever made.
Ezekiel 1:15-21: A wheel stands by each living creature, wheels within wheels, moving with the spirit of the creatures, which is where the order of angel called wheels comes from.

translationNotes.note: Ophan is the ordinary Hebrew word for a wheel, the wheel of a cart or a chariot. Ezekiel 1:15-21 and 10:9-13 describe wheels beside the living creatures, wheels within wheels, their rims full of eyes, moving wherever the spirit of the creatures went. Out of that description the wheels became the name of an order of angel, which is what 61:10 and 71:7 list alongside the Cherubim and the Seraphim.

Cherubim are set at the east of Eden with a flaming sword at Genesis 3:24, and two of hammered gold stand over the ark at Exodus 25:18-22. Seraphim means burning ones, and Isaiah 6:2-3 gives them six wings each and the threefold Holy. The King James forms cherubims and seraphims add an English plural to an ending that is already plural in Hebrew.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קָו (qav, a measuring line) - חֶבֶל (chevel, a cord)
translationNotes.note: A measuring line was a knotted cord, and the same cord was used to allot land, which is why chevel means both the rope and the portion measured out with it, as at Psalm 16:6, the lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places. Zechariah 2:1-5 and Ezekiel 40:3 both have a man holding one. 61:1-4 puts the cords in the hands of angels and calls the result the measures of the righteous.

translationNotes.term: Devoured by the beasts and by the fish of the sea
translationNotes.note: 61:5 names three ways a body is lost without burial: perishing in the desert, eaten by animals, eaten by fish. Being left unburied was the worst end a man could come to in that world, which is why 1 Kings 14:11 and Jeremiah 22:19 use it as a curse. The verse says these return, and that none can be destroyed before the Lord of Spirits.

translationNotes.term: The angels of principalities and powers
translationNotes.note: 61:10 lists ranks in order: the Cherubic, Seraphin and Ophannin, then the angels of power and the angels of principalities. Paul ranks them the same way at Colossians 1:16, thrones, dominions, principalities and powers, and again at Ephesians 6:12. The terms name orders of heavenly beings, not human offices.

61:1 sends the measuring angels north. In Hebrew usage the north is the direction of the divine mountain: Psalm 48:2 calls Zion beautiful for situation, on the sides of the north, and Isaiah 14:13 has the king of Babylon boast that he will sit upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north.

stories.keyTakeaway: Angels are given long cords and fly north to measure. The measures are for the righteous, and they reach those destroyed in the desert or devoured by beasts or fish, since none can be lost before the Lord of Spirits. The Elect One is set on the throne of glory and all heaven blesses him.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 62
summaryBullets: And thus the Lord commanded the kings and the mighty and the exalted, and those who dwell on the earth, and said: 'Open your eyes and lift up your horns if you are able to recognize the Elect One.' (62:1).

And the Lord of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face. (62:2).

And there shall stand up in that day all the kings and the mighty, And the exalted and those who hold the earth, And they shall see and recognize How he sits on the throne of his glory, And righteousness is judged before him, And no lying word is spoken before him. (62:3).
Then shall pain come upon them as on a woman in travail, And she has pain in bringing forth When her child enters the mouth of the womb, And she has pain in bringing forth. (62:4).

And one portion of them shall look on the other, And they shall be terrified, And they shall be downcast of countenance, And pain shall seize them, When they see that Son of Man Sitting on the throne of his glory. (62:5).
And the kings and the mighty and all who possess the earth shall bless and glorify and extol him who rules over all, who was hidden. (62:6).
For from the beginning the Son of Man was hidden, And the Most High preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect. (62:7).
And the congregation of the elect and holy shall be sown, And all the elect shall stand before him on that day. (62:8).

And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Man, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands. (62:9).

Nevertheless that Lord of Spirits will so press them That they shall hastily go forth from His presence, And their faces shall be filled with shame, And the darkness grow deeper on their faces. (62:10).
And He will deliver them to the angels for punishment, To execute vengeance on them because they have oppressed His children and His elect (62:11).

And they shall be a spectacle for the righteous and for His elect: They shall rejoice over them, Because the wrath of the Lord of Spirits resteth upon them, And His sword is drunk with their blood. (62:12).
And the righteous and elect shall be saved on that day, And they shall never thenceforward see the face of the sinners and unrighteous. (62:13).
And the Lord of Spirits will abide over them, And with that Son of Man shall they eat And lie down and rise up for ever and ever. (62:14).
And the righteous and elect shall have risen from the earth, And ceased to be of downcast countenance. And they shall have been clothed with garments of glory, (62:15).
And these shall be the garments of life from the Lord of Spirits: And your garments shall not grow old, Nor your glory pass away before the Lord of Spirits. (62:16).
crossRefs: Psalm 75:4-5: I said unto the fools, deal not foolishly, and to the wicked, lift not up the horn, speak not with a stiff neck.
Isaiah 13:8: They shall be afraid, pangs and sorrows shall take hold of them, and they shall be in pain as a woman that travaileth.
1 Thessalonians 5:3: When they shall say peace and safety, sudden destruction cometh upon them as travail upon a woman with child, and they shall not escape.
Isaiah 25:6: In this mountain the LORD of hosts makes unto all people a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees well refined.
Isaiah 61:10: He hath clothed me with the garments of salvation and covered me with the robe of righteousness, the clothing 62:15-16 describes.

translationNotes.note: The horn stands for strength and standing, taken from an animal that fights with its head up. To lift the horn is to assert power or boast, which Psalm 75:4-5 forbids in those words, and to have the horn cut down is to be humbled, as at Lamentations 2:3. 62:1 tells the kings to open their eyes and lift up their horns if they are able to recognize the Elect One.

translationNotes.term: Pain as on a woman in travail
translationNotes.note: This is the standing prophetic picture for terror that arrives suddenly and cannot be put off, and it is chosen because labour cannot be stopped once it has started. Isaiah 13:8, Jeremiah 30:6-7 and Micah 4:9-10 all use it of judgment, and Paul uses it of the day of the Lord at 1 Thessalonians 5:3. 62:4 spends a whole verse on it.

62:6-7 says the Son of Man was hidden from the beginning, that the Most High preserved him in the presence of his might, and that he was revealed to the elect. 48:6 says the same thing, chosen and hidden before the creation of the world. 62:5 is the moment the kings see him for the first time.

translationNotes.term: With that Son of Man shall they eat
translationNotes.note: 62:14 has the righteous eat, lie down and rise up with him for ever. A shared meal was the strongest form of covenant and welcome in that world: Exodus 24:9-11 has the elders of Israel eat and drink before God on the mountain, and Isaiah 25:6 sets a feast of fat things on the mountain for all peoples. Revelation 19:9 calls it the marriage supper of the Lamb.

translationNotes.term: Garments of life that shall not grow old
translationNotes.note: 62:15-16 clothes the risen righteous in garments of glory that never wear out and never fade. Clothing marked standing, which is why Joseph is given a coat at Genesis 37:3 and Mordecai royal apparel at Esther 6:8-11. Deuteronomy 8:4 says Israel's clothes did not wear out in forty years in the wilderness, and Revelation 7:9 puts the great multitude in white robes.

translationNotes.term: His sword is drunk with their blood
translationNotes.note: A sword that drinks is standard prophetic language for slaughter. Isaiah 34:5-6 says the sword of the LORD is bathed in heaven and filled with blood, and Jeremiah 46:10 says the sword shall devour and be made drunk with their blood. 62:12 uses it of the wrath of the Lord of Spirits resting on the kings.

stories.keyTakeaway: The kings and the mighty are told to open their eyes and see whether they can recognize the Elect One. When they see the Son of Man on the throne of glory, pain seizes them like a woman in labour and their pleading is refused. The righteous eat with him and are clothed in garments of glory.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 63
summaryBullets: In those days shall the mighty and the kings who possess the earth implore (Him) to grant them a little respite from His angels of punishment to whom they were delivered, that they might fall down and worship before the Lord of Spirits, and confess their sins before Him. (63:1).

And they shall bless and glorify the Lord of Spirits, and say: 'Blessed is the Lord of Spirits and the Lord of kings, And the Lord of the mighty and the Lord of the rich, And the Lord of glory and the Lord of wisdom, (63:2).

And splendid in every secret thing is Your power from generation to generation, And Your glory for ever and ever: Deep are all Your secrets and innumerable, And Your righteousness is beyond reckoning. (63:3).
We have now learnt that we should glorify And bless the Lord of kings and Him who is king over all kings.' (63:4).
And they shall say: 'Would that we had rest to glorify and give thanks And confess our faith before His glory! (63:5).
And now we long for a little rest but find it not: We follow hard upon and obtain (it) not: And light has vanished from before us, And darkness is our dwelling-place for ever and ever: (63:6).
For we have not believed before Him Nor glorified the name of the Lord of Spirits, nor glorified our Lord But our hope was in the sceptre of our kingdom, And in our glory. (63:7).

And in the day of our suffering and tribulation He saves us not, And we find no respite for confession That our Lord is true in all His works, and in His judgements and His justice, And His judgements have no respect of persons. (63:8).
And we pass away from before His face on account of our works, And all our sins are reckoned up in righteousness.' (63:9).
Now they shall say to themselves: 'Our souls are full of unrighteous gain, but it does not prevent us from descending from the midst thereof into the †burden† of Sheol.' (63:10).

And after that their faces shall be filled with darkness And shame before that Son of Man, And they shall be driven from his presence, And the sword shall abide before his face in their midst. (63:11).
Thus spoke the Lord of Spirits: 'This is the ordinance and judgement with respect to the mighty and the kings and the exalted and those who possess the earth before the Lord of Spirits.' (63:12).
crossRefs: Wisdom 5:1-8: The ungodly see the righteous man they mocked standing in great boldness, and ask among themselves what their pride has profited them.
Proverbs 1:24-28: Because they refused when he called, they shall call and he will not answer, and shall seek him early but shall not find him.
Luke 16:24-26: The rich man asks for a drop of water on his tongue and is told a great gulf is fixed so that none may pass from one side to the other.
Revelation 6:15-17: The kings of the earth and the great men hide in the dens and rocks and ask the mountains to fall on them and hide them from the wrath to come.
Isaiah 26:16: In trouble they have visited thee, they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them, the same turning to God only under punishment.

translationNotes.note: A sceptre was a rod carried as the sign of the right to rule, and holding it out was how a king granted access, which is why Esther 5:2 has Ahasuerus hold out the golden sceptre to Esther and she touches the top of it. Genesis 49:10 says the sceptre shall not depart from Judah. 63:7 has the kings confess that their hope was in that rod and in their own glory.

translationNotes.original: Aramaic: מֶלֶךְ מַלְכַיָּא (melekh malkaya, king of kings)
translationNotes.note: 63:2 and 63:4 stack titles: Lord of kings, Lord of the mighty, Lord of the rich, Lord of glory, and him who is king over all kings. King of kings was the standing style of a Persian great king, and Daniel 2:37 uses it of Nebuchadnezzar while Ezra 7:12 uses the same Aramaic of Artaxerxes. Deuteronomy 10:17 turns the form upward, God of gods and Lord of lords.

translationNotes.term: His judgements have no respect of persons
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נָשָׂא פָנִים (nasa panim, to lift the face)
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew idiom for favouritism is lifting a man's face, meaning treating him better because of who he is. Deuteronomy 10:17 says God regardeth not persons nor taketh reward, and Leviticus 19:15 forbids a judge to favour either the poor man or the mighty. 63:8 has the kings admit this out loud, which is the one thing their rank cannot buy.

63:10 has the kings say their souls are full of unrighteous gain and that it does not keep them from going down into Sheol, with the translator marking the word rendered burden as uncertain. Psalm 49:16-17 makes the same point plainly: be not thou afraid when one is made rich, for when he dieth he shall carry nothing away.

63:1 and 63:6 have the kings ask for a short pause in which to confess and glorify, and find none. Proverbs 1:24-28 gives that refusal in the same shape, that those who would not listen when called will call and not be answered. Luke 16:24-26 makes it a fixed gulf that cannot be crossed from either side.

stories.keyTakeaway: The kings beg a short respite from the angels of punishment so that they may worship and confess. They call God the Lord of kings and admit their hope had been in the sceptre of their kingdom. No rest is given, their sins are counted up, and they are driven from the presence of the Son of Man.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 64
summaryBullets: And other forms I saw hidden in that place. (64:1).

I heard the voice of the angel saying: 'These are the angels who descended to the earth, and revealed what was hidden to the children of men and seduced the children of men into committing sin.' (64:2).
crossRefs: Genesis 6:1-4: The sons of God see the daughters of men and take wives of all which they chose, and there were giants in the earth in those days.
Jude 1:6: The angels which kept not their first estate but left their own habitation are reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.
2 Peter 2:4: God spared not the angels that sinned but cast them down and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment.
1 Enoch 6:1-6: Two hundred of them bind themselves by a mutual oath on the summit of Mount Hermon in the days of Jared and come down.
1 Enoch 8:1-2: What they taught men, the making of swords and shields, the working of metals, the painting of the eyelids, enchantments and root-cutting.

translationNotes.note: 64:2 makes the charge revelation rather than desire: these angels showed men what had been kept from them. 8:1-2 lists what they showed, the making of swords, knives, shields and breastplates, the working of the metals of the earth, the use of antimony and the beautifying of the eyelids, and enchantments and root-cutting. 65:6 repeats the same charge as the reason the flood is coming.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פָּתָה (pathah, to entice or persuade)
translationNotes.note: The verb behind a charge of this shape is persuasion, not force, the same word Exodus 22:16 uses of a man who entices a girl. 64:2 says the angels led men into committing sin rather than committing it for them. 69:4-6 names the individual chiefs and says exactly what each of them taught.

64:1 says only that Enoch saw other forms hidden in that place, and the whole chapter is two verses. The place is the one from chapter 63, where the kings are driven from the presence of the Son of Man. The book never describes what the forms looked like.

Genesis 6:1-4 records the sons of God taking the daughters of men, and giants in the earth in those days. This book tells a descent at length at 6:1-6, where two hundred of them swear a mutual oath on the summit of Mount Hermon in the days of Jared. Jude 1:6 and 2 Peter 2:4 both say the angels who sinned are held in chains and darkness until the judgment.

Hermon is the mountain at the north end of the Anti-Lebanon range, on the northern edge of Israel's land, rising above 9,000 feet and snow-capped for most of the year. Deuteronomy 3:8-9 says the Sidonians called it Sirion and the Amorites called it Shenir, and Psalm 133:3 speaks of the dew of Hermon. This book puts the oath of the descending angels on its summit at 6:6.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch sees other forms hidden in that place. The voice of the angel tells him who they are: the angels who came down to the earth, revealed what had been hidden to the children of men, and led them into sin.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 65
summaryBullets: And in those days Noah saw the earth that it had sunk down and its destruction was near. (65:1).
And he arose from from there and went to the ends of the earth, and cried aloud to his grandfather Enoch: and Noah said three times with an embittered voice: Hear me, hear me, hear me.' (65:2).
And I said to him: 'Tell me what it is that is falling out on the earth that the earth is in such evil plight and shaken, lest perchance I shall perish with it?' (65:3).
And thereupon there was a great commotion, on the earth, and a voice was heard from heaven, and I fell on my face. (65:4).
And Enoch my grandfather came and stood by me, and said to me: 'Why have you cried to me with a bitter cry and weeping? (65:5).

And a command has gone forth from the presence of the Lord concerning those who dwell on the earth that their ruin is accomplished because they have learnt all the secrets of the angels, and all the violence of the Satans, and all their powers--the most secret ones--and all the power of those who practice sorcery, and the power of witchcraft, and the power of those who make molten images for the whole earth: (65:6).
And how silver is produced from the dust of the earth, and how soft metal originates in the earth. (65:7).
For lead and tin are not produced from the earth like the first: it is a fountain that produces them, and an angel stands therein, and that angel is pre-eminent.' (65:8).
And after that my grandfather Enoch took hold of me by my hand and raised me up, and said to me: 'Go, for I have asked the Lord of Spirits as touching this commotion on the earth. (65:9).

And He said to me: "Because of their unrighteousness their judgement has been determined upon and shall not be withheld by Me for ever. Because of the sorceries which they have searched out and learnt, the earth and those who dwell upon it shall be destroyed." (65:10).

And these--they have no place of repentance for ever, because they have shown them what was hidden, and they are the damned: but as for you, my son, the Lord of Spirits knows that you are pure, and guiltless of this reproach concerning the secrets. (65:11).

And He has destined your name to be among the holy, And will preserve you amongst those who dwell on the earth, And has destined your righteous seed both for kingship and for great honours, And from your seed shall proceed a fountain of the righteous and holy without number for ever. (65:12).
crossRefs: Genesis 6:11-13: The earth is corrupt before God and filled with violence, and God tells Noah that the end of all flesh is come before him.
Genesis 6:8-9: Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD, and Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.
Genesis 5:21-29: Enoch begets Methuselah, Methuselah begets Lamech, and Lamech begets Noah, the line behind the word grandfather in this chapter.
Deuteronomy 18:10-12: There shall not be found among you any that useth divination, an observer of times, an enchanter, or a witch, for all that do these things are an abomination.
Exodus 32:4: Aaron takes the gold, fashions it with a graving tool and makes a molten calf, which is the casting of images 65:6 names.

translationNotes.note: Noah calls Enoch his grandfather here and again in chapters 66 to 68. Genesis 5:21-29 makes Enoch his great-grandfather: Enoch begat Methuselah, Methuselah begat Lamech, and Lamech begat Noah. The word is being used in the wider sense of forefather, and Tertullian, writing about AD 200, calls Noah the great-grandson of Enoch.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כָּשַׁף (kashaph, to practise sorcery) - Greek: φαρμακεία (pharmakeia)
translationNotes.note: 65:6 lists what men learnt: the secrets of the angels, the violence of the Satans, sorcery, witchcraft, and the making of molten images. Exodus 22:18 and Deuteronomy 18:10-12 forbid the whole class of practice and name its parts, divination, observing times, enchanting, consulting the dead. The Greek pharmakeia at Galatians 5:20 and Revelation 18:23 covers the same ground and carries the sense of the drugs used in it.

A massekah was cast, not carved: metal melted and poured into a mould, then worked up with a tool. Exodus 32:4 has Aaron do exactly that with the gold to make the calf, and Exodus 34:17 forbids molten gods outright. 65:6 puts the men who make them in the same list as the sorcerers.

translationNotes.term: How silver is produced from the dust of the earth
translationNotes.note: 65:7-8 draws a distinction between the metals. Silver comes from the dust of the earth and soft metal originates in the earth, but lead and tin are said not to be produced from the earth like the first, coming instead from a fountain with a pre-eminent angel standing in it. The chapter counts knowing where metals come from as part of what men were not meant to be taught.

translationNotes.term: Hear me, hear me, hear me
translationNotes.note: 65:2 has Noah say it three times in an embittered voice. Threefold repetition is how Hebrew marks the strongest possible emphasis: Jeremiah 7:4 has the temple of the LORD three times over, Jeremiah 22:29 has O earth, earth, earth, and Isaiah 6:3 has Holy, holy, holy.

translationNotes.term: They have no place of repentance
translationNotes.original: Greek: μετανοίας τόπον (metanoias topon, place of repentance)
translationNotes.note: 65:11 says of those who revealed the secrets that they have no place of repentance for ever. Hebrews 12:17 uses that exact expression of Esau, who found no place of repentance though he sought it carefully with tears. It means an opportunity to reverse the outcome, not a location.

stories.keyTakeaway: Noah sees the earth sinking and its destruction near, and cries out three times to his forefather Enoch. Enoch tells him the ruin is settled because men have learnt the secrets of the angels, sorcery and the casting of images, and that Noah is guiltless and his seed will be preserved.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 66
summaryBullets: And after that he showed me the angels of punishment who are prepared to come and let loose all the powers of the waters which are beneath in the earth in order to bring judgement and destruction on all who abide and dwell on the earth. (66:1).

And the Lord of Spirits gave commandment to the angels who were going forth, that they should not cause the waters to rise but should hold them in check; for those angels were over the powers of the waters. (66:2).
And I went away from the presence of Enoch. (66:3).
crossRefs: Genesis 7:11: The fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven were opened, in the six hundredth year of Noah's life.
Genesis 8:2: The fountains of the deep and the windows of heaven were stopped, and the rain from heaven was restrained.
Job 38:8-11: God shuts up the sea with doors and bars and says hitherto shalt thou come but no further, and here shall thy proud waves be stayed.
Revelation 7:1-3: Four angels hold the four winds of the earth so that no wind blows, and are told to hurt nothing until the servants of God are sealed.
Revelation 16:5: The angel of the waters speaks, the same idea of a single angel set over one element.

translationNotes.term: The powers of the waters which are beneath
translationNotes.note: Tehom is the deep, the mass of water under and around the land, which Genesis 1:2 says darkness was on the face of, and which Genesis 7:11 says was broken up so that its fountains came out. 66:1 has angels standing ready to let it loose, and 66:2 has them ordered to hold it back instead.

66:2 says those angels were over the powers of the waters. This book gives an angel to each thing of that kind: 60:17-21 assigns one to the hoarfrost, the hail, the snow, the mist, the dew and the rain. Revelation 7:1-3 has four angels holding the four winds, and Revelation 16:5 speaks of the angel of the waters.

66:2 is a restraining order and not a cancellation. Job 38:8-11 has the same shape, the sea shut behind doors and bars and told how far it may come. Revelation 7:3 holds four angels back in the same way until the servants of God have been sealed in their foreheads.

translationNotes.term: The waters beneath and the waters above
translationNotes.note: This chapter names only the waters beneath the earth. 54:7-8 named both, the chambers of waters above the heavens and the fountains beneath the earth, and said the two would be joined. Genesis 7:11 gives both as well, the fountains of the great deep and the windows of heaven.

translationNotes.term: I went away from the presence of Enoch
translationNotes.note: 66:3 is spoken in the first person by the one who came to Enoch, which is how chapters 65 to 68 read throughout. It is the plainest signal in these chapters that the speaker is not Enoch, since Enoch is the one being left behind.

stories.keyTakeaway: The angels of punishment are shown ready to let loose the waters under the earth and bring destruction on everyone living. The Lord of Spirits orders the angels set over those waters not to let them rise but to hold them in check, and Noah leaves Enoch.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 67
summaryBullets: And in those days the word of God came to me, and He said to me: 'Noah, your lot has come up before Me, a lot without blame, a lot of love and uprightness. (67:1).

And now the angels are making a wooden (building), and when they have completed that task I will place My hand upon it and preserve it, and there shall come forth from it the seed of life, and a change shall set in so that the earth will not remain without inhabitant. (67:2).

And I will make fast your seed before me for ever and ever, and I will spread abroad those who dwell with you: it shall not be unfruitful on the face of the earth, but it shall be blessed and multiply on the earth in the name of the Lord.' (67:3).

And He will imprison those angels, who have shown unrighteousness, in that burning valley which my grandfather Enoch had formerly shown to me in the west among the mountains of gold and silver and iron and soft metal and tin. (67:4).
And I saw that valley in which there was a great convulsion and a convulsion of the waters. (67:5).

And when all this took place, from that fiery molten metal and from the convulsion thereof in that place, there was produced a smell of sulphur, and it was connected with those waters, and that valley of the angels who had led astray (mankind) burned beneath that land. (67:6).
And through its valleys proceed streams of fire, where these angels are punished who had led astray those who dwell upon the earth. (67:7).

But those waters shall in those days serve for the kings and the mighty and the exalted, and those who dwell on the earth, for the healing of the body, but for the punishment of the spirit; now their spirit is full of lust, that they may be punished in their body, for they have denied the Lord of Spirits and see their punishment daily, and yet believe not in His name. (67:8).

And in proportion as the burning of their bodies becomes severe, a corresponding change shall take place in their spirit for ever and ever; for before the Lord of Spirits none shall utter an idle word. (67:9).
For the judgement shall come upon them, because they believe in the lust of their body and deny the Spirit of the Lord. (67:10).

And those same waters will undergo a change in those days; for when those angels are punished in these waters, these water-springs shall change their temperature, and when the angels ascend, this water of the springs shall change and become cold. (67:11).
And I heard Michael answering and saying: 'This judgement with which the angels are judged is a testimony for the kings and the mighty who possess the earth.' (67:12).

Because these waters of judgement minister to the healing of the body of the kings and the lust of their body; therefore they will not see and will not believe that those waters will change and become a fire which burns for ever. (67:13).
crossRefs: Genesis 6:14-16: Make thee an ark of gopher wood with rooms in it, pitched within and without, three hundred cubits long, fifty broad and thirty high.
Genesis 6:18: I will establish my covenant with thee, and thou shalt come into the ark, thou and thy sons and thy wife and thy sons' wives with thee.
Genesis 9:1: God blesses Noah and his sons and tells them to be fruitful and multiply and replenish the earth, which is the seed of life 67:3 promises.
Genesis 19:24: The LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire out of heaven, the same sulphur and burning this valley gives off.
Revelation 20:10: The devil is cast into the lake of fire and brimstone where the beast and the false prophet are, and they are tormented day and night for ever.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תֵּבָה (tevah, a chest or box)
translationNotes.note: 67:2 never uses the word ark. It says the angels are making a wooden building, that God will place his hand on it and preserve it, and that the seed of life will come out of it. Genesis 6:14-16 gives the thing its measurements, three hundred cubits by fifty by thirty, in gopher wood, pitched inside and out. The Hebrew tevah is a chest, and the only other object it names in Scripture is the basket Moses is laid in at Exodus 2:3.

translationNotes.term: Your lot has come up before Me
translationNotes.note: A goral is a marked stone or object cast to settle a question, and then the share it assigns. Joshua 14:2 uses it for the territory each tribe received, and Jonah 1:7 has the sailors cast lots to find who had brought the storm. 67:1 says Noah's lot came up before God, a lot without blame, a lot of love and uprightness.

Brimstone is sulphur. It burns with a blue flame and a choking smell and is found in volcanic ground and around hot springs. Genesis 19:24 rains brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah, and Revelation 20:10 gives a lake of fire and brimstone. 67:6 says the smell came from the fiery molten metal and mixed with the waters.

translationNotes.term: Waters for the healing of the body
translationNotes.note: Hot mineral springs were the medicine of the ancient world for skin disease, wounds and joint pain, and men travelled to reach them. Josephus records that Herod the Great, in his last illness, was carried across the Jordan to the hot springs at Callirrhoe and lowered into a vessel of warm oil. 67:8 and 67:13 say these waters serve the kings and the mighty for the healing of the body and for the punishment of the spirit.

translationNotes.term: The burning valley in the west
translationNotes.note: 67:4 puts the prison in the valley Enoch had already shown Noah, in the west, among the mountains of gold and silver and iron and soft metal and tin. Those are the metal mountains of 52:2-6. 67:7 says streams of fire run through its valleys, and it is the same valley described at 53:1 and 56:3-4.

translationNotes.term: The waters shall change and become cold
translationNotes.note: 67:11 says the springs change temperature with the angels punished in them, running hot while the angels are there and turning cold when they ascend. 67:12 has Michael call that judgment a testimony for the kings and the mighty who possess the earth, and 67:13 says they will not believe the same waters will one day become fire.

stories.keyTakeaway: God tells Noah his lot is without blame, that the angels are making a wooden building, and that a seed of life will come out of it. The angels who led men astray are shut in a burning valley in the west, where molten metal makes the waters smell of sulphur and run with fire.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 68
summaryBullets: And after that my grandfather Enoch gave me the teaching of all the secrets in the book in the Parables which had been given to him, and he put them together for me in the words of the book of the Parables. (68:1).

And on that day Michael answered Raphael and said: 'The power of the spirit transports and makes me to tremble because of the severity of the judgement of the secrets, the judgement of the angels: who can endure the severe judgement which has been executed, and before which they melt away?' (68:2).

And Michael answered again, and said to Raphael: 'Who is he whose heart is not softened concerning it, and whose reins are not troubled by this word of judgement (that) has gone forth upon them because of those who have thus led them out?' (68:3).

And it came to pass when he stood before the Lord of Spirits, Michael said thus to Raphael: 'I will not take their part under the eye of the Lord; for the Lord of Spirits has been angry with them because they do as if they were the Lord. Therefore all that is hidden shall come upon them for ever and ever; for neither angel nor man shall have his portion (in it), but alone they have received their judgement for ever and ever.' (68:4).
crossRefs: Jude 1:9: Michael the archangel, disputing with the devil about the body of Moses, durst not bring a railing accusation but said, The Lord rebuke thee.
Nahum 1:6: Who can stand before his indignation, and who can abide in the fierceness of his anger, for his fury is poured out like fire.
Malachi 3:2: Who may abide the day of his coming, and who shall stand when he appeareth, for he is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap.
Isaiah 14:14: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds, I will be like the most High, the boast 68:4 charges these angels with.
Ezekiel 28:2: Thine heart is lifted up and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, yet thou art a man and not God.

translationNotes.note: 68:1 says Enoch gave over the teaching of all the secrets in the book of the Parables and put them together in the words of that book. That names the section the reader has just come through, chapters 37 to 71. 37:5 called the same material three parables imparted to him.

68:2-4 is a conversation between two of the four angels named at 40:9. Michael speaks three times and Raphael is the one spoken to. Michael's restraint here matches Jude 1:9, where he disputes with the devil over the body of Moses and will not bring a railing accusation, but says only, The Lord rebuke thee.

Reins is old English for the kidneys, and Hebrew treats them as the seat of the deepest feeling, which is why Psalm 16:7 says his reins instruct him in the night seasons and Jeremiah 17:10 has God try the heart and the reins. 68:3 uses the phrase of Michael himself, shaken by the judgment he is describing.

translationNotes.term: They do as if they were the Lord
translationNotes.note: 68:4 gives Michael's reason for not taking their part: the Lord of Spirits has been angry with them because they act as though they were the Lord. Isaiah 14:14 puts the same boast in the mouth of the king of Babylon, I will be like the most High, and Ezekiel 28:2 has a ruler say I am a God, I sit in the seat of God.

translationNotes.term: Neither angel nor man shall have his portion in it
translationNotes.note: 68:4 says this judgment belongs to these angels alone and that nobody else shares in it. These chapters keep two judgments apart throughout: chains and the burning furnace for the angels at 54:3-6, and the throne and the sentence for the kings and the mighty at 62:1-13.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch hands over the teaching of all the secrets in the book of the Parables. Michael tells Raphael that the severity of the judgment on the angels makes him tremble, and asks who could endure it. He will not take their part, because they acted as though they were the Lord.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 69
summaryBullets: And these are the chiefs of their angels and their names, and their chief ones over hundreds and over fifties and over tens . (69:3).
The name of the first Jeqôn: that is, the one who led astray all the sons of God , and brought them down to the earth, and led them astray through the daughters of men. (69:4).
And the second was named Asbeêl: he imparted to the holy sons of God evil counsel, and led them astray so that they defiled their bodies with the daughters of men. (69:5).

And the third was named Gâdreêl: he it is who showed the children of men all the blows of death, and he led astray Eve, and showed the weapons of death to the sons of men the shield and the coat of mail, and the sword for battle, and all the weapons of death to the children of men. (69:6).
And from his hand they have proceeded against those who dwell on the earth from that day and for evermore. (69:7).
And the fourth was named Pênêmûe: he taught the children of men the bitter and the sweet, and he taught them all the secrets of their wisdom. (69:8).
And he instructed mankind in writing with ink and paper, and thereby many sinned from eternity to eternity and until this day. (69:9).
For men were not created for such a purpose, to give confirmation to their good faith with pen and ink. (69:10).

For men were created exactly like the angels, to the intent that they should continue pure and righteous, and death, which destroys everything, could not have taken hold of them, but through this their knowledge they are perishing, and through this power it is consuming me†. (69:11).

And the fifth was named Kâsdejâ: this is he who showed the children of men all the wicked smitings of spirits and demons, and the smitings of the embryo in the womb, that it may pass away, and the smitings of the soul the bites of the serpent, and the smitings which befall through the noontide heat, the son of the serpent named Tabââ‘ĕt. (69:12).
And this is the task of Kâsbeêl, the chief of the oath which he showed to the holy ones when he dwelt high above in glory, and its name is Bîqâ. (69:13).

This (angel) requested Michael to show him the hidden name, that he might enunciate it in the oath, so that those might quake before that name and oath who revealed all that was in secret to the children of men. (69:14).

And this is the power of this oath, for it is powerful and strong, and he placed this oath Akâe in the hand of Michael. 16 And these are the secrets of this oath . . . And they are strong through his oath: And the heaven was suspended before the world was created, And for ever. (69:15).
And these are the secrets of this oath, and they are strong through his oath: and the heaven was suspended before the world was created, and for ever. (69:16).
And through it the earth was founded upon the water, And from the secret recesses of the mountains come beautiful waters, From the creation of the world and to eternity. (69:17).

And through that oath the sea was created, And †as its foundation† He set for it the sand against the time of (its) anger, And it dare not pass beyond it from the creation of the world to eternity. (69:18).
And through that oath are the depths made fast, And abide and stir not from their place from eternity to eternity. (69:19).
And through that oath the sun and moon complete their course, And deviate not from their ordinance from eternity to eternity. (69:20).
And through that oath the stars complete their course, And He calls them by their names, And they answer Him from eternity to eternity. (69:21).
And in like manner the spirits of the water, and of the winds, and of all zephyrs, and (their) paths from all the quarters of the winds. (69:22).

And there are preserved the voices of the thunder and the light of the lightnings: and there are preserved the chambers of the hail and the chambers of the hoarfrost, and the chambers of the mist, and the chambers of the rain and the dew. (69:23).

And all these believe and give thanks before the Lord of Spirits, and glorify (Him) with all their power, and their food is in every act of thanksgiving: they thank and glorify and extol the name of the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever. (69:24).
And this oath is mighty over them And through it they are preserved and their paths are preserved, And their course is not destroyed. Close of the Third Parable . (69:25).
And there was great joy amongst them, And they blessed and glorified and extolled Because the name of that Son of Man had been revealed to them. (69:26).

And he sat on the throne of his glory, And the sum of judgement was given to the Son of Man, And he caused the sinners to pass away and be destroyed from off the face of the earth, And those who have led the world astray. (69:27).
With chains shall they be bound, And in their assemblage-place of destruction shall they be imprisoned, And all their works vanish from the face of the earth. (69:28).

And from henceforth there shall be nothing corruptible; For that Son of Man has appeared, And has seated himself on the throne of his glory, And all evil shall pass away before his face, And the word of that Son of Man shall go forth And be strong before the Lord of Spirits. This is the Third Parable of Enoch. (69:29).
crossRefs: Genesis 3:1-6: The serpent speaks to the woman, she takes of the fruit and eats and gives to her husband with her, the deception 69:6 refers to.
Job 38:8-11: God shuts up the sea with doors and bars and says hitherto shalt thou come but no further, the bound 69:18 says the oath fixed.
Jeremiah 5:22: God placed the sand for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, so that though the waves toss they cannot prevail nor pass over it.
Proverbs 8:27-29: When he set a compass upon the face of the depth and gave to the sea his decree that the waters should not pass his commandment.
Psalm 147:4: He telleth the number of the stars and calleth them all by their names, which is what 69:21 says they answer to.

translationNotes.term: The chiefs and what each taught
translationNotes.note: 69:4-12 names five and says what each gave men. Jeqon led the sons of God astray. Asbeel gave them the counsel. Gadreel showed men the shield, the coat of mail and the sword. Penemue taught writing with ink and paper. Kasdeja showed the smitings of spirits and demons, the bite of the serpent, the sickness of the noonday heat, and the striking of the child in the womb so that it passes away. 69:13 then names a sixth, Kasbeel, the chief of the oath.

translationNotes.original: Greek: χάρτης (chartes, a papyrus sheet) - μέλαν (melan, ink)
translationNotes.note: Ink was lamp soot or charcoal ground up with gum and water, and paper here means papyrus, made by laying strips of the reed's pith crosswise and pressing them into a sheet. The pen was a cut reed. 2 John 1:12 says paper and ink, 3 John 1:13 says ink and pen, and Jeremiah 36:18 has Baruch write with ink in a book. 69:9-10 says men were not created to confirm their good faith with pen and ink.

69:14 has an angel ask Michael to show him the hidden name so that he could speak it in the oath. The name God gives Moses at Exodus 3:15 is written with four Hebrew consonants and was not pronounced, so a reader saying the text aloud said Adonai, Lord, in its place. That is why English Bibles print LORD in capitals wherever those four letters stand, and Leviticus 24:16 makes blaspheming the Name a capital matter.

69:13-25 gives the oath two names, Biqa and Akae, and says it was placed in the hand of Michael. Through it the heaven was hung before the world was created, the earth was founded on the water, the sea was given sand for its bound, the sun and moon hold their course, and the stars answer when they are called. 41:5 had already said the sun and moon were bound together by an oath, and this is where the book says what that oath is.

translationNotes.term: The sand as the sea's bound
translationNotes.note: 69:18 says the oath set the sand as the sea's foundation and that it dare not pass beyond it against the time of its anger. Jeremiah 5:22 says God placed the sand for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, so that though the waves toss they cannot pass over. Job 38:8-11 and Proverbs 8:29 say the same with doors, bars and a decree.

translationNotes.term: Gadreel and the weapons of death
translationNotes.note: 69:6 says Gadreel showed men all the blows of death and lists them: the shield, the coat of mail, the sword for battle. That is armour first and the blade after, which is the equipment of a man standing in a battle line. 8:1 gives the same teaching to Azazel, so the book attributes it in two places to two different chiefs.

translationNotes.term: The smitings of the embryo in the womb
translationNotes.note: 69:12 says Kasdeja showed the children of men the striking of the child in the womb so that it passes away, listed together with the smitings of spirits and demons, the bites of the serpent, and the sickness that comes with the noontide heat. Psalm 91:5-6 names that same class of dangers, the pestilence that walketh in darkness and the destruction that wasteth at noonday.

translationNotes.term: The end of the Third Parable
translationNotes.note: 69:29 closes with the words this is the Third Parable of Enoch. The line at the end of 69:25 that reads Close of the Third Parable is the editor's heading and not part of that verse. All three parables are finished here, and chapters 70 and 71 stand after them.

The text here opens at 69:3. The first two verses are not carried in this edition, so the chapter starts partway into the introduction to the list of names, which is why 69:3 reads as the end of a sentence already under way. Chapters 49, 52 and 54 begin the same way.

stories.keyTakeaway: The chiefs of the fallen angels are named one by one with what each taught: seduction, the weapons of death, writing with ink, and the striking of the child in the womb. Then comes the oath by which heaven hangs and the sea keeps its bound, and the Son of Man is seated on the throne of glory.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 70
summaryBullets: And it came to pass after this that his name during his lifetime was raised aloft to that Son of Man and to the Lord of Spirits from amongst those who dwell on the earth. (70:1).
And he was raised aloft on the chariots of the spirit and his name vanished among them. (70:2).

And from that day I was no longer numbered amongst them: and he set me between the two winds, between the North and the West, where the angels took the cords to measure for me the place for the elect and righteous. (70:3).
And there I saw the first fathers and the righteous who from the beginning dwell in that place. (70:4).
crossRefs: Genesis 5:24: Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him, which is the whole account Scripture gives of his end.
Hebrews 11:5: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death, and was not found, because God had translated him.
2 Kings 2:11: A chariot of fire and horses of fire part Elijah from Elisha, and Elijah goes up by a whirlwind into heaven.
Psalm 68:17: The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels, and the Lord is among them as in Sinai.
Matthew 8:11: Many shall come from the east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, the gathering of the fathers 70:4 describes.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לָקַח (laqach, to take) - Greek: μετατίθημι (metatithemi, to transfer)
translationNotes.note: Genesis 5:24 says Enoch walked with God and was not, for God took him, using laqach, the ordinary verb for taking a thing away. Hebrews 11:5 renders that with metatithemi, to move something from one place to another, and says he was translated that he should not see death and was not found. Translated in older English means carried across, not turned into another language.

70:2 has Enoch raised aloft on chariots. 2 Kings 2:11 has a chariot of fire and horses of fire carry Elijah up in a whirlwind, and 2 Kings 6:17 has Elisha's servant see the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire around him. Psalm 68:17 says the chariots of God are twenty thousand.

70:2 and 70:3 say his name vanished and that he was no longer numbered among those on the earth. To be numbered was to stand on a register, a household counted in a census, as at Numbers 1:2-3. The text describes his disappearance from the world of men as a name coming off the count.

translationNotes.term: Between the North and the West
translationNotes.note: 70:3 sets Enoch between two winds, the north and the west, at the place where the angels took the cords to measure for the elect and the righteous. That measuring is the scene of 61:1-4, where angels are given long cords and fly north. This verse puts him inside the ground those measures were taken for.

70:4 says he saw the first fathers and the righteous who have dwelt in that place from the beginning. The fathers in Hebrew usage are the ancestors of the nation, and Exodus 3:15 names them as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Matthew 8:11 has many come from east and west and sit down with those three.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch's name is lifted up from among those who dwell on the earth to the Son of Man and to the Lord of Spirits. He is carried away on the chariots of the spirit, is no longer counted among men, and is set between the north and the west, where he sees the first fathers and the righteous.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 71
summaryBullets: And it came to pass after this that my spirit was translated And it ascended into the heavens: And I saw the holy sons of God . They were stepping on flames of fire: Their garments were white and their raiment , And their faces shone like snow. (71:1).
And I saw two streams of fire, And the light of that fire shone like hyacinth, And I fell on my face before the Lord of Spirits. (71:2).
And the angel Michael one of the archangels seized me by my right hand, And lifted me up and led me forth into all the secrets, And he showed me all the secrets of righteousness. (71:3).
And he showed me all the secrets of the ends of the heaven, And all the chambers of all the stars, and all the luminaries, Whence they proceed before the face of the holy ones. (71:4).
And he translated my spirit into the heaven of heavens, And I saw there as it were a structure built of crystals, And between those crystals tongues of living fire. (71:5).
And my spirit saw the girdle which girt that house of fire, And on its four sides were streams full of living fire, And they girt that house. (71:6).
And round about were Seraphin, Cherubic, and Ophannin: And these are they who sleep not And guard the throne of His glory. (71:7).

And I saw angels who could not be counted, A thousand thousands, and ten thousand times ten thousand, Encircling that house. And Michael, and Raphael, and Gabriel, and Phanuel, And the holy angels who are above the heavens, Go in and out of that house. (71:8).
And they came forth from that house, And Michael and Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel, And many holy angels without number. (71:9).
And with them the Head of Days, His head white and pure as wool, And His raiment indescribable. (71:10).
And I fell on my face, And my whole body became relaxed, And my spirit was transfigured; And I cried with a loud voice, . . .with the spirit of power, And blessed and glorified and extolled. (71:11).
And these blessings which went forth out of my mouth were well pleasing before that Head of Days. (71:12).

And that Head of Days came with Michael and Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel, thousands and ten thousands of angels without number. Lost passage in which the Son of Man was described as accompanying the Head of Days, and Enoch asked one of the angels (as in 46 3 ) concerning the Son of Man as to who he was. (71:13).

And he ( i.e. the angel) came to me and greeted me with His voice, and said to me: ' This is the Son of Man who is born to righteousness; And righteousness abides over him, And the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes him not.' (71:14).

And he said to me: 'He proclaims to you peace in the name of the world to come; For from from here has proceeded peace since the creation of the world, And so shall it be to you for ever and for ever and ever. (71:15).

And all shall walk in his ways since righteousness never forsaketh him : With him will be their dwelling-places, and with him their heritage, And they shall not be separated from him for ever and ever and ever. (71:16).
And so there shall be length of days with that Son of Man, And the righteous shall have peace and an upright way In the name of the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever.' (71:17).
crossRefs: Daniel 7:9: The Ancient of Days takes his seat, the hair of his head like the pure wool, his throne like the fiery flame and his wheels as burning fire.
Ezekiel 1:22-28: Over the heads of the living creatures is a firmament like the colour of the terrible crystal, and above it a throne with the appearance of fire round about.
Genesis 5:24: Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him.
Hebrews 11:5: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death, and had this testimony, that he pleased God.
Exodus 24:10: They saw the God of Israel, and under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness.

translationNotes.note: 71:5 describes a structure built of crystals with tongues of living fire between them. Ezekiel 1:22 puts a firmament like the colour of the terrible crystal over the heads of the living creatures, and Exodus 24:10 has under God's feet a paved work of sapphire stone as clear as the body of heaven. The same house is described at length earlier in this book, at 14:9-18, walls of crystal surrounded by tongues of fire.

Hyacinth here names a colour, a deep blue running to violet, not a flower. It is a stone name in older English Bibles, printed as jacinth for the breastplates at Revelation 9:17 and for the eleventh foundation of the city wall at Revelation 21:20. 71:2 says the light of the two streams of fire shone like hyacinth.

The three names mean the burning ones, the cherubim, and the wheels. Isaiah 6:2-3 gives the seraphim six wings each and the threefold Holy, Genesis 3:24 sets cherubim at the east of Eden with a flaming sword, and Ezekiel 1:15-21 describes the wheels that move with the living creatures. 71:7 says these are they who sleep not and who guard the throne of his glory.

translationNotes.term: The girdle which girt that house of fire
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵזוֹר (ezor, a belt or girdle)
translationNotes.note: A girdle was the wide band wound round the waist to hold a loose robe in, so a building called girt is one bound about on every side. 71:6 says streams full of living fire ran on the house's four sides and girt it. 14:12 describes the same thing earlier, a flaming fire surrounding the walls with portals that blazed.

translationNotes.original: Greek: μεταμορφόω (metamorphoo, to be changed in form)
translationNotes.note: 71:11 says Enoch fell on his face, his whole body became relaxed, and his spirit was transfigured, after which he cried out with the spirit of power and blessed and glorified. Collapse before a heavenly figure followed by strength given to speak is the same sequence at Daniel 10:8-19 and at Revelation 1:17.

The sentence in 71:13 that begins Lost passage is not part of the book. It is the editor's note marking a place where he judged that words describing the Son of Man accompanying the Head of Days had dropped out, and it points back to the question Enoch asks at 46:3. The verse itself ends with the angels without number.

translationNotes.term: This is the Son of Man who is born to righteousness
translationNotes.note: 71:14 is the last thing said to Enoch in these chapters, and the book closes the section four verses later with peace and length of days in the name of the Lord of Spirits. The title Son of Man has been in use since 46:2, and Daniel 7:13 is where Scripture uses it of the figure who comes with the clouds. The greeting is given here without explanation.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch's spirit is taken into the heaven of heavens, where he sees a house of crystals with tongues of living fire and streams of fire around it. The Head of Days comes out with Michael, Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel, and an angel greets Enoch: This is the Son of Man who is born to righteousness.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 72
summaryBullets: The book of the courses of the luminaries of the heaven, the relations of each, according to their classes, their dominion and their seasons, according to their names and places of origin, and according to their months, which Uriel, the holy angel, who was with me, who is their guide, showed me; and he showed me all their laws exactly as they are, and how it is with regard to all the years of the world and to eternity, till the new creation is accomplished which dureth till eternity. (72:1).
And this is the first law of the luminaries: the luminary the Sun has its rising in the eastern portals of the heaven, and its setting in the western portals of the heaven. (72:2).

And I saw six portals in which the sun rises, and six portals in which the sun sets and the moon rises and sets in these portals, and the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead: six in the east and six in the west, and all following each other in accurately corresponding order: also many windows to the right and left of these portals. (72:3).
And first there goes forth the great luminary, named the Sun, and his circumference is like the circumference of the heaven, and he is quite filled with illuminating and heating fire. (72:4).

The chariot on which he ascends, the wind drives, and the sun goes down from the heaven and returns through the north in order to reach the east, and is so guided that he comes to the appropriate (lit. 'that') portal and shines in the face of the heaven. (72:5).
In this way he rises in the first month in the great portal, which is the fourth those six portals in the cast . (72:6).
And in that fourth portal from which the sun rises in the first month are twelve window-openings, from which proceed a flame when they are opened in their season. (72:7).
When the sun rises in the heaven, he comes forth through that fourth portal thirty mornings in succession, and sets accurately in the fourth portal in the west of the heaven. (72:8).
And during this period the day becomes daily longer and the night nightly shorter to the thirtieth morning. (72:9).
On that day the day is longer than the night by a ninth part, and the day amounts exactly to ten parts and the night to eight parts. (72:10).
And the sun rises from that fourth portal, and sets in the fourth and returns to the fifth portal of the east thirty mornings, and rises from it and sets in the fifth portal. (72:11).
And then the day becomes longer by †two† parts and amounts to eleven parts, and the night becomes shorter and amounts to seven parts. (72:12).
And it returns to the east and enters into the sixth portal, and rises and sets in the sixth portal one-and-thirty mornings on account of its sign. (72:13).
On that day the day becomes longer than the night, and the day becomes double the night, and the day becomes twelve parts, and the night is shortened and becomes six parts. (72:14).
And the sun mounts up to make the day shorter and the night longer, and the sun returns to the east and enters into the sixth portal, and rises from it and sets thirty mornings. (72:15).
And when thirty mornings are accomplished, the day decreases by exactly one part, and becomes eleven parts, and the night seven. (72:16).
And the sun goes forth from that sixth portal in the west, and goes to the east and rises in the fifth portal for thirty mornings, and sets in the west again in the fifth western portal. (72:17).
On that day the day decreases by †two† parts, and amounts to ten parts and the night to eight parts. (72:18).

And the sun goes forth from that fifth portal and sets in the fifth portal of the west, and rises in the fourth portal for one-and-thirty mornings on account of its sign, and sets in the west. (72:19).
On that day the day is equalized with the night, and becomes of equal length , and the night amounts to nine parts and the day to nine parts. (72:20).
And the sun rises from that portal and sets in the west, and returns to the east and rises thirty mornings in the third portal and sets in the west in the third portal. (72:21).

And on that day the night becomes longer than the day, and night becomes longer than night, and day shorter than day till the thirtieth morning, and the night amounts exactly to ten parts and the day to eight parts. (72:22).

And the sun rises from that third portal and sets in the third portal in the west and returns to the east, and for thirty mornings rises in the second portal in the east, and in like manner sets in the second portal in the west of the heaven. (72:23).
And on that day the night amounts to eleven parts and the day to seven parts. (72:24).

And the sun rises on that day from that second portal and sets in the west in the second portal, and returns to the east into the first portal for one-and-thirty mornings, and sets in the first portal in the west of the heaven. (72:25).
And on that day the night becomes longer and amounts to the double of the day: and the night amounts exactly to twelve parts and the day to six. (72:26).

And the sun has (therewith) traversed the divisions of his orbit and turns again on those divisions of his orbit, and enters that portal thirty mornings and sets also in the west opposite to it. (72:27).
And on that night has the night decreased in length by a †ninth† part, and the night has become eleven parts and the day seven parts. (72:28).
And the sun has returned and entered into the second portal in the east, and returns on those his divisions of his orbit for thirty mornings, rising and setting. (72:29).
And on that day the night decreases in length, and the night amounts to ten parts and the day to eight. (72:30).
And on that day the sun rises from that portal, and sets in the west, and returns to the east, and rises in the third portal for one-and-thirty mornings, and sets in the west of the heaven. (72:31).
On that day the night decreases and amounts to nine parts, and the day to nine parts, and the night is equal to the day and the year is exactly as to its days three hundred and sixty-four. (72:32).
And the length of the day and of the night, and the shortness of the day and of the night arise--through the course of the sun these distinctions are made (lit. 'they are separated'). (72:33).
So it comes that its course becomes daily longer, and its course nightly shorter. (72:34).
And this is the law and the course of the sun, and his return as often as he returns sixty times and rises, i.e. the great luminary which is named the sun, for ever and ever. (72:35).
And that which (thus) rises is the great luminary, and is so named according to its appearance, according as the Lord commanded. (72:36).
As he rises, so he sets and decreases not, and rests not, but runs day and night, and his light is sevenfold brighter than that of the moon; but as regards size they are both equal. (72:37).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:14-18: God sets the lights in the expanse to divide day from night and to mark signs, seasons, days and years, which is the office this chapter watches the sun perform.
Psalm 19:4-6: A tent is set for the sun in the heavens and it runs its circuit from one end of them to the other, the daily course this chapter measures portal by portal.
Psalm 74:16-17: The day and the night both belong to God, who set the boundaries of the earth and made summer and winter, the turning points this chapter counts out in mornings.
Ecclesiastes 1:5: The sun rises and goes down and hurries back to the place where it rises, the same closed circuit the portals describe.
Jubilees 6:32-38: Another book on this shelf fixes the year at three hundred and sixty-four days and warns that a reckoning left short moves the appointed times out of their season.

translationNotes.original: Aramaic: תְּרַע (teraʿ), gate - Hebrew: שַׁעַר (shaʿar), gate
translationNotes.note: Not doors in a building. They are the points on the horizon where the sun comes up, six in the east and six matching them in the west. The sun rises through one of them for a month at a time, works outward to the sixth at the longest day, back to the first at the shortest, and returns, so the twelve portals are a map of where sunrise moves across a year.

The chapter never counts hours. It divides the whole day and night into eighteen parts, so one part is one hour and twenty minutes by our clock. The figures run 10 and 8, then 11 and 7, then 12 and 6 at the longest day (72:14), back through 9 and 9 at the equinox (72:20), down to 6 and 12 at the shortest (72:26), and back to 9 and 9 (72:32). Light and dark always total eighteen.

The number at 72:32 is built out of the mornings the chapter has just counted.
