Eight of the sun's monthly stations run thirty mornings and four run thirty-one, at 72:13, 72:19, 72:25 and 72:31, which are the turning points of the year. Eight thirties and four thirty-ones make 364, and 364 divides by seven exactly, giving fifty-two whole weeks with nothing left over.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אוּרִיאֵל (ʾUriʾel), God is my light
translationNotes.note: The angel who guides Enoch through the whole astronomical section and is said to lead the luminaries. The name is ordinary Hebrew, built from a word for flame or light and the word for God, and it belongs to two men in the record as well, a Levite and the father of Micaiah. As an angel's name it stands outside Scripture, and 2 Esdras 4:1 gives it to the angel who answers Ezra.

The book pictures the sun carried across the sky in a chariot pushed by the wind (72:5). That picture was not harmless in the ancient world. Kings of Judah had dedicated horses and a chariot to the sun and stationed them at the entrance of the temple, and Josiah removed the horses and burned the chariot, as 2 Kings 23:11 records.

Small cross-shaped marks appear around a few words here and later, as at 72:12 and 72:28. They are the translator's printed warning that the manuscripts disagree or that the wording is damaged at that point, so the reading inside them is uncertain. They are not part of what the book says.

stories.keyTakeaway: Uriel shows Enoch the sun's course through six portals in the east and six in the west, month by month, with day and night divided into eighteen parts running from twelve and six at the longest day to nine and nine at the equinox, and the year closing at three hundred and sixty-four days.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 73
summaryBullets: And after this law I saw another law dealing with the smaller luminary, which is named the Moon. (73:1).
And her circumference is like the circumference of the heaven, and her chariot in which she rides is driven by the wind, and light is given to her in (definite) measure. (73:2).
And her rising and setting change every month: and her days are like the days of the sun, and when her light is uniform ( i.e. full) it amounts to the seventh part of the light of the sun. (73:3).

And thus she rises. And her first phase in the east comes forth on the thirtieth morning: and on that day she becomes visible, and constitutes for you the first phase of the moon on the thirtieth day together with the sun in the portal where the sun rises. (73:4).

And the one half of her goes forth by a seventh part, and her whole circumference is empty, without light, with the exception of one-seventh part of it, (and) the fourteenth part of her light. (73:5).
And when she receives one-seventh part of the half of her light, her light amounts to one-seventh part and the half thereof. (73:6).

And she sets with the sun, and when the sun rises the moon rises with him and receives the half of one part of light, and in that night in the beginning of her morning in the commencement of the lunar day the moon sets with the sun, and is invisible that night with the fourteen parts and the half of one of them. (73:7).
And she rises on that day with exactly a seventh part, and comes forth and recedes from the rising of the sun, and in her remaining days she becomes bright in the (remaining) thirteen parts. (73:8).
crossRefs: Genesis 1:16: God makes the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night, the ranking this chapter assumes when it calls the moon the smaller luminary.
Psalm 81:3: The trumpet is blown at the new moon and at the full moon, so the two points this chapter describes are the ones Israel was told to mark.
Isaiah 30:26: The moon's light is promised to become like the sun's and the sun's to become sevenfold, a comparison of the two lights by ratio like the sevenfold reckoning here.
Jeremiah 31:35: The sun is given for light by day and the fixed order of the moon and the stars for light by night, the settled arrangement this chapter is describing.
Sirach 43:6-8: The moon is said to mark the seasons, to give the month its name, and to change wonderfully as she waxes, the same monthly change tracked here.

translationNotes.term: Light is given to her in measure
translationNotes.note: The chapter does not treat the moon as a source of light. Light is given to her, transferred to her, and taken away again (73:2, 73:7), and it is reckoned out in fixed portions. That is why the book can put a number on her brightness at all, calling her full light one seventh of the sun's.

This is the first sliver of the new moon. The book has her appear on the thirtieth day of the previous month, together with the sun and in the same portal, which means she is close enough to the sun in the sky to be lost in its glare for a day or two before and after. That narrow window is what the chapter is counting.

The book measures the lit face of the moon in fourteenths and half-fourteenths rather than describing a shape. One fourteenth is added each day as she waxes and one is taken away as she wanes. The half of a seventh mentioned at 73:5 and 73:7 is the same scale carried one step finer.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יָרֵחַ (yareach), moon - חֹדֶשׁ (chodesh), new moon, month
translationNotes.note: In Hebrew the month is named from the moon. Chodesh comes from the verb to be new, and it means both the new moon itself and the month it begins. A reader who knows that hears why a chapter on the moon's phases is also a chapter on the calendar.

The book says twice that the moon's circumference is like the circumference of the heaven and that the sun's is the same (72:4, 73:2). It is describing the two discs as equal in apparent size and different only in the light given them, which is the point it returns to when it ranks the sun's light as seven times the moon's.

stories.keyTakeaway: A second law governs the moon. Her light is given in measure and comes to a seventh of the sun's when she is full, her rising and setting shift every month, and her first thin phase appears on the thirtieth morning in the portal where the sun rises.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 74
summaryBullets: And I saw another course, a law for her, (and) how according to that law she performs her monthly revolution. (74:1).

And all these Uriel, the holy angel who is the leader of them all, showed to me, and their positions, and I wrote down their positions as he showed them to me, and I wrote down their months as they were, and the appearance of their lights till fifteen days were accomplished. (74:2).
In single seventh parts she accomplishes all her light in the east, and in single seventh parts accomplishes all her darkness in the west. (74:3).
And in certain months she alters her settings, and in certain months she pursues her own peculiar course. (74:4).
In two months the moon sets with the sun: in those two middle portals the third and the fourth. (74:5).

She goes forth for seven days, and turns about and returns again through the portal where the sun rises, and accomplishes all her light: and she recedes from the sun, and in eight days enters the sixth portal from which the sun goes forth. (74:6).

And when the sun goes forth from the fourth portal she goes forth seven days, until she goes forth from the fifth and turns back again in seven days into the fourth portal and accomplishes all her light: and she recedes and enters into the first portal in eight days. (74:7).
And she returns again in seven days into the fourth portal from which the sun goes forth. (74:8).
Thus I saw their position--how the moons rose and the sun set in those days. (74:9).
And if five years are added together the sun has an overplus of thirty days, and all the days which accrue to it for one of those five years, when they are full, amount to 364 days. (74:10).
And the overplus of the sun and of the stars amounts to six days: in 5 years 6 days every year come to 30 days: and the moon falls behind the sun and stars to the number of 30 days. (74:11).

And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day to eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days. (74:12).
In 3 years there are 1092 days, and in 5 years 1820 days, so that in 8 years there are 2912 days. (74:13).
For the moon alone the days amount in 3 years to 1062 days, and in 5 years she falls 50 days behind: i.e. to the sum (of 1770) there is to be added (1000 and) 62 days. (74:14).
And in 5 years there are 1770 days, so that for the moon the days in 8 years amount to 2832 days. (74:15).
For in 8 years she falls behind to the amount of 80 days , all the days she falls behind in 8 years are (74:16).
And the year is accurately completed in conformity with their world-stations and the stations of the sun, which rise from the portals through which it (the sun) rises and sets 30 days. (74:17).
crossRefs: Exodus 12:2: This month is made the beginning of months and the first month of the year, which is the unit the moon's circuit in this chapter measures out.
Numbers 28:11-15: A burnt offering with bulls, a ram and lambs is appointed at the beginning of every month, so the moon's return carried a fixed obligation with it.
Job 38:33: God asks whether a man knows the ordinances of the heavens or can establish their rule on the earth, the exact knowledge this chapter says Uriel handed over.
Psalm 104:19: The moon is made for the appointed times and the sun knows its going down, the two clocks whose counts this chapter sets side by side.
Jubilees 6:36-38: Another book on this shelf describes a year followed by the moon running short of the sun's and dragging the appointed seasons out of place.

translationNotes.note: Every figure in the chapter comes from two numbers. The solar count is 364: three years is 1092, five years is 1820, eight years is 2912, exactly as 74:13 gives them. The lunar count is 354: three years is 1062 and five years is 1770 and eight years is 2832, exactly as 74:14 and 74:15 give them. The gap is ten days a year, which is why 74:14 says fifty days in five years and 74:16 says eighty in eight.

An old English word this translation uses for a surplus or excess, the amount by which one count runs past another. When the chapter says the sun has an overplus of thirty days in five years, it means the solar reckoning has run thirty days further than the reckoning it is compared with over that span.

The moon is not described as moving more slowly. Her twelve months add up to fewer days than the sun's year, so after one year her count stands ten days short of his, after three years thirty, after five fifty and after eight eighty. The chapter is stating a difference between two totals of days, not a defect in the moon.

Enoch is shown as a working recorder rather than a listener. He is given positions, months and the appearance of the lights, and he writes each of them down as they are shown (74:2). The whole astronomical section is presented in this book as a copied set of observations handed on.

The translation's term for the fixed places in the heavens at which the luminaries stand, turn, or begin a new stretch of their course. The chapter ties the accuracy of the year to them: the sun rises and sets thirty days at a station before moving on, so counting the stations is the same work as counting the year.

stories.keyTakeaway: Uriel shows the moon's monthly circuit through the portals and Enoch writes the figures down: the sun and the stars complete 364 days a year, 1092 days in three years and 2912 in eight, while the moon falls fifty days behind in five years and eighty in eight.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 75
summaryBullets: And the leaders of the heads of the thousands, who are placed over the whole creation and over all the stars, have also to do with the four intercalary days, being inseparable from their office, according to the reckoning of the year, and these render service on the four days which are not reckoned in the reckoning of the year. (75:1).

And owing to them men go wrong therein, for those luminaries truly render service on the world-stations, one in the first portal, one in the third portal of the heaven, one in the fourth portal, and one in the sixth portal, and the exactness of the year is accomplished through its separate three hundred and sixty-four stations. (75:2).

For the signs and the times and the years and the days the angel Uriel showed to me, whom the Lord of glory has set for ever over all the luminaries of the heaven, in the heaven and in the world, that they should rule on the face of the heaven and be seen on the earth, and be leaders for the day and the night, i.e. the sun, moon, and stars, and all the ministering creatures which make their revolution in all the chariots of the heaven. (75:3).

In like manner twelve doors Uriel showed me, open in the circumference of the sun's chariot in the heaven, through which the rays of the sun break forth: and from them is warmth diffused over the earth, when they are opened at their appointed seasons. (75:4).
And for the winds and the spirit of the dew† when they are opened, standing open in the heavens at the ends. (75:5).
As for the twelve portals in the heaven, at the ends of the earth, out of which go forth the sun, moon, and stars, and all the works of heaven in the east and in the west. (75:6).

There are many windows open to the left and right of them, and one window at its (appointed) season produces warmth, corresponding (as these do) to those doors from which the stars come forth according as He has commanded them, and in which they set corresponding to their number. (75:7).
And I saw chariots in the heaven, running in the world, above those portals in which revolve the stars that never set. (75:8).
And one is larger than all the rest, and it is that that makes its course through the entire world. (75:9).
crossRefs: Exodus 18:21: Moses appoints able men as chiefs over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, the ranked command language this chapter borrows for the heavenly bodies.
Job 38:31-33: God asks whether Job can bind the Pleiades, loose the belt of Orion, lead out the Bear with her children, or know the ordinances of the heavens.
Psalm 147:4: God fixes the number of the stars and calls each one by name, the same picture of a counted and named host that stands behind the leaders here.
Nehemiah 9:6: Heaven and the heaven of heavens with all their host are named as made things that worship their maker, not as powers in their own right.
Genesis 1:16-18: The two great lights are set to govern day and night and to separate light from darkness, the rule this chapter parcels out among appointed leaders.

translationNotes.note: To intercalate is to insert a day into a calendar that the ordinary months do not account for. Here four such days stand outside twelve months of thirty, one at each turning of the year, and twelve thirties plus four is 364. They are the same four the sun's own course produced, since the thirty-first mornings at 72:13, 72:19, 72:25 and 72:31 fall in the sixth, fourth, first and third portals, which is exactly the list 75:2 gives.

translationNotes.term: Leaders of the heads of the thousands
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׂר־אֶלֶף (sar-eleph), commander of a thousand
translationNotes.note: The book ranks the heavenly bodies the way an army was ranked, in thousands under officers, the arrangement Moses used when he appointed judges. The four named here are the ones assigned to the days that fall outside the months, and the text calls that assignment inseparable from their office.

translationNotes.term: Doors of the chariot and portals of the earth
translationNotes.note: The chapter uses two different sets of twelve and a reader runs them together. The twelve doors at 75:4 are openings in the sun's own chariot through which its rays and heat break out. The twelve portals at 75:6 are the gates at the ends of the earth through which the sun, moon and stars come and go. One travels with the sun; the other stands still on the horizon.

Stars near the celestial pole never dip below the horizon. They wheel around the pole all night and are visible in every season, unlike the stars that rise in the east and set in the west. The chapter puts chariots above the portals precisely where those stars turn, marking them off from the ones that use the gates.

The complaint at 75:1-2 is about arithmetic, not about morals. Four days do duty in the year without being counted among the months, so anyone who reckons only the months is four days short and his year drifts. The book returns to the same charge at 1 Enoch 82:4-6.

stories.keyTakeaway: Four leaders of the thousands serve on the four days that are not counted in the reckoning of the year, standing in the first, third, fourth and sixth portals, and men go wrong over them; above the portals run chariots where the stars that never set revolve.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 76
summaryBullets: And at the ends of the earth I saw twelve portals open to all the quarters of the heaven, from which the winds go forth and blow over the earth. (76:1).
Three of them are open on the face ( i.e. the east) of the heavens, and three in the west, and three on the right ( i.e. the south) of the heaven, and three on the left ( i.e. the north). (76:2).
And the three first are those of the east, and three are of †the north, and three after those on the left of the south†, and three of the west. (76:3).

Through four of these come winds of blessing and prosperity, and from those eight come hurtful winds: when they are sent, they bring destruction on all the earth and on the water upon it, and on all who dwell thereon, and on everything which is in the water and on the land. (76:4).

And the first wind from those portals, called the east wind, comes forth through the first portal which is in the east, inclining towards the south: from it come forth desolation, drought, heat, and destruction. (76:5).

And through the second portal in the middle comes what is fitting, and from it there come rain and fruitfulness and prosperity and dew; and through the third portal which lies toward the north come cold and drought. (76:6).
And after these come forth the south winds through three portals: through the first portal of them inclining to the east comes forth a hot wind. (76:7).
And through the middle portal next to it there come forth fragrant smells, and dew and rain, and prosperity and health. (76:8).
And through the third portal lying to the west come forth dew and rain, locusts and desolation. (76:9).
And after these the north winds: from the seventh portal in the east come dew and rain, locusts and desolation. (76:10).

And from the middle portal come in a direct direction health and rain and dew and prosperity; and through the third portal in the west come cloud and hoar-frost, and snow and rain, and dew and locusts. (76:11).

And after these four are the west winds: through the first portal adjoining the north come forth dew and hoar-frost, and cold and snow and frost. And from the middle portal come forth dew and rain, and prosperity and blessing; and through the last portal which adjoins the south come forth drought and desolation, and burning and destruction. (76:12).

And from the middle portal come forth dew and rain, and prosperity and blessing; and through the last portal which adjoins the south come forth drought and desolation, and burning and destruction. (76:13).
And the twelve portals of the four quarters of the heaven are therewith completed, and all their laws and all their plagues and all their benefactions have I shown to you, my son Methuselah. (76:14).
crossRefs: Psalm 135:7: God is said to bring the wind out of his storehouses and to raise the clouds from the ends of the earth, the same picture of wind kept in a place and released.
Jeremiah 49:36: The four winds are brought against Elam from the four quarters of heaven and scatter its people everywhere, a judgement built out of the same four-quarter map.
Zechariah 6:5: Four chariots are identified as the four winds of heaven going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth.

Exodus 10:13-19: An east wind blowing a whole day and night carries the locusts into Egypt and a west wind lifts them out again, the exact pairing of wind and locust this chapter assigns to particular portals.
Jonah 4:8: A scorching east wind rises with the sun and beats on Jonah's head until he faints, which is what the desolation and heat from the eastern portal means on the ground.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קֶדֶם (qedem), east or front - יָם (yam), sea or west - תֵּימָן (teman), right or south - שְׂמֹאל (semol), left or north
translationNotes.note: The verse that calls the south the right of the heaven and the north the left is not being poetic. Hebrew direction words assume a man facing the sunrise: east is in front, west is the sea behind him, south is on his right and north on his left. Genesis 14:15 locates Hobah by saying it is on the left of Damascus, which means north of it.

In the land of Israel the east wind comes off the desert. It arrives hot, dry and full of dust, and it can shrivel a standing crop within a day, which is why Pharaoh's dream has the ears of grain blighted by it at Genesis 41:6. That is the whole content of the desolation, drought and heat this chapter assigns to the first eastern portal.

The chapter lists dew alongside rain as a blessing because in that climate it is one. No rain falls from about May to October, and heavy night dew off the sea is what carries vines, melons and summer crops through the dry months. Withheld dew is a curse in the same register as withheld rain.

The desert locust swarms in the millions, rides the prevailing wind, and eats roughly its own body weight in green matter every day. A swarm arrives with a wind and leaves with a wind, which is exactly why this chapter files locusts under the wind portals rather than under weather.

An older English word for the white frost that forms on clear cold nights, hoar meaning white with age. Scripture uses it as a size and colour comparison for the manna lying on the ground, and it is the frost this chapter sends out of the northern and western portals.

stories.keyTakeaway: Twelve portals stand at the ends of the earth, three on each of the four quarters, and the winds blow out of them; four bring rain, dew and prosperity, and the other eight bring drought, heat, locusts, frost and destruction on land and water alike.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 77
summaryBullets: And the first quarter is called the east, because it is the first: and the second, the south, because the Most High will descend there, yea, there in quite a special sense will He who is blessed for ever descend . (77:1).
And the west quarter is named the diminished, because there all the luminaries of the heaven wane and go down. (77:2).

And the fourth quarter , named the north, is divided into three parts: the first of them is for the dwelling of men: and the second contains seas of water, and the abysses and forests and rivers, and darkness and clouds; and the third part contains the garden of righteousness. (77:3).
I saw seven high mountains, higher than all the mountains which are on the earth: and from there comes forth hoar-frost, and days, seasons, and years pass away. (77:4).
I saw seven rivers on the earth larger than all the rivers: one of them coming from the west pours its waters into the Great Sea. (77:5).
And these two come from the north to the sea and pour their waters into the Erythraean Sea in the east. (77:6).

And the remaining four come forth on the side of the north to their own sea, two of them to the Erythraean Sea, and two into the Great Sea and discharge themselves there and some say: into the desert . (77:7).
Seven great islands I saw in the sea and in the mainland: two in the mainland and five in the Great Sea. (77:8).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 33:2: The Lord comes from Sinai, dawns from Seir and shines out from Mount Paran, all of them southern places, which is the ground of this chapter's claim about the southern quarter.
Habakkuk 3:3: God is said to come from Teman and the Holy One from Mount Paran, naming the same southern approach that this chapter gives as the reason for the south's name.
Genesis 2:8-14: A garden is planted in the east and a river goes out of it and parts into four named heads, the pattern of a garden set in a quarter with counted rivers.
Numbers 34:6: The western boundary of the land is the Great Sea and its coast, which fixes what the Great Sea in this chapter is.
Joshua 1:4: The territory is measured out to the Great Sea toward the going down of the sun, the standard Hebrew way of saying west that stands behind calling the west the diminished.

translationNotes.note: In this translation a quarter is one of the four sides of the horizon, not a fourth part of a town. The chapter is naming the compass points and giving a reason for each name, so east, south, west and north are the four quarters throughout.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל (hayyam haggadol), the Great Sea
translationNotes.note: The Mediterranean. It is the standing Hebrew name for it, and it is fixed as the western boundary of the land in the survey at Numbers 34:6. When this chapter pours rivers into the Great Sea and sets five islands in it, that is the sea it means.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Ἐρυθρὰ Θάλασσα (Erythra Thalassa), Red Sea
translationNotes.note: Erythros is simply Greek for red, so the name means the Red Sea. Ancient geographers used it far more widely than we do, covering the northwestern Indian Ocean and the Persian Gulf as well as the arm of water beside Egypt, which is why this chapter can run rivers from the north into it in the east.

The west is named from what happens there: every luminary loses its light and goes down in that quarter. Hebrew names the same direction from the sea that lies to the west, and its ordinary phrase for the west is the going down of the sun, which is the sense this name reproduces.

The book's own name for the garden it has already described, the place Enoch reaches at 1 Enoch 32:3 where the tree of knowledge stands and its fruit gives great wisdom. This chapter files the garden as one of the three parts of the northern quarter, alongside the dwelling of men and the waters.

translationNotes.term: Seven mountains, seven rivers, seven islands
translationNotes.note: The chapter counts all three sets in sevens and names none of them. Seven is the standard number of completeness in Hebrew usage, so the count is doing the work of saying the survey is finished rather than pointing at seven particular peaks. The only named water in the whole list is the Great Sea and the Erythraean Sea.

stories.keyTakeaway: The four quarters are named for what they are: the east is first, the south is where the Most High descends, the west is the diminished because the lights wane there, and the north holds men, waters and the garden of righteousness; seven mountains, seven rivers and seven islands are counted.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 78
summaryBullets: And the names of the sun are the following: the first Orjârês, and the second Tômâs. (78:1).
And the moon has four names: the first name is Asônjâ, the second Eblâ, the third Benâsê, and the fourth Erâe. (78:2).
These are the two great luminaries: their circumference is like the circumference of the heaven, and the size of the circumference of both is alike. (78:3).

In the circumference of the sun there are seven portions of light which are added to it more than to the moon, and in definite measures it is s transferred till the seventh portion of the sun is exhausted. (78:4).
And they set and enter the portals of the west, and make their revolution by the north, and come forth through the eastern portals on the face of the heaven. (78:5).
And when the moon rises one-fourteenth part appears in the heaven: the light becomes full in her : on the fourteenth day she accomplishes her light. (78:6).

And fifteen parts of light are transferred to her till the fifteenth day (when) her light is accomplished, according to the sign of the year, and she becomes fifteen parts, and the moon grows by (the addition of) fourteenth parts. (78:7).

And in her waning (the moon) decreases on the first day to fourteen parts of her light, on the second to thirteen parts of light, on the third to twelve, on the fourth to eleven, on the fifth to ten, on the sixth to nine, on the seventh to eight, on the eighth to seven, on the ninth to six, on the tenth to five, on the eleventh to four, on the twelfth to three, on the thirteenth to two, on the fourteenth to the half of a seventh, and all her remaining light disappears wholly on the fifteenth. (78:8).
And in certain months the month has twenty-nine days and once twenty-eight. (78:9).
And Uriel showed me another law: when light is transferred to the moon, and on which side it is transferred to her by the sun. (78:10).

During all the period during which the moon is growing in her light, she is transferring it to herself when opposite to the sun during fourteen days her light is accomplished in the heaven , and when she is illumined throughout, her light is accomplished full in the heaven. (78:11).
And on the first day she is called the new moon, for on that day the light rises upon her. (78:12).

She becomes full moon exactly on the day when the sun sets in the west, and from the east she rises at night, and the moon shines the whole night through till the sun rises over against her and the moon is seen over against the sun. (78:13).

On the side from where the light of the moon comes forth, there again she wanes till all the light vanishes and all the days of the month are at an end, and her circumference is empty, void of light. (78:14).

And three months she makes of thirty days, and at her time she makes three months of twenty-nine days each, in which she accomplishes her waning in the first period of time, and in the first portal for one hundred and seventy-seven days. (78:15).
And in the time of her going out she appears for three months (of) thirty days each, and for three months she appears (of) twenty-nine each. (78:16).
At night she appears like a man for twenty days each time, and by day she appears like the heaven, and there is nothing else in her save her light. (78:17).
crossRefs: Numbers 10:10: Trumpets are blown over the offerings at the appointed feasts and at the beginnings of the months, so the first sighting of the moon set a public signal going.
1 Samuel 20:5: David expects to sit at the king's table because tomorrow is the new moon, showing the day as a fixed appointment in ordinary court life.
2 Kings 4:23: A husband asks why his wife would go to the prophet when it is neither new moon nor sabbath, which shows the new moon as a regular day for going up.
Isaiah 66:23: Worship is described as coming from new moon to new moon and from sabbath to sabbath, using the moon's return as the unit of time.
Psalm 89:37: The moon is called a faithful witness in the skies because it keeps coming back, the reliability this chapter spells out day by day.

translationNotes.term: The names of the sun and the moon
translationNotes.original: Ethiopic: Orjârê and Tômâs (sun); Asônjâ, Eblâ, Benâsê and Erâe (moon)
translationNotes.note: The book survives complete only in Ethiopic, and these names are printed as they are transliterated from it, with the accents marking vowel length. The text gives two names for the sun and four for the moon and does not explain any of them; nothing in the surviving book says what they mean.

The chapter defines it plainly at 78:12: she is called the new moon on the first day, because on that day light rises on her. What that describes is the thin crescent that becomes visible again after the moon has been lost in the sun's glare, not the invisible dark moon.

The mechanism at 78:13 is exact. The moon is full on the day she rises in the east as the sun sets in the west, she shines the whole night, and she is seen over against the sun. That is what standing opposite the sun means, and it is why a full moon and only a full moon lights a whole night from dusk to dawn.

The figure at 78:15 is the sum of the six months just described: three of thirty days and three of twenty-nine, which is ninety plus eighty-seven. That is half of the moon's year of 354 days in this book, so the number marks the halfway point of her circuit.

translationNotes.term: Months of twenty-nine and thirty days
translationNotes.note: The moon returns to the same phase in about twenty-nine and a half days. A calendar counting whole days cannot hold that, so months of twenty-nine and thirty alternate, which is the pattern this chapter sets out. The remark at 78:9 that a month is once twenty-eight days stands alone, and the surviving text does not explain it.

The phrase at 78:17 is rendered word for word out of the Ethiopic, and what it is describing is not clear from the surviving text. The translator has left it standing rather than smoothing it into something the manuscripts do not support.

stories.keyTakeaway: The sun and the moon are given names, and the moon's light is measured in fourteen parts, one added a day until she is full and one taken away a day until she is empty; her months run thirty days and twenty-nine, and six of them make one hundred and seventy-seven days.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 79
summaryBullets: And now, my son, I have shown you everything, and the law of all the stars of the heaven is completed. (79:1).

And he showed me all the laws of these for every day, and for every season of bearing rule, and for every year, and for its going forth, and for the order prescribed to it every month and every week: (79:2).
And the waning of the moon which takes place in the sixth portal: for in this sixth portal her light is accomplished, and after that there is the beginning of the waning: (79:3).
And the waning which takes place in the first portal in its season, till one hundred and seventy-seven days are accomplished: reckoned according to weeks, twenty-five (weeks) and two days. (79:4).
She falls behind the sun and the order of the stars exactly five days in the course of one period, and when this place which you see has been traversed. (79:5).
Such is the picture and sketch of every luminary which Uriel the archangel, who is their leader, showed to me. (79:6).
crossRefs: Genesis 8:22: Seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night are promised not to cease while the earth remains, the fixed order every count in this section rests on.
Jeremiah 33:20-21: God speaks of his covenant with the day and with the night, that they come at their appointed time, and stakes the promise to David on it holding.
Psalm 148:3-6: Sun, moon and shining stars are called to praise because they were established forever by a decree that will not pass away.
Daniel 10:13: Michael is named as one of the chief princes who comes to help the messenger, the same idea of a ranking angel that stands behind calling Uriel an archangel.
2 Esdras 4:1: The angel sent to answer Ezra is named Uriel, the only place in the books on these shelves where that name is given to an angel.

translationNotes.note: Twenty-five sevens are one hundred and seventy-five, and two more make 177, so 79:4 is restating the same total in weeks. Counting in weeks matters in this book because its year of 364 days is exactly fifty-two weeks, which lets any stretch of it be given as whole weeks plus a remainder.

translationNotes.term: Five days in the course of one period
translationNotes.note: A period here is half the year. Half of the solar 364 is 182, the moon's half-circuit in this book is 177, and the difference is five. Twice five is ten, which is the ten days a year that produce the thirty, fifty and eighty day gaps counted out at 74:14 and 74:16. The chapter's figures hold together.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שָׁבוּעַ (shavua), a seven, a week
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew word for a week is simply the word for a seven, which is why the same term can carry a group of seven days or a group of seven years. This book uses the week as a working unit of measurement and later builds its whole survey of history out of weeks.

The word joins a prefix meaning chief or ruling to the ordinary word for messenger, which is the same word translated angel. It appears twice in the New Testament, at Jude 1:9 and in Paul's description of the Lord's descent, and in both places it is Michael or an unnamed voice. This book applies the office to Uriel over the luminaries.

The shrinking of the lit face after the full moon. The chapter puts the moment her light is complete in the sixth portal and traces the decrease from there down to the first portal, so the phase and the position on the horizon are being tracked as one thing.

stories.keyTakeaway: Uriel completes the law of the stars. The moon's light is full in the sixth portal and wanes down to the first across one hundred and seventy-seven days, which is twenty-five weeks and two days, and in that period she falls exactly five days behind the sun and the stars.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 80
summaryBullets: And in those days the angel Uriel answered and said to me: 'Behold, I have shown you everything, Enoch, and I have revealed everything to you that you should see this sun and this moon, and the leaders of the stars of the heaven and all those who turn them, their tasks and times and departures. LXXX. 2-8. Perversion of Nature and the heavenly Bodies owning to the Sin of Men . (80:1).

And in the days of the sinners the years shall be shortened, And their seed shall be tardy on their lands and fields, And all things on the earth shall alter, And shall not appear in their time: And the rain shall be kept back And the heaven shall withhold (it). (80:2).
And in those times the fruits of the earth shall be backward, And shall not grow in their time, And the fruits of the trees shall be withheld in their time. (80:3).
And the moon shall alter her order, And not appear at her time. (80:4).

And in those days the sun shall be seen and he shall journey in the evening †on the extremity of the great chariot† in the west And shall shine more brightly than accords with the order of light. (80:5).
And many chiefs of the stars shall transgress the order (prescribed). And these shall alter their orbits and tasks, And not appear at the seasons prescribed to them. (80:6).

And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, And the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, And they shall be altered from all their ways , Yea, they shall err and take them to be gods. (80:7).
And evil shall be multiplied upon them, And punishment shall come upon them So as to destroy all.' (80:8).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 11:16-17: If Israel turns aside to serve other gods, the heavens are shut so that there is no rain and the ground yields no fruit, the same sequence of apostasy and withheld rain.
Leviticus 26:19-20: The heavens are made like iron and the earth like bronze, so that strength is spent for nothing and the land does not yield its increase.
Haggai 1:10-11: The heavens withhold their dew and the earth its produce, and a drought is called on the grain, the new wine, the oil and on men and cattle alike.
Deuteronomy 4:19: Israel is warned not to look up at the sun, moon and stars and be drawn away to bow down to them, the exact error this chapter says the sinners fall into.
2 Kings 23:5: Josiah puts down the priests who burned offerings to the sun, the moon, the constellations and all the host of the heavens in the cities of Judah.

translationNotes.note: The next lines say what the phrase means, and it is not that a year loses days. Seed is slow, rain is held back, fruit does not come in its season and the trees hold their crop (80:2-3). The growing year is what shrinks, so a season's work no longer fits inside the time the season allows.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יוֹרֶה (yoreh), early rain - מַלְקוֹשׁ (malqosh), latter rain
translationNotes.note: The farming year in that land turns on two rains, and Deuteronomy 11:14 names them together. The early rain in autumn softens ground baked hard all summer so it can be ploughed and sown; the latter rain in spring fills the grain before harvest. Hold either one back and the seed is tardy and the fruit fails, which is exactly the picture this chapter draws.

translationNotes.term: They shall take them to be gods
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם (tseva hashamayim), the host of heaven
translationNotes.note: Worship of the sun, moon and stars was ordinary practice across the ancient Near East, and it reached inside Judah. Incense was burned to the host of heaven on the housetops, horses and a chariot dedicated to the sun stood at the entrance of the temple, and Josiah had to remove both, as 2 Kings 23:11 records.

The same ranked officers this section has already set over the days and the seasons. The charge at 80:6 is that they leave the orbits and duties assigned to them and stop appearing at the fixed times, so the disorder is described as a failure of command rather than an accident of weather.

The cross-shaped marks at 80:5 are the translator's signal that the manuscripts are damaged or in disagreement at that exact phrase. What the sun is said to do in the evening on the extremity of the great chariot cannot be recovered from the surviving copies.

stories.keyTakeaway: Uriel tells Enoch that in the days of the sinners the order breaks. The years are shortened, the rain is held back and the crops come late, the moon and the chiefs of the stars leave their appointed times, and men take the luminaries for gods and are punished.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 81
summaryBullets: And he said to me: 'Observe, Enoch, these heavenly tablets, And read what is written thereon, And mark every individual fact.' 2 And I observed the heavenly tablets, and read everything which was written (thereon) and understood everything, and read the book of all the deeds of mankind, and of all the children of flesh that shall be upon the earth to the remotest generations. (81:1).

And I observed the heavenly tablets, and read everything which was written thereon and understood everything, and read the book of all the deeds of mankind, and of all the children of flesh that shall be upon the earth to the remotest generations. (81:2).

And forthwith I blessed the great Lord the King of glory for ever, in that He has made all the works of the world, And I extolled the Lord because of His patience, And blessed Him because of the children of men. (81:3).

And after that I said: 'Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness and goodness, Concerning whom there is no book of unrighteousness written, And against whom no day of judgement shall be found.' (81:4).

And those seven holy ones brought me and placed me on the earth before the door of my house, and said to me: 'Declare everything to your son Methuselah, and show to all your children that no flesh is righteous in the sight of the Lord, for He is their Creator. (81:5).

One year we will leave you with your son, till you givest your (last) commands, that you may teach your children and record (it) for them, and testify to all your children; and in the second year they shall take you from their midst. (81:6).
Let your heart be strong, For the good shall announce righteousness to the good; The righteous with the righteous shall rejoice, And shall offer congratulation to one another. (81:7).
But the sinners shall die with the sinners, And the apostate go down with the apostate. (81:8).
And those who practice righteousness shall die on account of the deeds of men, And be taken away on account of the doings of the godless.' (81:9).
And in those days they ceased to speak to me, and I came to my people, blessing the Lord of the world. (81:10).
crossRefs: Genesis 5:24: Enoch walked with God and was not, for God took him, which is the removal this chapter says he is given a year's notice of.
Exodus 32:32-33: Moses asks to be blotted out of the book God has written, and the answer is that whoever sins will be blotted out of it, a written record with names in it that can be struck.
Psalm 143:2: No one living is righteous before God, the same plain statement this chapter puts in Enoch's mouth for Methuselah and his children.
Malachi 3:16: A book of remembrance is written before the Lord for those who feared him and thought on his name, a record kept of what men do.
Daniel 7:10: The court sits in judgement and the books are opened, the setting in which such a record is used.

translationNotes.note: A tablet was a flat writing surface of stone, clay or wax, the medium used for a permanent public text rather than a letter. Scripture's tablets of the testimony are written with the finger of God and given to Moses. This book uses the phrase for a fixed heavenly record that Enoch is told to read and mark, holding both what is decreed and what men have done.

Holy ones is a standing term for angels, and Daniel 4:17 uses this Aramaic form of it beside the watchers. The seven who carry Enoch back to his door are the same seven archangels the book has already named at 1 Enoch 20:1-8.

Enoch's son, born when Enoch was sixty-five and living nine hundred and sixty-nine years, the longest life recorded in Scripture. Whole sections of this book are addressed to him by name, which is why the instruction here is to declare everything to him first.

Flesh in Hebrew usage stands for a man as a creature: mortal, made, dependent. It is not the body as opposed to the soul. All flesh means every living thing, so no flesh is righteous before the Lord is a statement about the whole human race and its maker, and the chapter gives the reason in the same breath, that he is their Creator.

Genesis 5:24 uses this ordinary verb for what happened to Enoch, and it is the same verb used of Elijah when the sons of the prophets say the Lord will take his master from over him. The chapter turns it into a schedule: one year with Methuselah, and in the second year he is taken.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch reads the heavenly tablets and the book of all the deeds of mankind, blesses God for his patience, and is set down at the door of his house by seven holy ones, with one year left to teach Methuselah and write everything for him before he is taken.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 82
summaryBullets: And now, my son Methuselah, all these things I am recounting to you and writing down for you, and I have revealed to you everything, and given you books concerning all these: so preserve, my son Methuselah, the books from your father's hand, and (see) that you deliver them to the generations of the world. (82:1).

I have given Wisdom to you and to your children, And your children that shall be to you , That they may give it to their children for generations, This wisdom (namely) that passeth their thought. (82:2).
And those who understand it shall not sleep, But shall listen with the ear that they may learn this wisdom, And it shall please those that eat thereof better than good food. (82:3).

Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days. (82:4).
Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year : yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately. (82:5).

For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly recorded (thereon) for ever, one in the first portal and one in the third, and one in the fourth and one in the sixth, and the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days. (82:6).

And the account thereof is accurate and the recorded reckoning thereof exact; for the luminaries, and months and festivals, and years and days, has Uriel shown and revealed to me, to whom the Lord of the whole creation of the world has subjected the host of heaven. (82:7).
And he has power over night and day in the heaven to cause the light to give light to men--sun, moon, and stars, and all the powers of the heaven which revolve in their circular chariots. (82:8).
And these are the orders of the stars, which set in their places, and in their seasons and festivals and months. (82:9).

And these are the names of those who lead them, who watch that they enter at their times, in their orders, in their seasons, in their months, in their periods of dominion, and in their positions. (82:10).

Their four leaders who divide the four parts of the year enter first; and after them the twelve leaders of the orders who divide the months; and for the three hundred and sixty (days) there are heads over thousands who divide the days; and for the four intercalary days there are the leaders which sunder the four parts of the year. (82:11).

And these heads over thousands are intercalated between leader and leader, each behind a station, but their leaders make the division. And these are the names of the leaders who divide the four parts of the year which are ordained: Mîlkî’êl, Hel’emmêlêk, and Mêl’êjal, and Nârêl. (82:12).

And the names of those who lead them: Adnâr’êl, and Îjâsûsa’êl, and ’Elômê’êl--these three follow the leaders of the orders, and there is one that follows the three leaders of the orders which follow those leaders of stations that divide the four parts of the year. (82:13).

And the names of those who lead them: Adnâr'êl, and Îjâsûsa'êl, and 'Elômê'êl — these three follow the leaders of the orders, and there is one that follows the three leaders of the orders which follow those leaders of stations that divide the four parts of the year. (82:14).
In the beginning of the year Melkejâl rises first and rules, who is named †Tam’âinî† and sun, and all the days of his dominion whilst he bears rule are ninety-one days. (82:15).

And these are the signs of the days which are to be seen on earth in the days of his dominion: sweat, and heat, and calms; and all the trees bear fruit, and leaves are produced on all the trees, and the harvest of wheat, and the rose-flowers, and all the flowers which come forth in the field, but the trees of the winter season become withered. (82:16).

And these are the names of the leaders which are under them: Berka’êl, Zêlebs’êl, and another who is added a head of a thousand, called Hîlûjâsĕph: and the days of the dominion of this (leader) are at an end. (82:17).
The next leader after him is Hêl’emmêlêk, whom one names the shining sun, and all the days of his light are ninety-one days. (82:18).

And these are the signs of (his) days on the earth: glowing heat and dryness, and the trees ripen their fruits and produce all their fruits ripe and ready, and the sheep pair and become pregnant, and all the fruits of the earth are gathered in, and everything that is in the fields, and the winepress: these things take place in the days of his dominion. (82:19).

These are the names, and the orders, and the leaders of those heads of thousands: Gîdâ’îjal, Kê’êl, and Hê’êl, and the name of the head of a thousand which is added to them, Asfâ’êl’: and the days of his dominion are at an end. (82:20).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 6:6-7: The words are to be kept on the heart and taught diligently to the children, spoken of at home, on the road, lying down and rising, the handing-down this chapter charges Methuselah with.
Psalm 78:5-6: A testimony is established and the fathers are commanded to teach their children so that the next generation and their children after them will know it.
Proverbs 4:1-5: A father tells his sons what his own father taught him and presses them to get wisdom and not forget it, the same chain of instruction across three generations.
Sirach 24:19-21: Wisdom calls people to come and eat of her and says those who eat will hunger for more, the taste image this chapter uses when it says wisdom pleases better than good food.
Job 38:33: God asks whether a man knows the ordinances of the heavens and can set their rule over the earth, the knowledge Enoch here claims to have been given and written down.

translationNotes.term: The four leaders of the quarters
translationNotes.note: Milkiel, Helemmelek, Melejal and Narel are set over the four parts of the year, and each rules ninety-one days. Every one of the names ends in the ordinary Hebrew word for God, the same element that ends Michael, Gabriel, Uriel and Israel. The surviving text describes only the first two reigns before it breaks off.

A quarter of this book's year. Ninety-one is thirteen sevens, so each quarter holds exactly thirteen whole weeks, and four quarters give fifty-two weeks and 364 days. That is why the four leaders can each be given an equal reign with nothing left over.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׂר־אֶלֶף (sar-eleph), commander of a thousand
translationNotes.note: A real military rank in Israel, the officer over a unit of a thousand, used both in the army and in the appointment of judges. The book takes the ranking straight over: three hundred and sixty days are divided among heads of thousands, the twelve leaders divide the months, and four leaders divide the year.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גַּת (gat), winepress - יֶקֶב (yeqev), the vat below it
translationNotes.note: A winepress was cut into bedrock: a shallow basin where grapes were trodden barefoot, with a channel running the juice down into a lower vat. Pressing came at the end of the dry season after the grain was already in, which is why 82:19 files it with ripened fruit and gathered harvest as a mark of that leader's season.

translationNotes.term: The sheep pair and become pregnant
translationNotes.note: Sheep breed as the days shorten, so the ram goes to the ewes at the end of summer. A ewe carries about one hundred and forty-seven days, roughly five months, which drops the lambs in late winter when new grass is coming up. The detail is a season marker, like the ripe fruit and the winepress beside it.

translationNotes.term: Preserve the books and deliver them
translationNotes.note: The charge at 82:1 is about physical copies. Enoch says he has written these things down and given Methuselah books, and the instruction is to keep them from his father's hand and hand them on to the generations of the world. The book presents itself throughout as a copied text with a chain of custody.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch hands his books to Methuselah to pass down the generations and states the reckoning: the sun spends thirty days in each portal, four intercalated days divide the four parts of the year, the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days, and named leaders rule ninety-one days each.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 83
summaryBullets: And now, my son Methuselah, I will show you all my visions which I have seen, recounting them before you. (83:1).

Two visions I saw before I took a wife, and the one was quite unlike the other: the first when I was learning to write: the second before I took your mother, (when) I saw a terrible vision. And regarding them I prayed to the paragraph continues Lord. (83:2).
I had laid me down in the house of my grandfather Mahalalel, (when) I saw in a vision how the heaven collapsed and was borne off and fell to the earth. (83:3).

And when it fell to the earth I saw how the earth was swallowed up in a great abyss, and mountains were suspended on mountains, and hills sank down on hills, and high trees were rent from their stems, and hurled down and sunk in the abyss. (83:4).
And thereupon a word fell into my mouth, and I lifted up (my voice) to cry aloud, and said: 'The earth is destroyed.' (83:5).
And my grandfather Mahalalel waked me as I lay near him, and said to me: 'Why do you cry so, my son, and why do you make such lamentation?' (83:6).

And I recounted to him the whole vision which I had seen, and he said to me: 'A terrible thing have you seen, my son, and of grave moment is your dream-vision as to the secrets of all the sin of the earth: it must sink into the abyss and be destroyed with a great destruction. (83:7).
And now, my son, arise and make petition to the Lord of glory, since you are a believer, that a remnant may remain on the earth, and that He may not destroy the whole earth. (83:8).
My son, from heaven all this will come upon the earth, and upon the earth there will be great destruction. (83:9).
After that I arose and prayed and implored and besought, and wrote down my prayer for the generations of the world, and I will show everything to you, my son Methuselah. (83:10).

And when I had gone forth below and seen the heaven, and the sun rising in the east, and the moon setting in the west, and a few stars, and the whole earth, and everything as †He had known† it in the beginning, then I blessed the Lord of judgement and extolled Him because He had made the sun to go forth from the windows of the east, †and he ascended and rose on the face of the heaven, and set out and kept traversing the path shown to him. (83:11).
crossRefs: Genesis 5:15-18: Mahalalel fathers Jared and Jared fathers Enoch, which is why the man who wakes Enoch in this chapter is his grandfather and not a stranger.
Isaiah 24:18-20: The windows on high are opened, the foundations of the earth shake, the earth is split apart and staggers like a drunkard, the same picture of a world coming undone.
Genesis 7:23: Everything on the face of the ground is blotted out and only Noah is left, with those who were with him, which is what praying for a remnant asks for.
Genesis 18:23-32: Abraham stands before the Lord and pleads for a city to be spared for the sake of the righteous inside it, the same work Mahalalel puts Enoch to here.
Amos 7:2-6: Amos sees a coming destruction, asks how Jacob can stand because he is so small, and the Lord relents from what he had shown.

translationNotes.note: Enoch's grandfather. The line in Genesis 5 runs Adam, Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch, and the lifespans there overlap so heavily that four generations are alive at once. That is why this chapter can put a young Enoch asleep in his grandfather's house and have the old man interpret the dream for him.

The pairing is standard. Numbers 12:6 has God making himself known to a prophet in a vision and speaking to him in a dream, and Job 33:15 places both in deep sleep on the bed. What follows the pattern here is the rest of the procedure: the dreamer cries out, an elder wakes him, hears the whole thing, and tells him what it means.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἄβυσσος (abyssos), bottomless - Hebrew: תְּהוֹם (tehom), the deep
translationNotes.note: The English word comes from a Greek adjective meaning without a bottom. In the Greek Old Testament it translates the Hebrew word for the deep, the water under the world that Genesis 1:2 has darkness over and that bursts open in the flood. That is the pit this vision swallows the earth into, and the same word carries the prison of the fallen stars later in these visions.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁאָר (shear), remnant - שְׁאֵרִית (sheerit), what is left over
translationNotes.note: A fixed term rather than a mood. It names the part of a people left standing after a disaster has run through, and the prophets use it constantly for the survivors of war and exile. Mahalalel does not tell Enoch to ask that the judgement be cancelled; he tells him to ask that some be left.

This translation puts round brackets around words the translator has supplied so the English works, as with the lifted up (my voice) here. They are not in the Ethiopic. Square brackets and italics elsewhere mark other editorial additions, and the cross-shaped daggers mark places where the manuscripts are damaged or disagree, as at 83:11.

translationNotes.term: When I was learning to write
translationNotes.note: The book dates the first vision to Enoch's schooling and has him write his prayer down for the generations of the world (83:10). Writing is what he does with everything he is shown, and it is the ground of the book's own claim to be a copied record handed on.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch tells Methuselah the first of two visions he saw before he married. Heaven collapses and falls to the earth, the earth is swallowed in a great abyss, and his grandfather Mahalalel wakes him and tells him to pray that a remnant may be left on the earth.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 84
summaryBullets: And I lifted up my hands in righteousness and blessed the Holy and Great One, and spoke with the breath of my mouth, and with the tongue of flesh, which God has made for the children of the flesh of men, that they should speak therewith, and He gave them breath and a tongue and a mouth that they should speak therewith: (84:1).

'Blessed be You, O Lord, King, Great and mighty in Your greatness, Lord of the whole creation of the heaven, King of kings and God of the whole world. And Your power and kingship and greatness abide for ever and ever, And throughout all generations Your dominion; And all the heavens are Your throne for ever, And the whole earth Your footstool for ever and ever. (84:2).

For You have made and You rulest all things, And nothing is too hard for You, Wisdom departs not from the place of Your throne , Nor turns away from Your presence. And You know and see and hearest everything, And there is nothing hidden from You for You see everything . (84:3).
And now the angels of Your heavens are guilty of trespass, And upon the flesh of men abideth Your wrath until the great day of judgement. (84:4).

And now, O God and Lord and Great King, I implore and beseech You to fulfil my prayer, To leave me a posterity on earth, And not destroy all the flesh of man, And make the earth without inhabitant, So that there should be an eternal destruction. (84:5).

And now, my Lord, destroy from the earth the flesh which has aroused Your wrath, But the flesh of righteousness and uprightness establish as a plant of the eternal seed, And hide not Your face from the prayer of Your servant, O Lord.' (84:6).
crossRefs: Isaiah 66:1: Heaven is called God's throne and the earth his footstool, the exact pair of images this prayer opens with.
Jeremiah 32:17: Nothing is too hard for the God who made the heavens and the earth by his great power and outstretched arm, the same claim this prayer makes in the same words.
Psalm 139:1-4: God searches and knows a man, discerns his thoughts from far off, and knows a word on the tongue before it is spoken, which is the knowledge Enoch ascribes to him here.
1 Timothy 6:15: God is called the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords, the title this prayer uses at its start.
Isaiah 60:21: A people are called the branch of God's planting and the work of his hands, the same planting figure Enoch uses when he asks for a plant of the eternal seed.

translationNotes.note: Real furniture. A throne stood on a platform and a king rested his feet on a low stool in front of it, and putting something under a king's feet was the standard picture of it being subject to him. Psalm 110:1 has enemies made a footstool, and David calls the ark the footstool of God at 1 Chronicles 28:2.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מֶלֶךְ מְלָכִים (melekh melakhim), king of kings
translationNotes.note: A working title in the ancient East, not a flourish. A great king who ruled other kings styled himself that way, and Ezra 7:12 preserves the Persian ruler Artaxerxes using it of himself in an official letter. The prayer takes the highest title a man could hold and puts it where it belongs.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כַּפַּיִם (kappayim), the palms of the hands
translationNotes.note: The ordinary posture for prayer in that world was to stand with the arms raised and the palms open toward heaven. Solomon prays that way at the dedication of the temple, and Psalm 141:2 sets the lifting of the hands beside the evening offering. Kneeling and lying face down were used as well, but the raised open hand was the default.

translationNotes.term: The angels of Your heavens are guilty of trespass
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַעַל (maal), trespass, an act of treachery
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew word behind trespass is not a general term for wrongdoing. It means a breach of trust by someone holding a position, the word used for stealing what is dedicated to God or for a wife's unfaithfulness. The book has already described what it means by it, in the chapters where the watchers leave their station, take wives and teach what they were not to teach.

translationNotes.term: A plant of the eternal seed
translationNotes.note: Planting language for a preserved people runs through Scripture, from the branch of God's planting in Isaiah to oaks of righteousness called the planting of the Lord at Isaiah 61:3. This book returns to the same figure repeatedly and calls the line that survives the plant of righteousness.

The opening of the prayer is careful about who is speaking: a man addresses the maker of the heavens with breath, a tongue and a mouth that were given to him for the purpose. Flesh here means man as a made and mortal creature, which is the same sense the prayer uses when it asks that not all the flesh of man be destroyed.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch lifts his hands and blesses God as king of the whole creation, whose throne is the heavens and whose footstool is the earth, then names the trespass of the angels of heaven and asks that a posterity be left on the earth and not all flesh destroyed.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 85
summaryBullets: And after this I saw another dream, and I will show the whole dream to you, my son. (85:1).
And Enoch lifted up (his voice) and spoke to his son Methuselah: 'To you, my son, will I speak: hear my words--incline yours ear to the dream-vision of your father. (85:2).

Before I took your mother Edna, I saw in a vision on my bed, and behold a bull came forth from the earth, and that bull was white; and after it came forth a heifer, and along with this (latter) came forth two bulls, one of them black and the other red. (85:3).
And that black bull gored the red one and pursued him over the earth, and thereupon I could no longer see that red bull. (85:4).
But that black bull grew and that heifer went with him, and I saw that many oxen proceeded from him which resembled and followed him. (85:5).
And that cow, that first one, went from the presence of that first bull in order to seek that red one, but found him not, and lamented with a great lamentation over him and sought him. (85:6).
And I looked till that first bull came to her and quieted her, and from that time onward she cried no more. (85:7).
And after that she bore another white bull, and after him she bore many bulls and black cows. (85:8).

And I saw in my sleep that white bull likewise grow and become a great white bull, and from Him proceeded many white bulls, and they resembled him. And they began to beget many white bulls, which resembled them, one following the other, (even) many. (85:9).
crossRefs: Genesis 2:7: The man is formed of dust from the ground and becomes a living creature, which is the event a bull coming forth out of the earth stands at the head of.
Genesis 4:1-2: Eve bears Cain and then his brother Abel, one a keeper of sheep and the other a worker of the ground, the two who follow the first pair.
Genesis 4:8: Cain rises up against his brother Abel in the field and kills him, and the killing is the turn this dream builds its whole opening on.
Genesis 4:25: Another son is born and named Seth, because God appointed another offspring in place of Abel, which is the third birth this chapter ends with.
1 John 3:12: The first murder is named outright, with the reason given that the killer's own deeds were evil and his brother's righteous.

translationNotes.note: From here to the end of chapter 90 the vision tells its story with animals instead of men. The book says plainly that this is a dream (85:1-3), so the beasts are the dream's own figures and not a claim about anyone's nature. It supplies no key. Species and colour are all the description any figure gets, and the events are what identify them.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פַּר (par), bull - עֶגְלָה (eglah), heifer - פָּרָה (parah), cow
translationNotes.note: The translation uses four herd words and keeps them distinct. A bull is an intact male, an ox is a castrated working male, a heifer is a young female that has not yet calved, and a cow has. Following the generations in this vision means following those words, because a heifer that becomes a cow has borne young in between.

The verb for an ox killing with its horns. The Torah devotes a whole case law to it at Exodus 21:28-32: an ox that gores a man to death is stoned, and if the owner had been warned and did nothing, he is liable with his life. The vision uses the one animal killing in the law for the first killing in the world.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִסְפֵּד (misped), wailing for the dead
translationNotes.note: Mourning in that world was loud and public: crying aloud, tearing the clothes, sackcloth and ashes, and often hired mourners to keep the wailing going for days. The vision has the cow searching for the red bull and crying until she is quieted, which is grief carried out the way the period carried it out.

The name this book gives Enoch's wife. Scripture does not name her; Genesis 5:21-24 records only that Enoch fathered Methuselah and walked with God. The word itself is real Hebrew for pleasure or delight, used by Sarah at Genesis 18:12, and it shares a root with Eden.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch tells Methuselah a second dream. A white bull comes up out of the earth, then a heifer, then two bulls, one black and one red; the black gores the red and it is seen no more, the cow searches and mourns for it, and afterward she bears another white bull whose line multiplies.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 86
summaryBullets: And again I saw with mine eyes as I slept, and I saw the heaven above, and behold a star fell from heaven, and it arose and eat and pastured amongst those oxen. (86:1).
And after that I saw the large and the black oxen, and behold they all changed their stalls and pastures and their cattle, and began to live with each other. (86:2).

And again I saw in the vision, and looked towards the heaven, and behold I saw many stars descend and cast themselves down from heaven to that first star, and they became bulls amongst those cattle and pastured with them amongst them . (86:3).

And I looked at them and saw, and behold they all let out their privy members, like horses, and began to cover the cows of the oxen, and they all became pregnant and bare elephants, camels, and asses. (86:4).
And all the oxen feared them and were affrighted at them, and began to bite with their teeth and to devour, and to gore with their horns. (86:5).
And they began, moreover, to devour those oxen; and behold all the children of the earth began to tremble and quake before them and to flee from them. (86:6).
crossRefs: Genesis 6:1-4: The sons of God take wives from the daughters of men, and the Nephilim are on the earth in those days and afterward, the account this vision retells with beasts in place of men.
Jude 1:6: The angels who did not stay within their own position of authority but left their proper dwelling are kept in eternal chains under gloomy darkness until the judgement of the great day.
2 Peter 2:4: God did not spare angels when they sinned but cast them down and committed them to chains of gloomy darkness to be kept until the judgement.
Numbers 13:33: The spies report seeing the Nephilim and say they seemed like grasshoppers beside them, which is the terror this chapter describes at the end.
Revelation 9:1: A star fallen from heaven to earth is given the key to the shaft of the bottomless pit, the same image of a star that comes down and then opens a pit.

translationNotes.note: The vision keeps heavenly beings as stars while men are cattle, so a star that falls, feeds among the herd and fathers on the cows is a heavenly being that came down and lived on the earth. This book has already told the same events without figures, in the chapters where the watchers descend, take wives and are bound; see 1 Enoch 6:1-6.

The three kinds born from the union are large beasts of a different order from the cattle, and the vision never lets them be cattle. Told straight, this book calls the offspring of the watchers giants and says they consumed the produce of men and then turned on men themselves; see 1 Enoch 7:2.

An older English term for the genitals, kept here because the translation renders the line bluntly rather than smoothing it. The comparison to horses is Scripture's own way of describing gross sexual appetite, used of Egypt at Ezekiel 23:20. The detail matters because it is how the vision marks out which stars are later bound.

To pasture is to graze in company with the herd. Saying the fallen star arose, ate and pastured among the oxen is the vision's way of saying it took up life among men as one of them, which is the step that comes before anything else it does.

The phrase the vision uses for mankind, set deliberately against the stars that came from heaven. The whole chapter turns on that pairing: what belongs above comes down, mixes with what belongs below, and the result is a third kind that belongs nowhere.

stories.keyTakeaway: A star falls from heaven and pastures among the oxen, then many stars come down after it and become bulls among the cattle. They cover the cows and the offspring are elephants, camels and asses, which begin to devour the oxen until all the children of the earth flee before them.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 87
summaryBullets: And again I saw how they began to gore each other and to devour each other, and the earth began to cry aloud. (87:1).

And I raised mine eyes again to heaven, and I saw in the vision, and behold there came forth from heaven beings who were like white men: and four went forth from that place and three with them. (87:2).

And those three that had last come forth grasped me by my hand and took me up, away from the generations of the earth, and raised me up to a lofty place, and showed me a tower raised high above the earth, and all the hills were lower. (87:3).
And one said to me: 'Remain here till you see everything that befalls those elephants, camels, and asses, and the stars and the oxen, and all of them.' (87:4).
crossRefs: Genesis 4:10: The voice of a murdered brother's blood is said to cry to God from the ground, which is what an earth crying aloud over slaughter means.
Genesis 18:2: Abraham lifts his eyes and three men are standing in front of him, and they turn out to be no ordinary travellers.
Genesis 19:16: The men take Lot by the hand, with his wife and daughters, and bring him out of the city and set him outside it.
Daniel 10:5-6: A man clothed in linen with a face like lightning and eyes like flaming torches, which is how Scripture describes a messenger who looks like a man and is not one.
Revelation 4:1: A voice tells the seer to come up here and be shown what must take place, the same summons to a raised place to watch.

translationNotes.term: Beings who were like white men
translationNotes.note: In a vision where every man is an animal, anything that looks like a man is not one. These come out of heaven and are described only by that likeness and by the colour white, the same marking the vision has used for particular animals. Four come first and three more with them, and it is one of the four who acts in the next chapter.

The counts are not decoration. Four beings act in the chapters that follow, and this book has already had four archangels bring the earth's complaint before God at 1 Enoch 9:1 and has named seven of them at 1 Enoch 20:1-8. Four plus three is seven, which is the number this vision gathers again at 90:21.

translationNotes.term: The earth began to cry aloud
translationNotes.note: Scripture treats spilled blood as something that makes a noise. Abel's blood cries from the ground, and Numbers 35:33 says blood pollutes the land and that nothing atones for it except the blood of the man who shed it. An earth that cries aloud is not scenery; it is a legal complaint.

translationNotes.term: A tower raised high above the earth
translationNotes.note: Being set on a height to watch is the standing posture of a seer. Habakkuk takes his stand at his watchpost and stations himself on the tower to see what will be said to him, and Ezekiel is appointed a watchman for the house of Israel. Enoch is put where he can see, and told to stay there until it is over.

translationNotes.term: Away from the generations of the earth
translationNotes.note: The phrase marks a removal, not a journey. Enoch is lifted out of the line of men whose story the vision is telling and set above it, which is why he can report what happens to the elephants, the camels, the asses, the stars and the oxen without being one of them.

stories.keyTakeaway: As the beasts gore and devour each other and the earth cries out, beings like white men come out of heaven, four of them and three more. The three take Enoch by the hand, raise him above the generations of the earth to a high tower, and tell him to stay and watch everything that follows.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 88
summaryBullets: And I saw one of those four who had come forth first, and he seized that first star which had fallen from the heaven, and bound it hand and foot and cast it into an abyss: now that abyss was narrow and deep, and horrible and dark. (88:1).
And one of them drew a sword, and gave it to those elephants and camels and asses: then they began to smite each other, and the whole earth quaked because of them. (88:2).

And as I was beholding in the vision, lo, one of those four who had come forth stoned (them) from heaven, and gathered and took all the great stars whose privy members were like those of horses, and bound them all hand and foot, and cast them in an abyss of the earth. (88:3).
crossRefs: Genesis 6:11-13: The earth is corrupt before God and filled with violence, and he tells Noah that the end of all flesh has come because the earth is filled with violence through them.

Isaiah 24:21-22: The host of heaven is punished in heaven, gathered like prisoners in a pit, shut up in a prison, and punished after many days, which is exactly the sequence of arrest, holding and later sentence here.
2 Peter 2:4: Angels who sinned are cast down and committed to chains of gloomy darkness, held for judgement rather than destroyed on the spot.
Revelation 20:1-3: An angel with the key to the bottomless pit seizes the dragon, binds him, throws him into the pit and shuts and seals it over him.
Judges 7:22: The Lord sets every man's sword against his comrade throughout the camp, and the army destroys itself, which is what handing a sword to enemies accomplishes here.
