translationNotes.note: Binding is an arrest, not an execution. The star is tied and put somewhere it cannot leave, which holds it for a judgement that has not happened yet. This book has already described the same sentence carried out on Azazel, bound and cast into darkness in the desert and left there until the great day; see 1 Enoch 10:4-6.

The weapon of the period was short, a straight or slightly curved blade of bronze or iron about half a metre long, made for stabbing at close quarters and worn at the belt. The Hebrew word covers it and also the dagger and the knife. Giving one to the beasts is giving them the means to finish each other.

translationNotes.term: An abyss narrow and deep and dark
translationNotes.note: The vision gives the holding place three measurements and no location. Narrow means no room to move, deep means no way up, dark means nothing to see. Scripture uses a cistern or a dry pit the same way, as the place a man is put when he is to be kept and not killed.

translationNotes.term: The great stars whose privy members were like those of horses
translationNotes.note: The phrase is a back-reference, not a new description. It points at 86:4 and marks out exactly which stars are seized: the ones that came down and fathered the elephants, camels and asses. The vision is careful to bind the ones it has already charged.

The pronoun in round brackets is supplied by the translator; the Ethiopic does not have it, and the sense of the verb here is difficult. What the rest of the verse describes is plain enough: the same figure gathers the great stars, binds them and casts them into a pit in the earth.

stories.keyTakeaway: One of the four seizes the star that fell first, binds it hand and foot and casts it into an abyss that is narrow and deep and dark. Another gives a sword to the elephants, camels and asses so that they cut each other down, and a third binds all the great stars and casts them into an abyss of the earth.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 89
summaryBullets: And one of those four went to that white bull and instructed him in a secret, without his being terrified: he was born a bull and became a man, and built for himself a great vessel and dwelt thereon; and three bulls dwelt with him in that vessel and they were covered in. (89:1).
And again I raised mine eyes towards heaven and saw a lofty roof, with seven water torrents thereon, and those torrents flowed with much water into an enclosure. (89:2).

And I saw again, and behold fountains were opened on the surface of that great enclosure, and that water began to swell and rise upon the surface, and I saw that enclosure till all its surface was covered with water. (89:3).

And the water, the darkness, and mist increased upon it; and as I looked at the height of that water, that water had risen above the height of that enclosure, and was streaming over that enclosure, and it stood upon the earth. (89:4).
And all the cattle of that enclosure were gathered together until I saw how they sank and were swallowed up and perished in that water. (89:5).

But that vessel floated on the water, while all the oxen and elephants and camels and asses sank to the bottom with all the animals, so that I could no longer see them, and they were not able to escape, (but) perished and sank into the depths. (89:6).
And again I saw in the vision till those water torrents were removed from that high roof, and the chasms of the earth were levelled up and other abysses were opened. (89:7).
Then the water began to run down into these, till the earth became visible; but that vessel settled on the earth, and the darkness retired and light appeared. (89:8).

But that white bull which had become a man came out of that vessel, and the three bulls with him, and one of those three was white like that bull, and one of them was red as blood, and one black: and that white bull departed from them. LXXXIX. 10-27. From the Death of Noah to the Exodus . (89:9).

And they began to bring forth beasts of the field and birds, so that there arose different genera: lions, tigers, wolves, dogs, hyenas, wild boars, foxes, squirrels, swine, falcons, vultures, kites, eagles, and ravens; and among them was born a white bull. (89:10).
And they began to bite one another; but that white bull which was born amongst them begat a wild ass and a white bull with it, and the wild asses multiplied. (89:11).
But that bull which was born from him begat a black wild boar and a white sheep; and the former begat many boars, but that sheep begat twelve sheep. (89:12).
And when those twelve sheep had grown, they gave up one of them to the asses, and those asses again gave up that sheep to the wolves, and that sheep grew up among the wolves. (89:13).
And the Lord brought the eleven sheep to live with it and to pasture with it among the wolves: and they multiplied and became many flocks of sheep. (89:14).

And the wolves began to fear them, and they oppressed them until they destroyed their little ones, and they cast their young into a river of much water: but those sheep began to cry aloud on account of their little ones, and to complain to their Lord. (89:15).

And a sheep which had been saved from the wolves fled and escaped to the wild asses; and I saw the sheep how they lamented and cried, and besought their Lord with all their might, till that Lord of the sheep descended at the voice of the sheep from a lofty abode, and came to them and pastured them. (89:16).
And He called that sheep which had escaped the wolves, and spoke with it concerning the wolves that it should admonish them not to touch the sheep. (89:17).

And the sheep went to the wolves according to the word of the Lord, and another sheep met it and went with it, and the two went and entered together into the assembly of those wolves, and spoke with them and admonished them not to touch the sheep from henceforth. (89:18).
And thereupon I saw the wolves, and how they oppressed the sheep exceedingly with all their power; and the sheep cried aloud. (89:19).
And the Lord came to the sheep and they began to smite those wolves: and the wolves began to make lamentation; but the sheep became quiet and forthwith ceased to cry out. (89:20).
And I saw the sheep till they departed from amongst the wolves; but the eyes of the wolves were blinded, and those wolves departed in pursuit of the sheep with all their power. (89:21).
And the Lord of the sheep went with them, as their leader, and all His sheep followed Him: and his face was dazzling and glorious and terrible to behold. (89:22).
But the wolves began to pursue those sheep till they reached a sea of water. (89:23).
And that sea was divided, and the water stood on this side and on that before their face, and their Lord led them and placed Himself between them and the wolves. (89:24).
And as those wolves did not yet see the sheep, they proceeded into the midst of that sea, and the wolves followed the sheep, and those wolves ran after them into that sea. (89:25).

And when they saw the Lord of the sheep, they turned to flee before His face, but that sea gathered itself together, and became as it had been created, and the water swelled and rose till it covered those wolves. (89:26).
And I saw till all the wolves who pursued those sheep perished and were drowned. LXXXIX. 28-40. Israel in the Desert, the Giving of the Law, the Entrance into Palestine . (89:27).

But the sheep escaped from that water and went forth into a wilderness, where there was no water and no grass; and they began to open their eyes and to see; and I saw the Lord of the sheep pasturing them and giving them water and grass, and that sheep going and leading them. (89:28).
And that sheep ascended to the summit of that lofty rock, and the Lord of the sheep sent it to them. (89:29).
And after that I saw the Lord of the sheep who stood before them, and His appearance was great and terrible and majestic, and all those sheep saw Him and were afraid before His face. (89:30).
And they all feared and trembled because of Him, and they cried to that sheep with them which was amongst them : "We are not able to stand before our Lord or to behold Him." (89:31).

And that sheep which led them again ascended to the summit of that rock, but the sheep began to be blinded and to wander from the way which he had showed them, but that sheep wot not thereof. (89:32).

And the Lord of the sheep was wrathful exceedingly against them, and that sheep discovered it, and went down from the summit of the rock, and came to the sheep, and found the greatest part of them blinded and fallen away. (89:33).
And when they saw it they feared and trembled at its presence, and desired to return to their folds. (89:34).

And that sheep took other sheep with it, and came to those sheep which had fallen away, and began to slay them; and the sheep feared its presence, and thus that sheep brought back those sheep that had fallen away, and they returned to their folds. (89:35).
And I saw in this vision till that sheep became a man and built a house for the Lord of the sheep, and placed all the sheep in that house. (89:36).

And I saw till this sheep which had met that sheep which led them fell asleep: and I saw till all the great sheep perished and little ones arose in their place, and they came to a pasture, and approached a stream of water. (89:37).
Then that sheep, their leader which had become a man, withdrew from them and fell asleep, and all the sheep sought it and cried over it with a great crying. (89:38).

And I saw till they left off crying for that sheep and crossed that stream of water, and there arose the two sheep as leaders in the place of those which had led them and fallen asleep (lit. "had fallen asleep and led them"). (89:39).

And I saw till the sheep came to a goodly place, and a pleasant and glorious land, and I saw till those sheep were satisfied; and that house stood amongst them in the pleasant land. LXXXIX. 41-50. From the Time of the Judges till the Building of the Temple . (89:40).
And sometimes their eyes were opened, and sometimes blinded, till another sheep arose and led them and brought them all back, and their eyes were opened. (89:41).
And the dogs and the foxes and the wild boars began to devour those sheep till the Lord of the sheep raised up another sheep a ram from their midst, which led them. (89:42).
And that ram began to butt on either side those dogs, foxes, and wild boars till he had destroyed them †all†. (89:43).

And that sheep whose eyes were opened saw that ram, which was amongst the sheep, till it †forsook its glory† and began to butt those sheep, and trampled upon them, and behaved itself unseemly. (89:44).
And the Lord of the sheep sent the lamb to another lamb and raised it to being a ram and leader of the sheep instead of that ram which had †forsaken its glory†. (89:45).
And it went to it and spoke to it alone, and raised it to being a ram, and made it the prince and leader of the sheep; but during all these things those dogs oppressed the sheep. (89:46).
And the first ram pursued that second ram, and that second ram arose and fled before it; and I saw till those dogs pulled down the first ram. (89:47).
And that second ram arose and led the little sheep. (89:48).

And those sheep grew and multiplied; but all the dogs, and foxes, and wild boars feared and fled before it, and that ram butted and killed the wild beasts, and those wild beasts had no longer any power among the sheep and robbed them no more of ought. 48 b . And that ram begat many sheep and fell asleep; and a little sheep became ram in its stead, and became prince and leader of those sheep. (89:49).

And that house became great and broad, and it was built for those sheep: (and) a tower lofty and great was built on the house for the Lord of the sheep, and that house was low, but the tower was elevated and lofty, and the Lord of the sheep stood on that tower and they offered a full table before Him. LXXXIX. 51-67. The Two Kingdoms of Israel and Judah, to the Destruction of Jerusalem . (89:50).

And again I saw those sheep that they again erred and went many ways, and forsook that their house, and the Lord of the sheep called some from amongst the sheep and sent them to the sheep, but the sheep began to slay them. (89:51).

And one of them was saved and was not slain, and it sped away and cried aloud over the sheep; and they sought to slay it, but the Lord of the sheep saved it from the sheep, and brought it up to me, and caused it to dwell there. (89:52).
And many other sheep He sent to those sheep to testify to them and lament over them. (89:53).

And after that I saw that when they forsook the house of the Lord and His tower they fell away entirely, and their eyes were blinded; and I saw the Lord of the sheep how He wrought much slaughter amongst them in their herds until those sheep invited that slaughter and betrayed His place. (89:54).

And He gave them over into the hands of the lions and tigers, and wolves and hyenas, and into the hand of the foxes, and to all the wild beasts, and those wild beasts began to tear in pieces those sheep. (89:55).
And I saw that He forsook that their house and their tower and gave them all into the hand of the lions, to tear and devour them, into the hand of all the wild beasts. (89:56).
And I began to cry aloud with all my power, and to appeal to the Lord of the sheep, and to represent to Him in regard to the sheep that they were devoured by all the wild beasts. (89:57).
But He remained unmoved, though He saw it, and rejoiced that they were devoured and swallowed and robbed, and left them to be devoured in the hand of all the beasts. (89:58).

And He called seventy shepherds, and cast those sheep to them that they might pasture them, and He spoke to the shepherds and their companions: "Let each individual of you pasture the sheep henceforward, and everything that I shall command you that do you. (89:59).
And I will deliver them over to you duly numbered, and tell you which of them are to be destroyed--and them destroy you." And He gave over to them those sheep. (89:60).
And He called another and spoke to him: "Observe and mark everything that the shepherds will do to those sheep; for they will destroy more of them than I have commanded them. (89:61).

And every excess and the destruction which will be wrought through the shepherds, record (namely) how many they destroy according to my command, and how many according to their own caprice: record against every individual shepherd all the destruction he effects. (89:62).

And read out before me by number how many they destroy, and how many they deliver over for destruction, that I may have this as a testimony against them, and know every deed of the shepherds, that I may comprehend and see what they do, whether or not they abide by my command which I have commanded them. (89:63).

But they shall not know it, and you will not declare it to them, nor admonish them, but only record against each individual all the destruction which the shepherds effect each in his time and lay it all before me." (89:64).
And I saw till those shepherds pastured in their season, and they began to slay and to destroy more than they were bidden, and they delivered those sheep into the hand of the lions. (89:65).
And the lions and tigers eat and devoured the greater part of those sheep, and the wild boars eat along with them; and they burnt that tower and demolished that house. (89:66).

And I became exceedingly sorrowful over that tower because that house of the sheep was demolished, and afterwards I was unable to see if those sheep entered that house. LXXXIX. 68-71. First Period of the Angelic Rulers--from the Destruction of Jerusalem to the Return from the Captivity . (89:67).

And the shepherds and their associates delivered over those sheep to all the wild beasts, to devour them, and each one of them received in his time a definite number: it was written by the other in a book how many each one of them destroyed of them. (89:68).
And each one slew and destroyed many more than was prescribed; and I began to weep and lament on account of those sheep. (89:69).

And thus in the vision I saw that one who wrote, how he wrote down every one that was destroyed by those shepherds, day by day, and carried up and laid down and showed actually the whole book to the Lord of the sheep--(even) everything that they had done, and all that each one of them had made away with, and all that they had given over to destruction. (89:70).

And the book was read before the Lord of the sheep, and He took the book from his hand and read it and sealed it and laid it down. LXXXIX. 72-77. Second Period--from the time of Cyrus to that of Alexander the Great . (89:71).

And forthwith I saw how the shepherds pastured for twelve hours, and behold three of those sheep turned back and came and entered and began to build up all that had fallen down of that house; but the wild boars tried to hinder them, but they were not able. (89:72).

And they began again to build as before, and they reared up that tower, and it was named the high tower; and they began again to place a table before the tower, but all the bread on it was polluted and not pure. (89:73).

And as touching all this the eyes of those sheep were blinded so that they saw not, and (the eyes of) their shepherds likewise; and they delivered them in large numbers to their shepherds for destruction, and they trampled the sheep with their feet and devoured them. (89:74).

And the Lord of the sheep remained unmoved till all the sheep were dispersed over the field and mingled with them ( i.e. the beasts), and they ( i.e. the shepherds) did not save them out of the hand of the beasts. (89:75).

And this one who wrote the book carried it up, and showed it and read it before the Lord of the sheep, and implored Him on their account, and besought Him on their account as he showed Him all the doings of the shepherds, and gave testimony before Him against all the shepherds. And he took the actual book and laid it down beside Him and departed. (89:76).
crossRefs: Genesis 7:17-23: The waters lift the ark and prevail over the earth, everything on dry land dies, and only Noah and those with him in the ark are left.
Exodus 14:21-28: The sea is driven back and divided, Israel walks through on dry ground with the waters a wall on either side, and the sea returns and covers the pursuing army.
Exodus 32:7-10: While Moses is still on the mountain the people turn aside quickly from the way they were commanded, and God's anger burns against them.
2 Kings 25:8-10: Nebuchadnezzar's captain of the guard burns the house of the Lord, the king's house and every great house in Jerusalem, and breaks down the walls around the city.
Ezekiel 34:1-10: The shepherds of Israel are charged with feeding themselves and not the flock, and God declares himself against the shepherds and says he will require his sheep at their hand.

translationNotes.note: The arrangement is spelled out at 89:59-64 and is worth reading slowly. Seventy are called and the sheep are handed to them by number, each to pasture in his own period, with a set count of sheep they are permitted to destroy. Another is appointed to watch and write down every one destroyed beyond that count, against each shepherd by name, and the shepherds are not to be told they are being recorded.

The title the vision uses for God from here on. Shepherd and flock is Scripture's ordinary language for the same relation, from the Lord is my shepherd in the psalms to the whole indictment of Israel's shepherds in Ezekiel, and a shepherd in that world owned the flock, led it out and back, slept beside it and answered for anything taken.

The vision has only two buildings and never names either. A house is built, the flock is put inside it, a tower is raised on it, and the Lord of the sheep stands on the tower with a full table set before him. Later the tower is burned and the house demolished, then three sheep return and rebuild, and the bread on the new table is called polluted, the same charge Malachi 1:7 lays against a defiled table.

translationNotes.term: Wolves, lions, foxes, dogs and wild boars
translationNotes.note: The vision divides its animals into flocks and predators and keeps the line hard. Sheep and cattle are herded and eaten from; wolves, lions, hyenas, foxes, dogs and boars take and tear. Scripture reaches for the same set, as when Jeremiah 5:6 sends a lion, a wolf and a leopard against a people, and Psalm 80:13 has a boar out of the forest ravaging the vine.

This is the chapter's own running measure and it is used more than a dozen times. The sheep open their eyes in the wilderness, are blinded at the rock, are blinded again when they forsake the house, and the shepherds themselves are blinded later. Tracking that one detail is the easiest way to follow a chapter of seventy-six verses without names.

The English here is a century old and several words no longer mean what they look like. Wot not thereof is did not know it (89:32); robbed them no more of ought is robbed them of anything (89:49); affrighted is terrified; privy members is genitals; a full table is a table set with food. None of these are technical terms.

stories.keyTakeaway: The vision runs from the flood to the rebuilt house. A bull becomes a man and builds a vessel, sheep are led out from the wolves through a divided sea, a house and a tower are raised, and when the sheep go blind the Lord of the sheep hands them to seventy shepherds who kill more than they were told.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 90
summaryBullets: And I saw till that in this manner thirty-five shepherds undertook the pasturing (of the sheep), and they severally completed their periods as did the first; and others received them into their hands, to pasture them for their period, each shepherd in his own period. (90:1).

And after that I saw in my vision all the birds of heaven coming, the eagles, the vultures, the kites, the ravens; but the eagles led all the birds; and they began to devour those sheep, and to pick out their eyes and to devour their flesh. (90:2).
And the sheep cried out because their flesh was being devoured by the birds, and as for me I looked and lamented in my sleep over that shepherd who pastured the sheep. (90:3).

And I saw until those sheep were devoured by the dogs and eagles and kites, and they left neither flesh nor skin nor sinew remaining on them till only their bones stood there: and their bones too fell to the earth and the sheep became few. (90:4).

And I saw until that twenty-three had undertaken the pasturing and completed in their several periods fifty-eight times. XC. 6-12. Fourth Period--from the Graeco-Syrian Domination to the Maccabæan Revolt . (90:5).
But behold lambs were borne by those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to cry to the sheep. (90:6).
Yea, they cried to them, but they did not hearken to what they said to them, but were exceedingly deaf, and their eyes were very exceedingly blinded. (90:7).
And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs and took one of those lambs, and dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them. (90:8).
And I saw till horns grew upon those lambs, and the ravens cast down their horns; and I saw till there sprouted a great horn of one of those sheep, and their eyes were opened. (90:9).
And it †looked at† them and their eyes opened , and it cried to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it. (90:10).

And notwithstanding all this those eagles and vultures and ravens and kites still kept tearing the sheep and swooping down upon them and devouring them: still the sheep remained silent, but the rams lamented and cried out. (90:11).

And those ravens fought and battled with it and sought to lay low its horn, but they had no power over it. XC. 13-19. The Last Assault of the Gentiles on the Jews (where vv. 13-15 and 16-18 are doublets). (90:12).

And I saw till the †shepherds and† eagles and those vultures and kites came, and †they cried to the ravens† that they should break the horn of that ram, and they battled and fought with it, and it battled with them and cried that its help might come. (90:13).

And I saw till that man, who wrote down the names of the shepherds and carried up into the presence of the Lord of the sheep came and helped it and showed it everything: he had come down for the help of that ram . (90:14).
And I saw till the Lord of the sheep came to them in wrath, and all who saw Him fled, and they all fell †into His shadow† from before His face. (90:15).

All the eagles and vultures and ravens and kites were gathered together, and there came with them all the sheep of the field, yea, they all came together, and helped each other to break that horn of the ram. (90:16).

And I saw that man, who wrote the book according to the command of the Lord, till he opened that book concerning the destruction which those twelve last shepherds had wrought, and showed that they had destroyed much more than their predecessors, before the Lord of the sheep. (90:17).

And I saw till the Lord of the sheep came to them and took in His hand the staff of His wrath, and smote the earth, and the earth clave asunder, and all the beasts and all the birds of the heaven fell from among those sheep, and were swallowed up in the earth and it covered them. XC. 20-27. Judgement of the Fallen Angels, the Shepherds, and the Apostates . (90:18).

And I saw till a great sword was given to the sheep, and the sheep proceeded against all the beasts of the field to slay them, and all the beasts and the birds of the heaven fled before their face. (90:19).

And I saw till a throne was erected in the pleasant land, and the Lord of the sheep sat Himself thereon, and the other took the sealed books and opened those books before the Lord of the sheep. (90:20).

And the Lord called those men the seven first white ones, and commanded that they should bring before Him, beginning with the first star which led the way, all the stars whose privy members were like those of horses, and they brought them all before paragraph continues Him. (90:21).

And He said to that man who wrote before Him, being one of those seven white ones, and said to him: "Take those seventy shepherds to whom I delivered the sheep, and who taking them on their own authority slew more than I commanded them." (90:22).
And behold they were all bound, I saw, and they all stood before Him. (90:23).

And the judgement was held first over the stars, and they were judged and found guilty, and went to the place of condemnation, and they were cast into an abyss, full of fire and flaming, and full of pillars of fire. (90:24).
And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss. (90:25).

And I saw at that time how a like abyss was opened in the midst of the earth, full of fire, and they brought those blinded sheep, and they were all judged and found guilty and cast into this fiery abyss, and they burned; now this abyss was to the right of that house. (90:26).
And I saw those sheep burning †and their bones burning†. XC. 28-38. The New Jerusalem, the Conversion of the surviving Gentiles, the Resurrection of the Righteous, the Messiah . (90:27).

And I stood up to see till they folded up that old house; and carried off all the pillars, and all the beams and ornaments of the house were at the same time folded up with it, and they carried it off and laid it in a place in the south of the land. (90:28).

And I saw till the Lord of the sheep brought a new house greater and loftier than that first, and set it up in the place of the first which had beer folded up: all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first, the old one which He had taken away, and all the sheep were within it. (90:29).

And I saw all the sheep which had been left, and all the beasts on the earth, and all the birds of the heaven, falling down and doing homage to those sheep and making petition to and obeying them in every thing . (90:30).

And thereafter those three who were clothed in white and had seized me by my hand who had taken me up before , and the hand of that ram also seizing hold of me, they took me up and set me down in the midst of those sheep before the judgement took place†. (90:31).
And those sheep were all white, and their wool was abundant and clean. (90:32).

And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house. (90:33).

And I saw till they laid down that sword, which had been given to the sheep, and they brought it back into the house, and it was sealed before the presence of the Lord, and all the sheep were invited into that house, but it held them not. (90:34).
And the eyes of them all were opened, and they saw the good, and there was not one among them that did not see. (90:35).
And I saw that that house was large and broad and very full. (90:36).
And I saw that a white bull was born, with large horns and all the beasts of the field and all the birds of the air feared him and made petition to him all the time. (90:37).

And I saw till all their generations were transformed, and they all became white bulls; and the first among them became a lamb , and that lamb became a great animal and had great black horns on its head; and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced over it and over all the oxen. (90:38).
And I slept in their midst: and I awoke and saw everything. (90:39).
This is the vision which I saw while I slept, and I awoke and blessed the Lord of righteousness and gave Him glory. (90:40).

Then I wept with a great weeping and my tears stayed not till I could no longer endure it: when I saw, they flowed on account of what I had seen; for everything shall come and be fulfilled, and all the deeds of men in their order were shown to me. (90:41).
On that night I remembered the first dream, and because of it I wept and was troubled--because I had seen that vision.' (90:42).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 34:11-16: God says he will search for his sheep himself, bring them out from where they were scattered, feed them on the mountains, bind up the broken and strengthen the sick.
Daniel 7:9-10: Thrones are placed and the Ancient of Days takes his seat, a stream of fire goes out before him, the court sits and the books are opened.
Isaiah 65:17-19: New heavens and a new earth are promised, the former things are not remembered, and God rejoices over his people and no longer hears weeping in them.
Isaiah 2:2-3: The mountain of the house of the Lord is established as the highest and all the nations flow to it, saying, let us go up to the house of the God of Jacob.
Revelation 21:1-3: A new heaven and a new earth appear, the holy city comes down from God, and a voice says the dwelling place of God is with man.

translationNotes.term: How the seventy shepherds are counted
translationNotes.note: The numbers are running totals, not fresh batches, and they add up. Twelve pasture at 89:72, the total stands at thirty-five here at 90:1, at fifty-eight by 90:5, and 90:17 speaks of the twelve last shepherds. That is twelve, twenty-three, twenty-three and twelve, which fills the seventy handed over at 89:59 exactly.

A horn is an animal's weapon and the seat of its strength, and Scripture uses the word for a ruler or a kingdom on that basis. Daniel 8:3-8 counts kingdoms as horns on a ram and a goat, and Psalm 75:10 speaks of horns cut off and lifted up. When a great horn sprouts on one sheep and the birds try to break it, the vision is describing a leader who fights.

A shepherd carried two sticks: a club for driving off predators and breaking a beast's skull, and a long staff for walking, guiding and hooking a sheep back. Psalm 23:4 names both. The vision puts the staff in the Lord of the sheep's hand and has him strike the ground with it hard enough to split it open.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נֶשֶׁר (nesher), eagle or griffon vulture - עֹרֵב (orev), raven
translationNotes.note: All four are carrion birds and all four appear on the list of birds Israel was forbidden to eat, at Leviticus 11:13-19 and again at Deuteronomy 14:12-17. They are the birds that gather over a battlefield and pick the eyes out of the dead, which is precisely what 90:2 has them do to the sheep.

translationNotes.term: To the right of that house
translationNotes.note: Right and left are compass directions here, not sides of a room. On the orientation this book set out at 76:2, where a man faces the sunrise, the right hand is the south. The fiery abyss opened in the earth is therefore placed south of the house.

translationNotes.term: They folded up that old house
translationNotes.note: Folding is what you do to a tent, and the vision describes the removal that way: pillars, beams and ornaments taken down together, carried off and laid in a place in the south of the land. Nothing is broken. The new house that replaces it is described as greater, loftier and new in every part, with the whole flock inside it.

stories.keyTakeaway: Birds of prey tear the sheep, a great horn sprouts on one of them and fights back, and the Lord of the sheep comes in wrath. The stars, the shepherds and the blinded sheep are cast into a fiery abyss, the old house is folded up, a greater one replaces it, and a white bull is born.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 91
summaryBullets: 'And now, my son Methuselah, call to me all your brothers And gather together to me all the sons of your mother; For the word calls me, And the spirit is poured out upon me, That I may show you everything That shall befall you for ever.' 2 And there upon Methuselah went and summoned to him all his brothers and assembled his relatives. 3 And he spoke to all the children of righteousness and said: 'Hear, you sons of Enoch, all the words of your father, And hearken aright to the voice of my mouth; For I exhort you and say to you, beloved: Love uprightness and walk therein. (91:1).
And thereupon Methuselah went and summoned to him all his brothers and assembled his relatives. (91:2).

And he spoke to all the children of righteousness and said: 'Hear, you sons of Enoch, all the words of your father, And hearken aright to the voice of my mouth; For I exhort you and say to you, beloved.' (91:3).

And draw not near to uprightness with a double heart, And associate not with those of a double heart, But walk in righteousness, my sons. And it shall guide you on good paths, And righteousness shall be your companion. (91:4).

For I know that violence must increase on the earth, And a great chastisement be executed on the earth, And all unrighteousness come to an end: Yea, it shall be cut off from its roots, And its whole structure be destroyed. (91:5).
And unrighteousness shall again be consummated on the earth, And all the deeds of unrighteousness and of violence And transgression shall prevail in a twofold degree. (91:6).

And when sin and unrighteousness and blasphemy And violence in all kinds of deeds increase, And apostasy and transgression and uncleanness increase, A great chastisement shall come from heaven upon all these, And the holy Lord will come forth with wrath and chastisement To execute judgement on earth. (91:7).
In those days violence shall be cut off from its roots, And the roots of unrighteousness together with deceit, And they shall be destroyed from under heaven. (91:8).

And all the idols of the heathen shall be abandoned, And the temples burned with fire, And they shall remove them from the whole earth, And they ( i.e. the heathen) shall be cast into the judgement of fire, And shall perish in wrath and in grievous judgement for ever. (91:9).
And the righteous shall arise from their sleep, And wisdom shall arise and be given to them. (91:10).

And after that the roots of unrighteousness shall be cut off, and the sinners shall be destroyed by the sword . . . shall be cut off from the blasphemers in every place, and those who plan violence and those who commit blasphemy shall perish by the sword. (91:11).

And after that there shall be another, the eighth week, that of righteousness, And a sword shall be given to it that a righteous judgement may be executed on the oppressors, And sinners shall be delivered into the hands of the righteous. (91:12).

And at its close they shall acquire houses through their righteousness, And a house shall be built for the Great King in glory for evermore, And all mankind shall look to the path of uprightness. (91:13).

And after that, in the ninth week, the righteous judgement shall be revealed to the whole world, And all the works of the godless shall vanish from all the earth, And the world shall be written down for destruction. (91:14).
And after this, in the tenth week in the seventh part, There shall be the great eternal judgement, In which He will execute vengeance amongst the angels. (91:15).
And the first heaven shall depart and pass away, And a new heaven shall appear, And all the powers of the heavens shall give sevenfold light. (91:16).
And after that there will be many weeks without number for ever, And all shall be in goodness and righteousness, And sin shall no more be mentioned for ever. (91:17).
And now I tell you, my sons, and show you The paths of righteousness and the paths of violence. Yea, I will show them to you again That you may know what will come to pass. (91:18).
And now, hearken to me, my sons, And walk in the paths of righteousness, And walk not in the paths of violence; For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.' (91:19).
crossRefs: Genesis 49:1-2: Jacob calls his sons together and tells them to gather and listen while he says what will happen to them in days to come, the same deathbed assembly this chapter opens with.
Psalm 12:2: Men are charged with speaking flattery with a double heart, the Hebrew being a heart and a heart, which is the divided loyalty Enoch warns his sons off here.
Deuteronomy 12:2-3: Israel is commanded to tear down the altars of the nations, smash their pillars, burn their poles with fire and cut down the carved images of their gods.
Daniel 12:2: Many who sleep in the dust of the earth are said to awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame, which is what rising from sleep means in this chapter.
Isaiah 66:22: New heavens and a new earth are promised as things God makes and that remain before him, the same replacement this chapter puts in the tenth week.

translationNotes.term: Where the weeks are, and why they are out of order
translationNotes.note: This book divides history into ten periods and calls each one a week. The first seven are set out at 93:3-10 and the eighth, ninth and tenth are here at 91:12-17, so the second half stands two chapters ahead of the first. That is how the Ethiopic manuscripts carry it. An Aramaic copy of this book found among the Dead Sea Scrolls has the weeks in numerical order.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֵב וָלֵב (lev valev), a heart and a heart - Greek: δίψυχος (dipsychos), double-souled
translationNotes.note: Hebrew says it as a doubling: a man with a heart and a heart, one for what he says and one for what he means. The Greek of James 1:8 builds the same idea as a compound, a two-souled man unstable in all his ways, and 1 Chronicles 12:33 praises troops who came to David not of a double heart.

Chastisement in older English is corrective punishment, not annihilation. The word behind it is the ordinary term for the discipline a father gives a son, used that way at Proverbs 3:11-12. The chapter uses it for what comes from heaven on a world where violence has grown, which is a sentence with a purpose in it.

translationNotes.term: The idols of the heathen and their temples
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גּוֹיִם (goyim), the nations - Greek: ἔθνη (ethne), the nations
translationNotes.note: Heathen here is just the old English for the nations, the peoples outside Israel. Their idols were housed in temples and treated as living: washed, clothed, fed with daily offerings and carried in procession on festival days. That is what the law was aimed at when it commanded the altars pulled down and the images burned.

The chapter uses the same figure three times, at 91:5, 91:8 and 91:11. Cutting a tree down leaves a stump that sprouts again, and cutting it out at the root does not. The point of the repetition is that the removal described is meant to be final rather than a pruning.

translationNotes.term: A house shall be built for the Great King
translationNotes.note: The eighth week ends with the righteous acquiring houses and a house built in glory for the Great King. This book uses a house that way throughout, most plainly in the dream vision at 89:36 and 89:50, where a house is built for the Lord of the sheep and a tower raised on it.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch has Methuselah gather his brothers and charges them to love uprightness and keep clear of a double heart. He tells them violence will grow until judgement comes from heaven and the idols of the nations are burned, and the eighth, ninth and tenth weeks bring judgement, a new heaven and weeks without number.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 92
summaryBullets: The book written by Enoch-- Enoch indeed wrote this complete doctrine of wisdom, (which is) praised of all men and a judge of all the earth for all my children who shall dwell on the earth. And for the future generations who shall observe uprightness and peace. (92:1).
Let not your spirit be troubled on account of the times; For the Holy and Great One has appointed days for all things. (92:2).
And the righteous one shall arise from sleep, Shall arise and walk in the paths of righteousness, And all his path and conversation shall be in eternal goodness and grace. (92:3).

He will be gracious to the righteous and give him eternal uprightness, And He will give him power so that he shall be (endowed) with goodness and righteousness. And he shall walk in eternal light. (92:4).
And sin shall perish in darkness for ever, And shall no more be seen from that day for evermore. (92:5).
crossRefs: Ecclesiastes 3:1: There is a season for everything and a time for every matter under heaven, the same claim about appointed times that this chapter grounds its comfort on.
Psalm 31:15: My times are in your hand, says the psalmist while asking to be delivered from those who pursue him.
Isaiah 26:19: The dead are told they shall live and their bodies rise, and those who dwell in the dust are called to awake and sing for joy.
Proverbs 4:18: The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until full day, the same figure of a life that walks in growing light.
Wisdom 3:1-4: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and though in the sight of men they seemed to die, their hope is full of immortality.

translationNotes.note: This heading opens the section usually called the Epistle of Enoch, which runs from here to the end of the book. It is written as an address to his children and to the generations after them, and it keeps the shape of a letter: an opening, a body of exhortation and warning, and a closing charge about books at 104:12-13.

The word means teaching and nothing more. It comes from the Latin doctrina, a thing taught, and older English uses it for any body of instruction. Complete doctrine of wisdom at 92:1 means a full course of teaching, not a creed or a set of required beliefs.

Another word that has moved. In this English, a man's conversation is his whole way of life and conduct, not his talk. All his path and conversation at 92:3 means everything he does and the way he goes about it.

Sleep is the standing figure for death across Scripture, which is why kings are said to sleep with their fathers and why Daniel speaks of those who sleep in the dust of the earth awaking. When this chapter says the righteous one shall arise from sleep, it is using that figure and not describing an ordinary morning.

The comfort in 92:2 rests on a claim about time rather than about circumstances. Days are appointed, so a bad stretch is a stretch inside a fixed order and not a sign that the order has failed. Nothing is promised here about how long the stretch is.

stories.keyTakeaway: The book of Enoch is addressed to his children and to the generations after them. Because the Holy and Great One has appointed days for all things, they are told not to let their spirits be troubled by the times; the righteous will rise from sleep and walk in eternal light, and sin will perish in darkness.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 93
summaryBullets: And after that Enoch both †gave† and began to recount from the books. And Enoch said: 'Concerning the children of righteousness and concerning the elect of the world, And concerning the plant of uprightness, I will speak these things, Yea, I Enoch will declare (them) to you, my sons: According to that which appeared to me in the heavenly vision, And which I have known through the word of the holy angels, And have learnt from the heavenly tablets.' (93:1).

Concerning the children of righteousness and concerning the elect of the world, And concerning the plant of uprightness, I will speak these things, Yea, I Enoch will declare them to you, my sons. (93:2).
And Enoch began to recount from the books and said: 'I was born the seventh in the first week, While judgement and righteousness still endured. (93:3).

And after me there shall arise in the second week great wickedness, And deceit shall have sprung up; And in it there shall be the first end. And in it a man shall be saved; And after it is ended unrighteousness shall grow up, And a law shall be made for the sinners. (93:4).
And after that in the third week at its close A man shall be elected as the plant of righteous judgement, And his posterity shall become the plant of righteousness for evermore. (93:5).
And after that in the fourth week, at its close, Visions of the holy and righteous shall be seen, And a law for all generations and an enclosure shall be made for them. (93:6).
And after that in the fifth week, at its close, The house of glory and dominion shall be built for ever. (93:7).

And after that in the sixth week all who live in it shall be blinded, And the hearts of all of them shall godlessly forsake wisdom. And in it a man shall ascend; And at its close the house of dominion shall be burnt with fire, And the whole race of the chosen root shall be dispersed. (93:8).
And after that in the seventh week shall an apostate generation arise, And many shall be its deeds, And all its deeds shall be apostate. (93:9).
And at its close shall be elected The elect righteous of the eternal plant of righteousness, To receive sevenfold instruction concerning all His creation. (93:10).

For who is there of all the children of men that is able to hear the voice of the Holy One without being troubled? And who can think His thoughts? and who is there that can behold all the works of heaven? (93:11).

And how should there be one who could behold the heaven, and who is there that could understand the things of heaven and see a soul or a spirit and could tell thereof, or ascend and see all their ends and think them or do like them? (93:12).
And who is there of all men that could know what is the breadth and the length of the earth, and to whom has been shown the measure of all of them? (93:13).

Or is there any one who could discern the length of the heaven and how great is its height, and upon what it is founded, and how great is the number of the stars, and where all the luminaries rest? (93:14).
crossRefs: Jude 1:14: Enoch is named as the seventh from Adam, which is the position this chapter claims when it says he was born the seventh in the first week.
Genesis 6:8-9: Noah finds favour in the eyes of the Lord and is called a righteous man, blameless in his generation, who walked with God, the one man saved when the first end comes.
Job 38:4-5: God asks where a man was when the earth was founded and who determined its measurements, the same set of unanswerable questions this chapter ends on.
Isaiah 40:12-13: God is described measuring the waters in the hollow of his hand and marking off the heavens with a span, and asks who has measured his Spirit or been his counsellor.
Proverbs 30:4: A string of questions asks who has ascended to heaven and come down, gathered the wind in his fists and established all the ends of the earth.

translationNotes.note: Not seven days. The chapter divides all of history into ten stretches and calls each of them a week, so a week here is an age of unstated length. Enoch places himself inside the first one as the seventh born. The numbering runs one to seven here and picks up with the eighth at 91:12.

Count the line in Genesis 5 with Adam as the first: Adam, Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch. That makes Enoch the seventh, which is the description Jude 1:14 attaches to his name. Seventh is a position in a list here, not a value judgement.

The book's phrase for the flood. The second week brings great wickedness, a first end, and one man saved out of it, which is the same sequence this book told with animals at 89:1-9, where a bull becomes a man, builds a vessel and rides out the waters.

An enclosure is a walled fold: a rough stone ring or a courtyard where a flock is shut in at night, with one gap for a gate that the shepherd lies across. The fourth week gets a law and an enclosure together, and this book has already used a fold and a house the same way in the dream vision.

The chapter names three sources in one breath at 93:2: what appeared in the heavenly vision, what he learned from the word of the holy angels, and what he read on the heavenly tablets. The book consistently presents itself as a written report drawn from written things, not as remembered speech.

Planting is the book's regular figure for a line of people that is put in place deliberately and expected to last. A man is elected as the plant of righteous judgement and his posterity becomes the plant of righteousness for ever, so the figure covers both the individual and the line that comes from him.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch recounts from the books. He was born seventh in the first week, and the weeks run on through wickedness and a first end from which one man is saved, a man chosen as a plant of righteousness, a law and an enclosure, a house of glory, blindness and the burning of that house, and an apostate seventh week.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 94
summaryBullets: And now I say to you, my sons, love righteousness and walk therein; For the paths of righteousness are worthy of acceptation, But the paths of unrighteousness shall suddenly be destroyed and vanish. (94:1).
And to certain men of a generation shall the paths of violence and of death be revealed, And they shall hold themselves afar from them, And shall not follow them. (94:2).
And now I say to you the righteous: Walk not in the paths of wickedness, nor in the paths of death, And draw not near to them, lest you be destroyed. (94:3).
But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And you will live and prosper. (94:4).

And hold fast my words in the thoughts of your hearts, And suffer them not to be effaced from your hearts; For I know that sinners will tempt men to evilly-entreat wisdom, So that no place may be found for her, And no manner of temptation may minish. XCIV. 6-11. Woes for the Sinners . (94:5).
Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression And lay deceit as a foundation; For they shall be suddenly overthrown, And they shall have no peace. (94:6).

Woe to those who build their houses with sin; For from all their foundations shall they be overthrown, And by the sword shall they fall. And those who acquire gold and silver in judgement suddenly shall perish. (94:7).
Woe to you, you rich, for you have trusted in your riches, And from your riches shall you depart, Because you have not remembered the Most High in the days of your riches. (94:8).
You have committed blasphemy and unrighteousness, And have become ready for the day of slaughter, And the day of darkness and the day of the great judgement. (94:9).
Thus I speak and declare to you: He who has created you will overthrow you, And for your fall there shall be no compassion, And your Creator will rejoice at your destruction. (94:10).
And your righteous ones in those days shall be A reproach to the sinners and the godless. (94:11).
crossRefs: Psalm 1:1-6: Two ways are set side by side, the way of the righteous which the Lord knows and the way of the wicked which perishes, the same two-path frame this chapter opens with.
Proverbs 4:18-19: The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn and the way of the wicked is like deep darkness in which they do not know what makes them stumble.
Jeremiah 22:13: Woe is pronounced on the man who builds his house by unrighteousness and his upper rooms by injustice, making his neighbour work for nothing and not paying him his wages.
Isaiah 5:8: Woe falls on those who join house to house and field to field until there is no more room and they are made to dwell alone in the land.
Luke 12:16-21: A rich man plans bigger barns for his crops and tells himself to relax, and that night his life is required of him.

translationNotes.note: A woe is a funeral cry. The word was shouted over a corpse, and the prophets took it and aimed it at the living, so a woe is an announcement that someone is as good as dead. Isaiah, Amos and Habakkuk stack them in runs, and this book stacks them for the next dozen chapters.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: דֶּרֶךְ (derekh), way, road, manner of life
translationNotes.note: Hebrew uses the word for a road as the word for how a man lives, so a path is both a route and a pattern of conduct. Setting two of them side by side and telling the hearer to pick is a standard form; Deuteronomy 30:15-19 sets life and good against death and evil in exactly the same shape.

A house in that country was built on a footing of undressed stone laid in a trench, with sun-dried mudbrick above it. Get the footing wrong and the first heavy winter rain takes the wall down. The figure is not decoration; it names the one part of a building nobody can see and everything else rests on.

Wealth then was land, flocks, stored grain, oil and wine, silver by weight and slaves. There was nothing invisible about it and no way to hold it privately, which is why the prophets can name the rich as a class and why the charge against them is always specific: what they took, from whom, and what they did with the court.

The phrase treats the rich as livestock fattening toward a killing day. James 5:5 uses it the same way, telling the rich they have lived in luxury and fattened their hearts in a day of slaughter. The image is a beast eating well right up to the moment it is taken out.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch tells his sons to choose the paths of righteousness and keep off the paths of violence, then turns on the sinners with woes: on those who lay deceit as a foundation, on those who build their houses with sin, and on the rich who trusted their riches and never remembered the Most High.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 95
summaryBullets: Oh that mine eyes were a cloud of waters That I might weep over you, And pour down my tears as a cloud †of† waters: That so I might rest from my trouble of heart! (95:1).
†Who has permitted you to practice reproaches and wickedness? And so judgement shall overtake you, sinners. † (95:2).
Fear not the sinners, you righteous; For again will the Lord deliver them into your hands, That you may execute judgement upon them according to your desires. (95:3).
Woe to you who fulminate anathemas which cannot be reversed: Healing shall therefore be far from you because of your sins. (95:4).
Woe to you who requite your neighbour with evil; For you will be requited according to your works. (95:5).
Woe to you, lying witnesses, And to those who weigh out injustice, For suddenly shall you perish. (95:6).
Woe to you, sinners, for you persecute the righteous; For you will be delivered up and persecuted because of injustice, And heavy shall its yoke be upon you. (95:7).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 9:1: The prophet wishes his head were waters and his eyes a fountain of tears so that he might weep day and night for the slain of his people, the same wish in almost the same words.
Deuteronomy 19:16-19: A malicious witness who accuses a man falsely is investigated by the judges, and if he is lying he receives exactly what he intended to do to his brother.
Proverbs 20:23: Unequal weights are called an abomination to the Lord and a false balance is called not good, which is what weighing out injustice means.
Leviticus 19:18: The law forbids taking vengeance or bearing a grudge against one's own people and commands loving the neighbour as oneself.
Romans 12:17: Paul tells believers to repay no one evil for evil and to give thought to doing what is honourable in the sight of all.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἀνάθεμα (anathema), a thing devoted - Hebrew: חֵרֶם (cherem), the ban
translationNotes.note: An anathema is a curse pronounced with binding force, handing a person or thing over to destruction so that it cannot be bought back or taken into use. The Hebrew behind it is the ban, and Leviticus 27:28-29 says a thing under it may not be sold or redeemed. The woe here is aimed at men who use that weapon on their neighbours.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֵד שֶׁקֶר (ed sheqer), false witness
translationNotes.note: A capital case turned entirely on witnesses. No one could be put to death on the word of one man; two or three were required, and Deuteronomy 17:6-7 puts the witnesses' own hands on the condemned first, before the rest of the people. A false witness was therefore an executioner, which is why the law gives him the sentence he was trying to obtain.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֶבֶן וָאָבֶן (even va-even), a weight and a weight
translationNotes.note: Silver was weighed for every purchase, on a hand balance against stone weights a trader carried in a pouch. Hebrew names the fraud by doubling the word for stone: a weight and a weight, one heavy for buying and one light for selling. The law forbids carrying two sets, and the woe here is on men who used them.

A shaped wooden beam laid across the necks of a pair of oxen and tied under the throat, harnessing them to a plough or a cart. Because it is the thing that makes an animal work for someone else, it became the standard word for servitude, forced labour and tribute, which is the sense at 95:7.

translationNotes.term: Oh that mine eyes were a cloud of waters
translationNotes.note: The opening line puts the speaker in the position of a mourner rather than an accuser, weeping over the people he is about to pronounce woe on. Jeremiah opens the same way. The wish is for enough water to weep with, which is a way of saying the grief is larger than the man.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch wishes his eyes were a cloud of water so he could weep over the sinners, and tells the righteous not to fear them. Woes fall on those who pronounce curses that cannot be taken back, who repay a neighbour with evil, who bear false witness and weigh out injustice, and who persecute the righteous.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 96
summaryBullets: Be hopeful, you righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you, And you will have lordship over them according to your desires. (96:1).

And in the day of the tribulation of the sinners, Your children shall mount and rise as eagles, And higher than the vultures will be your nest, And you will ascend and enter the crevices of the earth, And the clefts of the rock for ever as coneys before the unrighteous, And the sirens shall sigh because of you-and weep. (96:2).
Wherefore fear not, you that have suffered; For healing shall be your portion, And a bright light shall enlighten you, And the voice of rest you will hear from heaven. (96:3).

Woe to you, you sinners, for your riches make you appear like the righteous, But your hearts convict you of being sinners, And this fact shall be a testimony against you for a memorial of (your) evil deeds. (96:4).
Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls , And tread under foot the lowly with your might. (96:5).
Woe to you who drink water from every fountain , For suddenly shall you be consumed and wither away, Because you have forsaken the fountain of life. (96:6).
Woe to you who work unrighteousness And deceit and blasphemy: It shall be a memorial against you for evil. (96:7).

Woe to you, you mighty, Who with might oppress the righteous; For the day of your destruction is coming. In those days many and good days shall come to the righteous--in the day of your judgement. (96:8).
crossRefs: Amos 6:4-7: Men lie on beds of ivory, eat lambs from the flock, drink wine in bowls and anoint themselves with the finest oils, and are not grieved over the ruin of their people.
Amos 2:6-7: The righteous are sold for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and the head of the poor is trampled into the dust of the earth.
Jeremiah 2:13: A people are charged with two evils, forsaking the fountain of living waters and hewing out for themselves broken cisterns that can hold no water.
Isaiah 40:31: Those who wait for the Lord are promised that they will mount up with wings like eagles, run and not be weary, and walk and not faint.
Psalm 104:18: The high mountains are for the wild goats and the rocks are a refuge for the rock badgers, the small cliff-dwelling animal this chapter calls the coney.

translationNotes.note: Not rabbits. The coney of older English Bibles is the rock hyrax, a thickset animal about the size of a large cat that lives in colonies in the rock crevices of the Judean hills and the cliffs above the Dead Sea, and vanishes into a crack at any alarm. Proverbs 30:26 calls them a people not mighty who make their homes in the cliffs, which is exactly the picture this verse wants.

Nothing to do with mermaids or with alarms. The Greek Old Testament uses this word for the wild creatures that howl in a ruined and abandoned place, standing where the Hebrew has jackals or ostriches, as at Isaiah 13:21 and Micah 1:8. Sirens sighing is the sound of desolation, not of song.

The word Amos uses for the vessel these men drink from is the name of the broad basin used to catch sacrificial blood and dash it against the altar. Drinking wine out of one is drinking by the basinful, out of a vessel made for the altar. The insult is in the size and in the choice of container at once.

Wheat was the expensive grain and barley was what most people ate; fine flour was wheat sifted to the top grade, and it is what the law calls for in the grain offering. A household eating sifted wheat every day was announcing what it could afford, which is why the woe pairs it with treading the lowly underfoot.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַיִם חַיִּים (mayim chayyim), living water
translationNotes.note: Hebrew calls running spring water living water and sets it against still water stored in a cistern. A spring gives without being filled and a cistern holds only what is carried to it and cracks. That contrast is the whole of the woe here and it is what Jeremiah 2:13 is built on.

stories.keyTakeaway: The righteous are told to be hopeful because the sinners will perish before them. Woes follow on those whose riches make them look righteous, on those who eat the finest of the wheat and drink wine from bowls while treading the lowly underfoot, and on the mighty who oppress.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 97
summaryBullets: Believe, you righteous, that the sinners will become a shame And perish in the day of unrighteousness. (97:1).
Be it known to you (you sinners) that the Most High is mindful of your destruction, And the angels of heaven rejoice over your destruction. (97:2).
What will you do, you sinners, And where will you flee on that day of judgement, When you hear the voice of the prayer of the righteous? (97:3).
Yea, you will fare like to them, Against whom this word shall be a testimony: "You have been companions of sinners." (97:4).
And in those days the prayer of the righteous shall reach to the Lord, And for you the days of your judgement shall come. (97:5).

And all the words of your unrighteousness shall be read out before the Great Holy One, And your faces shall be covered with shame, And He will reject every work which is grounded on unrighteousness. (97:6).
Woe to you, you sinners, who live on the mid ocean and on the dry land, Whose remembrance is evil against you. (97:7).
Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: "We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired. (97:8).

And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, 9 d And many are the husbandmen in our houses." 9 e And our granaries are (brim) full as with water, 10 Yea and like water your lies shall flow away; For your riches shall not abide But speedily ascend from you; For you have acquired it all in unrighteousness, And you will be given over to a great curse. (97:9).
crossRefs: James 5:1-4: The rich are told to weep and howl, their gold and silver are corroded, and the wages kept back by fraud from the labourers who mowed their fields are crying out against them.
Amos 5:11-12: Men who trample the poor and take grain from them build houses of hewn stone but will not live in them, and plant pleasant vineyards but will not drink their wine.
Revelation 8:3-4: The smoke of incense rises before God together with the prayers of all the saints from the hand of an angel at the altar.
Habakkuk 2:9-11: Woe to the man who gets evil gain for his house to set his nest on high, for the stone will cry out from the wall and the beam from the woodwork will answer it.
Psalm 34:15: The eyes of the Lord are toward the righteous and his ears are open to their cry, which is the hearing this chapter says will arrive on a fixed day.

translationNotes.note: Farm workers. In older English a husbandman is a man who works the soil, and husbandry is farming; the word has nothing to do with marriage. Many husbandmen in our houses at 97:9 is a boast about the size of the workforce a household could employ.

Grain had to be held for a full year and through a bad one. It was stored in plastered pits, in large jars and in built silos, kept dry and guarded, and a man with full granaries in a lean year held his neighbours' lives in his hand. That is why a boast about storage is a boast about power.

translationNotes.term: On the mid ocean and on the dry land
translationNotes.note: A figure that names two extremes to mean everything in between, the way Hebrew says heaven and earth for the whole creation or from Dan to Beersheba for the whole land. Sea and dry land is not a list of two places; it is a way of saying that no place is outside the woe.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כֶּסֶף (keseph), silver, and also money
translationNotes.note: For most of the period behind these books silver was weighed and not counted. Wealth was held as ingots, cut pieces and jewellery, put on a balance for every deal, which is why the same Hebrew word means both silver and money. Acquiring silver, in the boast at 97:8, means accumulating weighed metal in a strongroom.

translationNotes.term: Read out before the Great Holy One
translationNotes.note: The book keeps returning to one courtroom picture: a written record, kept daily, carried in, and read aloud in the presence of the judge. It runs the seventy shepherds that way at 89:61-64 and repeats it at 98:7-8. This chapter applies it to the sinners' own words.

stories.keyTakeaway: The righteous are told to believe that the sinners will be shamed, and the sinners are asked where they will flee on the day of judgement when the prayer of the righteous reaches the Lord and every word of their unrighteousness is read out. Woe falls on those who gathered silver and gold unjustly and boast of full granaries.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 98
summaryBullets: And now I swear to you, to the wise and to the foolish, For you will have manifold experiences on the earth. (98:1).

For you men shall put on more adornments than a woman, And coloured garments more than a virgin: In royalty and in grandeur and in power, And in silver and in gold and in purple, And in splendour and in food they shall be poured out as water. (98:2).

Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire. (98:3).

I have sworn to you, you sinners, as a mountain has not become a slave, And a hill does not become the handmaid of a woman, Even so sin has not been sent upon the earth, But man of himself has created it, And under a great curse shall they fall who commit it. (98:4).
And barrenness has not been given to the woman, But on account of the deeds of her own hands she dies without children. (98:5).
I have sworn to you, you sinners, by the Holy Great One, That all your evil deeds are revealed in the heavens, And that none of your deeds of oppression are covered and hidden. (98:6).
And do not think in your spirit nor say in your heart that you do not know and that you do not see that every sin is every day recorded in heaven in the presence of the Most High. (98:7).
From henceforth you know that all your oppression with which you oppress is written down every day till the day of your judgement. (98:8).
Woe to you, you fools, for through your folly shall you perish: and you transgress against the wise, and so good hap shall not be your portion. (98:9).

And now, know you that you are prepared for the day of destruction: wherefore do not hope to live, you sinners, but you will depart and die; for you know no ransom; for you are prepared for the day of the great judgement, for the day of tribulation and great shame for your spirits. (98:10).

Woe to you, you obstinate of heart, who work wickedness and eat blood: Whence have you good things to eat and to drink and to be filled? paragraph continues From all the good things which the Lord the Most High has placed in abundance on the earth; therefore you will have no peace. (98:11).

Woe to you who love the deeds of unrighteousness: wherefore do you hope for good hap to yourselves? know that you will be delivered into the hands of the righteous, and they shall cut off your necks and slay you, and have no mercy upon you. (98:12).
Woe to you who rejoice in the tribulation of the righteous; for no grave shall be dug for you. (98:13).
Woe to you who set at nought the words of the righteous; for you will have no hope of life. (98:14).
Woe to you who write down lying and godless words; for they write down their lies that men may hear them and act godlessly towards (their) neighbour. (98:15).
Therefore they shall have no peace but die a sudden death. (98:16).
crossRefs: Genesis 4:7: Sin is described as crouching at the door with its desire against a man, who is told that he must rule over it.
James 1:13-15: No one is to say he is tempted by God, since each person is lured and enticed by his own desire, which conceives and gives birth to sin.
Isaiah 3:16-24: A long inventory of finery is listed and then taken away, the anklets, headbands, crescents, pendants, bracelets, signet rings, nose rings, festal robes, mirrors and veils.
Leviticus 17:10-14: Anyone who eats blood is cut off, because the life of the flesh is in the blood and it was given for making atonement on the altar.
Psalm 56:8: God is said to keep count of a man's tossings and to store his tears in a bottle, and the psalmist asks whether they are not in his book.

translationNotes.note: Purple was a dye squeezed from a gland in the murex sea snail, gathered on the Phoenician coast. It took thousands of shells to dye a single garment, so purple cloth cost a fortune and in practice marked out royalty and the very rich. Acts 16:14 introduces a woman of Thyatira as a seller of purple, which is a way of saying she was wealthy.

Blood was never eaten. An animal was bled out and the blood poured on the ground or dashed against the altar, because the life of the creature was held to be in it. The rule predates the law given at Sinai and is repeated in it, so eating blood at 98:11 is not a dietary lapse but a deliberate crossing of a line everyone knew was there.

An old English phrase meaning good luck or a good outcome. Hap is chance or fortune, the same root that gives us happen and happy. Good hap shall not be your portion at 98:9 means things will not turn out well for you.

A ransom is the payment that buys a life out of a penalty. Israel's law allows it in some cases and forbids it absolutely in one: Numbers 35:31 says no ransom may be taken for the life of a murderer. Telling the sinners they know no ransom at 98:10 puts them in that category, where money cannot reach.

translationNotes.term: No grave shall be dug for you
translationNotes.note: Being left unburied was the worst thing that could be said about a man's end. Bodies were washed, wrapped and laid in a family tomb, and a corpse left in the open for dogs and birds was the standard shape of a curse; Jeremiah 22:19 says a king will be buried with the burial of a donkey, dragged out and thrown beyond the gates of Jerusalem.

translationNotes.term: Sin has not been sent upon the earth
translationNotes.note: The chapter states it under oath at 98:4 and argues it from two impossibilities: a mountain does not become a slave and a hill does not become a woman's servant. Sin was not issued from above and did not arrive as part of the arrangement of things. On this book's account man produced it himself.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch swears to the wise and the foolish. Men will put on more finery than women and be poured out in silver, gold and purple and perish with it, and sin was not sent down on the earth but made by man himself. Every act of oppression is written down in heaven every day until the day of judgement.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 99
summaryBullets: Woe to you who work godlessness, And glory in lying and extol them: You will perish, and no happy life shall be yours. (99:1).

Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law, And transform themselves into what they were not into sinners : They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth. (99:2).

In those days make ready, you righteous, to raise your prayers as a memorial, And place them as a testimony before the angels, That they may place the sin of the sinners for a memorial before the Most High. (99:3).
In those days the nations shall be stirred up, And the families of the nations shall arise on the day of destruction. (99:4).

And in those days the destitute shall go forth and carry off their children, And they shall abandon them, so that their children shall perish through them: Yea, they shall abandon their children (that are still) sucklings, and not return to them, And shall have no pity on their beloved ones. (99:5).
And again I swear to you, you sinners, that sin is prepared for a day of unceasing bloodshed. (99:6).

And they who worship stones, and grave images of gold and silver and wood and stone and clay, and those who worship impure spirits and demons, and all kinds of idols not according to knowledge, shall get no manner of help from them. (99:7).
And they shall become godless by reason of the folly of their hearts, And their eyes shall be blinded through the fear of their hearts And through visions in their dreams. (99:8).
Through these they shall become godless and fearful; For they shall have wrought all their work in a lie, And shall have worshiped a stone: Therefore in an instant shall they perish. (99:9).

But in those days blessed are all they who accept the words of wisdom, and understand them, And observe the paths of the Most High, and walk in the path of His righteousness, And become not godless with the godless; For they shall be saved. (99:10).
Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbours; For you shall be slain in Sheol. (99:11).
Woe to you who make deceitful and false measures, And (to them) who cause bitterness on the earth; For they shall thereby be utterly consumed. (99:12).
Woe to you who build your houses through the grievous toil of others, And all their building materials are the bricks and stones of sin; I tell you you will have no peace. (99:13).
Woe to them who reject the measure and eternal heritage of their fathers And whose souls follow after idols; For they shall have no rest. (99:14).
Woe to them who work unrighteousness and help oppression, And slay their neighbours until the day of the great judgement. (99:15).

For He shall cast down your glory, And bring affliction on your hearts, And shall arouse His fierce indignation , And destroy you all with the sword; And all the holy and righteous shall remember your sins. (99:16).
crossRefs: Isaiah 44:9-17: A man cuts down a tree, burns half of it to warm himself and bake his bread, and out of what is left makes a god, bows down to it and prays to it to deliver him.
Psalm 115:4-8: Idols of silver and gold are the work of human hands, with mouths that do not speak and eyes that do not see, and those who make them become like them.
Amos 8:4-6: Traders wait for the new moon to be over so they can sell grain, making the measure small and the shekel heavy and cheating with false balances.
Micah 6:10-11: Scant measures, wicked scales and a bag of deceitful weights are named as things the Lord will not acquit a man for holding.
Deuteronomy 27:17: A curse is pronounced on anyone who moves his neighbour's boundary marker, the stone that fixed a family's allotted land.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פֶּסֶל (pesel), carved image - מַסֵּכָה (massekah), cast image
translationNotes.note: Hebrew keeps two words apart that English blurs. A pesel is cut from wood or stone; a massekah is poured metal, often a wooden core sheathed in beaten gold or silver. Either way the finished figure was housed in a temple and treated as a resident: washed, dressed, given food and drink daily and carried out in procession on festival days.

The Hebrew word appears twice in Scripture and both times the offering is human. Deuteronomy 32:17 says they sacrificed to demons that were not God, and Psalm 106:37 says outright that they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons. That is the practice standing behind the word in 99:7.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵיפָה (ephah), dry measure - שֶׁקֶל (sheqel), a weight
translationNotes.note: The ephah was the standard dry measure, holding somewhere near twenty-two litres, and the shekel was the standard weight, about eleven and a half grams judging from inscribed stone weights dug up in Judah. A trader with a shallow ephah for selling grain and a heavy shekel for taking payment robbed every customer twice, in the open, which is what Amos 8:5 describes.

The Hebrew name for the place of the dead. It is always spoken of as down, dark and silent, and everyone goes there.
