The Greek Old Testament renders it Hades, and older English Bibles often print it as hell or the grave, which is why the same underlying word can look like three different places in translation.

translationNotes.term: The eternal heritage of their fathers
translationNotes.note: A family's land was not simply property. It was the portion assigned to that clan, and Leviticus 25:23-28 says the land is not to be sold in perpetuity and must return to the family in the jubilee year. That is why moving a boundary stone falls under a curse, and why Naboth refuses to sell his vineyard to a king.

translationNotes.term: The bricks and stones of sin
translationNotes.note: Ordinary building material. Bricks were clay mixed with straw and dried in the sun, laid on a footing of field stone, and every one of them was made and carried by hand. Building your house through the grievous toil of others means labour taken without paying for it, which is what the woe at 99:13 is naming.

stories.keyTakeaway: More woes: on those who glory in lying, who pervert the words of uprightness and transgress the eternal law, who worship stones and images of gold, silver, wood and clay, who make false measures, who build their houses out of other men's labour, and who help oppression and kill their neighbours.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 100
summaryBullets: And in those days in one place the fathers together with their sons shall be smitten And brothers one with another shall fall in death Till the streams flow with their blood. 2 .For a man shall not withhold his hand from slaying his sons and his sons' sons, And the sinner shall not withhold his hand from his honoured brother: From dawn till sunset they shall slay one another. (100:1).

For a man shall not withhold his hand from slaying his sons and his sons' sons, And the sinner shall not withhold his hand from his honoured brother: From dawn till sunset they shall slay one another. (100:2).

And the horse shall walk up to the breast in the blood of sinners, And the chariot shall be submerged to its height. 4 In those days the angels shall descend into the secret places And gather together into one place all those who brought down sin And the Most High will arise on that day of judgement To execute great judgement amongst sinners. (100:3).

In those days the angels shall descend into the secret places And gather together into one place all those who brought down sin, And the Most High will arise on that day of judgement To execute great judgement amongst sinners. (100:4).

And over all the righteous and holy He will appoint guardians from amongst the holy angels To guard them as the apple of an eye, Until He makes an end of all wickedness and all sin, And though the righteous sleep a long sleep, they have nought to fear. (100:5).

And (then) the children of the earth shall see the wise in security , And shall understand all the words of this book, And recognize that their riches shall not be able to save them In the overthrow of their sins. (100:6).
Woe to you, Sinners, on the day of strong anguish, You who afflict the righteous and burn them with fire: You will be requited according to your works. (100:7).
Woe to you, you obstinate of heart, Who watch in order to devise wickedness: Therefore shall fear come upon you And there shall be none to help you. (100:8).

Woe to you, you sinners, on account of the words of your mouth, And on account of the deeds of your hands which your godlessness as wrought, In blazing flames burning worse than fire shall you burn. 10 And now, know you that from the angels He will inquire as to your deeds in heaven, from the sun and from the moon and from the stars in reference to your sins because upon the earth you execute judgement on the righteous. (100:9).

And now, know you that from the angels He will inquire as to your deeds in heaven, from the sun and from the moon and from the stars in reference to your sins because upon the earth you execute judgement on the righteous. (100:10).

And He will summon to testify against you every cloud and mist and dew and rain; for they shall all be withheld because of you from descending upon you, and they shall be mindful of your sins. (100:11).
And now give presents to the rain that it be not withheld from descending upon you, nor yet the dew, when it has received gold and silver from you that it may descend. (100:12).
When the hoar-frost and snow with their chilliness, and all the snow-storms with all their plagues fall upon you, in those days you will not be able to stand before them. (100:13).
crossRefs: Micah 7:2-6: A man's enemies are the people of his own house, son treats father with contempt and daughter rises against mother, and no upright man is left in the land.
Revelation 14:20: The winepress is trodden outside the city and blood flows from it as high as a horse's bridle for about sixteen hundred stadia.
Zechariah 2:8: Whoever touches God's people is said to touch the pupil of his eye, the same phrase this chapter uses for how the guardians keep the righteous.
Deuteronomy 32:1: Moses opens his song by calling on the heavens to give ear and the earth to hear, summoning them as witnesses to what he is about to say.
Psalm 91:11: God is said to command his angels concerning a man, to guard him in all his ways, which is the arrangement this chapter describes for the righteous.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אִישׁוֹן (ishon), the pupil, literally the little man
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew word for the pupil is a small form of the word for man, because if you look closely into someone's eye you see a tiny reflection of yourself standing in it. The point of the phrase is that the pupil is the most delicate part of the body and the one the whole body moves to protect without being asked.

translationNotes.term: Blood to the breast of a horse
translationNotes.note: A deliberate exaggeration for slaughter past counting. The measure is the depth a rider's mount would have to wade through, and Revelation 14:20 pushes the same image up to the bridle. Neither text is reporting a level; both are saying the killing is beyond what a number could carry.

This is a sneer about bribery, and it lands because bribery worked. The law bans it in the strongest terms, saying a bribe blinds the clear-sighted and twists the words of the righteous, and the prophets treat a bought court as the ordinary condition of things. The verse tells men who buy verdicts to try buying weather.

translationNotes.term: Every cloud and mist and dew and rain summoned to testify
translationNotes.note: This is the form of a covenant lawsuit. When Israel was given terms, heaven and earth were called as witnesses to the transaction, and the prophets later summon those same witnesses when they bring the charge, as Micah 6:1-2 does with the mountains. Calling the weather to the stand is the same legal move applied to the sinners.

translationNotes.term: Guardians from amongst the holy angels
translationNotes.note: The arrangement mirrors the one in the dream vision and reverses it. There, seventy shepherds were put over the flock and destroyed more than they were allowed. Here, guardians are appointed over the righteous with a single instruction, to guard them, and the section that follows says nothing about them exceeding it.

stories.keyTakeaway: Fathers, sons and brothers cut each other down from dawn to sunset until the streams run with blood and a horse walks breast-deep in it. Angels gather those who brought down sin, guardians are set over the righteous, and the sinners are told the sun, moon, stars, clouds and rain will testify against them.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 101
summaryBullets: Observe the heaven, you children of heaven, and every work of the Most High, and fear you Him and work no evil in His presence. (101:1).
If He closes the windows of heaven, and withholds the rain and the dew from descending on the earth on your account, what will you do then? (101:2).
And if He sends His anger upon you because of your deeds, you cannot petition Him; for you spoke proud and insolent words against His righteousness: therefore you will have no peace. (101:3).
And see you not the sailors of the ships, how their ships are tossed to and fro by the waves, and are shaken by the winds, and are in sore trouble? (101:4).

And therefore do they fear because all their goodly possessions go upon the sea with them, and they have evil forebodings of heart that the sea will swallow them and they will perish therein. (101:5).
Are not the entire sea and all its waters, and all its movements, the work of the Most High, and has He not set limits to its doings, and confined it throughout by the sand? (101:6).
And at His reproof it is afraid and dries up, and all its fish die and all that is in it; But you sinners that are on the earth fear Him not. (101:7).
Has He not made the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein? Who has given understanding and wisdom to everything that moves on the earth and in the sea. (101:8).
Do not the sailors of the ships fear the sea? Yet sinners fear not the Most High. (101:9).
crossRefs: Job 38:8-11: God asks who shut in the sea with doors, made the cloud its garment, and set a limit for it saying that its proud waves come this far and no farther.
Jeremiah 5:22: God says he placed the sand as the boundary for the sea, a perpetual barrier it cannot pass, so that the waves toss and roar but do not prevail.
Psalm 107:23-30: Men who go down to the sea in ships see the storm lifted, reel like drunkards at their wits' end, cry out, and are brought to their desired haven when the waves are hushed.
Nahum 1:4: God rebukes the sea and makes it dry and dries up all the rivers, which is what the sea being afraid at his reproof means.
Genesis 7:11: The fountains of the great deep burst open and the windows of the heavens were opened, the same picture of rain kept above and released through openings.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֲרֻבּוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם (arubbot hashamayim), the windows of heaven
translationNotes.note: The picture behind the phrase is of water held above a solid sky and let down through openings that can be shut. Genesis uses it when the flood begins, and 2 Kings 7:2 has an officer sneer at a promise of cheap grain by asking whether the Lord could make windows in heaven. This chapter's threat is simply that the windows stay closed.

Israel was not a seafaring people. When Solomon wanted a fleet he had to borrow crews, and 1 Kings 9:27 says Hiram sent his own servants, seamen who knew the sea, to work with Solomon's men. The sea in these books is the frightening edge of the world, and the argument here rests on that: even men who make their living on it are afraid of it.

translationNotes.term: All their goodly possessions go upon the sea with them
translationNotes.note: A trading voyage put everything in one hull. The merchant sailed with his own cargo, there was no insurance and no way off, and a single storm took the goods, the ship and the crew together. That is why the chapter treats a sailor's fear as the most reasonable fear a man can have.

translationNotes.term: Confined it throughout by the sand
translationNotes.note: The boundary named is not a cliff or a wall but a beach. Sand is the least substantial thing that could hold back an ocean, and Scripture uses exactly that detail to make the point that the limit holds because it was set and not because it is strong.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יָרֵא (yare), to fear, to revere
translationNotes.note: One Hebrew verb covers being frightened of something and holding it in awe, and this chapter runs both senses against each other on purpose. Sailors fear the sea in the first sense. The sinners do not fear the Most High in the second, and the chapter's whole argument is that the smaller thing gets the respect the greater one does not.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch tells them to look at the heaven and every work of the Most High and to fear him. If he shuts the windows of heaven and holds back rain and dew, nothing can be done about it; sailors fear the sea because everything they own rides on it, yet the sea itself is his work and is fenced in by the sand.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 102
summaryBullets: In those days when He has brought a grievous fire upon you, Whither will you flee, and where will you find deliverance? And when He launches forth His Word against you Will you not be affrighted and fear? (102:1).
And all the luminaries shall be affrighted with great fear, And all the earth shall be affrighted and tremble and be alarmed. (102:2).

And all the †angels shall execute their commands† And shall seek to hide themselves from the presence of the Great Glory, And the children of earth shall tremble and quake; And you sinners shall be cursed for ever, And you will have no peace. (102:3).
Fear you not, you souls of the righteous, And be hopeful you that have died in righteousness. (102:4).

And grieve not if your soul into Sheol has descended in grief, And that in your life your body fared not according to your goodness, But wait for the day of the judgement of sinners And for the day of cursing and chastisement. (102:5).
And yet when you die the sinners speak over you: "As we die, so die the righteous, And what benefit do they reap for their deeds? (102:6).
Behold, even as we, so do they die in grief and darkness, And what have they more than we? From henceforth we are equal. (102:7).
And what will they receive and what will they see for ever? Behold, they too have died, And henceforth for ever shall they see no light." (102:8).
I tell you, you sinners, you are content to eat and drink, and rob and sin, and strip men naked, and acquire wealth and see good days. (102:9).
Have you seen the righteous how their end falls out, that no manner of violence is found in them till their death? (102:10).
"Nevertheless they perished and became as though they had not been, and their spirits descended into Sheol in tribulation." (102:11).
crossRefs: Wisdom 3:1-4: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God and no torment will touch them, and though in the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died, they are at peace.
Malachi 3:14-15: People are quoted saying it is vain to serve God and asking what profit there is in keeping his charge, and calling the arrogant blessed.
Ecclesiastes 3:19-20: The Preacher observes that the same event happens to man and beast, that all go to one place, and that all are from the dust and return to dust.
Psalm 73:3-12: The psalmist admits he envied the arrogant when he saw the prosperity of the wicked, who have no pangs, are not in trouble like other men and always increase in riches.
Isaiah 2:19: Men go into the caves of the rocks and the holes of the ground from before the terror of the Lord when he rises to terrify the earth.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נֶפֶשׁ (nephesh), soul, living being - רוּחַ (ruach), breath, wind, spirit
translationNotes.note: The two words are not interchangeable. Nephesh is the living creature itself, from a root for throat and breathing, so it can be translated soul, life, person or appetite. Ruach is moving air: wind, breath, and by extension spirit. This chapter uses both within a few lines and English flattens the difference.

One of this book's titles for God, standing in for the presence itself. The Hebrew word is built on a root meaning heavy, so glory is weight, substance, the thing that carries the most. It is what fills the tabernacle at Exodus 40:34-35 so that Moses cannot go in.

translationNotes.term: The sinners' speech is quoted, not endorsed
translationNotes.note: Verses 102:6-11 are in quotation marks in this translation for a reason. They are what the sinners say over the graves of the righteous: that everyone dies alike and there is no difference. The book answers it in the chapter that follows. Reading those verses as the book's own view gets the passage backwards.

The word is treated as a thing sent, the way a spear or an arrow is sent. The same picture is drawn out in Wisdom 18:15-16, where the all-powerful word leaps from heaven like a stern warrior carrying a sharp sword. Nothing here is about speaking; it is about dispatch.

The comfort at 102:5 concedes the facts rather than denying them. It does not say the righteous were spared a hard death or a sorrowful burial. It says they should not draw a conclusion from it, and tells them to wait for a day the book names.

stories.keyTakeaway: When the fire comes the luminaries and the whole earth are terrified and the sinners have nowhere to flee. The souls of the righteous are told not to grieve if they went down to Sheol in sorrow, and the sinners' own speech is quoted: the righteous die as we die and have nothing more than we have.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 103
summaryBullets: Now, therefore, I swear to you, the righteous, by the glory of the Great and Honoured and 2 Mighty One in dominion, and by His greatness I swear to you: (103:1).
I know a mystery And have read the heavenly tablets, And have seen the holy books, And have found written therein and inscribed regarding them: (103:2).

That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living. (103:3).

And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, And their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One To all the generations of the world: wherefore no longer fear their contumely. (103:4).
Woe to you, you sinners, when you have died, If you die in the wealth of your sins, And those who are like you say regarding you: 'Blessed are the sinners: they have seen all their days. (103:5).

And how they have died in prosperity and in wealth, And have not seen tribulation or murder in their life; And they have died in honour, And judgement has not been executed on them during their life." (103:6).
Know you, that their souls will be made to descend into Sheol And they shall be wretched in their great tribulation. (103:7).

And into darkness and chains and a burning flame where there is grievous judgement shall your spirits enter; And the great judgement shall be for all the generations of the world. Woe to you, for you will have no peace. (103:8).

Say not in regard to the righteous and good who are in life: "In our troubled days we have toiled laboriously and experienced every trouble, And met with much evil and been consumed, And have become few and our spirit small. (103:9).
And we have been destroyed and have not found any to help us even with a word: We have been tortured and destroyed , and not hoped to see life from day to day. (103:10).

We hoped to be the head and have become the tail: We have toiled laboriously and had no satisfaction in our toil; And we have become the food of the sinners and the unrighteous, And they have laid their yoke heavily upon us. (103:11).
They have had dominion over us that hated us †and smote us; And to those that hated us† we have bowed our necks But they pitied us not. (103:12).
We desired to get away from them that we might escape and be at rest, But found no place whereunto we should flee and be safe from them. (103:13).
And are complained to the rulers in our tribulation, And cried out against those who devoured us, But they did not attend to our cries And would not hearken to our voice. (103:14).

And they helped those who robbed us and devoured us and those who made us few; and they concealed their oppression, and they did not remove from us the yoke of those that devoured us and dispersed us and murdered us, and they concealed their murder, and remembered not that they had lifted up their hands against us. (103:15).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 28:13: The Lord promises to make his people the head and not the tail, always at the top and never at the bottom, which is the exact pair of words the complaint here reverses.
Ecclesiastes 4:1: The Preacher looks at all the oppressions done under the sun, sees the tears of the oppressed with no one to comfort them, and notes that power was on the side of their oppressors.
Exodus 2:23-25: The people groan under their slavery and cry out, and their cry comes up to God, who hears their groaning and remembers his covenant.
Wisdom 5:1-5: The righteous man stands with great confidence before those who afflicted him, and they say in astonishment that this was the man they once held in derision.
Psalm 73:16-19: The psalmist says the prosperity of the wicked was wearisome to him until he went into the sanctuary of God and then discerned their end.

translationNotes.note: A fixed proverbial pair from the blessings and curses of Deuteronomy 28, where being the head means lending and ruling and being the tail means borrowing and serving. When the oppressed at 103:11 say they hoped to be the head and have become the tail, they are quoting that passage back and saying they got the curse instead.

translationNotes.original: Aramaic: רָז (raz), a secret - Greek: μυστήριον (mysterion)
translationNotes.note: A mystery in this vocabulary is not a puzzle that stays dark. It is something hidden that has now been shown to someone, which is exactly how Daniel uses the Aramaic word when the king's dream is revealed to him at night. Enoch says he knows one because he has read the tablets, not because he has worked it out.

An old word for insulting contempt, the kind aimed at humiliating someone in public rather than merely insulting them. Fear their contumely at 103:4 means do not be troubled by their sneering. The word is dead in modern English and looks like a misprint.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׁעַר (shaar), the gate, the place of judgement
translationNotes.note: Legal business happened in the open space just inside the city gate. Elders sat there, cases were heard in public, witnesses were produced and deals were closed in front of everyone, which is where Boaz settles the matter of Ruth. The complaint at 103:14-15 is that this system was bought, and that the men who ran it protected the ones doing the robbing.

translationNotes.term: Died in prosperity and in wealth
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׂבַע יָמִים (seva yamim), full of days
translationNotes.note: The formula for a good end was to die old and full of days, with property intact and sons to bury you. That is what the sinners at 103:5-6 are congratulating each other on. The chapter does not dispute that they got it; it disputes that it settles anything.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch swears by the glory of the Mighty One that he has read the heavenly tablets and found good and joy written down for the spirits of those who died in righteousness, warns the sinners that their souls go down to Sheol, and then quotes the complaint of the oppressed whose cries the rulers would not hear.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 104
summaryBullets: I swear to you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One. (104:1).

Be hopeful; for aforetime you were put to shame through ill and affliction; but now you will shine as the lights of heaven, you will shine and you will be seen, and the portals of heaven shall be opened to you. (104:2).
And in your cry, cry for judgement, and it shall appear to you; for all your tribulation shall be visited on the rulers, and on all who helped those who plundered you. (104:3).
Be hopeful, and cast not away your hopes for you will have great joy as the angels of heaven. (104:4).

What shall you be obliged to do? You will not have to hide on the day of the great judgement and you will not be found as sinners, and the eternal judgement shall be far from you for all the generations of the world. (104:5).

And now fear not, you righteous, when you see the sinners growing strong and prospering in their ways: be not companions with them, but keep afar from their violence; for you will become companions of the hosts of heaven. (104:6).
And, although you sinners say: "All our sins shall not be searched out and be written down," nevertheless they shall write down all your sins every day. paragraph continues (104:7).
And now I show to you that light and darkness, day and night, see all your sins. (104:8).

Be not godless in your hearts, and lie not and alter not the words of uprightness, nor charge with lying the words of the Holy Great One, nor take account of your idols; for all your lying and all your godlessness issue not in righteousness but in great sin. (104:9).

And now I know this mystery, that sinners will alter and pervert the words of righteousness in many ways, and will speak wicked words, and lie, and practice great deceits, and write books concerning their words. (104:10).

But when they write down truthfully all my words in their languages, and do not change or minish ought from my words but write them all down truthfully--all that I first testified concerning them. (104:11).
Then, I know another mystery, that books will be given to the righteous and the wise to become a cause of joy and uprightness and much wisdom. (104:12).

And to them shall the books be given, and they shall believe in them and rejoice over them, and then shall all the righteous who have learnt therefrom all the paths of uprightness be recompensed.' (104:13).
crossRefs: Daniel 12:3: Those who are wise are promised that they will shine like the brightness of the sky above, and those who turn many to righteousness like the stars for ever.
Luke 10:20: The seventy-two are told not to rejoice that the spirits are subject to them but to rejoice that their names are written in heaven.
Isaiah 49:16: God says he has engraved his people on the palms of his hands and that their walls are continually before him, a picture of being kept in mind by being written down.
Deuteronomy 4:2: Israel is told to add nothing to the word commanded and to take nothing from it, the same double instruction this chapter gives about writing down its words.
Revelation 22:18-19: A warning closes the book against anyone who adds to the words of its prophecy or takes away from them.

translationNotes.note: An old form of diminish, meaning to take away from or make smaller. The request at 104:11 is that the words be written down truthfully with nothing changed and nothing subtracted, which is the same pair of prohibitions Scripture attaches to its own text.

In Hebrew, remembering is doing something, not thinking about something. When God remembers Noah the wind passes over the waters, when he remembers Hannah she conceives, when he remembers his covenant he acts on it. Angels remembering the righteous before the glory of the Great One means their case is being actively kept, not merely recalled.

The chapter at 104:11 asks that the words be written truthfully in the languages men use. The book's own history reads like a commentary on that request: it survives complete only in Ethiopic, in substantial pieces in Greek, and in Aramaic fragments recovered from the Dead Sea caves.

translationNotes.term: The portals of heaven shall be opened to you
translationNotes.note: The same word the astronomical chapters used for the gates through which the sun, moon and stars come and go. The promise at 104:2 borrows that vocabulary and applies it to people, putting the righteous through the openings the luminaries use.

translationNotes.term: Books will be given to the righteous and the wise
translationNotes.note: The whole epistle ends on the handing over of written books, which is where it started at 92:1 and where the astronomical section ended at 82:1 with Enoch giving his books to Methuselah. Whatever else this book claims for itself, it consistently claims to be a document meant to be copied and passed on.

stories.keyTakeaway: The angels remember the righteous before the Great One and their names are written there. They are told to be hopeful, since they will shine as the lights of heaven and the portals of heaven will be opened to them. Sinners will alter and pervert the words, but books will be given to the righteous and the wise.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 105
summaryBullets: In those days the Lord told (them) to summon and testify to the children of earth concerning their wisdom: Show (it) to them; for you are their guides, and a recompense over the whole earth. (105:1).
For I and My son will be united with them for ever in the paths of uprightness in their lives; and you will have peace: rejoice, you children of uprightness. Amen. (105:2).
crossRefs: Proverbs 4:11: A teacher says he has taught the way of wisdom and led his hearer in the paths of uprightness, the same phrase this chapter ends on.
Matthew 5:14-16: A city set on a hill cannot be hidden, and a lamp is put on a stand rather than under a basket so that it gives light to everyone in the house.
Isaiah 42:6: A servant is given as a covenant for the people and a light for the nations, so that what he carries is for those outside as well.
Deuteronomy 30:19-20: Heaven and earth are called to witness that life and death have been set before the people, with the charge to choose life, the closing form of a testament.
Psalm 25:4: The psalmist asks to be made to know God's ways and taught his paths, the request that matches the instruction to guides here.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָמֵן (amen), truly, so be it
translationNotes.note: From a root meaning firm, steady, reliable. Saying it is not a decoration at the end of a speech; it is taking the thing said onto yourself. Deuteronomy 27:15-26 has the whole nation answer Amen to each curse in turn, and Nehemiah 8:6 has the people answer it with lifted hands and then bow to the ground.

The last chapter of the epistle closes with the same courtroom vocabulary the whole section has run on: witnesses, testimony, a record kept and a book read out. Being told to testify to the children of earth puts the hearers in the witness box rather than in the pulpit.

translationNotes.term: A recompense over the whole earth
translationNotes.note: Recompense here means a return made for something done, a repayment. The sentence says the guides themselves are that return, which is an unusual way to put it, and the chapter does not expand on it.

The chapter is two verses long and closes the epistle with a promise spoken in the first person. The Ethiopic reads that he and his son will be united with them for ever in the paths of uprightness. The book says nothing further about the phrase and offers no explanation of it anywhere else.

The book's standing phrase for mankind, used from the dream visions onward and set against the children of heaven. The instruction here is to go to them, which makes the last word of the epistle an errand rather than a verdict.

stories.keyTakeaway: The Lord tells them to summon the children of earth and testify to them about wisdom, since they are their guides and a recompense over the whole earth, and says that he and his son will be united with them for ever in the paths of uprightness. The chapter closes with Amen.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 106
summaryBullets: And after some days my son Methuselah took a wife for his son Lamech, and she became pregnant by him and bore a son. (106:1).

And his body was white as snow and red as the blooming of a rose, and the hair of his head †and his long locks were white as wool, and his eyes beautiful†. And when he opened his eyes, he lighted up the whole house like the sun, and the whole house was very bright. (106:2).
And thereupon he arose in the hands of the midwife, opened his mouth, and †conversed with† the Lord of righteousness. (106:3).
And his father Lamech was afraid of him and fled, and came to his father Methuselah. (106:4).

And he said to him: 'I have begotten a strange son, diverse from and unlike man, and resembling the sons of the God of heaven; and his nature is different and he is not like us, and his eyes are as the rays of the sun, and his countenance is glorious. (106:5).
And it seems to me that he is not sprung from me but from the angels, and I fear that in his days a wonder may be wrought on the earth. (106:6).
And now, my father, I am here to petition you and implore you that you may go to Enoch, our father, and learn from him the truth, for his dwelling-place is amongst the angels.' (106:7).

And when Methuselah heard the words of his son, he came to me to the ends of the earth; for he had heard that I was there, and he cried aloud, and I heard his voice and I came to him. And 1 said to him: 'Behold, here am I, my son, wherefore have you come to me?' (106:8).
And he answered and said: 'Because of a great cause of anxiety have I come to you, and because of a disturbing vision have I approached. (106:9).

And now, my father, hear me: to Lamech my son there has been born a son, the like of whom there is none, and his nature is not like man's nature, and the colour of his body is whiter than snow and redder than the bloom of a rose, and the hair of his head is whiter than white wool, and his eyes are like the rays of the sun, and he opened his eyes and thereupon lighted up the whole house. (106:10).
And he arose in the hands of the midwife, and opened his mouth and blessed the Lord of heaven. (106:11).

And his father Lamech became afraid and fled to me, and did not believe that he was sprung from him, but that he was in the likeness of the angels of heaven; and behold I have come to you that you may make known to me the truth.' (106:12).

And I, Enoch, answered and said to him: 'The Lord will do a new thing on the earth, and this I have already seen in a vision, and make known to you that in the generation of my father Jared some of the angels of heaven transgressed the word of the Lord. (106:13).
And behold they commit sin and transgress the law, and have united themselves with women and commit sin with them, and have married some of them, and have begot children by them. (106:14).
Yea, there shall come a great destruction over the whole earth, and there shall be a deluge and a great destruction for one year. (106:15).

And this son who has been born to you shall be left on the earth, and his three children shall be saved with him: when all mankind that are on the earth shall die he and his sons shall be saved . (106:16).

And they shall produce on the earth giants not according to the spirit, but according to the flesh, and there shall be a great punishment on the earth, and the earth shall be cleansed from all impurity. (106:17).

And now make known to your son Lamech that he who has been born is in truth his son, and call his name Noah; for he shall be left to you, and he and his sons shall be saved from the destruction, which shall come upon the earth on account of all the sin and all the unrighteousness, which shall be consummated on the earth in his days. (106:18).

And after that there shall be still more unrighteousness than that which was first consummated on the earth; for I know the mysteries of the holy ones; for He, the Lord, has showed me and informed me, and I have read (them) in the heavenly tablets. (106:19).
crossRefs: Genesis 5:28-29: Lamech fathers a son at a hundred and eighty-two and names him Noah, saying this one shall bring relief from the work and the painful toil of hands on ground the Lord has cursed.
Genesis 6:17-18: God announces a flood of waters to destroy all flesh, and in the same breath establishes his covenant with one man who will go into the ark with his sons and their wives.
Genesis 7:13: On that very day Noah and his three sons entered the ark with their wives, which is the count of survivors this chapter gives in advance.
Judges 13:6: A woman describes a visitor as having the appearance of the angel of God, very awesome, and says she did not ask where he came from, the same reaction Lamech has to his own son.
Luke 3:36-37: The genealogy runs back through Noah, Lamech, Methuselah, Enoch and Jared, which is the exact chain of fathers this chapter sends its messages up and down.

translationNotes.term: Jared, and what his name means
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יֶרֶד (Yered), from יָרַד (yarad), to go down
translationNotes.note: Enoch dates the angels' transgression to the generation of his father Jared, and the name is built on the ordinary Hebrew verb meaning to descend. This book makes the connection explicit earlier on, at 1 Enoch 6:6, where the watchers are said to have come down in the days of Jared on the summit of Mount Hermon.

translationNotes.term: The line of fathers in this chapter
translationNotes.note: Four generations are moving at once and the chapter assumes you can keep them straight. Genesis 5 gives the order: Jared fathers Enoch, Enoch fathers Methuselah, Methuselah fathers Lamech, and Lamech fathers the child born here. Lamech runs to his father, Methuselah runs to his, and the answer comes back down the same line.

Birth was women's business and a midwife ran it. She delivered the child, cut and tied the cord, washed it, rubbed it with salt and wrapped it tightly in cloth strips, which is the procedure Ezekiel 16:4 lists by naming what was left undone. Exodus 1:15-21 names two of them, Shiphrah and Puah.

The English word comes in through the Greek Old Testament, which renders the Hebrew Nephilim of Genesis 6:4 with gigantes. This chapter says at 106:17 that what will be produced is giants according to the flesh and not according to the spirit, which is this book's way of insisting they were physical offspring.

Genesis dates it precisely. The waters come on the seventeenth day of the second month of Noah's six hundredth year, and the earth is dry on the twenty-seventh day of the second month of the following year, which is a year and ten days from start to finish. The figure of one year here is that span rounded to its unit.

The chapter describes the newborn twice, at 106:2 and again at 106:10 when Methuselah repeats it to Enoch: skin white as snow and red as a rose, hair white as wool, eyes like the rays of the sun. The cross-shaped daggers in the middle of the first description mark the place where the manuscripts do not agree.

stories.keyTakeaway: Methuselah takes a wife for his son Lamech and a boy is born whose body is white and red, whose hair is white as wool and whose eyes light up the whole house. Lamech is afraid the child came from the angels, and Methuselah travels to the ends of the earth to ask Enoch, who tells him the child is truly his.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 107
summaryBullets: And I saw written on them that generation upon generation shall transgress, till a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed and sin passes away from the earth, and all manner of good comes upon it. (107:1).
And now, my son, go and make known to your son Lamech that this son, which has been born, is in truth his son, and that (this) is no lie.' (107:2).

And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch--for he had shown to him everything in secret--he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction. (107:3).
crossRefs: Genesis 5:29: The child is named and the reason is given in the same sentence, that out of the ground the Lord has cursed this one shall bring relief from work and painful toil.
Genesis 8:21: After the flood God says he will never again curse the ground because of man, nor strike down every living creature as he has done.
Sirach 44:17: Noah is called perfect and righteous, taken in exchange for the world in the time of wrath, and left as a remnant to the earth.
Isaiah 11:9: The earth is promised to be full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea, with nothing hurting or destroying in all his holy mountain.
Jeremiah 31:33-34: A covenant is promised in which the law is written on the heart and every one of them knows the Lord, from the least to the greatest.

translationNotes.term: Noah, and the wordplay in the name
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נֹחַ (Noach), rest - נָחַם (nacham), to comfort, to bring relief
translationNotes.note: The name itself is built on the root meaning rest. The reason given for it in Genesis 5:29 uses a different verb that sounds close to it, nacham, to comfort or bring relief, and the two are set beside each other on purpose. This chapter gives the same reason in the same shape when it says he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.

The English word has softened. It comes from Latin words meaning to strengthen thoroughly, and in older English to comfort someone was to give them strength to carry something, not to soothe them. That is the sense in this verse and in Genesis 5:29, where what the child brings is relief from the hard labour of working cursed ground.

translationNotes.term: Called the name of that son
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קָרָא שֵׁם (qara shem), to call a name
translationNotes.note: Naming in these books is a public act with a reason attached, usually spoken aloud at the time by the mother or the father. Genesis is full of the pattern: a name, then the word for, then the circumstance it came out of. This verse follows it exactly, which is why the name and the explanation arrive together.

The chapter says Enoch showed Methuselah everything in secret before sending him home with the answer. The book repeatedly frames its contents that way, as hidden things given to one man and passed to a named heir, which is the same claim the epistle makes when it hands over books at 82:1 and 104:12-13.

The whole of history between the flood and the end is summed up in one clause. It says the pattern repeats and does not improve, and that the change, when it comes, arrives as a generation of righteousness rather than as an improvement on the last one.

stories.keyTakeaway: Enoch reads on the tablets that generation after generation will transgress until a generation of righteousness arises, transgression is destroyed and sin passes from the earth. He sends Methuselah back to tell Lamech the child is truly his son, and the boy is named Noah, because he will comfort the earth after the destruction.

stories.title: 📜 1 Enoch (Book of Enoch) 108
summaryBullets: Another book which Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah and for those who will come after him, and keep the law in the last days. (108:1).
You who have done good shall wait for those days till an end is made of those who work evil; and an end of the might of the transgressors. (108:2).

And wait you indeed till sin has passed away, for their names shall be blotted out of the book of life and out of the holy books, and their seed shall be destroyed for ever, and their spirits shall be slain, and they shall cry and make lamentation in a place that is a chaotic wilderness, and in the fire shall they burn ; for there is no earth there. (108:3).

And I saw there something like an invisible cloud; for by reason of its depth I could not look over, and I saw a flame of fire blazing brightly, and things like shining mountains circling and sweeping to and fro. (108:4).

And I asked one of the holy angels who was with me and said to him: 'What is this shining thing? for it is not a heaven but only the flame of a blazing fire, and the voice of weeping and crying and lamentation and strong pain.' (108:5).

And he said to me: 'This place which you see--here are cast the spirits of sinners and blasphemers, and of those who work wickedness, and of those who pervert everything that the Lord has spoken through the mouth of the prophets--(even) the things that shall be. (108:6).

For some of them are written and inscribed above in the heaven, in order that the angels may read them and know that which shall befall the sinners, and the spirits of the humble, and of those who have afflicted their bodies, and been recompensed by God; and of those who have been put to shame by wicked men: (108:7).
Who love God and loved neither gold nor silver nor any of the good things which are in the world, but gave over their bodies to torture. (108:8).

Who, since they came into being, longed not after earthly food, but regarded everything as a passing breath, and lived accordingly, and the Lord tried them much, and their spirits were found pure so that they should bless His name. (108:9).

And all the blessings destined for them I have recounted in the books. And he has assigned them their recompense, because they have been found to be such as loved heaven more than their life in the world, and though they were trodden under foot of wicked men, and experienced abuse and reviling from them and were put to shame, yet they blessed Me. (108:10).

And now I will summon the spirits of the good who belong to the generation of light, and I will transform those who were born in darkness, who in the flesh were not recompensed with such honour as their faithfulness deserved. (108:11).
And I will bring forth in shining light those who have loved My holy name, and I will seat each on the throne of his honour. (108:12).
And they shall be resplendent for times without number; for righteousness is the judgement of God; for to the faithful He will give faithfulness in the habitation of upright paths. (108:13).
And they shall see those who were, born in darkness led into darkness, while the righteous shall be resplendent. (108:14).
And the sinners shall cry aloud and see them resplendent, and they indeed will go where days and seasons are prescribed for them.' (108:15).
crossRefs: Psalm 69:28: The psalmist asks that his enemies be blotted out of the book of the living and not enrolled among the righteous, the same register this chapter says names are struck from.
Revelation 3:5: The one who conquers is promised white garments and that his name will never be blotted out of the book of life, with his name confessed before the Father and the angels.

Hebrews 11:35-38: Some were tortured and refused release, others faced mocking, flogging, chains, stoning and being sawn in two, went about in skins, destitute and afflicted, and the world was not worthy of them.
Isaiah 66:24: The book of Isaiah ends with the dead bodies of those who rebelled, whose worm does not die and whose fire is not quenched.
Matthew 19:28: Those who followed are told that in the new world they will sit on thrones, which is the seating this chapter promises to the humble.

translationNotes.note: The heading marks this chapter as an appendix. The epistle has already closed with Amen at 105:2, and this is a separate piece written to Methuselah and to those who keep the law in the last days. It stands last in the Ethiopic and is not part of the sections that come before it.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סֵפֶר הַחַיִּים (sepher hachayyim), the book of the living
translationNotes.note: The picture behind it is a civic register, the roll of names of the people who belong to a place and are counted alive in it. Being written in it is enrolment; being blotted out is having your entry struck through. Moses asks to be blotted out of the book God has written at Exodus 32:32, and the answer keeps the register in God's own hands.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תֹּהוּ וָבֹהוּ (tohu vavohu), formless and empty
translationNotes.note: The phrase renders the pair of Hebrew words used of the earth before it was ordered, without form and void, at Genesis 1:2. Jeremiah 4:23 takes the same pair and applies it to a land under judgement, which is the sense here: not a rough place, but a place with no order left in it. The chapter adds that there is no earth there.

translationNotes.term: Those who have afflicted their bodies
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עִנָּה נֶפֶשׁ (innah nephesh), to afflict the soul
translationNotes.note: This is fasting, not self-harm. Afflicting the soul is the standing Hebrew expression for it, and it is what the law commands on the Day of Atonement at Leviticus 16:29-31 and 23:27-32. In practice it meant going without food and drink, without washing and without ordinary comforts for a set day.

translationNotes.term: Gave over their bodies to torture
translationNotes.note: The class of people the chapter is describing is the ones who died rather than comply. 2 Maccabees 7 tells of a mother and seven sons put to death one by one for refusing to eat swine's flesh under Antiochus, with the tortures described in detail. That is the shape of what is being praised here, not asceticism for its own sake.

The word is the one Ecclesiastes 1:2 repeats and older English renders vanity: not worthlessness but a puff of air, something real that cannot be held or kept. Regarding everything as a passing breath means treating possessions as things that are already on their way out of your hands.

stories.keyTakeaway: Another book Enoch wrote for Methuselah and for those who keep the law in the last days. The good are to wait until the workers of evil are ended and their names blotted from the book of life. Enoch is shown a place of blazing fire where the spirits of sinners are cast, and the humble are promised light and thrones.

intro:
1 Enoch is transmitted under the name of Enoch son of Jared, the seventh generation from Adam, who "walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away" (Genesis 5:21-24). The book opens by naming him: "The words of the blessing of Enoch, with which he blessed the elect and righteous, who will be living in the day of tribulation" (1:1). It traces his descent through Jared, Mahalalel, Cainan, Enos, Seth, and Adam at 37:1, and at 60:8 it calls him "the seventh from Adam." Jude 1:14-15 quotes it: "Enoch, the seventh from Adam, also prophesied about them: 'Behold, the Lord is coming with myriads of His holy ones to execute judgment on everyone, and to convict all the ungodly of every ungodly act of wickedness and every harsh word spoken against Him by ungodly sinners.'" Those words are 1 Enoch 1:9. Jude attributes the prophecy to Enoch; he does not name a book.

The text is a collection of five works. No manuscript from Qumran carries all five, and the Astronomical Book was copied there on its own; the Ge'ez manuscripts join them and number straight through to 108 chapters. (1) The Book of the Watchers, chapters 1-36. An opening oracle of judgment, then two hundred angels who bind themselves by oath on the summit of Mount Hermon in the days of Jared (6:6), the wives they take, the giants born to them, the metalwork, weapons, cosmetics, and sorcery they teach (8:1), the binding of Azazel in the desert place called Dudael (10:4), Enoch's intercession for the Watchers and its refusal (12-16), and his journeys to the ends of the earth, the mountain of the dead, and the places of punishment (17-36). (2) The Book of Parables, chapters 37-71, also called the Similitudes. Three parables on the Elect One, the Son of Man, the Head of Days, and the Lord of Spirits, ending at 71:14 when the angel greets Enoch, "This is the Son of Man who is born to righteousness." (3) The Astronomical Book, chapters 72-82, in which the angel Uriel shows Enoch the gates of the sun and moon, the winds, and the stars. It fixes the year at 364 days (72:32; 74:12; 82:6) and counts the four intercalary days that divide the seasons (82:4-6). (4) The Book of Dreams, chapters 83-90. Two visions, the first of the flood, the second a survey of history from Adam to the judgment told as a story of sheep, bulls, and wild beasts. (5) The Epistle of Enoch, chapters 91-105, which contains the Apocalypse of Weeks (93:1-10 and 91:11-17) and the woes against the rich and the violent. Two further sections follow it: the birth of Noah (106-107), and a closing book that introduces itself at 108:1 as "another book which Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah."

The oldest copies are Aramaic. Eleven of them were found in Qumran Cave 4 (4Q201-4Q202 and 4Q204-4Q212) and published by J. T. Milik with Matthew Black at Oxford in 1976. They carry four of the five parts: the Watchers, the Astronomical Book, the Dreams, and the Epistle. No fragment of the Parables was found at Qumran. The script of 4Q208, an astronomical copy, places it at the end of the third century BC or the beginning of the second. Greek survives in two principal witnesses: Codex Panopolitanus, found in a grave at Akhmim in Upper Egypt in the winter of 1886-87 by the French Archaeological Mission and published by Urbain Bouriant in 1892, carrying 1:1-32:6; and the Chester Beatty papyrus, carrying 97:6-107:3. George Syncellus quotes further Greek around AD 810. Latin survives for 1:9 and for 106:1-18 only. The complete text exists in Ge'ez alone, in manuscripts of the fifteenth to nineteenth centuries, on which R. H. Charles built his critical edition in 1906. James Bruce brought three Ge'ez copies out of Abyssinia in 1773, and Richard Laurence published the first English translation from the Bodleian copy in 1821. The Ge'ez title is Metsehafe Henok, the Book of Enoch; the numeral distinguishes it from the Slavonic 2 Enoch and the Hebrew 3 Enoch, a modern convention following the order in which the three became known in Europe.

1 Enoch is canonical in the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church and in the Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church, where it stands among the books of the Old Testament, and it is received in the Haymanot tradition of the Beta Israel. No other communion receives it. It is not in the Jewish canon, not in the Septuagint or Vulgate collections received by the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches, and not in the Protestant Bible or its Apocrypha. Ancient attestation runs from the second century. The Epistle of Barnabas quotes it as scripture (16:5, early second century). Tertullian defends it in On the Apparel of Women 1.3 (c. AD 200): he records that some do not receive it, argues that Noah, Enoch's great-grandson, could have carried its contents through the flood by memory, and appeals to the point that "Enoch possesses a testimony in the Apostle Jude." Origen quotes it in Against Celsus 5.54-55 (c. AD 248) and states there that the books under Enoch's name do not circulate in the churches as divine. Jerome records in Lives of Illustrious Men 4 (AD 392) that Jude was rejected by many because it cites the apocryphal Enoch, and that the letter had nevertheless gained authority by age and use. Augustine, in City of God 18.38 (finished c. AD 426), grants on Jude's authority that Enoch left divine writings and says they were not placed in the canon kept in the temple because their antiquity made them suspect.
